nest_recommendations.impact: Directly serves the north-star whole-repo/whole-database/parquet payloads where LDM + max level dominate; cheap one-time build cost, decode speed roughly level-independent. No format change (still SECTION_ENCODING_ZSTD bytes).

nest_recommendations.idea: Vendor a pure-Rust FSE/tANS + Huff0 entropy codec for skewed integer/token streams, registered as new additive encoding ids, applied to delta-coded BM25 postings (0x08) and HNSW neighbor lists (0x07) and term dictionaries -- never to embeddings. Share the spread/normalize/table-build core between encode and decode; FSEU16 variant for 16-bit tokenized terms. Use libdeflate's two-level decode table + packed-u32 entries + branchless 64-bit refill for a tiny mmap-friendly decoder.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/fse.rs + huff0.rs (new, <300 loc each, shared table core) + new SECTION_ENCODING_FSE id in layout/mod.rs + decode arm in encoding/mod.rs; encode-side delta + entropy in nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs and ann/codec.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: A sovereign in-house entropy floor below generic zstd on skewed residuals (tANS within a fraction of a percent of Shannon entropy where Huffman loses up to ~1 bit/symbol). Table build is a pure function of the histogram -> byte-identical/deterministic, content_hash and reproducible builds preserved. Larger surface, so lower priority than dict+shuffle.

nest_recommendations.idea: Formalize a skippable-optional vs unskippable-required bit on section entries so a future v1 file with an unknown OPTIONAL section (e.g. a new graph index, audio/video payload) still validates and serves on an older runtime, while unknown REQUIRED sections error cleanly via NestError -- extending the additive guarantee without a v2 bump. Mirror zstd's 0x184D2A5x skippable-magic pattern and snappy's reserved-range partitioning.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/layout/section_entry.rs (a flags field on SectionEntry) + reader/parse.rs + reader/validate.rs (skip-or-error logic) + manifest capabilities
nest_recommendations.impact: Protects the additive-only guarantee as the format grows toward repos/audio/video/parquet; an older binary keeps working against newer optional extensions. Pure format-hardening, no ratio impact, but load-bearing for the north-star expansion of payload types.

nest_recommendations.idea: Chunk large compressed sections into independently-decodable sub-blocks with a self-describing 12-16 byte header (skippable-frame style: magic + compressed-size + uncompressed-size hint), so a single chunk decodes for nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation reopen without inflating the whole section, materialize() pre-allocates exactly (no realloc), and large text sections can decode in parallel via rayon. Pair with the shared dictionary so small-chunk random access does not cost ratio.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (sub-block framing inside the existing zstd/dict encoding id, no new section id, no version bump) + nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs (per-chunk decode + parallel path)
nest_recommendations.impact: Unlocks O(1) citation reopen and parallel materialize at scale without breaking single-file/offline/deterministic (fixed chunk size + fixed params -> deterministic byte layout -> stable per-section physical SHA-256). Slight ratio cost per chunk window-reset, recovered by the shared dict. Use rayon/crossbeam, NOT zstdmt's two-mutex pool.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a GB/s-class byte-aligned LZ77 codec (lz4/snappy block format: token + LSIC/varint length extension + 2-byte LE offset, wildcopy decode) as a new additive encoding id, as the first compressor nest can legally apply to hot-path-adjacent surfaces zstd is banned from: per-citation text materialize (always-compressed text without per-query latency) and, longer term, an lz4-framed transparent layer over int8 embeddings decoded into a small scratch buffer just-in-time before the SIMD dot product. Also reuse the LSIC add-255 varint for nest's own section-length/manifest varints.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/lz4_block.rs (new, <300 loc, panic-free) + new SECTION_ENCODING_LZ4 id in layout/mod.rs + decode in encoding/mod.rs; just-in-time embeddings decode path would sit in nest-runtime/src/search.rs scratch buffer before simd/mod.rs::score_int8_section
nest_recommendations.impact: Does NOT beat zstd on cold ratio (lz4 loses), so not the headline lever -- its value is widening the SET of compressible bytes to surfaces with a tight decode budget, and a zero-C-dependency sovereign fallback for one-binary vendoring. Embeddings-over-lz4 is speculative and must prove it does not regress the AVX2/NEON kernel latency.

nest_recommendations.idea: Generalize the SimdBackend OnceLock into a functable-style struct of fn pointers (resolve-once, indirect-call-forever) so new kernels register one entry each, and add CRC32-C via carryless multiply (PCLMULQDQ on x86_64, PMULL on aarch64) behind it as a fast NON-crypto hash for dedup keys / section identity probes that precede compression. The four SHA-256 surfaces stay cryptographic and unchanged.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/mod.rs (functable struct replacing the BACKEND OnceLock + per-fn match arms) + a new simd/crc32c.rs kernel; keep each simd/*.rs under 300 loc as kernels multiply (shuffle/un-delta, f16 convert, i8 widen all become entries)
nest_recommendations.impact: Engineering scaffolding only (no ratio win): keeps the SIMD layer under the file-size cap as shuffle/un-delta/entropy kernels arrive, and speeds dedup/identity work before compression. CRC-as-hash must never be confused with the SHA-256 integrity contract.

compression_wins: Trained shared zstd dictionary over chunks_canonical (and spans/provenance/bm25 terms) -- the single biggest unrealized win for nest's thousands-of-short-similar-chunks shape; kills per-section entropy-table + cold-start redundancy that level-19-no-dict pays on every blob; expected to push the tiny preset's text bytes below today's 0.283 ratio while keeping content_hash stable.

Byte-shuffle + bytedelta in front of zstd on chunks_original_spans (near-constant high bytes of u64 offsets -> long runs) and the int8 scale array (contiguous f32 LE) -- pure multiplier on structured numeric sections, zero new dependency, Blosc-measured 3.9x->5.9x headroom on float arrays.

Cost-driven per-section encoding selection (trial-encode, keep smallest measured output) -- guarantees each section's best available codec/params without hand-tuning, never regresses since raw is always a candidate, deterministic by smallest-size total order.

zstd level 22 + long-distance-matching for the north-star large payloads (whole-repo / whole-database / parquet) -- LDM catches far-apart cross-file duplication the 64KB-window match-finder misses, at one-time build cost with level-independent decode speed.

In-house FSE/tANS over delta-coded BM25 postings (0x08), HNSW adjacency (0x07), and term dictionaries -- within a fraction of a percent of Shannon entropy on skewed residuals where Huffman loses up to ~1 bit/symbol and where zstd's generic stage carries unnecessary container/table overhead; a sovereign entropy floor below generic zstd.

Repeat-offset cache awareness for periodic/structured metadata (chunk_ids, spans deltas) -- structured data spends ~1 offset code instead of a full offset, compounding with shuffle on the same arrays.
Shared-dictionary + per-chunk framing together -- recover the small-chunk ratio loss from seekable chunking so citation-reopen random access costs no ratio.
watch_outs: NEVER apply shuffle/bytedelta/dictionary/zstd to the embeddings BODY scored from mmap on the hot path. Shuffle destroys the row-contiguous layout AVX2/NEON dot-products read; any entropy/dict stage breaks 'scored directly from mmap'. Gate every transform strictly by section id in writer/encoding_choice.rs. Embeddings stay raw/f16/int8 forever in v1. (Only the int8 SCALE array -- not the i8 bodies -- is a safe shuffle target.)

Dictionary training must be a pure deterministic function: feed ZDICT samples in canonical/alphabetical order and seed any randomized step, or reproducible builds (same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file) break. Same for FSE/tANS: table build must be a pure function of the histogram. Verify byte-identical output across two builds before shipping.

content_hash is over DECODED canonical bytes and section checksums are over PHYSICAL bytes -- confirm a dict-compressed or shuffled section yields the SAME content_hash as raw (it does only if decode is exact and lossless). bytedelta/shuffle must round-trip bit-exactly; trunc_prec (lossy mantissa zeroing) is explicitly OUT of any required/content-hashed section.

All new codecs are additive within v1: encoding ids in reserved 4-255, section ids in reserved 0x09+, and do NOT bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION (that is only for a true v2 where an existing field changes meaning). Adding the dictionary section must not enter content_hash (keep it OPTIONAL, hash over the canonical six only) so citations survive.

Do NOT add a DEFLATE/zlib/zlib-ng codec or a Snappy/lz4 codec to beat zstd on cold ratio -- they all LOSE to zstd-19 on text. Their value is structural (fallback, hot-path-adjacent surfaces, format discipline), not headline ratio. lz4-over-int8-embeddings is speculative and must prove no AVX2/NEON latency regression before it ships.

500xCompressor and any neural/semantic compression is incompatible with the frozen offline v1: it needs an 8B-LLM forward pass at decode time, breaks determinism (float GPU kernels), offline/single-file/small-core, and cannot losslessly reconstruct bytes for nest://content_hash/chunk_id reopen. Keep it OUT; cite it only as the reason semantic compression is excluded.

No panics in library code -- every new codec (shuffle, bytedelta, fse, huff0, lz4_block, zstd_dict) returns typed thiserror NestError on malformed/oversized input; reject unknown encoding ids cleanly (decode_payload already does for unknown ids). lz4 wildcopy needs output over-allocation slack -- handle bounds without UB.

File hygiene: <=300 lines per rust source file (333 hard cap), single-responsibility. Split shuffle/bytedelta/fse/huff0/lz4 into separate modules and share table/spread cores between encode and decode to stay under the cap as the encoding/ directory grows from 4 files to many.

zstdmt's two-mutex worker pool is the WRONG concurrency model for Rust -- steal only the on-disk skippable-frame chunk format, implement parallel decode with rayon/crossbeam. CRC32-C as a hash is non-cryptographic and must never be conflated with the four SHA-256 integrity surfaces.

Per-chunk framing and multithreaded chunking slightly HURT ratio (each chunk resets the codec window/dictionary). Only chunk LARGE sections, and always pair chunking with the shared trained dictionary so small-chunk random access stops costing ratio; keep small metadata sections as single frames.

Runtime is offline by construction -- none of these codecs may open a socket or fetch anything; dictionaries live INSIDE the container, trained at build time in python, decoded from mmap in rust. All zstd/dict/shuffle cost is amortized one-time at build/cold-decode and must stay off the SIMD scoring hot path.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The field has converged on a clean separation of concerns that maps directly onto nest. (1) DECORRELATION/MODELING is split from ENTROPY CODING: c-blosc2 proves the cheapest ratio gains come from a SIMD byte-transform stage (shuffle/bitshuffle/bytedelta) that merely presents better-conditioned bytes to an unchanged downstream coder; klauspost and zstd factor entropy into reusable primitives (FSE/tANS + Huff0). (2) tANS (FSE) is the modern entropy floor -- near-arithmetic accuracy at single-LUT-lookup speed, with Huff0 (4 interleaved bitstreams for ILP) for literals; this is the zstd/klauspost back-end and the libdeflate two-level packed-table + branchless-refill decoder is its fast deterministic decode form. (3) TRAINED SHARED DICTIONARIES are the decisive lever for the many-small-similar-records regime that nest IS: zstd ZDICT/COVER, brotli's 13.5k-word static dictionary + 121 transforms, zlib deflateSetDictionary, and c-blosc2's superchunk dict all attack cold-start and inter-record redundancy that per-blob compression cannot touch. (4) FORMAT DISCIPLINE is standardized: self-describing frames with skippable-magic ranges (zstd 0x184D2A5x, snappy reserved skippable/unskippable partitioning, zstdmt 12-16 byte chunk headers) give additive forward-compatibility and per-chunk seekability/parallelism, and resolve-once functable dispatch (zlib-ng) decouples algorithm from microarchitecture. (5) ENCODING CHOICE is measured, not heuristic: libdeflate iterates LZ parsing on real post-entropy bit cost to a fixpoint and selects block types by measured size -- 'compress once, serve many' fits nest's deterministic offline build exactly. At the extreme, 500xCompressor's neural KV-cache compression marks the boundary nest will NOT cross: lossy, LLM-at-decode, non-deterministic, the antithesis of offline/single-file/byte-exact. nest sits in the sweet spot to exploit (1)+(3)+(5) immediately on its non-embedding sections with zero hot-path risk, and to grow (2) into a sovereign in-house entropy stage over its postings/adjacency residuals.

categories.name: compression-integer
categories.focus: integer and posting-list compression (bitpacking, varint, elias-fano)

repos.one_liner: A C library of the world's fastest integer-array codecs, anchored by TurboPFor (a SIMD/AVX2 patched-frame-of-reference scheme) that bitpacks fixed 128/256-int blocks with per-block exception lists and integrated FOR/delta/zigzag, plus directly-addressable random access into compressed data without full block decode.
repos.core_innovation: Patched bitpacking on small fixed blocks: pick a base bit-width b sized so MOST values fit, store the few outliers as cheap exceptions (either an exception bitmap + secondary bit-width, or variable-byte), and lay the packed bits out vertically across SIMD lanes so a whole block decodes branch-free. A 2-bit per-block header selects {constant, plain bitpack, bitpack+bitmap-exceptions, bitpack+vbyte-exceptions}, and dedicated DA functions allow O(1) random access to a single value without decompressing the block.
key_techniques: TurboPFor patched-FOR: per-block base bit-width b + exception list for outliers, 2-bit block-type header (constant/bitpack/bitmap-exc/vbyte-exc)
Exception encoding two ways: popcount-addressed exception BITMAP + secondary bit-width for exception values, OR variable-byte for non-uniform exceptions
SIMD vertical/interleaved bitpacking (TurboPackV128 SSE, TurboPackV256 AVX2): 8x uint32 LE values packed across lanes, branch-free unpack >20 Gint/s (80 Gb/s)
Integrated FOR (subtract min), delta (d/d1 for sorted-with-dup / strictly-increasing) and zigzag (z) transforms folded into the codec, plus delta-of-delta + RLE for timestamps
Direct/random access (TurboPForDA / TurboForDA): decode a single packed entry by bit-offset arithmetic with zero block decompression
Byte/nibble TRANSPOSE+XOR+zigzag (TPbyte, 2D/3D/4D) SIMD pre-transform that columnarizes mantissa bytes before packing (~9.4 GB/s)
Gorilla-style TurboFloat / TurboFloat-LzXor float codecs: delta-of-delta + RLE on f32/f64, FCM/DFCM context-model prediction
Space-efficient varbyte byte-range classifier: 0-176 in 1 byte, 177-240 -> 14 bit, 241-248 -> 19 bit, 249-255 -> 32 bit (denser than LEB128)
repos.nest_application: Build a new additive encoding id (reserved range 4-255) in nest-format crates/nest-format/src/encoding/* that adds a TurboPFor-style patched-bitpacking codec for INTEGER sections, not embeddings. First target: chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans (offset/length arrays) and future bm25 posting lists in nest-runtime/src/bm25 -- monotone-ish u32/u64 arrays where delta(d1)+FOR+bitpack with exceptions crushes size below zstd. Highest-value target is hnsw_index(0x07) neighbor-id adjacency lists: per-node sorted neighbor ids delta-encode and patch-bitpack beautifully, shrinking the index section that dominates the tiny preset. The DA random-read property lets nest-runtime read one neighbor id or one span straight off mmap without decoding the whole block, preserving the zero-copy hot path. Reimplement clean-room in pure safe Rust (GPL-2.0 forbids vendoring) with portable u32 lane packing; gate SIMD unpack behind the existing simd dispatcher (AVX2/NEON/scalar). Determinism is trivial: fixed block size 256, canonical b = max-bits-after-FOR, exceptions in ascending index order -> byte-identical. Keep little-endian repr per nest invariants. Each piece (block header, bitpack/unpack, exception list, delta transform) fits under the 300-line cap as single-responsibility modules.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on the north star: patched-bitpacking + delta-FOR is state-of-the-art for the exact data nest stores as integers (ids, spans, hnsw adjacency, bm25 postings), routinely 15-25% size at >10 Gint/s decode -- smaller than zstd on these arrays AND faster, while direct-access compresses without sacrificing nest's mmap-and-score-off-disk hot path. Single biggest lever to shrink the index/metadata sections (everything except f32 embeddings) below the current tiny preset.
repos.license: GPL-2.0 (dual-licensed; commercial license from author). GPL is incompatible with nest vendoring -- the algorithm must be CLEAN-ROOM reimplemented in Rust from the format description, never copied.
repos.perf_notes: Benchmarks (ZIPF/gov2): TurboPFor256 ~2.4 GB/s enc, ~11 GB/s dec at 15.7% ratio; SIMD bitpack alone >20 Gint/s (80 Gb/s); TurboByte+TurboPack hybrid ~17 GB/s enc / 12 GB/s dec at 25%; EliasFanoV ~3.2/3.6 GB/s at 15.8%. Fixed 128 (SSE) / 256 (AVX2) int blocks are deliberate: whole-block decode fits L1/L2, vertical lane layout is branch-free. Per-block overhead is tiny (2-bit header + width byte + exception list). Vertical SIMD layout needs care to port to NEON (128-bit -> 4x u32) vs AVX2 (256-bit -> 8x u32); scalar fallback is a straightforward bit-cursor unpack.

repos.one_liner: A C++11 library of vectorized integer-array codecs (SIMD-BP128, FastPFor/SIMD-FastPFor, StreamVByte, VByte, Simple9/16, varint-G8IU) that decode 4+ billion 32-bit ints/sec (~15 GB/s) by combining frame-based binary bit-packing with patched frame-of-reference exception handling over fixed blocks of 128 integers.
repos.core_innovation: Patched binary packing: split an integer array into fixed 128-int blocks, pick a single bit-width b per block so most values fit in b bits, vertically bit-pack all 128 lanes at width b (compression ratio 32/b, decoded branchlessly with SIMD shift+mask), and store the rare values exceeding b bits ("exceptions") out-of-band in a separate compressed exception stream keyed by position + high-bits. Combined with delta coding for sorted lists, this turns monotone ID arrays into a few bits per element while keeping decode fully vectorizable and branch-free.
key_techniques: SIMD-BP128: vertical bit-packing of 128 ints at a uniform bit-width b, decoded with SSE2 shift/mask (32/b ratio, no branches in hot loop)
FastPFor / SIMD-FastPFor: patched frame-of-reference -- per-block bit-width minimizing total bits, exceptions (values >= 2^b) stored separately as position bytes + packed high-bit residuals
Delta / differential coding with a stored offset so sorted ID lists become small gaps before packing; SIMD 4-lane delta for vectorized prefix-sum on decode
StreamVByte: byte-oriented varint with 2-bit length control codes in a separate stream so payload bytes are gathered via SSSE3 pshufb
Simple9 / Simple16: pack as many ints as fit into a 32-bit word with a 4-bit selector describing the layout
Self-delimiting block framing: 'length u32 then that many 32-bit ints, repeat'
Hand-tuned unrolled per-bit-width (1..32) bitpack kernels, also shipped standalone as the simdcomp C library
repos.nest_application: Two concrete targets, both storing raw u32 arrays today with zero compression. (1) nest-runtime/src/ann/codec.rs HnswIndex::to_bytes writes every neighbor id as a 4-byte LE u32 ('for &id in nbrs { out.extend_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes()) }'); per-layer neighbor lists are small bounded id sets -- sort each list then delta+bitpack (SIMD-BP128 style) so each id costs ~b bits not 32, shrinking section 0x07. (2) nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs Bm25Index::to_bytes writes each posting as doc:u32 + tf:u32; doc ids per term are strictly increasing, the canonical FastPFor/delta case -- delta-code doc gaps then FastPFor-pack, bitpack tf separately, shrinking section 0x08. Implement as a pure-Rust scalar port of SIMD-BP128+FastPFor (new nest-runtime module, single-responsibility, <=300 loc; no SIMD needed for correctness, decode stays deterministic). Both are additive: index payloads are versioned (HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION / BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION), so bump the per-section payload version, NOT NEST_FORMAT_VERSION, keeping v1 frozen. Also seeds a future general 'bitpacked/varint' section encoding id (4-255 reserved) for other integer-heavy sections like chunks_original_spans offsets.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission for 'compress more than everyone': the tiny/hybrid presets ship hnsw (0x07) and bm25 (0x08), both storing integer id arrays at a fixed 32 bits each -- the largest uncompressed integer surface in a .nest file. zstd is deliberately NOT on the embeddings hot path, but these index sections are cold-decoded once at load, so FastPFor-style delta+bitpack can cut them several-fold (sorted doc-id gaps routinely pack to 4-8 bits) with no recall loss, pushing the tiny-preset size ratio below today's 0.283 while preserving deterministic/offline/single-file guarantees.
repos.perf_notes: Reference C++ decodes >4e9 ints/s (~15 GB/s) on x64 via SSE2/SSSE3; SIMD-BP128 ~2x faster than varint-G8IU/PFOR while saving up to 2 bits/int; SIMD-FastPFor within ~10% of Simple-8b compression at ~2x decode speed. For nest, a scalar Rust port loses SIMD throughput but index sections are tiny and cold-loaded once at mmap time, so even scalar decode is negligible; memory cost is one 128-int block buffer. NEON/AVX2 kernels could later mirror nest-runtime's existing simd dispatcher pattern.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (patent-free except varint-G8IU, which is patented and must be avoided)

repos.one_liner: A tiny Apache-2.0 ANSI-C scalar codec for Frame-of-Reference (FOR) integer compression that bit-packs 32-bit integer residuals against a per-block minimum and supports random access, search, and append operating directly on the compressed bytes.
repos.core_innovation: Frame-of-Reference: store one block minimum (base) plus a single bit-width b = ceil(log2(max-min+1)), then bit-pack every value as a fixed-width b-bit residual (value - base). This makes the compressed array a flat, addressable bit-matrix so you can random-access element i in O(1) (bit offset = i*b), binary-search a sorted block, and append in place WITHOUT decoding the whole stream -- the codec computes over compressed bytes, not just stores them.
key_techniques: 5-byte block metadata header: 4-byte LE uint32 base/min + 1-byte bit-width b (#define METADATA 5)
Residual = value - block_min, bit-packed at b = ceil(log2(max-min+1)) bits (frame of reference removes the high-order common prefix)
Cascaded byte-aligned bitpacking via dispatch tables for_pack32/16/8/x[bits] with fully unrolled generated kernels in for-gen.c (32-, 16-, 8-, remainder groups)
for_select_bits(): O(1) random access by index*bits offset, mask across word boundary, add base -- no full decode
for_lower_bound_search_bits(): binary search executed directly on the compressed sorted block
for_append_*(): in-place append, only re-encodes (widen b) when new value exceeds current bit width
sorted vs unsorted variants: sorted extracts min/max from endpoints instead of full scan
for_compressed_size_bits/sorted/unsorted: precompute exact output size before allocating
repos.nest_application: Adopt FOR as a new additive encoding id (reserve one in 4-255) in nest-format/src/encoding.rs, targeting the integer-heavy required sections: chunk_ids and especially chunks_original_spans (byte-offset/length pairs that are monotonic and small-range -> ideal for delta+FOR). The select()/lower_bound primitives map directly onto nest-runtime materialize and citation resolution (nest://content_hash/chunk_id): a FOR-packed spans section lets the reader fetch span[i] with one O(1) bit-extract straight off mmap, no decode of the whole section, preserving the zero-copy hot path. For bm25_index(0x08) posting lists (doc ids in deterministic alphabetical-term order), delta-code doc ids then FOR-pack each term's postings -- shrinks the index while keeping deterministic byte layout. Because FOR residual width is data-derived and the base is stored, builds stay byte-identical (deterministic). Implement as a small repr(C)-friendly Rust module (<300 loc, pure scalar, no panic / thiserror on malformed bits) since the C is trivially portable; gives a cheaper alternative to zstd for integer sections where random access matters and zstd block decode would break zero-copy.
repos.compression_relevance: High for the specific axis of integer-section compression with preserved random access. FOR is the canonical first stage for compressing chunk_ids, chunks_original_spans, and bm25 posting lists. Unlike zstd (which nest already uses but must decode a whole block, breaking mmap zero-copy), FOR keeps elements individually addressable, so it compresses AND serves directly from disk -- exactly nest's north star. It is a building block, not a finished codec: pairing delta-coding + FOR (and later PFOR-style patching for outliers, which libfor omits) is the path to beating general-purpose compressors on the structured-integer sections.
repos.license: Apache License 2.0
repos.perf_notes: Pure scalar ANSI C, intentionally no SIMD (author trades peak throughput for portability/simplicity; runs on Linux/Windows/any sane system). Speed comes from fully unrolled, byte-aligned, table-dispatched pack/unpack kernels generated in for-gen.c rather than vectorization. Decode and especially select() are branch-light; select is O(1) per element with at most a 2-word read+mask. Memory overhead is just 5 bytes per block. Used in production in upscaledb to compress 32-bit keys. Caps at bits<=32 (no 64-bit path in the header). For nest, a NEON/AVX2 unpack kernel could be added later under nest-runtime's existing SIMD dispatcher to recover the throughput libfor leaves on the table.

repos.one_liner: A C/C++ Apache-2.0 library that compresses 32/64-bit integer arrays with variable-byte (VByte) coding, delta-encoding sorted sequences and using Daniel Lemire's MaskedVByte SSE/AVX kernel to decode billions of integers per second, while also exposing select/lower-bound-search/append primitives that operate over the compressed stream.
repos.core_innovation: Random-access and search directly on the compressed VByte stream without full decompression: vbyte_select returns the i-th value, vbyte_search_lower_bound does a binary search over delta-coded sorted data, and vbyte_append extends a stream in place — turning a compressed integer array into a queryable structure rather than an opaque blob you must inflate first.
key_techniques: MaskedVByte SIMD decode (Lemire/Plaisance): uses per-byte high-bit continuation masks + SSE/AVX pshufb shuffle tables to unpack variable-length codes in vectorized batches
Delta + VByte for sorted/monotonic sequences (vbyte_compress_sorted32/64 take a `previous` seed so deltas, not absolute values, are stored)
Separate sorted vs unsorted codecs so unsorted data skips the delta transform
vbyte_select_sorted/unsorted: fetch index i by walking length-prefixed varints without materializing the array
vbyte_search_lower_bound_sorted: lower_bound over the delta stream returning position plus reconstructed actual value
vbyte_append_sorted/unsorted: append one integer to the tail of a compressed buffer in place, returns bytes written
vbyte_compressed_size_* sizing functions to pre-compute output buffer length before encoding
32-bit and 64-bit width variants throughout, little-endian-only assumption
repos.nest_application: Target nest-format, path crates/nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs plus a new encoding/varint codec under crates/nest-format/src/encoding/. Today chunks_original_spans stores byte_start/byte_end as fixed 16 raw LE bytes per chunk (spans.rs lines 21-24); within one source_uri these offsets are monotonically increasing, the exact delta+VByte sorted case. Re-encode each source's offsets as a delta-coded sorted varint stream to cut ~16 bytes/chunk toward ~2-4 bytes for close-packed chunks, shrinking a required non-embedding section that delta-varint beats structurally even after zstd. Make it purely additive: register a new reserved encoding id (4-255 free in v1) so old readers ignore it and NEST_FORMAT_VERSION never bumps; content_hash stays stable because it hashes DECODED canonical values, not the encoding. Implement in pure safe Rust (no C FFI) with a scalar varint loop first respecting the never-panic typed-error and small-core rules; MaskedVByte SSE/AVX is a later perf upgrade behind the existing nest-runtime SIMD dispatcher. The select/lower_bound primitives also map onto bm25 posting lists in crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25 if doc-id lists move to compressed deltas, enabling search over compressed postings without full inflate.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission: delta+varint is the canonical way to compress sorted integer columns (byte spans, posting-list doc ids, chunk-id maps) below fixed-width or even zstd-on-raw-u64, deterministically and byte-reproducibly. It adds a structural integer codec to nest's toolbox (raw/zstd/f16/int8 today, none of which exploit monotonicity), advancing the compress-more-than-everyone north star for every integer-bearing section, and random-access select means compression does not cost queryability.
repos.perf_notes: MaskedVByte decodes billions of ints/sec on AVX/AVX2 by branchlessly resolving continuation-bit masks with pshufb shuffle tables; scalar VByte is branchy (one branch per continuation byte) but tiny and cache-friendly. Monotonic 64-bit offsets whose deltas fit in ~12-14 bits drop from 8 bytes to 1-2 bytes each. Library is little-endian-only, matching nest's all-LE invariant. select/search walk the stream so they avoid allocating the decoded array entirely.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A BSD-licensed C library that compresses blocks of 128 (or 256) 32-bit integers by SIMD "vertical" binary bit-packing — computing the minimal common bit-width b and packing values into b bits each — with an integrated delta+prefix-sum path for sorted lists, decoding at ~15 GB/s (0.3 cycles/int) on SSE4.1/AVX2.
repos.core_innovation: Vertical (transposed/lane-interleaved) bit-packing: instead of concatenating b-bit integers end-to-end (the scalar BitPacker1x layout), values are laid out so each SIMD lane owns a strided subset (4 lanes for SSE = BitPacker4x/128 ints, 8 lanes for AVX2 = BitPacker8x/256 ints). All 128/256 integers in a block share one bit-width b=maxbits() and are packed/unpacked with a single branch-free shift-mask-OR loop across vector lanes. For sorted lists this is fused with a SIMD delta encoder (alignr/shift to subtract the previous lane, seeded by an initvalue) and a SIMD prefix-sum decoder (shift-add across lanes + a shuffle that carries the top lane into the next block), so compress/decompress is integrated, not a two-pass delta-then-pack.
key_techniques: Vertical/lane-transposed bit-packing in blocks of 128 (SSE) or 256 (AVX2) ints, all values sharing one bit-width b=maxbits()
maxbits/maxbitsd1: OR-reduce a block (or its deltas) to find the minimal common bit-width in one SIMD pass
Integrated delta-1 coding: simdpackd1/simdunpackd1 carry a uint32 initvalue seed so block N continues block N-1's running offset
SIMD prefix-sum decode: shift-and-add across 128-bit lanes + _mm_shuffle to propagate the highest lane as carry
SIMD delta encode via _mm_alignr_epi8 (SSSE3) with a plain shift-or SSE2 fallback
withoutmask fast path: when deltas are provably < 2^b, skip the AND-mask step
Frame-of-reference (simdfor.h): pack value-minus-min so packed words stay directly range-searchable in place
Format-agnostic kernels: library ships only pack/unpack + simdpack_compressedbytes() sizing; container and b-selector byte are the caller's job
repos.nest_application: Add an integer codec module in nest-format (crates/nest-format/src/encoding/bitpack.rs, <=300 loc) porting BitPacker4x-style vertical packing in safe Rust with NEON/AVX2/scalar dispatch mirroring nest-runtime/src/simd. Apply it to the two sorted-integer hot spots that today emit raw little-endian u32 with ZERO compression: (1) BM25 postings in nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs — per-term doc-id lists are monotonically increasing, so delta+bitpack (simdpackd1 path) collapses them while staying losslessly decodable; tf bitpacks on its tiny bit-width; (2) HNSW neighbor-id lists in nest-runtime/src/ann/codec.rs — small bounded u32 ids bitpack to ~ceil(log2(n)) bits instead of 32. Also delta-encode chunks_original_spans byte_start/byte_end (nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs), which are near-monotonic. Stays inside the frozen format: these are payload-internal layouts of optional sections 0x07/0x08 (bump only their per-section PAYLOAD_VERSION, never NEST_FORMAT_VERSION) plus a span-section internal encoding; embeddings untouched (still mmap-scored). Deterministic because packing is a pure function of the ints, and content_hash is unchanged since decode reproduces identical ints.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly advances 'compress more than everyone' on the two sections nest leaves uncompressed. BM25 posting lists and HNSW adjacency are pure sorted/small-integer data — the exact workload where delta+vertical-bitpack beats zstd in BOTH ratio and decode speed (15 GB/s, branch-free), shrinking the tiny/hybrid index sections without zstd decompress cost on the search path. Leaves the embedding mmap dot-product hot path untouched: pure upside for index-heavy presets.
repos.perf_notes: ~4-8 billion ints/s (~15 GB/s, 0.3 cycles/int Skylake) fully branch-free. Rust port quickwit-oss/bitpacking: BitPacker4x compress ~5.3B/s, BitPacker8x decompress ~6.5B/s, runtime SSE3/AVX2/scalar detection, no_std. Each 128-int block packs to exactly b*16 bytes plus a 1-byte b selector; no heap churn, mmap-friendly. NEON has no native 256-bit, so aarch64 targets the 128-int (4x-equivalent) layout to match nest's NEON dispatcher.
repos.license: BSD (simdcomp C lib); the Rust port quickwit-oss/bitpacking is MIT. Both permissive, compatible with vendoring or clean-room reimplementation.

repos.one_liner: Reference C++ implementation (Ottaviano & Venturini, SIGIR 2014) of Partitioned Elias-Fano: it slices a monotone integer sequence into variable-length chunks chosen by a linear-time approximate dynamic program, encoding each chunk with the cheapest of plain Elias-Fano, an all-ones run, or a raw bitvector, giving near-optimal compression with constant-time random access and nextGEQ.
repos.core_innovation: Elias-Fano is quasi-optimal only when gaps are uniform; real posting lists and ID sequences are bursty/clustered. The breakthrough is a two-level partition that adapts the universe locally: cut the sorted sequence into chunks, store per-chunk endpoints (upper bounds and value bases) at level 1, and at level 2 encode each chunk independently against its OWN small local universe, picking per chunk the cheapest representation (Elias-Fano, all-ones, or plain bitvector). Because EF size is computed exactly per prefix (not estimated), the optimal-cost partition is found by a DP recurrence that, via the Ferragina et al. (1+epsilon) pruning, runs in O(m log m) time / O(m) space while staying within (1+epsilon) of the true optimum. Result: strictly better-than-EF compression on clustered data with no loss of O(1) random access or skip (nextGEQ) speed.
key_techniques: Elias-Fano coding: split each value into floor(log(u/n)) low bits packed in a fixed-width array, and high bits as a unary-gap bitvector; random access and nextGEQ via constant-time broadword rank/select on the high-bits bitvector
Two-level partitioned layout: level-1 sequence stores partition upper-bounds + base offsets (themselves EF-coded); level-2 stores each chunk re-based to a small local universe
Per-chunk codec selection: each chunk encoded as the cheapest of compact/strict Elias-Fano, all_ones_sequence (consecutive-int run, ~0 bits), or a plain bitvector when the chunk universe is dense
optimal_partition.hpp: DP minimizing total encoded bits, made linear via Ferragina (1+epsilon) approximation that prunes candidate cuts; EF cost evaluated EXACTLY in O(1) per window, not estimated
uniform_partitioned_sequence: cheaper fixed-size-partition variant (EF uniform) avoiding the DP, trading a little size for build speed
Constant-time select via precomputed in-word select tables + 64-bit popcount over the high-bits bitvector (the succinct submodule), no SIMD required
indexed_sequence dispatch: one sequence abstraction tagging which sub-codec each chunk used, so decode is branch-on-tag
FastPFor / block_codecs integration (PForDelta, varint, simdbp) as fixed-block comparison baselines
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals, both landing in nest-format encoding plus nest-runtime readers. (1) A new ADDITIVE encoding id (in the reserved 4-255 range, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump) implementing partitioned Elias-Fano for monotone integer sections: chunks_original_spans (sorted byte offsets) and especially the HNSW adjacency/neighbor-id lists and BM25 posting lists inside hnsw_index(0x07)/bm25_index(0x08). These are exactly the sorted/clustered ID sequences EF was built for and are today raw or zstd; partitioned EF beats zstd on bits-per-id while ADDING O(1) random access and nextGEQ that zstd cannot give (zstd needs full-block decode). (2) The level-2 cheapest-of-three per-chunk selector plus the exact-cost linear DP partitioner are a reusable codec-selection pattern: nest-format/encoding can adopt a per-section/per-chunk pick-the-smallest tag scheme (raw vs delta vs EF vs all-ones) chosen at build time, keeping decode a deterministic branch-on-tag (preserves reproducible byte-identical builds since the DP is deterministic for fixed epsilon). The select/rank broadword primitives belong in nest-runtime as a small succinct module (repr(C), little-endian, no panic) so EF-coded sections are searchable straight off mmap with no decompression on the hot path, matching nest's existing score-from-mmap discipline. Keep each new file <=300 lines: a bitvector+select primitive file, an ef_chunk codec file, a partition-cost file.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on the north star. Posting lists and neighbor-id lists are a large, currently-underexploited part of the hnsw_index and bm25_index sections; partitioned EF is the state-of-the-art compression/query-time tradeoff for exactly this data and gives random access WITHOUT decompression, which zstd structurally cannot. It lets nest shrink index sections below zstd while making them directly searchable from mmap, compressing more than everyone while preserving the offline/single-file/deterministic guarantees.
repos.perf_notes: Plain EF uses ~2 + ceil(log(u/n)) bits per element and supports O(1) select / O(log) nextGEQ; partitioned EF typically cuts 10-30% off plain EF on clustered TREC/ClueWeb posting lists and reports the best compression-ratio/query-time frontier vs PForDelta, varint, simdbp, and interpolative coding. Decode/skip is constant-time via broadword popcount + in-word select tables on 64-bit words (no AVX/NEON needed, so it ports cleanly to nest's scalar fallback and stays branch-predictable). Build cost is dominated by the O(m log m) partition DP; the uniform-partition variant builds faster with slightly worse ratio. Memory-map friendly: all structures are flat bit-packed arrays addressable by offset, matching nest's mmap-and-score model.
repos.license: Believed Apache-2.0 (same license as the successor project ds2i/PISA into which this code was folded); confirm by reading the repo LICENSE before vendoring. README explicitly states the code now lives in ds2i, so prefer porting concepts/algorithms over copying C++ verbatim.

synthesis.summary: The category collectively defines the modern integer-compression playbook nest is missing entirely: transform the data (delta/d1 for sorted, frame-of-reference subtract-min, zigzag for signed) then pack residuals at a per-block minimal bit-width, with two escape hatches for the realistic non-uniform cases - patched exceptions (PFOR/FastPFor/TurboPFor) for a few large outliers, and locally re-based partitions (partitioned Elias-Fano) for clustered/bursty sequences. The decisive property for nest is that several of these (FOR/libfor select(), VByte select()/lower_bound, Elias-Fano broadword rank/select) support O(1) random access and nextGEQ DIRECTLY on the compressed bytes, which zstd structurally cannot - so they compress AND keep nest's mmap-and-score-off-disk discipline, unlike zstd which forces a full block inflate. nest today has the single largest uncompressed integer surface sitting in plain sight: ann/codec.rs writes every HNSW neighbor id as 4 raw LE bytes (line 29-31), bm25/codec.rs writes every posting as doc:u32+tf:u32 raw (line 33-36), and spans.rs stores 16 raw bytes per chunk as two u64 (line 22-23). All three are sorted or near-monotone u32/u64 arrays - the textbook delta+bitpack/FOR workload - and all three are version-gated by per-section payload versions (HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION/BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION) or could carry a new reserved encoding id (4-255 free), so the win is fully additive with NEST_FORMAT_VERSION frozen at 1. Determinism is free: packing is a pure function of the integers and content_hash hashes DECODED values, so byte-identical builds and stable content_hash are preserved. The pure-scalar ports are small and fit the 300-line single-responsibility cap; SIMD is a later throughput upgrade behind the existing simd dispatcher and is unnecessary for correctness since index sections are cold-loaded once at mmap time.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: State of the art is a layered pipeline: (1) a reversible integer transform chosen by data shape - delta/d1 (gaps) for sorted lists, frame-of-reference (subtract per-block min) for clustered-range values, zigzag for signed, delta-of-delta+RLE for timestamps; (2) fixed-block binary bit-packing at a per-block bit-width b = ceil(log2(max_residual+1)), giving a 32/b ratio that decodes branch-free with shift+mask; (3) an exception mechanism so a handful of outliers do not force a wide b for the whole block - either patched-FOR (FastPFor/TurboPFor: store outlier positions + high-bit residuals out-of-band, 128- or 256-int blocks, 2-bit block-type header selecting constant/bitpack/bitmap-exc/vbyte-exc) or locally re-based partitions (partitioned Elias-Fano: a linear-time (1+epsilon) DP cuts the sequence into variable chunks, each encoded as the cheapest of strict-EF / all-ones-run / raw bitvector against its own small universe). The frontier additionally insists compression must not cost queryability: libfor's for_select_bits() is O(1) random access by index*b bit-offset, vbyte_select/lower_bound walk a compressed varint stream without materializing it, and Elias-Fano gives O(1) select and O(log) nextGEQ via broadword popcount + in-word select tables on 64-bit words (no SIMD needed). SIMD (SIMD-BP128, TurboPackV256, MaskedVByte, simdcomp) pushes 10-20 Gint/s via vertical lane-transposed layout, but the scalar layouts are correct and deterministic on their own. Permissive ports exist (FastPFor Apache-2.0 minus the patented varint-G8IU, simdcomp BSD, quickwit-oss/bitpacking MIT, libfor/libvbyte Apache-2.0); TurboPFor is GPL-2.0 and must be clean-room reimplemented from the format description only.
top_innovations: Delta(d1)+bitpack for sorted id lists: gaps in a monotone u32 list pack to ceil(log2(max_gap)) bits not 32, the single highest-leverage transform for nest because HNSW neighbor ids (sortable per-list) and BM25 doc ids (already strictly increasing) are exactly this shape. Source: FastPFor SIMD-BP128, simdcomp simdpackd1, libvbyte sorted variants.

Frame-of-reference (subtract per-block min, store base+bit-width, pack residuals) with O(1) random access via index*b bit-offset arithmetic - the canonical first stage that ALSO keeps elements individually addressable off mmap, so spans[i] or neighbor[i] is one bit-extract with no whole-section decode. Source: libfor for_select_bits().

Patched frame-of-reference / PFOR exceptions: pick b so MOST values fit, store the rare outliers out-of-band, so one giant gap or degree spike does not inflate the whole block's bit-width. Decodes branch-free. Source: FastPFor/SIMD-FastPFor, TurboPFor 2-bit block-type header.

Partitioned Elias-Fano: locally re-based variable-length partitions chosen by a deterministic (1+epsilon) DP, each chunk the cheapest of EF/all-ones/raw-bitvector, giving 10-30% below plain EF on clustered data PLUS O(1) select and O(log) nextGEQ via broadword rank/select - random access without any decompression. Source: ot/partitioned_elias_fano.

Per-chunk/per-section cheapest-of-N codec selection with a branch-on-tag decode: pick the smallest of {raw, delta, FOR, patched, EF, all-ones} at build time, store a tiny tag, decode deterministically. A reusable codec-selection pattern that mirrors nest's existing encoding-choice axis. Source: partitioned_elias_fano level-2 selector, TurboPFor 2-bit header.

Random-access/search-over-compressed primitives (select, lower_bound/nextGEQ) that operate on the compressed stream - the property that lets a codec replace zstd on nest's mmap hot path instead of forcing a full inflate. Source: libfor, libvbyte, Elias-Fano broadword select.

Space-efficient byte-range varint denser than LEB128 (0-176 in 1 byte, then 14/19/32-bit tiers) and StreamVByte's control-bytes-separate-from-payload layout for branch-light scalar decode. Source: TurboPFor varbyte, FastPFor StreamVByte.

Vertical/lane-transposed bit-packing (block of 128 for SSE/NEON, 256 for AVX2, all sharing one b) as the SIMD throughput layer that maps cleanly onto nest's existing AVX2/NEON/scalar simd dispatcher when/if throughput matters. Source: simdcomp BitPacker4x/8x, TurboPackV128/V256.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a pure-safe-Rust scalar bitpack+delta(d1) codec module and apply it to HNSW neighbor-id lists. Sort each per-layer neighbor list at build time, delta-encode (d1), and pack residuals at per-list/per-block bit-width b=ceil(log2(max_gap+1)); store b as one byte. Replace the raw 4-byte-per-id loop. Bump HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION to 2 (NOT NEST_FORMAT_VERSION); decode reproduces identical id sets so search and the mandatory exact-cosine rerank are byte-for-byte unchanged.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/ann/codec.rs (replace the raw `for &id in nbrs { out.extend_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes()) }` at lines 29-31 and its mirror parse loop at lines 65-71); new shared codec in a new crates/nest-runtime/src/bitpack.rs (<=300 loc, single-responsibility). HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION lives at crates/nest-runtime/src/ann/mod.rs:40.
nest_recommendations.impact: Largest single shrink of the index section that dominates the tiny preset (0.283 ratio). Neighbor ids drop from 32 bits to roughly log2(n) bits (e.g. ~14-17 bits at 100k-1M nodes), often <50% of the raw adjacency bytes; pushes tiny/hybrid preset size down with zero recall change.

nest_recommendations.idea: Apply the same delta+bitpack codec to BM25 posting lists: doc ids per term are already strictly increasing (deterministic alphabetical term order), so delta-code doc gaps and bitpack them, and bitpack tf separately at its own tiny bit-width (tf is small). Bump BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION to 2. Keep df and the alphabetical term order untouched so determinism holds.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs (replace the raw `p.doc.to_le_bytes()` + `p.tf.to_le_bytes()` posting loop at lines 33-36 and the matching parse at lines 73-77); reuse the bitpack.rs module from rec #1. BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION at crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/index.rs:8.
nest_recommendations.impact: Sorted doc-id gaps routinely pack to 4-8 bits vs 32; tf to ~3-4 bits. Several-fold shrink of section 0x08 in the hybrid preset, beating zstd-on-raw-u32 in both ratio and (cold, one-time) decode cost, with no scoring change.

nest_recommendations.idea: Re-encode chunks_original_spans as delta-coded varint streams grouped by source_uri. Within one source the byte_start/byte_end offsets are monotonically increasing; store each source's offsets as delta+varint (or FOR) instead of two raw u64 (16 bytes/chunk). Register a NEW reserved encoding id (e.g. SECTION_ENCODING_BITPACK = 4) so old readers reject it cleanly and NEST_FORMAT_VERSION stays 1; content_hash is unchanged because it hashes decoded canonical OriginalSpan values.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs (lines 22-23 emit the raw u64 pair today); add codec under crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ and wire the new id into decode_payload in crates/nest-format/src/encoding/mod.rs:44 and into SectionEncoding in crates/nest-format/src/writer/encoding_choice.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: Cuts a REQUIRED non-embedding section from ~16 bytes/chunk toward ~2-4 bytes for close-packed chunks - structurally beats even zstd-on-raw because it exploits monotonicity zstd cannot see; shrinks every preset including exact.

nest_recommendations.idea: Make the new integer codec FOR-based with index*b bit-offset random access (libfor select semantics) so spans[i] and one neighbor id can be fetched by O(1) bit-extract straight off mmap, never decoding the whole section. This preserves nest's zero-copy hot path for citation resolution (nest://content_hash/chunk_id materialize) and keeps the option of search-over-compressed for bm25 nextGEQ later.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: the codec module shared by recs #1-#3 (crates/nest-runtime/src/bitpack.rs and/or crates/nest-format/src/encoding/); a tiny succinct rank/select primitive file kept separate (<=300 loc each) if Elias-Fano is added later. Wire select() into the materialize / citation path in nest-runtime.
nest_recommendations.impact: Keeps compression from costing queryability - the property that justifies these codecs over zstd on the mmap-and-score discipline. Enables shrinking spans/index while still serving span[i] zero-copy.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add patched exceptions (PFOR) once plain bitpack lands: pick b for the common case and store the few outliers out-of-band (position + high bits), with a 2-bit block-type header selecting constant/plain-bitpack/patched. This stops one huge gap (a sparse posting list term) or one high-degree HNSW node from widening b for the whole block. Clean-room from the FastPFor/TurboPFor format description only.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: extend crates/nest-runtime/src/bitpack.rs with an exceptions sub-path (separate file if it nears 300 loc); applies transparently to recs #1 and #2.
nest_recommendations.impact: 10-25% further shrink on real (bursty) distributions vs plain per-block bitpack; the difference between good and state-of-the-art on clustered posting lists and skewed adjacency.

nest_recommendations.idea: Adopt a cheapest-of-N per-section codec selector with a branch-on-tag decode: at build time try {raw, delta+bitpack, FOR, patched, all-ones} on each integer section/list, store the 1-byte winning tag, and pick the smallest. Mirror nest's existing SectionEncoding enum so the choice is explicit and the DP/selector is a deterministic pure function (byte-identical builds preserved).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/writer/encoding_choice.rs (extend SectionEncoding beyond Raw/Zstd) and the dispatch in crates/nest-format/src/encoding/mod.rs:44; tag read at decode time.
nest_recommendations.impact: Guarantees the codec never loses to raw/zstd on adversarial inputs and auto-adapts per dataset (e.g. PT-BR fake-news corpora) without manual tuning - turns compression into a build-time optimization rather than a fixed guess.

nest_recommendations.idea: Replace LEB128-style varints anywhere nest emits length prefixes / counts for integer arrays with the denser byte-range varint (0-176 in 1 byte, 14/19/32-bit tiers) or StreamVByte's controls-separate-from-payload layout, decoded with a branch-light scalar loop.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: the varint path in crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ and the count/df prefixes in bm25/codec.rs and ann/codec.rs headers; keep all-LE per nest invariant.
nest_recommendations.impact: Small but free uniform shrink on every count/length field; complements the bitpack codec for the non-block scalar fields.

nest_recommendations.idea: Later: add NEON(128)/AVX2(256) vertical bit-pack kernels behind the existing simd dispatcher for decode throughput, keeping the scalar path as the deterministic reference. The on-disk bit layout must be identical across scalar/SIMD so content_hash and decode are independent of CPU.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/simd (mirror the AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatch already used for dot products); SIMD touches DECODE only, never the on-disk layout produced by the python builder.
nest_recommendations.impact: Throughput only (10-20 Gint/s vs scalar). Low priority because index sections are cold-loaded once at mmap time, but useful if posting-list scan-over-compressed becomes hot.

compression_wins: HNSW neighbor ids (ann/codec.rs:29-31): sort-per-list + delta(d1) + bitpack drops each id from 32 bits to ~log2(n) bits (~14-17 bits at 100k-1M nodes) plus exceptions for high-degree nodes - the single biggest lever on the tiny-preset index section, no recall change since decode reproduces identical ids and the exact-cosine rerank is untouched.

BM25 doc ids (bm25/codec.rs:33-36): already strictly increasing, so delta-gap + bitpack packs to a typical 4-8 bits/id and tf to ~3-4 bits, several-fold over raw doc:u32+tf:u32 and below zstd-on-raw, shrinking section 0x08 in the hybrid preset.

chunks_original_spans (spans.rs:22-23): delta+varint/FOR per source_uri cuts a REQUIRED section from 16 bytes/chunk toward 2-4 bytes for close-packed chunks - a win in EVERY preset including exact, exploiting monotonicity zstd cannot.

These codecs beat zstd structurally on sorted integer columns AND keep O(1) random access (FOR/EF select), so they compress without breaking the mmap-and-score-off-disk hot path - zstd would force a full block inflate and forfeit zero-copy.
Cheapest-of-N build-time selection guarantees the integer sections are never larger than raw and auto-adapt per corpus, compounding toward pushing the tiny preset below its current 0.283 ratio.

All wins are lossless on the integer payload and stack on top of existing zstd/f16/int8 - they attack the metadata/index surface (everything except the f32 embeddings that must stay raw for scoring), the part nest leaves uncompressed today.
watch_outs: GPL-2.0 contamination: TurboPFor is GPL-2.0 (dual-licensed). Never vendor or copy - clean-room reimplement from the format description only. Prefer the permissive sources (FastPFor Apache-2.0, simdcomp BSD, quickwit-oss/bitpacking MIT, libfor/libvbyte Apache-2.0) for reference. Avoid FastPFor's varint-G8IU specifically (patented).

Determinism: bit-width selection, exception ordering, and any partition DP must be a pure deterministic function of the integers (fixed block size, canonical b=max-residual-bits, exceptions in ascending index order, fixed epsilon). Any data-dependent or floating-point-influenced choice in the encoder would break byte-identical reproducible builds. Note HNSW neighbor lists must be sorted in a canonical, seeded-deterministic order before delta-coding or the on-disk bytes will vary.

content_hash stability: content_hash hashes DECODED canonical sections, so a new INTEGER codec on chunks_original_spans is safe (decode yields identical OriginalSpan values). But the codec MUST decode to byte-identical canonical integers - any lossy or reordering transform would change content_hash and break nest:// citations.

Format-freeze discipline: index codecs (HNSW 0x07, BM25 0x08) must bump only their per-section PAYLOAD_VERSION (ann/mod.rs:40, bm25/index.rs:8), never NEST_FORMAT_VERSION. A new section encoding id for spans must use the reserved 4-255 range and old readers must reject it via the existing UnsupportedSectionEncoding path - do NOT change the meaning of an existing field (that would be a true v2).

Never-panic constraint: bit-cursor unpack, varint continuation, FOR base/width reads, and broadword select on malformed/truncated bytes must return typed thiserror errors (RuntimeError::Format / NestError::MalformedSectionPayload), never panic or index out of bounds. The hand-tuned C kernels assume well-formed input; the Rust port must bounds-check every word read.

Zero-copy vs decode-into-Vec: zstd already breaks zero-copy by decompressing whole blocks. To keep the mmap hot path, prefer FOR/EF layouts that support select() straight off mmap rather than codecs that force a full decode into an owned Vec. libfor's bits<=32 cap means 64-bit span offsets need a 64-bit path or delta-into-u32 - handle u64 spans explicitly.

300-line file cap: split into single-responsibility modules - block header / bitpack-unpack / exception list / delta transform / succinct rank-select each as its own file under the 300-line (333 hard) cap. Do not let a monolithic codec file grow past it.

SIMD is a throughput-only later step and must NOT alter the on-disk bit layout: the python builder produces the bytes scalar-deterministically, and AVX2/NEON/scalar decode in nest-runtime must all yield identical integers. Vertical lane layout differs between 128-bit (NEON, 4x u32) and 256-bit (AVX2, 8x u32) - if SIMD is added, the on-disk format must commit to ONE block size (256) and let NEON decode it as two 128-bit halves, or builds become CPU-dependent.
CJK/Thai BM25 tokenizer gap is orthogonal - posting-list compression does not fix the word-segmentation degradation; don't conflate the two.

Keep embeddings out of scope: these codecs are for integer sections only. The f32 embeddings are scored directly from mmap on the hot path and must stay raw/f16/int8 as today - never apply integer bitpacking to embeddings.
