repos.one_liner: A Merkle-tree hash built on a reduced-round (7-round) ChaCha-derived BLAKE2 compression function that splits input into fixed 1024-byte chunks, hashes them in parallel across SIMD lanes and threads, and combines chaining values pairwise into parent nodes, enabling parallelism, extendable XOF output, and verified streaming (Bao) where any byte range is verifiable against the single 256-bit root.
repos.core_innovation: A hash is a binary Merkle tree over fixed-size chunks (1024 B): the root is a single 32-byte commitment, but every interior chaining value lets you verify an arbitrary sub-range WITHOUT re-hashing the whole input. This decouples "one stable content hash for the whole artifact" from "cheap incremental/partial verification of just the bytes you touched" - exactly the tension nest has between its whole-file content_hash and per-section/per-chunk integrity.
key_techniques: Binary Merkle tree over fixed 1024-byte chunks; parent node = hash(left_CV || right_CV); odd nodes promoted to next level
Domain-separation flags (CHUNK_START/END, PARENT, ROOT, KEYED_HASH, DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT/MATERIAL): only the final root is flagged ROOT, preventing length-extension and tree-substitution attacks
7-round ChaCha-quarter-round permutation over a 16-word state with 8-word 256-bit chaining value and per-chunk 64-bit counter
SIMD batch hashing of independent chunks across SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON lanes with runtime CPU feature detection (AVX-512 = 16 chunks at once)
XOF extendable output via OutputReader (Read+Seek): root compression re-run with incrementing output-block counter yields unlimited seekable output
Bao verified-streaming format: 8-byte LE length prefix + chunks/parent nodes interleaved in pre-order so depth-first read needs no seeking
Bao slice format: transmit only parent CVs + chunks on the path to a target byte range, verifying that range against the root alone (~3.1% metadata at 1KiB chunks)
Configurable chunk groups (bao-tree): hash interior in 1024-B chunks for an unchanged root but emit parent nodes only every N KiB, cutting metadata overhead from ~6% to ~0.1%
repos.nest_application: Two concrete, additive moves. (1) nest-format/hashing.rs: nest computes file_hash and content_hash as flat SHA-256 over whole bodies. Adopt the BLAKE3 tree structure (or BLAKE3 via the `blake3` crate, CC0/Apache, vendorable, no_std, deterministic) so content_hash becomes a Merkle ROOT while interior chaining values let `nest validate` verify a single section or chunk's byte span WITHOUT re-hashing the whole file - turning O(file) validation into O(touched-bytes), which matters once nest serves whole databases/repos/video. (2) The Bao slice format maps onto nest citations: nest://content_hash/chunk_id already reopens an exact byte span; add a RESERVED section (id 0x09+, additive within v1) holding interleaved parent-node CVs (a merkle_index/bao_tree section) so a partial or remote consumer can cryptographically verify just the cited chunk_id against the root with ~0.1% overhead via chunk-grouped parents. Keep SHA-256 as the FROZEN default and introduce BLAKE3 as a new hashing-algorithm id so the format stays additive and v1 never bumps. The 7-round SIMD core is also a reference model for nest-runtime's AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatcher: the same lane-batching discipline (N independent items per SIMD width, runtime detection) is how nest batches dot products - so BLAKE3's guts are a reference kernel, not a dependency on the hot scoring path.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. BLAKE3 is not a compressor and does not shrink bytes. Its relevance to "compress more than everyone" is structural: the Merkle-tree-over-fixed-chunks layout is the standard substrate for content-defined chunking + dedup (the same boundary discipline underlies CDC dedup in restic/casync/IPFS). A nest that chunks artifacts on stable boundaries and addresses every chunk by its CV can dedup identical spans across files/datasets/versions before any entropy coder runs - cross-artifact dedup is often a larger win than the codec itself on repos/databases. The 1KiB-chunk vs chunk-group tradeoff (3.1% vs 0.1% metadata) is the exact knob nest must tune so verification metadata does not erode compression-ratio gains.
repos.license: Dual-licensed CC0-1.0 / Apache-2.0; the `blake3` Rust crate is permissive, vendor-friendly, no_std-capable with a portable scalar reference path - safe to vendor under nest's offline single-file constraints.
repos.perf_notes: b3sum is ~an order of magnitude faster than sha256sum on desktop hardware due to (a) SIMD batch hashing of independent chunks (AVX-512=16 lanes, AVX2=8, NEON=4) and (b) rayon multithreading across independent subtrees. Throughput scales near-linearly with cores and SIMD width because chunks are independent until a cheap combine step. Memory: streaming with an O(log n) stack of pending chaining values, no need to buffer the whole input. Chunk independence is what makes both parallelism AND partial verification free - the property nest wants for large artifacts.

repos.one_liner: A small C++ library computing CRC32C (Castagnoli/iSCSI polynomial 0x1EDC6F41) with a runtime-dispatched tiered backend: hardware SSE4.2 CRC32 intrinsics on x86_64, ARMv8 CRC32 intrinsics on aarch64, and a portable slicing-by-4 (16 bytes/iteration) software fallback.
repos.core_innovation: The runtime CPU-feature dispatch pattern: a single Extend() entry point picks the best implementation once via lazily-initialized static bools (CanUseSse42 / CanUseArm64Crc32 set from CPUID/getauxval), so the same binary runs an accelerated kernel where the silicon supports it and silently degrades to a portable scalar kernel everywhere else, with byte-identical output across all three paths.
key_techniques: CRC32C with the Castagnoli polynomial 0x1EDC6F41 (reflected), distinct from zip/zlib CRC32 0x04C11DB7

Three-way parallel hardware CRC: maintains 3 independent _mm_crc32_u64 accumulators over disjoint blocks, then folds them with precomputed kBlockNSkipTable lookup tables (XOR of polynomial-skip constants) instead of PCLMULQDQ
Hierarchical block sizes (Block0/1/2 nested loops) so the skip-table combine cost is amortized and cache/prefetch friendly
Portable slicing-by-4: 4 stride tables (kStrideExtensionTable0..3) plus a byte table, 256 x u32 each (~4KB), 16 bytes/loop iteration
ReadUint32LE little-endian reads for deterministic, endianness-stable results regardless of host architecture
Software prefetch (RequestPrefetch at a fixed kPrefetchHorizon) on large buffers; byte-by-byte head handling for unaligned starts
Incremental Extend(crc, buf, len) API enabling streaming/chunked checksums that compose across calls
Lazy one-time static-init feature detection to avoid per-call dispatch overhead
repos.nest_application: Two concrete uses. (1) nest-runtime SIMD dispatcher: nest already ships an AVX2/NEON/scalar dot-product dispatcher; crc32c's lazy-static CanUseX pattern is the exact template for a single clean cfg(target_arch)+is_x86_feature_detected!/std::arch aarch64 runtime selector that guarantees byte-identical scalar fallback (critical for nest's determinism guarantee). (2) nest-format hashing.rs (the 4 SHA-256 integrity surfaces, ~4.9k loc core): add an OPTIONAL fast integrity tier. SHA-256 is overkill and slow for the per-section physical-byte checksum on the validate/inspect hot path; a hardware CRC32C gives a cheap detect-corruption-fast pre-check (run CRC32C first during `nest validate`, only fall through to SHA-256 if you need cryptographic strength or it mismatches). Because format v1 is additive-only, this fits as a new reserved encoding/metadata field, not a version bump. The slicing-by-4 portable kernel is also a ready-made deterministic scalar reference for nest's never-panic, repr(C), little-endian, <=300-line-file constraints (the whole CRC32C core is small enough to vendor as one file). For nest's North Star (compress-more-than-everyone), CRC32C itself does not compress, but a fast checksum lets every codec (zstd/f16/int8) verify decode integrity per chunk almost for free, enabling more aggressive lossy quantization with cheap corruption detection.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. CRC32C does not reduce bytes, so it is orthogonal to the compress-more-than-everyone goal. Its value is enabling: a near-free hardware integrity check per chunk/section lets nest push harder on lossy/aggressive codecs (int8, f16, future entropy coders) while still cheaply detecting decode corruption, and the runtime-dispatch + deterministic-scalar-fallback pattern directly hardens nest's existing SIMD compute paths.
repos.perf_notes: Hardware SSE4.2 path: 3-way interleaved _mm_crc32_u64 hides the ~3-cycle latency / 1-per-cycle throughput of the crc32 instruction, reaching multiple bytes/cycle; combine done by table XOR (no PCLMULQDQ dependency, so it works even on hypervisors that hide the CLMUL CPUID bit). ARMv8 path uses native __crc32c intrinsics. Portable slicing-by-4 does 16 B/iter from ~4KB of L1-resident tables with software prefetch. All three are streaming/incremental and allocation-free. Note: google explicitly recommends HighwayHash for NEW file formats over CRC32C, so use CRC32C only as a fast non-cryptographic detect-corruption layer, not as nest's primary content-addressing hash (keep SHA-256 content_hash as the stable identity).
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause (Google), code originally derived from LevelDB

repos.one_liner: A non-cryptographic 32/64/128-bit hash that abuses the hardware AES round instruction (x86 aesenc/AES-NI, aarch64 NEON vaes) as a wide bit-mixer over a 128-bit SIMD state, currently the fastest in its class at all input sizes (often >30 GB/s on large inputs).
repos.core_innovation: Use one hardware AES round (aesenc) as a single-instruction, fully-avalanching 128-bit compression/mixing primitive instead of hand-rolled multiply-xor-shift chains. Because AES-NI is one ~4-cycle pipelined instruction with near-perfect diffusion, a few aesenc rounds over a 128-bit lane give SMHasher-passing quality (low collisions, high avalanche) at a fraction of the bytecode of ahash/xxh3, which inlines/caches better and saturates ILP.
key_techniques: aesenc/vaesenc (AES-NI / NEON-AES) as the core 128-bit mixing round, not for encryption
128-bit SIMD State with factor-of-8 loop unrolling (8 independent accumulators) to fill the AES-round pipeline and maximize ILP
get_partial / get_partial_unsafe: branchless masked load of the trailing <16-byte block so every byte influences the hash without OOB reads
finalize(): a few terminal aesenc rounds against a fixed KEYS constant array to emit 32/64/128-bit digests
wide-pipe (hybrid VAES+AVX2) construction for multicollision resistance when output <=64 bits
seed randomization for DoS resistance with an opt-in deterministic feature flag
cross-platform output stability guaranteed within a major version (same hash on x86 and aarch64)
repos.nest_application: Two non-overlapping uses. (1) DO NOT touch the four SHA-256 integrity surfaces in nest-format/src/reader/decode.rs and chunk.rs (header_checksum, per-section checksum, file_hash, content_hash): these are cryptographic identity/citation anchors (nest://content_hash/...) and must stay SHA-256. (2) Adopt gxhash only as the in-memory BuildHasher for hot-path tables that never persist: nest-runtime/src/bm25/index.rs (HashMap<String,TermEntry> built per query and at index build, plus per-doc tf maps), bm25/fusion.rs RRF HashMap<usize,f32>, and ann/search.rs visited HashSet<u32>. Replacing std SipHash with a gxhash/hashbrown BuildHasher cuts BM25 build/query and HNSW traversal CPU with zero format impact. A third, format-relevant use: a build-time content-defined chunk dedup pass in the nest-python/writer path (writer/encoding_choice.rs) -- gxhash chunk bytes to find duplicate chunks_canonical before encoding, storing each unique chunk once with refcounting in chunk_ids. Stays additive (build-time decision, frozen v1 layout unchanged). Enable gxhash's deterministic (fixed-seed) feature so identical corpora still yield byte-identical files.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. gxhash is a hasher, not a compressor, so it shrinks nothing by itself. Its leverage is enabling cheap content-defined chunk/block deduplication at build time: hash every chunk (and sub-block fingerprints for near-dup detection) fast enough to dedup large corpora and whole-repo ingestion before zstd, storing each unique chunk once. This dedup-then-compress pipeline (restic/borg/casync style) is the highest-yield path to beating everyone on multi-document and repo-scale corpora where cross-document redundancy dominates. The hot-table speedups are latency wins, not size wins.
repos.perf_notes: Often >30 GB/s on large inputs on modern x86 with AES-NI; fastest SMHasher-class non-crypto hash at every input size. Wins from (a) aesenc being a single pipelined ~4-cycle instruction with full diffusion, (b) 8-way unrolled 128-bit accumulators saturating ILP, (c) tiny inlinable bytecode. HARD CAVEATS for nest: requires AES+SSE2 (x86) or AES+NEON (aarch64) and HAS NO SCALAR FALLBACK -- fails to compile on unsupported targets, which collides with nest's scalar-fallback guarantee. Must be feature-gated behind target_feature detection with a portable fallback hasher (foldhash/ahash-fallback or std SipHash) on non-AES targets, never a hard dep. Uses heavy unsafe and aggressive opts (explicitly not for safety-critical use), so it must not enter never-panic nest-format library code; confine it to runtime in-memory tables and the build-time python/writer dedup pass.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A pure-Rust collection of cryptographic hash crates (sha2, sha3, blake2, blake3 via traits-preview, ripemd, etc.) unified under the `digest` crate's `Update`/`FixedOutput`/`ExtendableOutput` traits, with the heavy backends doing runtime-dispatched hardware acceleration (x86 SHA-NI, AArch64 sha2 extension, AVX2, NEON, WASM simd128) over a shared `block-buffer` block-accumulation abstraction.
repos.core_innovation: A single small trait surface (`Digest` = `Update` + `FixedOutput` + `Reset`, plus `ExtendableOutput`/`XofReader` for variable-length output) lets you write integrity code generically over any hash, while the concrete crate transparently selects the fastest CPU backend at runtime via the `cpufeatures` zero-sized-token model — so hashing becomes hardware-accelerated for free without the format ever naming a backend. The block-buffer abstraction cleanly separates "accumulate input into fixed compression blocks" from "compress a block," which is exactly the pattern nest's domain-separated, length-prefixed chunk_id preimage already imitates by hand.
key_techniques: digest trait split: Update (streaming input) + FixedOutput (finalize) + Reset + ExtendableOutput/XofReader for XOF, enabling generic-over-hash code
cpufeatures runtime CPU detection via a zero-sized token type (cpufeatures::new!) that gates SHA-NI / sha2-ext / AVX2 / NEON / simd128 backends with soft fallback, no_std-friendly
sha2 0.11 multi-backend cfg system: sha2_backend / sha2_256_backend override flags, plus soft 'compact' vs unrolled for binary-size vs speed tradeoff
block-buffer: accumulate arbitrary-length input into fixed compression-function blocks (64B for sha256), decoupled from the compression kernel
BLAKE3 Merkle-tree hashing: 1024B chunks, 64B blocks, 32B chaining values; tree shape enables SIMD-parallel and rayon multithreaded hashing of large inputs
BLAKE3 verified streaming: independently verifiable subtree chaining values let you authenticate a byte range without rehashing the whole input
BLAKE3 XOF: finalize_xof() -> OutputReader (Read+Seek) for arbitrary-length random-access keyed output; one primitive for hash, MAC (keyed_hash), and KDF (derive_key)
domain-separated + length-prefixed preimage construction to make hashes collision-safe across concatenated fields (nest already uses this in chunk_id)
repos.nest_application: nest-format already depends on sha2 = "0.11" and calls Sha256::digest/Update across exactly the right five places: header.rs (header_checksum), section_entry.rs (per-section checksum), footer.rs (file_hash), reader/decode.rs (content_hash), and chunk.rs (chunk_id). Three concrete steals: (1) Confirm/enable sha2's default runtime-dispatch backends so file_hash over the whole pre-footer body and per-section checksums get x86 SHA-NI / AArch64 sha2-ext acceleration for free on the validate path — pure additive, no format change, just verify no `sha2_backend="soft"` override and that 0.11 auto-detection is on; speeds up `validate` and build determinism checks. (2) Add a tiny internal Hasher abstraction in nest-format (new ~80-line src/hashing.rs, single-responsibility, under the 300-line cap) wrapping `impl digest::Update + FixedOutput` so all four integrity surfaces share one domain-separated builder instead of five hand-rolled call sites — reduces drift, makes the preimage spec auditable in one file. (3) For the content-addressing roadmap (graph search, dataset/repo/binary-blob compression, audio/video), evaluate BLAKE3 (blake3 crate, traits-preview) as an OPTIONAL additive hash-id scheme for large blobs: its Merkle-tree gives SIMD+rayon-parallel hashing of multi-GB inputs and verified-streaming of byte ranges, mapping onto nest://content_hash/chunk_id range reopen — but it must be a new version-tagged digest algorithm (the sha256: prefix in chunk_id stays the v1 default) to preserve determinism and the FROZEN v1 format.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. Hashing is not an entropy coder, so it does not shrink bytes; its relevance to 'compress more than everyone' is (a) making the four integrity surfaces cheap enough that nest can hash aggressively-compressed/deduplicated content on every build and validate without becoming a bottleneck, and (b) BLAKE3's verified-streaming + content-addressing enabling block-level dedup across datasets/repos/whole-databases (identical subtrees hash identically), a prerequisite for cross-document deduplication that actually drives corpus-level compression. Hardware-accelerated SHA-256 keeps deterministic reproducible builds fast as corpora grow.
repos.license: Dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT (sha2 and all RustCrypto/hashes crates; blake3 crate is CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0). All permissive and already compatible with nest's existing sha2 dependency.
repos.perf_notes: sha2 0.11 default = runtime dispatch: SHA-256 uses x86-sha (SHA-NI) or aarch64-sha2 extension (~2x soft on SHA-NI CPUs, far more vs naive); SHA-512 uses AVX2 / aarch64-sha3. soft backend unrolls rounds by default (faster, bigger binary); 'compact' cfg trades speed for size — relevant to nest-python abi3 cdylib and CLI footprint. block-buffer works in 64B blocks for sha256. BLAKE3 is 5-10x faster than SHA-256 on non-SHA-NI CPUs (~2x even with SHA-NI), SIMD across SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/WASM with rayon multithreading; its update() only reaches full SIMD width with >=16 KiB buffers (8 KiB hits AVX2 but not AVX-512) — feed it large mmap slices, not small chunks. cpufeatures detection is one-time and effectively zero-cost after init.

repos.one_liner: A no_std Rust committing AEAD that derives ChaCha20 + BLAKE3-keyed-MAC subkeys from a 24-byte nonce via one BLAKE3 XOF call, encrypts with a from-scratch SIMD-dispatched ChaCha20, and authenticates Encrypt-then-MAC with a length-framed BLAKE3 keyed hash.
repos.core_innovation: Using BLAKE3 as a single multi-purpose primitive: one new_keyed(master_key).update(nonce).finalize_xof() call streams out 72 bytes sliced into an encryption key (0..32), an independent MAC key (32..64), and an 8-byte cipher nonce (64..72) — so one tree-hash invocation does KDF, subkey separation, and long-nonce absorption, and the same keyed BLAKE3 provides the MAC. This collapses KDF + MAC + commitment into one fast, parallelizable, SIMD-scaling, deterministic hash family.
key_techniques: BLAKE3 XOF as KDF: new_keyed(key)||nonce -> finalize_xof().fill(72 bytes) sliced into enc_key|mac_key|cipher_nonce, absorbing the over-long 24B nonce for free

Encrypt-then-MAC committing AEAD: tag = BLAKE3.keyed(mac_key, aad || le64(aad.len) || ciphertext || le64(ct.len)) with explicit little-endian length framing to prevent canonicalization/extension ambiguity
Full key/context commitment via keyed-BLAKE3 over the whole context, defeating partitioning-oracle attacks (unlike Poly1305/GCM); constant_time_eq_32 tag check, decrypt only on match

Compile-time + runtime SIMD dispatch ladder: aarch64 assumes NEON, wasm32 simd128 via target_feature, x86_64 is_x86_feature_detected!(avx512f then avx2) under std, >=128-byte threshold, scalar quarter_round fallback
Stateful streaming stream-cipher: caches last_keystream_block + index so unaligned successive xor_keystream calls equal one contiguous call (zero re-derivation)
no_std-first crate factoring with granular std/alloc/zeroize features and Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop on key material
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals. (1) Hashing/KDF primitive swap in nest-format/src (the SHA-256 surfaces in layout/header.rs, layout/section_entry.rs, layout/footer.rs, manifest/, writer/build.rs, sections/chunk_ids.rs): adopt BLAKE3 as the integrity hash for the four surfaces (header_checksum, per-section physical checksum, file_hash, content_hash). BLAKE3 is 5-10x faster than SHA-256, internally SIMD-parallel (AVX2 on x86_64, NEON on aarch64 — matching nest's existing dispatch targets), deterministic, and its keyed/derive_key modes give domain separation so the four surfaces use distinct contexts and never collide. Speeds the deterministic-build hot path and big-file content addressing. NOTE: changing the meaning of existing hash fields is a true v2 (bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION), not a v1 add. (2) The exact ChaCha20-BLAKE3 AEAD is the blueprint for an optional encrypted-container codec as a RESERVED encoding id (4-255, additive within v1) in nest-format/src/encoding: wrap non-embedding section payloads in committing AEAD so a .nest file is encrypted-at-rest while staying single-file, offline, no_std-friendly, and deterministic given (key, fixed-nonce). The committing property binds ciphertext to exactly one key, which is the right guarantee for content-addressed citations (nest://content_hash/...).
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. BLAKE3-as-hash is not a compressor, but it removes hashing from the deterministic-build and content-addressing critical path (5-10x over SHA-256, SIMD-parallel on the same AVX2/NEON targets nest already uses), so re-hashing large compressed sections during build/validate stops being the bottleneck as nest scales to whole datasets/repos/databases. BLAKE3 derive_key/keyed modes also give cheap domain-separated subkeys for future per-section keying without extra primitives. The AEAD codec is orthogonal to ratio but unlocks compress-then-encrypt single-file containers. Net: enables the 'compress AND serve huge corpora' north star by making integrity cheap, not by improving ratio.
repos.perf_notes: Author benchmarks (AMD EPYC 9R45): ChaCha20-BLAKE3 reaches 2,153 MB/s at 64KB and 3,297 MB/s at 1MB, beating XChaCha20-Poly1305 (~1,650 MB/s) and AES-256-GCM (~1,476 MB/s) on large messages; loses on tiny 64B messages (103 vs 540 MB/s for AES-NI GCM) due to fixed BLAKE3+KDF overhead. SIMD threshold is 128 bytes before any vector path. BLAKE3 itself is internally SIMD (AVX-512/AVX2/NEON/SVE) and tree-parallel, so throughput scales with SIMD width and multicore for very large inputs — directly relevant to nest's large-file content_hash/file_hash. Stream cipher caches the last keystream block so chunked unaligned writes cost no re-derivation.
repos.license: Permissive MIT: the chacha and chacha20-blake3 crates declare license = "MIT" in Cargo.toml; repo-root LICENSE.txt is an MIT-style permissive grant 'Copyright (c) 2025 Arcane Services'. Safe to learn from with attribution. nest should depend on the upstream blake3 crate (also permissive) rather than re-vendoring the from-scratch ChaCha; only the construction/dispatch pattern is the reference.

synthesis.summary: nest already lives in exactly the design space these five repos exemplify: domain-separated, length-prefixed preimages (chunk.rs, content_hash_hex), four SHA-256 integrity surfaces, and a deterministic SIMD-dispatch discipline (simd/mod.rs OnceLock + scalar fallback) that mirrors crc32c/gxhash/RustCrypto runtime detection. The collective state of the art has moved past "flat hash over the whole body" in three directions that map directly onto nest's roadmap. (1) Merkle-tree-over-fixed-chunks hashing (BLAKE3, RustCrypto blake3, bao) turns one stable root commitment into cheap partial/incremental verification of any sub-range, plus 5-10x throughput via independent-chunk SIMD+rayon -- the exact decoupling nest has between whole-file content_hash and per-section/per-chunk integrity, and the substrate for content-addressed dedup. (2) Tiered integrity: a near-free hardware checksum (crc32c, or a fast non-crypto hash) as a detect-corruption-fast pre-check, falling through to a cryptographic hash only on mismatch or when identity is needed. (3) One hash family as KDF+MAC+commitment (chacha20-blake3) for an optional committing-AEAD encrypted-at-rest container. The high-value, format-safe moves are: factor the four hand-rolled SHA-256 call sites into one ~80-line domain-separated hashing.rs trait wrapper (digest crate, zero format change); confirm sha2 0.11 runtime SHA-NI/sha2-ext dispatch is on (free validate/build speedup); and introduce BLAKE3 as a NEW additive hash-algorithm id (never mutating the FROZEN sha256: surfaces -- that is a true v2) feeding a content-defined chunk-dedup pass at build time, which is the single biggest lever toward "compress more than everyone" on repo/dataset/database corpora where cross-document redundancy dominates the codec.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The field has converged on four ideas. (a) Hashing IS a Merkle tree over fixed-size chunks (BLAKE3: 1024B chunks, 64B blocks, 32B chaining values; parent = hash(left_CV || right_CV)); the root is one 32B commitment but every interior CV verifies an arbitrary byte range without re-hashing -- enabling free parallelism (chunks independent until a cheap combine) and verified streaming/slicing (bao: transmit only path CVs + chunk, ~3.1% metadata at 1KiB chunks, tunable to ~0.1% via chunk-grouped parents). (b) Domain separation by flags/contexts (BLAKE3 ROOT/PARENT/CHUNK/KEYED/DERIVE_KEY) prevents length-extension and tree-substitution and lets one primitive serve hash, MAC, and KDF -- nest already does the moral equivalent with length-prefixed name||len framing in content_hash_hex and the "nest:chunk_id:v1\n" domain tag. (c) Runtime CPU-feature dispatch with a guaranteed byte-identical scalar fallback is universal (crc32c CanUseSse42/Arm64; RustCrypto cpufeatures zero-sized token; gxhash target_feature) -- and determinism demands the scalar path produce identical output, which nest enforces and gxhash notably CANNOT (no scalar fallback). (d) Tiered integrity: hardware CRC32C (3-way interleaved crc32 + table combine, no PCLMULQDQ dependency) or AES-NI gxhash (>30 GB/s) as fast corruption detection, reserving cryptographic SHA-256/BLAKE3 for identity. Crypto trend: committing AEAD (chacha20-blake3) collapses KDF+subkey-separation+MAC+key-commitment into one keyed BLAKE3 XOF call, binding ciphertext to exactly one key -- the right guarantee for content-addressed citations. Throughput hierarchy on non-SHA-NI hardware: BLAKE3 ~5-10x SHA-256 (~2x even with SHA-NI), gxhash >30 GB/s (non-crypto), CRC32C multiple bytes/cycle (non-crypto). All cores share nest's exact discipline: N independent items per SIMD lane, runtime detection once, repr(C) little-endian, streaming/incremental.
top_innovations: BLAKE3 Merkle-tree-over-fixed-chunks: content_hash becomes a ROOT whose interior CVs verify a single section/chunk byte-span without re-hashing the file, turning O(file) validate into O(touched-bytes)
Content-defined chunking + CV-addressed dedup before the entropy coder -- the highest-yield path to 'compress more than everyone' on repo/dataset/database corpora
Tiered integrity: near-free hardware CRC32C / fast-hash detect-corruption pre-check, falling through to SHA-256 only on mismatch or for identity
One BLAKE3 family as hash + keyed-MAC + derive_key KDF, giving domain-separated subkeys for all four integrity surfaces from a single primitive
Runtime CPU-feature dispatch with byte-identical scalar fallback (crc32c CanUseX / RustCrypto cpufeatures) as the canonical template for any new hash kernel under nest's determinism guarantee
Committing AEAD binding ciphertext to exactly one key (Encrypt-then-MAC + keyed-BLAKE3 + LE length framing) as the blueprint for an optional encrypted-at-rest codec
Chunk-group metadata knob (bao-tree): same root, parent CVs only every N KiB, cutting verification overhead from ~3-6% to ~0.1%
Generic-over-hash digest trait surface so integrity code is written once and the crate auto-selects SHA-NI/sha2-ext/AVX2/NEON backends with no format change

nest_recommendations.idea: Extract the four hand-rolled SHA-256 surfaces (header.rs::compute_checksum, section_entry.rs::compute_checksum, footer.rs::compute_file_hash, decode.rs::file_hash_hex/content_hash_hex) plus chunk.rs::chunk_id into one new ~80-line src/hashing.rs that exposes a single domain-separated, length-prefixed preimage builder over `impl digest::Update + FixedOutput`. Each surface gets a distinct domain tag (already the convention: 'nest:chunk_id:v1\n', section name||len framing). Pure refactor: byte-for-byte identical output, validated by existing golden.rs + dual_integrity.rs tests.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new crates/nest-format/src/hashing.rs; rewire callers in layout/header.rs, layout/section_entry.rs, layout/footer.rs, reader/decode.rs, chunk.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: Eliminates preimage drift across five sites, makes the integrity spec auditable in one place, and creates the single seam where a future BLAKE3 algorithm-id can be added additively. Zero format/behavior change.

nest_recommendations.idea: Confirm sha2 0.11 default runtime-dispatch backends are enabled (no sha2_backend="soft" override) so file_hash over the whole pre-footer body, content_hash over decoded canonical sections, and per-section checksums get x86 SHA-NI / aarch64 sha2-ext acceleration for free. Add a `nest stats`/benchmark line reporting the active SHA backend like SimdBackend::name() already does for dot products.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/Cargo.toml (verify sha2="0.11" features), reader/decode.rs hot path; surface backend in nest-cli/src/cmd/stats.rs + benchmark.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: ~2x faster integrity on SHA-NI CPUs (far more vs naive) with no format change -- speeds `validate`, build determinism checks, and re-hashing of large compressed sections as corpora grow. Keeps deterministic builds cheap.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a build-time content-defined chunk dedup pass: fingerprint each chunks_canonical span (and sub-block CDC boundaries) with a fast deterministic hasher, detect duplicate/identical spans across the corpus, store each unique span once with refcounts in the chunk_ids section, BEFORE zstd runs. Keep the frozen v1 layout unchanged (this is a build-time encoding decision); reference each duplicate by its stored index. Use a deterministic fixed-seed hasher so identical corpora stay byte-identical.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/writer/encoding_choice.rs and writer/build.rs; sections/chunk_ids.rs for refcount/index representation; nest-python writer path
nest_recommendations.impact: Highest-yield compression lever on multi-document / repo / dataset / whole-database corpora where cross-document redundancy dominates the codec. Dedup-then-compress (restic/borg/casync style) can beat raw zstd ratio by a large margin before any codec change.

nest_recommendations.idea: Introduce BLAKE3 as a NEW additive hash-algorithm id (e.g. a 'blake3:' chunk_id prefix and a hashing-algorithm field) WITHOUT touching any existing sha256: surface. Use BLAKE3's Merkle structure so a future large-blob content_hash is a ROOT whose interior CVs verify a single cited chunk_id's byte span against the root alone. The sha256: surfaces stay the FROZEN v1 default; blake3 is opt-in for large blobs (audio/video/datasets) where 5-10x throughput and verified-streaming matter. Feed it large mmap slices (>=16 KiB) to reach full SIMD width.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new algorithm-id plumbing through the unified src/hashing.rs; chunk.rs chunk_id prefix; a future RESERVED merkle_index section id 0x09+ for interleaved parent CVs
nest_recommendations.impact: Removes hashing from the critical path for big-file content addressing as nest scales to whole databases/repos/video; enables cryptographic verification of just a cited chunk. Strictly additive -- v1 stays frozen, never bumps.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a RESERVED merkle_index / bao_tree section (id 0x09+, additive within v1) holding interleaved parent-node chaining values (chunk-grouped so overhead is ~0.1%, not ~3%) so a partial or remote consumer of a nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation can cryptographically verify just the cited span against the root without the whole file. Tunable chunk-group size is the knob that keeps verification metadata from eroding compression-ratio gains.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new layout constant SECTION_MERKLE_INDEX (0x09) in layout/mod.rs; new sections/ module; consumed by nest-cli/src/cmd/cite.rs and validate.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: Makes citations cryptographically verifiable for partial/remote consumers at ~0.1% overhead -- a real differentiator for sovereign, content-addressed serving of large artifacts. Additive, optional, off by default.

nest_recommendations.idea: Optional fast-integrity pre-check tier for `nest validate`/`inspect`: store a near-free non-cryptographic checksum (hardware CRC32C with 3-way interleaving, or an AES-NI/portable hash) per section in a reserved metadata field, run it FIRST to detect corruption fast, and only fall through to the SHA-256 per-section checksum on mismatch or when cryptographic strength is requested. Must ship a deterministic byte-identical scalar fallback (slicing-by-4 reference) to honor nest's determinism + never-panic + <=300-line constraints.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: reserved field alongside SectionEntry checksum (or a sidecar reserved section); validate path in reader/validate.rs and nest-cli/src/cmd/validate.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: Cheap per-chunk corruption detection lets nest push more aggressive lossy int8/f16 quantization while still catching decode corruption almost for free. Speeds the validate hot path on large files. Note: google recommends crypto/HighwayHash over CRC32C for primary content addressing -- keep this as a detect-fast layer only, SHA-256 stays the identity.

nest_recommendations.idea: Swap the in-memory BuildHasher for hot-path tables that NEVER persist to disk -- bm25/index.rs HashMap<String,TermEntry> + per-doc tf_map, bm25/fusion.rs RRF HashMap<usize,f32>, ann/search.rs visited HashSet<u32>, ann/mod.rs recall HashSets -- from std SipHash to a fast hasher (foldhash/ahash on portable targets, optionally AES-NI gxhash feature-gated behind target_feature). Zero format impact because these are query-time/build-time scratch structures, not serialized bytes.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/index.rs, bm25/fusion.rs, ann/search.rs, ann/mod.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: Cuts BM25 build/query and HNSW traversal CPU (latency win, not size). Helps the known search-text overhead. Determinism preserved as long as iteration-order-dependent outputs already sort (bm25 alphabetical term order, seeded hnsw) -- verify no output depends on hash iteration order.

nest_recommendations.idea: Blueprint (not yet build) an optional committing-AEAD encrypted-at-rest codec under a RESERVED encoding id (4-255, additive within v1) wrapping non-embedding section payloads: derive enc_key|mac_key|nonce from one keyed-BLAKE3 XOF over (master_key, nonce), Encrypt-then-MAC with explicit LE length framing, constant-time tag check. Depend on the upstream blake3 crate; do NOT vendor a from-scratch ChaCha into never-panic format code -- only the construction/dispatch pattern transfers. Determinism holds given (key, fixed-nonce).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: future crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ aead module under a reserved SECTION_ENCODING id; keep embeddings unencrypted on the mmap hot scoring path
nest_recommendations.impact: Unlocks compress-then-encrypt single-file containers while staying offline/single-file/deterministic; committing property binds ciphertext to exactly one key -- the right guarantee for content-addressed citations. Orthogonal to ratio but expands the sovereign story.

compression_wins: Content-defined chunking + CV-addressed dedup BEFORE zstd: store each unique chunks_canonical span once with refcounting, deduping identical content across documents/datasets/versions. On repo/database/multi-doc corpora cross-artifact redundancy usually dwarfs the codec's per-stream gain -- this is the single biggest lever toward 'compress more than everyone', and it stays additive (a build-time encoding decision, frozen v1 layout unchanged).

Sub-block near-duplicate detection via fast fingerprints (gxhash-speed hashing of CDC boundaries) lets nest find and collapse near-identical spans across whole-repo ingestion, extending dedup beyond exact matches before the entropy coder runs.

Chunk-group Merkle metadata tuning (bao-tree): emit parent CVs only every N KiB so verification/proof metadata is ~0.1% instead of ~3-6% -- keeps the integrity layer from eroding the compression ratio when nest adds verifiable partial citations to large artifacts.

Cheap per-chunk corruption detection (hardware CRC32C / fast non-crypto checksum tier) makes aggressive lossy quantization (int8, f16, future entropy coders) safer to push harder, because decode integrity is verifiable almost for free per chunk -- indirectly enabling smaller files at a given recall.

Hardware-accelerated SHA-256 (SHA-NI/sha2-ext, free in sha2 0.11) plus optional BLAKE3 for large blobs keep re-hashing of heavily-compressed/deduplicated content off the critical path, so nest can afford to hash on every build/validate as corpora grow -- removing the disincentive to compress more aggressively.

Identical-subtree hashing (BLAKE3 Merkle): two artifacts sharing a sub-range hash that range to the same CV, making block-level dedup across datasets/repos/whole-databases detectable by hash equality -- the structural prerequisite for corpus-level (not just per-file) compression.
watch_outs: DETERMINISM: nest guarantees same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file. Any new hasher used in build output (dedup fingerprints, chunk_id) MUST be fixed-seed and cross-platform-stable (gxhash only guarantees stability within a major version and needs its deterministic feature flag; foldhash/ahash default to randomized seeds). The scalar and SIMD paths of any new kernel MUST produce byte-identical output, exactly as simd/mod.rs already enforces.

FROZEN FORMAT: the four sha256: surfaces (header_checksum, per-section checksum, file_hash, content_hash) and the 'sha256:' chunk_id prefix are identity/citation anchors. Changing the meaning of any existing hash field is a TRUE v2 (bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION) -- do NOT swap SHA-256 for BLAKE3 in place. BLAKE3 must enter only as a NEW additive algorithm-id; new sections only at id 0x09+, new encodings only at id 4-255.

gxhash NO SCALAR FALLBACK: requires AES+SSE2 (x86) or AES+NEON (aarch64) and fails to compile on unsupported targets -- a direct collision with nest's scalar-fallback/portability guarantee. It must be feature-gated behind target_feature detection with a portable fallback hasher, NEVER a hard dependency, and confined to runtime in-memory tables / build-time dedup -- never into never-panic nest-format library code.

NEVER-PANIC + heavy unsafe: gxhash and the from-scratch ChaCha in chacha20-blake3 use aggressive unsafe and are explicitly 'not for safety-critical use'. They must not enter nest-format library code (typed thiserror, no panics). Depend on the upstream permissive blake3 crate (no_std, scalar reference path) rather than re-vendoring crypto primitives; only the construction/dispatch PATTERN transfers.

EMBEDDINGS HOT PATH: embeddings are scored directly from mmap via SIMD dot products and are never zstd-compressed. Do NOT route embeddings through an encrypted/AEAD codec or any transform that breaks zero-copy mmap scoring -- confine any encryption codec to non-embedding sections, exactly as zstd is.

CRC32C IS NOT IDENTITY: google explicitly recommends a stronger hash (HighwayHash/crypto) over CRC32C for new file formats. Use CRC32C/fast hashes only as a detect-corruption-fast tier; SHA-256 content_hash must remain the stable content-addressing identity behind nest:// citations.

BLAKE3 SIMD WIDTH: BLAKE3 update() only reaches full SIMD width on large buffers (>=16 KiB for AVX-512; 8 KiB hits AVX2). Feeding it small per-chunk slices forfeits the throughput win -- only adopt it where nest can hand it large mmap slices (large blobs), not for tiny per-section hashing where SHA-NI SHA-256 is already competitive.

FILE HYGIENE: <=300 lines/file (333 hard cap), single-responsibility, repr(C), little-endian unsigned, lowercase docs no emoji/em-dash. The unified hashing.rs, any merkle_index module, and dispatch glue must each stay within these limits and split rather than grow.

categories.name: simd-lowlevel
categories.focus: SIMD, vectorization, portable intrinsics, fast string ops

repos.one_liner: A Rust "SIMD for humans" library that exposes vectorized computation as iterator combinators (simd_iter / simd_map / simd_reduce / scalar_collect) over width-agnostic vector types (f32s, i8s, etc.), compiling each closure body down to 100% native SIMD via thin intrinsic wrappers plus scalar polyfills for missing instructions.
repos.core_innovation: see field
key_techniques: Iterator combinators over SIMD: simd_iter/simd_map/simd_reduce/scalar_collect mirroring std iterators, so vectorized math reads like scalar math
Width-agnostic vector types (f32s, i8s, u8s): a single source kernel auto-selects f32x8 (AVX2) / f32x4 (NEON) / scalar, sized to the largest register the target supports

Default-value tail padding: uneven collections are finished by padding the last partial vector with a user-supplied identity value (e.g. 0.0) so the full-width SIMD kernel runs end-to-end, eliminating the scalar remainder loop (benchmarks: uneven within ~1% of even)

Thin-wrapper + polyfill portability: each op is a 1-line wrapper around an intrinsic, with a scalar polyfill that only activates on targets lacking the instruction, so the same trait method compiles everywhere
Accumulator-vector reduction: simd_reduce keeps a full-width SIMD accumulator across the loop and does a single horizontal fold at the very end, not per-element
upcast/downcast lane-width conversions (e.g. i8 lanes widened to i32/f32 lanes) exposed as vector ops, matching mixed-precision dot products
Static dispatch with #[inline] + #[target_feature] so the hot loop has zero per-iteration CPUID/branch cost
repos.nest_application: Apply to nest-runtime/src/simd/. (1) Steal the default-value tail-padding trick to kill the scalar tail loops in avx2.rs/neon.rs dot_f32_*/dot_f32_i8_* (currently lines 18-28 and 52-55 are hand-written remainder loops): pad the embedding row's final partial vector with zeros (a safe FMA identity) so one masked/padded full-width FMA finishes the dim, shrinking each kernel and removing a per-query branch — directly helps since nest scores EVERY row off mmap on the hot path. (2) Adopt faster's thin-wrapper+polyfill discipline as the template for adding NEW quantized dtypes (int4/nf4/binary) to the search hot path without exploding the per-arch file count: define one dot_f32_qN trait with an avx2/neon wrapper plus a scalar polyfill, keeping files <=300 lines and the OnceLock dispatcher unchanged. (3) The upcast/downcast lane-widening pattern is exactly nest's i8->i32->f32 widening (avx2.rs lines 45-48) and is the blueprint for int4/binary kernels that unpack sub-byte lanes — the enabler for pushing the 'tiny' preset's 0.283 size ratio lower with binary/int4 embeddings while keeping a real-cosine rerank. Do NOT adopt faster's iterator API wholesale: it is compile-time-width-only and nest's OnceLock runtime dispatch is strictly better for shipping one portable binary.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: faster's lane-widening (upcast/downcast) and polyfill discipline are the practical pattern for adding sub-byte quantized dot-product kernels (int4, nf4, binary/Hamming) to nest's hot path. Those new dtypes are what actually push the 'tiny' preset below its current 0.283 size ratio, since embeddings (the bulk of bytes, never zstd-compressed because they are scored from mmap) can only shrink via lower-precision encodings that still vectorize. faster shows how to make each new precision a thin wrapper + scalar fallback rather than a new per-arch rewrite.
repos.perf_notes: Hot-loop body compiles to 100% SIMD instructions ordered by LLVM; overhead vs hand-written intrinsics is within ~5% worst case, ~1% on the README example. Tail-padding makes uneven collections essentially free (reduce_uneven_simd 838ns vs reduce_simd 839ns; map_uneven 884ns vs map 879ns). Critical caveat for nest: dispatch is COMPILE-TIME only (no runtime feature selection — confirmed by the simdeez comparison), so a faster-built binary is pinned to the build host's widest ISA. nest's OnceLock function-pointer runtime dispatch already beats this for a single portable offline binary, so borrow the kernel/tail tricks, not the dispatch model. Performance can degrade only when a slow scalar polyfill is hit on an old CPU.
repos.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual, standard Rust dual-license; permissive, safe to learn from or vendor patterns)

repos.one_liner: A production multi-ISA CPU/GPU kernel library (MIT) whose CPU core is `arm_gemm`: a bank of hand-tuned NEON/SVE/SVE2 micro-kernels selected at runtime by a CpuInfo feature-detection layer, including int8 GEMMLowp kernels that use SDOT/UDOT/I8MM dot-product instructions with int32 accumulation and an asymmetric (scale + zero-point) requantization output stage.
repos.core_innovation: Decouple "which SIMD instruction set the binary was compiled with" from "which kernel actually runs": a single fat binary carries multiple micro-kernel variants and a runtime CpuInfo probe (getauxval(AT_HWCAP)/AT_HWCAP2 on aarch64, CPUID leaves on x86) picks the best one per call. The int8 path then exploits hardware dot-product instructions (SDOT/UDOT, AVX-VNNI vpdpbusd) that compute 4 int8 MACs into one int32 lane in a single instruction, with int32 accumulators to avoid overflow and a fixed-point (scale + zero-point) requantization stage instead of float.
key_techniques: Runtime ISA detection: getauxval(AT_HWCAP/AT_HWCAP2) bits for FEAT_DotProd, FEAT_I8MM, FP16, SVE/SVE2 on aarch64; CPUID leaf 7 for AVX2/AVX-512F/VNNI on x86_64
Multi-ISA fat binary: compile all kernel variants, set an 'arch floor' minimum, select optimal variant at runtime via a function-pointer table keyed on detected features
int8 dot-product micro-kernels: NEON vdotq_s32 / SVE svdot / x86 _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 doing 4 int8 MACs/lane into int32 accumulators (GEMMLowp), avoiding int16 overflow
Asymmetric quantization: per-tensor/per-row scale (f32) + zero_point offset, with the (a-zp_a)*(b-zp_b) expansion folded into precomputed offset-correction terms
Fixed-point requantization output stage: int32 accumulator * int32 multiplier + rounding shift instead of float divide, for deterministic integer-only scoring
Kernel naming convention encoding ISA+dtypes+tile (e.g. sve_hybrid_u8u32_dot_6x4VL) plus microarch-specific variants (a64fx.cpp) for issue-width/cache tuning
MxN register tiling/blocking with weight pre-packing so the inner loop streams contiguously and reuses loaded vectors across accumulators
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals into nest-runtime's simd dispatcher (crates/nest-runtime simd module + search hot path). (1) Replace nest's compile-time cfg!(target_arch) dispatch with an ACL-style runtime feature probe: a std::sync::OnceLock<Cpu> populated via std::arch::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx512vnni"/"avx2") and is_aarch64_feature_detected!("dotprod"/"neon"), holding a fn pointer to the chosen dot kernel. ONE shipped nest binary then uses AVX-512/VNNI or NEON-dotprod when present and falls back to AVX2/NEON/scalar, all behind a typed never-panic dispatcher. (2) Add a dedicated int8 cosine kernel for the 'tiny' preset (int8 embeddings, encoding id already reserved): mirror GEMMLowp by accumulating int8*int8 into i32 with _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 (AVX-VNNI) / vdotq_s32 (NEON) / scalar i32 fallback, storing per-row scale (and optional zero_point) alongside the int8 block so cosine is reconstructed from the i32 dot + scales. This makes the smallest preset (0.283 ratio) also the fastest to score directly off mmap, and integer accumulation keeps scoring bit-deterministic across machines (a nest hard requirement) where float SIMD reduction order is not. The scale/zero_point metadata is additive in the int8 codec header, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly serves compress-more-than-everyone: nest's int8 preset is its most compact embedding encoding (0.283 size ratio, recall@10 0.992). ACL's GEMMLowp proves you can score that int8 representation natively with dot-product instructions instead of dequantizing to f32 first, so the smallest-on-disk format also becomes the cheapest-to-search. Asymmetric scale+zero_point quantization packs more fidelity per int8 than a symmetric scheme, enabling more aggressive quantization (toward int4) without recall loss, pushing the compression frontier while keeping search fast and deterministic.
repos.license: MIT
repos.perf_notes: SDOT/UDOT (FEAT_DotProd) and AVX-VNNI vpdpbusd give ~4x the int8 throughput of a naive multiply-then-widen-add loop by fusing 4 MACs/lane into one instruction with free int32 accumulation; I8MM/SME push further with outer-product matrix instructions. Integer accumulation is reduction-order-independent, so it is reproducible across CPUs unlike float horizontal sums (matters for nest determinism). MxN register tiling + weight pre-packing keeps the inner GEMM loop bound by dot/FMA issue rate rather than loads; for nest's single-query dot products the win is mainly the per-element instruction fusion + runtime dispatch, not the heavy tiling. int8 embeddings are 4x smaller than f32 in cache, so more vectors stay resident on the mmap hot path.

repos.one_liner: A single header-only C/C++ file (~11.7k LOC) that reimplements the entire x86 SSE/SSE2/SSE3/SSSE3/SSE4.1/SSE4.2/AES/CRC32 intrinsic surface (xmmintrin.h through wmmintrin.h) on top of ARM NEON, preserving x86 semantics so SSE codebases compile and run on aarch64/armv7 unchanged.
repos.core_innovation: Semantics-preserving cross-ISA intrinsic emulation: every x86 SIMD op gets a hand-tuned NEON instruction sequence that reproduces exact x86 corner-case behavior (sign-bit packing order, masked-lane multiply-by-zero, IEEE-754 rounding, saturation), with compile-time precision flags trading speed for bit-exact fidelity. The transferable kernel patterns are the NEON replacements for x86 ops that have no NEON equivalent: movemask via shift-and-horizontal-add, and 128-bit-compare-to-bitmask via shift-right-narrow-by-4 (vshrn).
key_techniques: movemask_epi8 on aarch64: vshrq_n_u8(x,7) isolates MSBs, vshlq_u8 by a per-lane shift table {0..7,0..7}, then vaddv_u8 over each 64-bit half packs 16 sign bits into a 16-bit integer
movemask on armv7 (no vaddv): cascaded vsraq_n_u64 shift-right-accumulate at offsets 7,14,28 folds MSBs into one byte per half

compare-mask-to-bitmask via vshrn_n_u16(mask,4): shift-right-narrow turns a 128-bit all-ones/all-zeros compare result into a 64-bit nibble mask, then ctz/clz gives first-match length (cmpestri string ops)
_mm_shuffle_epi8 (pshufb) via vqtbl1q_s8 with index pre-masked by 0x8F so the high bit zeroes the lane, matching x86; armv7 falls back to vtbl.8 over even/odd D registers
_mm_maddubs_epi16 / madd via vmull widening multiply + vrshrn rounding-narrow-shift-right; mulhrs uses vrshrn_n_s32(mul,15) for round-to-nearest fixed-point
compile-time fidelity knobs: PRECISE_DIV/SQRT add Newton-Raphson iterations, PRECISE_MINMAX fixes NaN ordering, PRECISE_DP forces masked-lane multiply-by-zero in dot product
AES emulation from vqtbl1q_u8 table lookups (ShiftRows/ror32by8 permutation constants) when hardware crypto extensions are absent
QEMU-based cross-ISA differential test harness: same inputs through real SSE and the NEON emulation, compared bit-for-bit across armv7/armv8 aarch32/aarch64
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime simd dispatcher (src/simd*.rs): nest already ships AVX2 + NEON + scalar dot-product kernels. Steal two NEON micro-patterns to harden/extend the aarch64 path. (1) The vshrn_n_u16(cmp,4) compare-to-nibble-mask trick: use in a NEON int8 cosine/dot kernel to find/skip zero lanes and to build candidate masks if nest adds SIMD-accelerated bm25 tokenization or pattern scanning over chunks_canonical (the known-gap word-segmented tokenizer). (2) The movemask shift-and-vaddv pattern: needed any time the NEON path reduces a per-lane boolean (quantization clamp detection, NaN guard before exact rerank). Also adopt sse2neon's compile-time precision philosophy: nest's int8 preset scores quantized embeddings directly off mmap, so a NEON vmull+vrshrn rounding-narrow widening-multiply (instead of plain truncation) gives bit-closer agreement with the AVX2/scalar reference on aarch64, protecting deterministic-build and exact-rerank guarantees across architectures. Reference its QEMU differential-test method to prove nest's three SIMD backends return identical dot products on the same .nest file.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-direct: a portability/correctness library, not a compressor, so it does not shrink the .nest file. Indirect relevance is real: extreme compression in nest leans on aggressive quantization (int8 today, possibly sub-byte later), and quantized vectors are only useful if the on-disk codes decode and score identically on every CPU. sse2neon's rounding-narrow multiply kernels and cross-ISA differential-testing discipline are exactly what keeps a denser quantization scheme bit-faithful across AVX2/NEON/scalar, so the compression frontier can advance without breaking deterministic builds or the exact-cosine ground truth.
repos.perf_notes: Header-only, zero runtime cost (all FORCE_INLINE). Most ops are 1-3 NEON instructions; expensive emulations are documented (_mm_maddubs_epi16 ~13 instructions; dp_ps and cmpestr* are multi-instruction). aarch64 movemask uses cheap vaddv horizontal add while armv7 needs the 3-stage vsra cascade. Per-op cost tracked in perf-tier.md. Known semantic gaps: _mm_rsqrt_ps(0.0) returns NaN on NEON vs INF on SSE; min/max NaN ordering differs unless PRECISE flags set. NEON is 128-bit only, so AVX2 256-bit ops are out of scope (sse2neon stops at SSE4.2/128-bit lanes).
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A C++ portable-SIMD library exposing a single width-agnostic ops API (Add/Mul/MulAdd/Load/Compress/Gather/Mask) that compiles each translation unit once per instruction set (SSE4/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/SVE/RVV/WASM) and selects the best kernel at runtime via a function-pointer table, plus contrib kernels for vectorized quicksort (vqsort), math, and reductions.
repos.core_innovation: The "compile every kernel once per SIMD target, then pick the best at runtime through a cached function-pointer table" pattern (foreach_target.h + HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH + HWY_EXPORT): one width-agnostic source body, N object-code variants, one CPU-feature detection paid once, then an indirect call per hot-path entry instead of a CPUID/branch per element. This is exactly the dispatch discipline nest's hot-path dot-product loop needs to scale beyond its current hand-written avx2/neon/scalar trio without bloating the small rust core.
key_techniques: foreach_target.h: include a -inl.h kernel body once per target in HWY_TARGETS via controlled re-inclusion + per-target namespace (hwy::HWY_NAMESPACE)

HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH + HWY_EXPORT: build a per-function pointer table, resolve once with GetChosenTarget().Update(SupportedTargets()), then indirect-call (mirrors nest's OnceLock function-pointer cache, but table-per-function not enum-per-call)
width-agnostic tag types (ScalableTag/CappedTag/FixedTag) so one loop body targets 128/256/512-bit and scalable SVE/RVV with automatic remainder handling
Compress/CompressStore: stream-compaction primitive (store only mask=yes lanes consecutively) — the engine of vqsort's branchless 3-region partition
AVX2 compress emulation via table-driven permute (precomputed shuffle-index LUT indexed by an 8-bit mask) when no native VPCOMPRESS exists
vqsort: branchless SIMD partition + recursive sorting-network base case (<=256 elts) + 384-byte robust pivot sampling with heapsort fallback for O(n log n) worst case
MaskedLoad/BlendedStore/FirstN for tail/remainder handling without scalar fallthrough
SoA + aligned-allocation discipline as the precondition for SIMD payoff (>=100KiB arrays before wide vectors pay off)
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals into nest-runtime/src/simd/. (1) Dispatch refactor: mod.rs currently does `match detect_backend()` (an enum compare) inside every dot_* wrapper, and each new dtype x target adds a match arm. Adopt Highway's per-function pointer-table idea: store `fn(&[f32],&[u8])->f32` resolved once in a OnceLock, so adding AVX-512 or SVE later is a new table entry, not a new hot-path branch — keeps files under the 300-line cap while widening target coverage. Also add an F16C-detected avx2 f16 path (today dot_f32_f16_bytes falls back to scalar on x86_64, a perf gap flagged in the file's own comment). (2) Compress-store primitive: port Highway's table-driven Compress (AVX2 permute-LUT / NEON / scalar) into a new simd/compress.rs. This unlocks the highest-leverage item on nest's roadmap: a deterministic SIMD candidate-compaction filter in ann/search.rs (compact surviving HNSW candidates branchlessly before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank), and it is the exact primitive needed if nest adds a vectorized RLE/sparse repack codec for non-embedding sections in nest-format/encoding. Keep it offline/deterministic: pure compute, fixed LUTs => byte-identical results, fits the additive-format and never-panic constraints.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. Highway is not a compressor; its payoff for nest's compress-more-than-everyone north star is the Compress/CompressStore stream-compaction primitive, the SIMD engine behind branchless partition, RLE/sparse repack, and mask-driven candidate pruning. Direct relevance: int8 quantization (tiny preset, 0.283 ratio) dot products and ANN rerank throughput; a faster, wider, table-dispatched kernel lets nest afford finer quantization (per-block int4/int8 with SIMD dequant) at serve time without blowing the mandatory exact-cosine rerank budget.
repos.perf_notes: vqsort beats std::sort by 10-20x on AVX2/AVX-512 and ips4o by geomean 2.89x single-core / 1.59x parallel; robust pivot sampling adds <2% CPU. vqsort uses ~1.2KiB stack + a 3-word TLS RNG cache, no heap. Guidance: wide-vector overhead only pays above ~100KiB arrays, and SoA + aligned loads are prerequisites — relevant because nest embedding rows are mmap'd contiguous f32/f16/i8 (already SoA) and dims are typically 384-1536, well above SIMD break-even. Highway f16 paths assume F16C/NEON-fp16; nest's avx2 f16 currently degrades to scalar.

repos.one_liner: A C++ header library of SIMD (AVX-512/AVX2) sorting primitives — quicksort, quickselect, partialsort, argsort/argselect, and key-value sort for 16/32/64-bit ints and floats — built as a hybrid of vectorized quicksort partitioning plus branch-free bitonic sorting networks for small partitions.
repos.core_innovation: Branch-free vectorized partitioning via AVX-512 compressstore (the single most transferable idea).
key_techniques: AVX-512 compressstore partitioning: cmp-vs-pivot -> mask -> _mm512_mask_compressstoreu writes selected lanes densely, branch-free
Branch-free bitonic sorting networks for small arrays (<= ~512 elems) built purely from min/max COEX (compare-exchange) over SIMD registers, sorting N vectors simultaneously
Hybrid quicksort: recurse with vectorized partition until partition size drops below a power-of-2 threshold (512/256/128/64), then switch to the in-register network
Key-value / argsort: a parallel index (or value) vector is permuted in lockstep with the keys using the same shuffle/permute masks, so the sort carries a payload
Runtime CPU-feature dispatch: pick AVX-512F+DQ / AVX2 / scalar kernel at load time
NaN canonicalization: NaNs hoisted to array end and rewritten as a single quiet-NaN bit pattern so the comparator stays total/branch-free
Per-march tuning (skylake-avx512 for 32/64-bit, icelake for 16-bit) showing the network must be specialized per lane-width
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime/src/simd (the dispatcher that already does AVX2/NEON/scalar dot products) is the natural home. Two concrete steals: (1) Branch-free top-k / threshold filtering on the search hot path. After exact-cosine rerank, nest must select top-k and filter candidates above a score threshold; today that is a scalar scan with branches. Adapt the compressstore trick — compute scores in a SIMD register, mask = (score >= threshold), then compressstore the surviving candidate indices densely (vpcompressd on AVX2 via _mm256_maskz_compress on AVX-512, or a NEON shuffle-table fallback). This collapses the candidate-pruning loop to branch-free SIMD and pairs directly with the existing dot-product kernel. (2) The key-value/argsort pattern maps onto materialize/search returning (score, chunk_id) pairs: permute the id payload in lockstep with the score vector so the final sorted top-k comes out without a separate gather. Keep all of this in the existing simd dispatcher behind the same AVX2/NEON/scalar feature-gates, never panic, scalar fallback mandatory. This does NOT touch the FROZEN nest-format container (no new section/encoding id), so it respects additive-only constraints — it is pure runtime acceleration.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect. This library is about sort/select throughput, not bytes-on-disk, so it does not advance the 'compress more than everyone' north star directly. Indirect leverage: (a) a fast branch-free argsort enables cheap reordering of chunks/embeddings by a similarity or cluster key at build time, and clustered/sorted embeddings compress better under delta+int8 quantization (locality improves residual entropy) — a real but second-order win for the tiny/compressed presets; (b) faster top-k keeps the mandatory exact-cosine rerank cheap even as corpora grow. It buys serving speed and a modest compression-locality assist, not a new codec.
repos.perf_notes: Reported 4-10x over std::sort for object/key-value sort on AVX-512; the upstream research (Bramas) reports ~8x on small arrays (<16 SIMD vectors), ~4x vs libstdc++ and ~1.4x vs Intel IPP on large arrays. Performance comes entirely from eliminating branch mispredictions (compressstore) and from branch-free min/max networks that saturate SIMD ports; OpenMP variant adds up to ~3x with <=16 threads. Memory: object/argsort needs arrsize*sizeof(key) + arrsize*4 bytes aux (O(N) scratch). Critical caveat for nest: compressstore (vpcompressd) is an AVX-512 instruction; on AVX2 it must be emulated with a 256-entry precomputed permute LUT, and on aarch64/NEON there is no compress so it needs a shuffle-table fallback — the scalar fallback path is mandatory under nest constraints.

Portable fixed-width vector types f32x4/f32x8/f32x16, f64x2/4/8, i8x16/u8x16, i16x8, i32x4 plus mask8x16/16x8/32x4 with overloaded +,*,FMA lowering to optimal intrinsics

repos.one_liner: A ~1-file MIT C99/C++ header that replaces integer division by a runtime-invariant divisor with one widening multiply-high plus two shifts, using the Granlund-Montgomery (1994) "division by invariant integers via multiplication" magic-number scheme, with portable mulhi backends per platform.
repos.core_innovation: Precompute a per-divisor "magic" reciprocal struct {value, m, s1, s2} once, then turn every later n/d and n%d into branch-free q = (mulhi(n,m) + ((n - mulhi(n,m)) >> s1)) >> s2 and r = n - q*value. This converts a 20-40 cycle hardware UDIV (which most SIMD ISAs lack for integers) into a 3-5 cycle mul+shift sequence that IS vectorizable, amortized across millions of dividends sharing the same divisor.
key_techniques: Granlund-Montgomery magic-number reciprocal: m = floor(2^(N+l)/d)+1 with l = ceil(log2(d)), giving exact quotient for all N-bit n
Round-up correction split into two shifts s1=1 and s2=l-1 to avoid an (N+1)-bit intermediate without a wider integer type

mulhi (high half of NxN product) abstracted over backends: __umulh/_umul128 (MSVC), unsigned __int128 shift (gcc/clang), __umulhi/__umul64hi (CUDA), mul_hi (OpenCL), and a 32x32->64 split-and-recombine portable fallback
Highest-set-bit via __builtin_clz / _BitScanReverse with a bit-twiddle fallback to compute l in O(1)
Trivial divisor==1 special-case (m=1, s1=s2=0)
Branch-free fxdiv_round_down(n,g) = (n/g.value)*g.value for size/offset alignment
POD divisor struct hoisted as loop-invariant and broadcast across SIMD lanes (used in NNPACK/QNNPACK to vectorize tiling index math)
repos.nest_application: Adopt as a tiny internal Rust module in nest-runtime, NOT a change to the current dot-product kernels. Today the hot loop in crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs and ann/build.rs addresses embedding rows with i*row_size / i*dim (pure multiply, no divide), so FXdiv buys nothing there. Its payoff is forward-looking: (a) a future tensor/Parquet/video section that maps a flat mmap offset back to (row,col,channel) and would need /dim and %dim per element; (b) product-quantization codecs (relevant to the tiny preset and extreme compression) where decoding sub-vector indices needs divide/modulo by codebook count; (c) deterministic seeded RNG / hash bucketing needing fast unbiased range reduction. In each, precompute a usize/u32 magic divisor once per build and reuse branch-free mul+shift, keeping kernels SIMD-friendly (AVX2/NEON have no integer UDIV) and integer-exact/identical across x86_64/aarch64/scalar, satisfying byte-reproducibility and never-panic. Port is ~60 lines of safe Rust using u128 widening mul ((n as u128 * m as u128) >> 64), well under the 300-line cap; MIT lets nest reimplement rather than vendor.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. It does not compress bytes itself; it is an enabling primitive for compression schemes that add integer division/modulo on the decode hot path -- specifically product quantization / residual codebooks (sub-vector = idx % K, codebook = idx / K) and packed multi-dim tensor layouts. If nest ships PQ for sub-int8 embedding compression (a real lever for beating the 0.283 tiny ratio), FXdiv-style magic division keeps the dequant loop branch-free and vectorizable. Until PQ/tensor sections exist, relevance to compress-more-than-everyone is latent, not active.
repos.perf_notes: Replaces a ~20-40 cycle non-pipelined integer UDIV with mulhi (3-5 cycle latency, fully pipelined) plus two 1-cycle shifts; the divisor struct is loop-invariant and stays in registers. x86 AVX2 and ARM NEON have NO integer divide instruction, so this is the only way to vectorize per-lane integer divide/modulo. Header-only, zero allocations, divisor struct is 8-24 bytes POD. Used in production inside NNPACK / QNNPACK / XNNPACK for convolution tiling index arithmetic.

repos.one_liner: Header-only C99 library that re-implements every native SIMD intrinsic (SSE/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/SVE/WASM128, thousands of functions) as a per-function compile-time cascade -- native passthrough, then cross-ISA emulation, then compiler vector builtins, then portable scalar fallback -- exposing the FULL native API instead of a lowest-common-denominator abstraction.
repos.core_innovation: The full-API per-function fallback cascade: each operation picks the fastest available implementation at compile time (native intrinsic, then another ISA's intrinsics, then __builtin_shufflevector/__builtin_convertvector, then plain C99), so one source compiles everywhere with zero overhead where native support exists, and the portable C99 fallback is written shuffle/convert-aware so the compiler auto-vectorizes it (often beating naive scalar even on the wrong arch). The scalar path is a first-class, correctness-checked sibling of the SIMD paths, not an afterthought.
key_techniques: Per-function implementation cascade (native -> cross-ISA -> compiler vector builtin -> scalar C99) selected at compile time via ifdefs
Cross-ISA emulation: implement SSE/AVX semantics with NEON ops and vice versa so one kernel runs on x86 and aarch64
Compiler vector extensions (__builtin_shufflevector, __builtin_convertvector, fixed-width vector typedefs) as a portable layer below intrinsics, above scalar
Auto-vectorization-friendly scalar fallbacks plus -fopenmp-simd / SIMDE_VECTORIZE pragmas to hint loop vectorization without rewriting kernels
Fixed-width types (int8_t/uint16_t) instead of ambiguous char/int for bit-identical results across architectures (determinism)
-DSIMDE_NO_NATIVE switch that forces the portable path purely for differential testing of fallback vs native equivalence
Reusable conversion primitives: f16<->f32 (F16C/fcvtl) and i8->i32 lane widening helpers shared across kernels
repos.nest_application: Target crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/ (mod.rs + avx2.rs + neon.rs + scalar.rs). nest hand-writes 3 dtype kernels (f32, f16, i8) x up to 3 ISAs as near-duplicated functions plus a OnceLock function-pointer dispatcher. Steal SIMDe's METHOD (not its C): (1) Make scalar a verified equivalence-sibling -- add to simd/tests.rs a differential test (the SIMDE_NO_NATIVE idea) asserting avx2/neon kernels equal the scalar kernel within epsilon on random vectors, gated on the existing NEST_FORCE_SCALAR env; this hardens the exact-cosine-is-ground-truth contract and the deterministic-build guarantee. (2) Factor the f16->f32 and i8->i32 widening steps (currently inlined in avx2.rs and neon.rs) into small shared inlined helpers so adding a new low-bit embedding dtype (int4/bf16 for a smaller tiny-class preset) becomes one widen-helper + one scalar reference, not a full new ISA matrix. Do NOT vendor SIMDe (C vs nest's repr(C) Rust + std::arch); borrow the cascade discipline only. This unlocks safe addition of lower-bit embedding quantization on the mmap hot path.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. SIMDe is a portability layer, not a compressor, so it does not shrink the .nest file. Its value to the compress-more-than-everyone goal is enabling lower-bit embedding quantization: the hot-path dot product must stay fast AND bit-exact for any new on-disk dtype, and SIMDe's pattern (first-class scalar oracle + auto-vectorizable fallback + factored widening primitives) is the testing/structure discipline that lets nest safely add int4/bf16 embedding encodings (encoding ids 4-255 are reserved/additive in v1) and push the tiny preset below its current 0.283 size ratio without breaking deterministic builds or exact rerank.
repos.license: MIT (SIMDe COPYING permissive license); safe to study and reimplement the pattern in Rust with no copyleft obligation.
repos.perf_notes: Native passthrough = zero overhead vs hand-written intrinsics (wrappers inline away). Key claim to internalize: well-structured portable fallbacks auto-vectorize and beat naive scalar even off-target because compilers won't turn a naive loop into PSHUFB/fcvtl on their own -- so nest's scalar fallback should stay shape-friendly (fixed chunked loops, fixed-width types) to keep vectorizing on non-AVX2/non-NEON targets (older x86, RISC-V), where nest's dispatcher currently drops straight to scalar. -O3 and -fopenmp-simd-equivalent hints maximize fallback throughput with no runtime dependency.

repos.one_liner: stdarch is the implementation home of Rust's `core::arch` / `std::arch` vendor intrinsics plus `std_detect` runtime CPU feature detection, organized as one `#[target_feature(enable=...)]`-gated intrinsic per machine instruction, with detection cached lock-free in an atomic bitset and verified by an `assert_instr` macro that disassembles the compiled shim to confirm the expected instruction was emitted.
repos.core_innovation: The two-layer "safe runtime dispatch" contract: each architecture-specific kernel is an `unsafe fn` carrying `#[target_feature(enable = "feat")]` (which lets LLVM emit that ISA's instructions for just that function without -C target-feature), and it is reached only behind an `is_x86_feature_detected!`/`is_aarch64_feature_detected!` guard whose result is computed once and cached in a lock-free atomic bitset, so a portable least-common-denominator binary picks the fastest available kernel at runtime with zero per-call CPUID cost. The matching trick is per-instruction granularity: one intrinsic == one named instruction, so capability can be detected and dispatched at the finest possible level (f16c, avxvnni, dotprod separately from avx2).
key_techniques: #[target_feature(enable="avx2,fma")] per-function ISA enablement (no global -C target-feature needed)

is_x86_feature_detected!/is_aarch64_feature_detected! macros over std_detect; detection cached in a lock-free atomic-usize bitset with an initialized sentinel bit so CPUID/getauxval(HWCAP)/sysctl runs exactly once

fine-grained gates: f16c (_mm256_cvtph_ps -> vcvtph2ps) for hw f16->f32, avxvnni/avx512vnni (_mm256_dpbusd_epi32 -> vpdpbusd) for single-instruction int8 dot, aarch64 dotprod (vdotq_s32) for NEON int8 dot
_mm256_fmadd_ps / vfmaq_f32 fused multiply-add accumulators (the core of a dot product)
#[assert_instr(vfmadd)] proc-macro emits a #[test] shim, compiles it, and greps the disassembly to prove the intended instruction was generated
static vs dynamic dispatch duality: same kernel reachable via #[cfg(target_feature)] or runtime guard
repr(simd) Simd<T,N> newtype over [T;N] with simd_fma/simd_cast LLVM intrinsics as the portable lowering substrate

(2) The int8 path dot_f32_i8_avx2 (lines 36-60) widens i8->i32->f32 then FMAs -- gate an avxvnni/avx512vnni tier using _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 (vpdpbusd) for int8 accumulate-to-i32 in one instruction, multiplying by the per-vector scale once at the end, accelerating the tiny preset (zstd/int8/hnsw, 0.283 ratio) hot path. (3) In neon.rs add an is_aarch64_feature_detected!(\"dotprod\") tier using vdotq_s32 for the same int8 win on Apple silicon. Add Avx2F16c/Avx2Vnni/NeonDotprod variants to the SimdBackend enum so nest stats reports the active tier. All additive, offline, deterministic (exact rerank stays ground truth); no format change.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: extreme compression in nest comes from the int8 and float16 codecs (tiny = 0.283 ratio), but those quantized formats are only viable on the hot path if they decode/score fast off mmap. stdarch's f16c (vcvtph2ps) and VNNI/dotprod (vpdpbusd/vdotq_s32) single-instruction kernels remove the widen-and-convert overhead that currently makes the compressed dtypes slower per query than f32, so the most-compressed presets stop paying a latency tax. repos.one_liner: A dual-licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0) C++ library for SIMD-accelerated Unicode validation, transcoding (UTF-8/16/32/Latin1), and WHATWG base64 codec that hits billions of chars/sec via per-arch kernels (SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512-VBMI2/NEON/SVE/RVV/POWER) selected by runtime CPU dispatch.

Sliding-window vectorization with prev1/prev2/prev3 lane-shifts to validate multi-byte sequences across register boundaries
Muła/Lemire base64 nibble-LUT range+shift via pshufb then multiply-add pack (vpmaddubsw/vpmulhuw+vpmullw) to repack 6-bit groups; 14 vec instrs / 32 bytes
AVX-512 VBMI single-pass base64 decode via vpermb 256-entry permute
Runtime per-arch implementation table chosen once via function pointer; AVX-512 gated on VBMI2 to avoid pre-Ice-Lake throttling
ASCII fast-path detecting zero high bits to skip full machinery (~66 GiB/s, 20x ICU)
Non-allocating, exception-free pointer+length API compiling to a few hundred KB

repos.one_liner: A Rust crate providing CPU-feature-dispatched SIMD byte-search (memchr/2/3) and substring search (memmem) built on a write-once `Vector` trait abstraction, a frequency-ranked "packed pair" rare-byte prefilter, the Two-Way string-matching algorithm as a linear-time fallback, and a SWAR (SIMD-within-a-register) scalar path.
