256-entry HeuristicFrequencyRank background byte-frequency table
PrefilterState dynamic false-positive-driven disabling
Two-Way O(m+n)/O(1) verifier backbone
Rabin-Karp small-haystack fast path
Write-once generic Vector trait with per-arch shims
SWAR has_zero_byte bit-twiddle + splat broadcast
Runtime AVX2/SSE2 feature dispatch with reusable amortized Finder
repos.nest_application: Two concrete wins, both in nest-runtime. (1) bm25_index (0x08) and search-text: the bm25 tokenizer/term scan and any substring/term lookup over chunks_canonical can use a memchr-style packed-pair prefilter to scan mmapped text without allocation; this directly attacks the known CJK/Thai degradation by letting a future codepoint-aware scanner stay vectorized. Practically, depend on the `memchr` crate (zero-dep, no_std-capable) in nest-runtime rather than hand-rolling -- it respects the never-open-a-socket / offline constraint and is deterministic. (2) The bigger steal is the architectural pattern for nest's simd dispatcher in nest-runtime: memchr's write-once `Vector` trait + per-target shim (AVX2/NEON/scalar) is exactly the shape nest's dot-product dispatcher already wants; adopt it so the f32/f16/int8 cosine kernels are one generic body with trivial AVX2/NEON/SWAR shims instead of three parallel copies, keeping files under the 300-line cap and removing duplication. The SWAR has_zero_byte/splat trick is a ready-made deterministic scalar fallback pattern for any byte-level scan added to nest-format (e.g. validating/section-scanning during reader.rs parsing) that must never panic and must run identically on every arch.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. memchr is not a compressor, so it does not shrink the .nest file. Its relevance to the compress-more-than-everyone goal is on the SERVE side: faster, allocation-free scanning over compressed/mmapped text sections means nest can afford to keep more sections zstd-compressed and still hit latency targets, because term/substring lookup over decoded text stays in vectorized loops. The packed-pair + frequency-rank idea is also directly transferable to building selective prefilters over int8-quantized embedding scans (pick the most discriminative dimensions first), which helps keep the tiny preset (int8/hnsw) fast at high compression ratio.
repos.perf_notes: Throughput is dominated by staying in the vector loop: AVX2 processes 32 bytes/iter, SSE2/NEON/wasm 16 bytes/iter, scalar SWAR 8 bytes (usize) per iter. The rare-byte pair keeps false positives near zero so verification is rarely triggered; the PrefilterState self-disable prevents pathological O(n*m)-ish blowups on adversarial inputs. Zero heap allocation in the hot path, no_std-capable (SSE2/NEON without std, AVX2 gated behind std feature detection). Reusable Finder amortizes searcher construction across many calls -- a measurable win over libc memmem and std which reconstruct per call.

repos.one_liner: A portable C/C++ string library exposing CPU-feature-dispatched SIMD microkernels (NEON, AVX2, AVX-512, SVE, SWAR fallback, CUDA) for substring search, AES-NI hashing, Rabin-rolling-hash MinHash sketches, Levenshtein/Needleman-Wunsch alignment, argsort, and lookup-table byte transforms.
repos.core_innovation: Runtime CPU-capability dispatch over a family of hand-written SIMD microkernels with named per-uarch variants (sz_find_skylake / sz_find_haswell / sz_find_westmere / sz_find_neon) selected once at load, each kernel built around the principle "you already fetch every cache line, so the only win is reducing comparisons per cache line": pick rare/anomalous needle bytes at strategic offsets, broadcast-compare them with one SIMD op, and only confirm full matches on the survivors.
key_techniques: AES-NI based non-cryptographic sz_hash: feed bytes through hardware AESENC rounds for a fast, well-mixed 64-bit hash (plus streaming sz_hash_state_t and sz_hash_sha256 for crypto checksums)
Rabin-style 64-bit rolling hash reused for both whole-string and substring (fingerprint) hashing, giving O(D*(T-N)) MinHash cost independent of window width N
MinHash / Fingerprints sketches: D rolling-hash functions over multiple window widths (e.g. 4,6,8,10), keeping per-dimension minima as a compact D-dim document signature; 52-bit hash variant in v4

Substring search via rare-byte + multi-offset SIMD comparison (compare characters at strategically chosen needle offsets to cut false positives), Boyer-Moore-Horspool with Raita heuristic for long needles, bit-parallel for mid needles, brute SIMD for 1-4 byte needles

Offset-based 'tape' layout (Strs): one contiguous byte tape plus a u32 offsets array, ~4 bytes overhead per string for sub-4GB datasets, zero-copy mmap and PyArrow-serializable, lazy split_iter avoids materialization
vpshufb / NEON vtbl lookup-table transform (sz_lookup) mapping bytes through a 256-entry table at ~21 GB/s, 80x std::transform, usable as int8 codec / case-fold / dna decode
Radix/parallel sz_sequence_argsort returning a permutation over a string collection (beats std::sort and 4x numpy.argsort) without moving the underlying bytes
Two-tier retrieve-then-rerank architecture: cheap MinHash fingerprints for candidate retrieval, expensive exact Levenshtein/NW scoring only on reranked survivors
repos.nest_application: Four concrete steals. (1) nest-runtime simd dispatcher: adopt StringZilla's named-per-uarch runtime dispatch pattern (currently nest has AVX2/NEON/scalar) so the dot-product kernel picks AVX-512/AVX2/SSE/NEON/scalar once at mmap time behind one fn pointer, keeping the never-panic typed-error boundary; optionally vendor StringZilla (Apache-2.0) for sz_hash. (2) nest-format hashing: replace or augment SHA-256 surfaces' hot-path data-integrity needs with AES-NI sz_bytesum/sz_hash for a fast non-crypto pre-check while keeping SHA-256 as the canonical content_hash (additive, no format bump). (3) nest-format new optional section (id 0x09+, RESERVED today): a deterministic MinHash 'sketch index' built from Rabin rolling fingerprints over chunks_canonical, giving an ultra-compact pre-filter that shrinks the candidate set before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank, mirroring nest's existing HNSW+rerank contract and StringZilla's retrieve-then-rerank design. (4) nest-format chunks layout + int8 codec: the offset-tape (u32 offsets + byte tape) is exactly nest's chunks_canonical/chunks_original_spans shape, and vpshufb/vtbl sz_lookup is a ready SIMD kernel for the int8 encoding decode path and for a SIMD bm25 tokenizer that fixes the CJK/Thai word-segmentation gap via byte-level scanning.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. StringZilla does not add a new entropy coder, so it does not directly beat zstd on ratio. Its compression-mission value is (a) MinHash sketches as a tiny deduplication/near-duplicate detector to drop redundant chunks before encoding, raising effective ratio; (b) the offset-tape layout minimizes per-string overhead (4 bytes) in the text sections; (c) vpshufb LUT transform accelerates int8 quantization decode so the tiny preset stays fast off mmap. The decisive contribution is making the serve path cheaper (AES hashing, dispatched SIMD, fingerprint pre-filter), which lets nest keep aggressive compression without hurting search latency.
repos.perf_notes: sz_find ~10.6 GB/s x86 / 7.1 GB/s ARM (vs libc strstr 7.4 / 2.0); sz_lookup ~21 GB/s (80x std::transform); AES sz_hash ~3x OpenSSL hashlib on mmap'd files; argsort 1.91s vs std::sort 2.79s and numpy 7.58s on 8M words; Levenshtein 3.4B CUPS x86 / 93.6B CUPS CUDA. Kernels are scalar-fallback-safe (SWAR on 64-bit words), header-only C with stable ABI, zero-alloc in-place ops, and the per-uarch backends are disablable via SZ_USE_X86_AVX512 / SZ_USE_X86_AVX2 / SZ_USE_ARM_NEON compile flags.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

synthesis.summary: This category is fundamentally a serve-side accelerator for nest's compression mission, not a compressor itself: none of the 12 repos add an entropy coder, but collectively they answer the one question that gates how far nest can push quantization: "can the smallest-on-disk embedding format also be the fastest to score directly off mmap, bit-identically on every CPU?" The state of the art has converged hard on one dispatch idiom that nest already implements correctly: detect CPU features once, cache in a OnceLock/atomic-bitset, then indirect-call a per-arch kernel with zero per-element CPUID cost (stdarch, Highway, memchr, StringZilla, ACL all do exactly this; nest's simd/mod.rs is a faithful copy). nest's current code is solid but leaves three concrete, code-confirmed wins on the table. (1) The AVX2 f16 path in simd/mod.rs lines 104-112 explicitly bails to scalar to dodge the F16C detection branch, taxing the compressed/tiny presets on x86; stdarch's vcvtph2ps (_mm256_cvtph_ps) converts 8 f16->f32 in one instruction. (2) The int8 path (avx2.rs lines 36-60, neon.rs 68-95) widens i8->i32->f32 then FMAs in f32, which is both slow AND reduction-order-dependent (float horizontal sum is not associative, so the cross-arch parity tests only pass within 1e-4, not bit-exact); ACL/stdarch show vpdpbusd (AVX-VNNI) and vdotq_s32 (NEON dotprod) do 4 int8 MACs/lane into i32 in ONE instruction with reduction-order-INDEPENDENT integer accumulation, which is both ~4x faster on the tiny preset's hot path AND restores true bit-determinism (a nest hard requirement that float reduction currently only approximates). (3) Top-k selection is a full sort_by over all n scored pairs (search.rs lines 128, 213, 260), where x86-simd-sort/Highway's branch-free compressstore partition + select gives a faster, branchless top-k that keeps the mandatory exact-cosine rerank cheap as corpora grow. The int8 codec's 8-byte prefix (payload_version + scale_kind discriminators, int8.rs lines 17-19) confirms asymmetric scale+zero_point quant and sub-byte formats (int4/binary) are genuinely additive — new scale_kind/payload_version values, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump, no new encoding id needed. The deepest structural steal is the witness-token / write-once-generic-kernel pattern (fearless_simd, memchr's Vector trait): nest currently hand-maintains a 3 dtype x 3 ISA matrix of near-duplicate unsafe functions, and every new quantized dtype (int4, bf16, binary) multiplies that matrix; one generic dot_f32<S: Simd> body with thin per-arch shims plus a verified scalar oracle collapses it, keeps files under the 300-line cap, and removes unsafe from the hot path — the enabler for pushing the tiny preset below its current 0.283 ratio without a portability tax. Watch-outs: never adopt faster's compile-time-only dispatch (pins the binary to the build host ISA, breaks the single-portable-offline-binary promise); vendor patterns clean-room rather than depending on experimental crates (fearless_simd is explicitly pre-stable) to protect the frozen-format/determinism guarantees; and the mandatory scalar fallback must remain a first-class verified sibling for sovereign portability to old-x86/RISC-V where the dispatcher drops straight to scalar.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The field has fully converged on "runtime feature dispatch over a write-once generic kernel": compile every kernel variant once (per ISA), detect CPU capability ONCE via getauxval(AT_HWCAP) on aarch64 / CPUID leaf 7 on x86, cache the result lock-free (atomic bitset in stdarch, OnceLock function-pointer in nest/Highway/memchr), then indirect-call the chosen kernel per hot-path entry with zero per-element branch cost. The frontier has moved to TWO refinements nest has not yet adopted. First, FINE-GRAINED feature detection: not just "avx2" but f16c, avxvnni/avx512vnni, aarch64 dotprod/i8mm as SEPARATE gates, because the single most valuable instructions for quantized scoring (vcvtph2ps for f16->f32, vpdpbusd/vdotq_s32 for 4-int8-MACs-into-i32) live behind those finer flags. Second, INTEGER-DOMAIN quantized dot products (ACL's GEMMLowp): accumulate int8*int8 into int32 with hardware dot-product instructions and apply scale/zero_point only at the end, which is both ~4x faster than widen-to-f32-then-FMA AND reduction-order-independent (hence bit-reproducible across CPUs, unlike float horizontal sums). The portable-kernel-authoring frontier is the witness-token pattern (fearless_simd: a ZST type-level proof of an enabled target_feature makes core::arch intrinsics safe to call) and the write-once Vector-trait shim (memchr, Highway, SIMDe's per-function cascade), both of which collapse the NxM (dtype x ISA) unsafe kernel matrix into one generic body. Two reusable SIMD primitives recur as the engine behind everything else: the nibble-LUT-via-byte-shuffle (pshufb/vpshufb/vtbl) for branchless byte classification (simdutf UTF-8 validation at <1 instr/byte, StringZilla's 21 GB/s sz_lookup, base64 codecs), and compressstore/Compress stream-compaction (vpcompressd on AVX-512, table-driven permute-LUT emulation on AVX2, shuffle-table on NEON) for branch-free partition/top-k/filter (x86-simd-sort, Highway vqsort). Correctness discipline has standardized on QEMU/SIMDE_NO_NATIVE differential testing (the scalar path is a verified equivalence sibling, not an afterthought) and stdarch's assert_instr (disassemble the compiled shim to prove the intended instruction was actually emitted). The one anti-pattern the field flags explicitly is compile-time-only width selection (faster, and any -C target-feature global build): it pins the binary to the build host's widest ISA, which is incompatible with shipping one portable offline binary.
top_innovations: Integer-domain int8 dot product via hardware dot-product instructions (ACL GEMMLowp): vpdpbusd (AVX-VNNI) / vdotq_s32 (NEON dotprod) do 4 int8 MACs/lane into int32 in one instruction, scale applied at the end. ~4x faster than nest's i8->i32->f32-widen-then-FMA AND reduction-order-independent, making the tiny preset both fastest AND truly bit-deterministic.

Fine-grained feature gates + single-instruction conversion (stdarch): is_x86_feature_detected!("f16c") -> _mm256_cvtph_ps (8 f16->f32 in one vcvtph2ps); avxvnni/dotprod gates. Fixes the perf gap nest's own mod.rs 104-112 documents.

Witness-token / write-once generic SIMD kernel (fearless_simd + memchr Vector trait): one dot_f32<S: Simd> body per dtype with thin per-arch shims and a verified scalar oracle, collapsing nest's 3x3 unsafe matrix and removing unsafe from the hot path.

Branch-free compressstore stream-compaction (x86-simd-sort + Highway): mask+compressstore for branchless top-k/threshold filter (vpcompressd / AVX2 permute-LUT / NEON shuffle-table), replacing the full sort_by top-k and keeping exact-cosine rerank cheap at scale.
Asymmetric scale+zero_point quantization (ACL): more fidelity per int8 than symmetric max_abs/127, enabling aggressive int4 without recall loss; additive via a new int8 scale_kind discriminator.
Default-value tail padding (faster): pad the final partial vector with the FMA identity so one full-width FMA finishes the dim, removing the hand-written remainder loops and per-query tail branch.
Lane-widening upcast/downcast + vtbl/pshufb bit-unpack (faster + StringZilla): the blueprint for int4 (2 lanes/byte) and binary kernels that push the tiny preset below 0.283.
Nibble-LUT-via-byte-shuffle (simdutf + StringZilla): <1 instr/byte UTF-8 validation before content_hash, plus the primitive for a codepoint-aware bm25 tokenizer that fixes the CJK/Thai gap.
Packed-pair rare-byte prefilter (memchr): allocation-free vectorized term scan over mmapped chunks_canonical for bm25/search-text, and selective prefilters over int8 dimensions.

MinHash/Rabin retrieve-then-rerank sketch (StringZilla): deterministic near-duplicate dedup to drop chunks before encoding (raising ratio) and a candidate pre-filter mirroring nest's HNSW+rerank contract.

Keep the current widen-to-f32 path as the fallback tier. Crucially this also makes int8 scoring reduction-order-independent (integer accumulation), restoring true cross-CPU bit-determinism that the current float-FMA path only approximates.

MinHash/Rabin-fingerprint near-duplicate dedup (StringZilla) drops redundant chunks BEFORE encoding, raising the effective compression ratio on the whole .nest file without any new entropy coder — a deterministic, seeded, reproducible-build-safe win.

Branch-free top-k/compressstore + faster dispatched kernels free up the rerank budget, which is what lets nest AFFORD finer per-block quantization (int4/int8 with SIMD dequant) at serve time without blowing the mandatory exact-cosine rerank latency target — the serve-side headroom that makes harder on-disk compression viable.

Sorted/clustered embeddings (cheap branch-free argsort from x86-simd-sort at build time) improve residual locality, so delta+int8 quantization of reordered rows compresses better — a real but second-order assist for the tiny/compressed presets.

Keeping more NON-embedding sections zstd-compressed is safe for latency because memchr/StringZilla give allocation-free vectorized term/substring scan over decoded text, so bm25/search-text stay fast even with compressed sections — buying ratio on the text side without hurting serve speed.
watch_outs: Do NOT adopt faster's (or any -C target-feature global) compile-time-only width selection: it pins the binary to the build host's widest ISA, directly breaking nest's single-portable-offline-binary promise. Borrow faster's tail-padding/lane-widening kernel tricks ONLY; keep nest's runtime OnceLock function-pointer dispatch, which is strictly better here.

Vendor patterns clean-room, never depend on the experimental crate: fearless_simd is explicitly 'extremely early experimental, no stability guarantees'; a frozen-format, deterministic-build database cannot pin its hot path to a pre-stable dependency. Same for any crate whose codegen could drift and break byte-reproducibility.

Float horizontal-sum reduction is NOT associative, so the current f32/f16/i8-widened paths are only ~1e-4 close across CPUs, not bit-identical — a latent risk to nest's deterministic guarantee if any caller ever hashes or compares raw scores. The integer-domain int8 path (VNNI/dotprod) FIXES this (reduction-order-independent); prefer it precisely for determinism, not just speed.

The mandatory scalar fallback must stay a first-class, parity-verified sibling (SIMDe NO_NATIVE discipline), because nest's dispatcher drops straight to scalar on old x86 / RISC-V / non-NEON ARM — sovereign portability means the scalar path is load-bearing, not an afterthought. Keep it shape-friendly (fixed chunked loops, fixed-width types) so it still auto-vectorizes off-target.

compressstore (vpcompressd) is AVX-512-native and must be permute-LUT-emulated on AVX2 and shuffle-table-emulated on NEON, with a mandatory scalar fallback — the top-k/compress steal is the highest-effort item and only pays once n is large; don't pay its complexity cost prematurely on small corpora.

Any new int8/int4/binary codec must keep the int8 prefix discriminators (payload_version/scale_kind) additive and must NOT touch existing field meanings, or it forces a true v2 NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump. Confirmed safe today: int8.rs lines 17-19 already version the layout. Validate that the writer stays deterministic (same chunks+model => byte-identical) for every new codec.

sse2neon-class semantic gaps are real on the quantized path: _mm_rsqrt_ps(0.0) is NaN on NEON vs INF on SSE, and min/max NaN ordering differs unless PRECISE flags are set. nest's NaN guard runs before rerank (search.rs validate_query lines 28-31) but any new SIMD reduction must preserve identical NaN/rounding behavior across backends or the cross-arch parity tests will (correctly) fail.

Sub-byte and SIMD kernels must not blow the <=300-line-per-file cap or the single-responsibility rule; the witness-token/generic-body refactor is what KEEPS them under the cap, so do that refactor BEFORE multiplying dtypes, not after. A missed #[inline(always)] in that pattern silently de-optimizes the hot loop — gate with assert_instr.

categories.name: serialization-parsing
categories.focus: zero-copy serialization, fast JSON/CSV parsing, mmap-friendly layouts

repos.one_liner: A branch-free two-stage SIMD JSON parser that classifies 64-byte chunks into structural-character bitmasks (stage 1) and materializes a flat 64-bit "tape" or lazily walks values via an On-Demand iterator (stage 2), with runtime CPU feature dispatch across AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/RISC-V.
repos.core_innovation: Separate "find the structure" from "interpret the values": a vectorized branch-free stage-1 pass builds a compact reusable structural index (offsets of all JSON tokens) at GB/s while validating UTF-8, so the semantic parse is either deferred per-accessed-field (On-Demand) or runs as a tight, well-predicted tape build. The structural skeleton is cheap, cacheable, and mmap-friendly.
key_techniques: Two-stage parse: stage 1 = SIMD structural indexing + UTF-8 validation, stage 2 = tape build or lazy On-Demand value walk

Prefix-XOR quote masking via PCLMULQDQ carry-less multiply by -1: turns a quote-position bitmask into an inside-string region mask in one shot; escaped quotes self-cancel by parity, cross-chunk state carried in prev_iter_inside_quote

Branch-free byte classification: AVX2 PCMPEQB / NEON VCEQ over 64-byte chunks producing structural(S)/whitespace(W)/quote(Q)/string-range(R) bitmasks, then S&=~R, W&=~R to drop in-string chars; pseudo-structural starts via P=(S|W)<<1 & ~W & ~R

Flat 64-bit tape in document order: type tag in high byte ('c'<<56)+payload, bidirectional array/object links (open stores closing index + 24-bit child count, close stores opening index) for O(1) container skip
Separate string buffer: each string is a 32-bit LE length header + UTF-8 bytes, main tape holds only an offset, keeping the tape fixed-stride and scannable
On-Demand API: defer number/string/atom validation until a field is accessed via get<T>(), giving 2-4x speedups when reading a subset of a large document
Runtime CPU dispatch: pick fastest compiled kernel (AVX-512/AVX2/SSE4.2/NEON/RISC-V) at load via cpuid, single binary, scalar fallback
Mandatory input padding (SIMDJSON_PADDING) so 64-byte SIMD loads never read past the buffer end
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals, all additive within nest-format v1. (1) STRUCTURAL-INDEX SECTION for JSON/YAML/Parquet-text ingestion: add a stage-1-style SIMD structural indexer in nest-format/src/encoding (new module e.g. structure.rs) that, when nest ingests a JSON/YAML doc into chunks_canonical, also emits a compact little-endian u32 offset index of structural-character positions as an OPTIONAL section (reserved id 0x09+). This reusable mmap-friendly skeleton lets the rust runtime re-walk or sub-cite into nested spans (nest://content_hash/chunk_id#json_pointer) without re-parsing, and the offset index compresses far better than raw text under zstd. (2) TAPE-STYLE OFFSET LAYOUT for chunks_original_spans and future nested-document sections: adopt simdjson's separate-buffer pattern (fixed-stride u64 tape of {type-tag, offset} + side blob with 32-bit LE length headers). Fixed-stride offset tables are mmap-scannable with zero allocation and zstd extremely well because offset deltas are low-entropy. (3) RUNTIME DISPATCH PATTERN: nest-runtime/src/simd already does AVX2/NEON/scalar dot products; lift simdjson's per-kernel-compiled + cpuid-select structure as the template if nest adds a SIMD UTF-8 validator or structural scanner, keeping one scalar fallback. Implement in pure rust (no PCLMULQDQ dependency required; use a portable carry-less/parity scan to stay deterministic and within never-panic/typed-error constraints).
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to the "compress AND serve json/yaml/parquet/datasets" north star. The structural-index/tape split lets nest store a parsed-document skeleton ONCE (low-entropy offset arrays that zstd crushes) while keeping canonical text byte-exact for content_hash stability, and serve sub-document citations and search WITHOUT re-parsing on the hot path. Fixed-stride offset tapes + separate length-prefixed payload buffers are textbook low-entropy, high-zstd-ratio layouts. On-Demand also maps to nest's lazy mmap philosophy: decode only the document subtree a query touches.
repos.perf_notes: Stage 1 ~2-6 GB/s; minification ~6 GB/s; NDJSON ~3.5 GB/s multithreaded; ~75% fewer instructions than RapidJSON. PCLMULQDQ has latency ~6 but reciprocal throughput 1 on Skylake, so schedule independent work to hide latency; a portable rust parity scan trades throughput for full determinism. SIMD loads need buffer padding (read-past-end safety) which nest must replicate for true 64-byte scans off mmap (pad section or bounds-guard the tail chunk). Parser-buffer reuse is the biggest practical win for many small documents.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (parts also MIT/Boost); permissive, safe to vendor or reimplement the algorithms.

repos.one_liner: A Rust port of simdjson that parses JSON at multi-GB/s by splitting parsing into a SIMD stage1 (branchless structural-character indexing over 64-byte chunks) and a stage2 that walks that index to emit a flat u64 "tape", with zero-copy BorrowedValue referencing the input buffer.
repos.core_innovation: Two-stage parsing: stage1 uses SIMD to classify every byte in bulk (whitespace/structural via pshufb lookup tables) and resolves string interiors with a branchless prefix-XOR quote mask computed by carry-less multiply (PCLMULQDQ / vmull_p64) of the quote-bit vector against all-ones, then ANDs the complement to drop in-string structurals. The result is a dense index of "where things are" so stage2 is near-branchless and data-driven. The transferable kernel: turn a per-byte stateful scan (classification, region-membership, delimiter finding) into a wide bitmask computation, carrying one parity bit between chunks.
key_techniques: prefix-XOR quote masking via carry-less multiply (PCLMULQDQ on x86, vmull_p64 on NEON) of the quote-bit vector by all-ones, carrying 1 parity bit across 64-byte chunks
pshufb/shuffle as a 16-entry lookup table to classify bytes into whitespace vs structural ({}[]:,) categories in parallel, producing bitmasks
branchless masking: AND(structural_mask, NOT(in_string_mask)) to exclude delimiters inside strings with no branches
flat u64 tape: a single Vec where each element packs a type tag in high bits + offset/length payload; the tree is indices into one contiguous buffer (no pointer chasing, mmap-friendly)
BorrowedValue zero-copy: string and key slices reference the input buffer directly instead of allocating per-token
SWAR 8-digits-at-a-time number parsing via one 64-bit multiply-add chain behind a feature flag
SIMD UTF-8 validation fused into the scan pass instead of a separate post-pass
runtime CPU feature detection selecting AVX2/SSE4.2/NEON/simd128/scalar fallback at dispatch time
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals. (1) bm25 tokenizer at nest-runtime/src/bm25/tokenize.rs is today a scalar per-char loop (is_alphanumeric + to_lowercase) which is the documented CJK/Thai gap and slow on big corpora; adapt simd-json's stage1 byte-classification to build a word-boundary bitmask (ASCII alnum vs separator) over UTF-8 bytes for fast Latin chunk-splitting with a scalar fallback for non-ASCII codepoints, wired through the existing dispatcher in nest-runtime/src/simd/{avx2,neon,scalar}.rs that already does AVX2/NEON/scalar selection. (2) The flat-tape idea maps onto a future structured-data ingest path (json/yaml/parquet on the north-star roadmap): store parsed docs as a contiguous repr(C) u64 tape (tag-in-high-bits + LE offset/length) as a new RESERVED section id (0x09+) in nest-format/src/sections, giving mmap-able, pointer-free, zero-copy reopen aligned with content_hash determinism. (3) BorrowedValue zero-copy discipline reinforces the chunks_original_spans model and the materialize path in nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs (parse-by-reference into the mmap, never materialize eagerly). The prefix-XOR carry-less-multiply parity trick is also a reusable region-detection kernel for future CSV/JSONL delimiter scanning in the SIMD crate.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect to raw ratio: simd-json is a speed play, not a compressor, so it does not shrink bytes directly. But it unlocks the north-star "compress AND serve json/yaml/parquet" goal by providing a fast, deterministic, mmap-friendly, pointer-free on-disk parse representation (the flat u64 tape) that can be zstd-compressed as a non-embedding section while remaining cheaply re-scannable. It also accelerates the bm25 build/query hot path (a known throughput gap), serving the light/cheap pillar even though it does not move the size ratio.
repos.perf_notes: simdjson family hits multi-GB/s on commodity x86; stage1 processes 64 input bytes per iteration as bitmasks. PCLMULQDQ is high-latency (~6 cycles on Skylake) but reciprocal-throughput ~1, so simd-json hides it by scheduling independent work after it — relevant if nest adopts the carry-less-multiply trick. pshufb classification and prefix-XOR are the throughput wins; SWAR number parsing avoids per-digit branches. The flat-Vec tape avoids per-node heap allocs and pointer chasing, matching the cache/mmap profile nest wants. nest constraints: gate any carry-less-multiply behind runtime detection with a scalar fallback (mirrors nest's existing avx2/neon/scalar dispatcher) and keep all on-disk tape integers little-endian.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 / MIT dual (Rust ecosystem standard; upstream simdjson is Apache-2.0). Compatible for vendoring or learning into nest.

repos.one_liner: A serialization framework that decouples N Rust data structures from M wire formats through a fixed 29-type abstract data model, with compile-time monomorphized derive codegen (no reflection, no intermediate Value tree) and lifetime-parameterized zero-copy deserialization (Deserialize<'de>) that borrows &str/&[u8] directly out of the input buffer.
repos.core_innovation: The visitor/data-model split that turns the NxM serialization problem into N+M: every type maps itself to one of 29 abstract model types via a Serializer trait, and every format implements that model once. Crucially for nest, the deserialize side is lifetime-parameterized (Deserialize<'de> with visit_borrowed_str returning &'de str) so decoded values are borrowed views into the source bytes with zero allocation and zero copy when the encoding permits it. This is exactly the discipline nest needs: a section decoder that returns borrowed slices straight off the mmap rather than owned Vecs.
key_techniques: 29-type abstract data model (bool, i8..i128, u8..u128, f32/f64, char, string, byte array, option, unit, unit_struct, unit_variant, newtype_struct, newtype_variant, seq, tuple, tuple_struct, tuple_variant, map, struct, struct_variant) decoupling N types from M formats into N+M impls
Visitor pattern: Deserializer drives a Visitor by calling exactly one visit_* method; struct keys known at compile time avoid map-style key hashing

Zero-copy via Deserialize<'de> lifetime + visit_borrowed_str(&'de str)/visit_borrowed_bytes vs transient visit_str/visit_string vs owned visit_string; Cow<'de, str> to fall back to owned only when escapes force it
Monomorphized compile-time codegen (serde_derive): static dispatch only, no vtables, no reflection, no intermediate Value tree, no per-field allocation
Three-phase compound encoding (serialize_struct/seq/map -> serialize_field/element -> end()) letting formats stream output without buffering the whole structure
DeserializeSeed / stateful deserialization: thread external state (arenas, interners, capacity hints) through the deserialize call without globals
Length-aware vs length-free distinction: structs/tuples carry compile-time-known arity so the format can omit length prefixes; maps/seqs carry runtime length
repos.nest_application: nest-format/src/sections/codec.rs and the per-section reader (crates/nest-format/src/reader/**) should adopt a borrowed decode trait: SectionDecode<'a> returning views (&'a [u8], &'a str, &'a [f32]) sliced directly from the mmap'd byte range instead of owned buffers. This is the single biggest lever for nest's 'serve straight off disk' promise -- chunks_canonical(text) and embeddings (raw/f16) can be returned as borrowed slices with zero allocation, mirroring nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs which already wants to hand back spans. Concretely: (1) add a content_view(section_id) -> Cow<'a, [u8]> on the reader where raw/f16/int8 encodings return Borrowed and only zstd returns Owned (decompression unavoidably allocates) -- this makes the borrow-vs-copy decision encoding-driven exactly like serde's visit_borrowed_str-vs-visit_string; (2) refactor encoding/mod.rs Encoding enum into a small visitor-style codec registry where each encoding id (raw/zstd/float16/int8) implements one decode(&[u8]) -> view method, keeping the additive encoding-id space (4-255 reserved) clean and each codec file under the 300-line cap; (3) thread a DeserializeSeed-style state param (out-buffer / scratch reused across calls) through int8 dequant in encoding/int8.rs so per-query embedding decode reuses one allocation instead of allocating per chunk on the hot search path in nest-runtime/src/search.rs. Do NOT pull in the serde crate itself for the frozen container -- the format is repr(C) little-endian and must stay dependency-light and byte-deterministic; steal the design patterns (borrowed-view codec, encoding-driven Cow, the N+M codec/section separation), not the dependency. serde_json/serde_yaml/serde_cbor ARE worth a real dependency only in nest-python or a build-time ingest path for parsing input json/yaml/parquet-adjacent sources before they become canonical chunks.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. serde is not a compressor and adds no entropy coding, so it does not advance the 'compress more than everyone' north star directly. Its relevance is to the SERVE half of compress-and-serve: zero-copy borrowed decoding lets nest keep aggressive encodings (int8, f16, zstd) while still materializing text/vectors at near-zero cost off mmap, so compression does not cost runtime allocation. The encoding-driven Cow pattern (borrow when raw/f16/int8, copy only when zstd) is the right architectural seam to add MORE codecs later (delta/varint/bitpacking for chunk_ids and spans, dictionary coding) without rewriting every section reader -- it makes the codec layer extensible, which is a prerequisite for pushing the compression frontier.
repos.perf_notes: serde's performance comes entirely from monomorphization + static dispatch: the derive generates a straight-line specialized function per type, so there is no vtable, no boxing, and the optimizer can inline the whole serialize/deserialize path. Zero-copy deserialization eliminates the dominant cost in real workloads (string/byte allocation and memcpy) -- serde_json borrows &'de str directly when no JSON escapes are present, falling back to owned only on escaped strings. No SIMD in serde core itself (some downstream JSON parsers like simd-json add it). For nest the lesson is: a borrowed-slice decode path keeps the SIMD dot-product hot loop (nest-runtime/src/simd) reading f32/int8 lanes straight from mmap with zero intervening copy, which is exactly the current design intent -- adopting serde's view discipline guarantees no accidental owning allocation creeps into the rerank/materialize path.
repos.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual-licensed)

repos.one_liner: A zero-copy cross-platform serialization library whose buffers are read in place (mmap-friendly) via a vtable indirection scheme, plus a schema-less sibling format (FlexBuffers) that auto-narrows every scalar/container to the smallest of 8/16/32/64-bit widths and pools strings/keys.
repos.core_innovation: Random-access read directly off raw bytes (no parse, no allocation, no copy) achieved through a layer of relative offsets plus a shared, deduplicated vtable: many records with identical field layout point at ONE vtable, so per-record metadata cost amortizes to near zero. The complementary FlexBuffers idea — encode each element at the minimum bit-width that fits its value and pool repeated strings/keys — is a self-describing, mmap-readable layout that is often smaller than a typed format while still allowing O(1) indexed access via a parallel width-tagged offset table.
key_techniques: vtable indirection: each table starts with a soffset to a vtable [vtable_size, object_size, field_offset_0..N]; absent field => offset 0 => return schema default (free optionality, no presence bitmap)
vtable deduplication/sharing: records with the same present-field set reference one identical vtable, so N homogeneous rows cost 1 vtable not N

three offset widths: uoffset_t (u32 forward to tables/vectors/strings), soffset_t (signed, vtable backref), voffset_t (u16 field slot), little-endian, self-relative so buffers are position-independent and DAG-shareable
shared subobjects via offset reuse: identical strings/vectors/subtables stored once and pointed to by multiple parents (string pooling / structural dedup) without a back-reference table
FlexBuffers minimum-width packing: a 1-byte type+bitwidth tag per value lets each int/float/offset use 8/16/32/64 bits, eliminating fixed-width padding on small values
FlexBuffers vectors carry a length prefix + a parallel array of equal-width offsets, enabling O(1) random indexing into a schema-less, mmap-resident blob
size-prefixed buffers + 4-byte file identifier magic for streaming framing and cheap type/format sniffing without a full header parse
build-backward construction (high to low address) so child offsets are known before parents are written, giving single-pass serialization with no fixups
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals into nest-format. (1) Offset-table layout for variable-length sections: today crates/nest-format/src/sections/{chunk_ids,canonical,spans}.rs write a count prefix then a flat run of length-prefixed strings, which forces a sequential scan to reach chunk N and gives no random access off mmap. Adapt FlatBuffers' uoffset vector: prepend a u32 (or width-narrowed) offset array so nest-runtime materialize/cite can jump to chunk N in O(1) directly from the mapped page without decoding earlier strings, the read-side enabler for nest://content_hash/chunk_id byte-span reopen. (2) Apply FlexBuffers minimum-width thinking as a new additive encoding id (reserved 4-255 space, no version bump) for the structural/metadata sections only: store per-chunk offset/length integers and provenance ints at the smallest width that fits (delta + varint or fixed 8/16/32-bit pick), shrinking non-embedding overhead at zero decode cost on the hot path. Most impactful for chunk_ids: stop storing sha256 as the 71-byte ASCII string 'sha256:<64 hex>'; store the 32 raw digest bytes (a 2.2x shrink before zstd) and reconstruct the prefix on read, a pure entropy win toward 'compress more than everyone'. Keep embeddings untouched (still scored from mmap). The vtable-default trick also informs provenance: omit absent optional fields and resolve to defaults rather than storing nulls. All of this respects single-file, offline, deterministic (offset tables are a pure function of inputs) and the additive format rule.
repos.compression_relevance: Direct. Two distinct wins: (a) the sha256 raw-bytes-vs-hex-string fix is an immediate ~2.2x reduction on the chunk_ids section pre-zstd and removes redundant 'sha256:' prefixes, pure entropy reduction. (b) FlexBuffers-style minimum-width integer packing trims structural/offset/provenance overhead with zero hot-path decode cost, complementing zstd which nest already applies to non-embedding sections. The offset-table idea is compression-neutral but unlocks O(1) mmap random access that nest's cite/materialize path currently lacks, strategically required to serve compressed corpora without full-section decode.
repos.perf_notes: Zero-copy reads: field access is one vtable lookup + one bounds check + one load, no allocation, no temp objects, good cache locality, ideal for mmap. All integers little-endian aligned to their own size; structs align to largest member (compiler-independent) so a memory-mapped struct can be cast and read in place on x86_64/aarch64 without misaligned-access penalties, matching nest's repr(C) + LE-unsigned discipline. Tradeoffs: FlexBuffers is slower to read than typed FlatBuffers (per-element type/width tag dispatch) and FlatBuffers trades some size for alignment padding; nest should apply min-width packing only to cold structural sections, never the embedding hot path. No SIMD in the format itself, it is a layout/encoding library, not a kernel.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A Rust single-writer/multi-reader IPC library that combines rkyv zero-copy archives with a tmpfs-backed mmap double-buffer and a wait-free RCU/Left-Right swap protocol so readers parse data in-place off the mmap with no locks and no copy.
repos.core_innovation: A 64-bit packed atomic InstanceVersion (1 bit active-instance index, 39 bits data size up to 549 GB, 24 bits truncated WyHash checksum) lets a writer atomically publish a new mmap'd buffer with a single SeqCst store while readers do wait-free zero-copy access; per-instance AtomicU32 reader counters plus a grace_duration timeout drain in-flight readers off the idle buffer before it is reused (and forcibly reset to handle crashed readers), giving lock-free publish-then-swap without ever blocking the read path.
key_techniques: InstanceVersion: pack {idx:1 | size:39 | checksum:24} into one u64 via mask/shift, swapped with a single AtomicU64 SeqCst store (RCU/Left-Right publish)
Double-buffer of two mmap data files plus a 3rd state file; writer always writes the idle buffer then flips the active index
Per-instance [AtomicU32;2] reader counters: rlock=fetch_add(1,SeqCst), unlock=fetch_sub(1,SeqCst); writer waits for idle count==0
grace_duration drain: poll-sleep until idle reader count hits 0, else store(0) to reclaim from crashed/stalled readers (reset=true)
rkyv 0.7 zero-copy archives: serialize_value then archived_root::<T>/check_archived_root::<T> to read structs straight off mmap with no deserialize step
24-bit truncated WyHash checksum embedded in the version word for cheap optional integrity validation on read (40ns checked vs 27ns unchecked)
RAII ReadGuard holds the reader-count increment and decrements on Drop, making reader bookkeeping leak-proof
tmpfs (/dev/shm) backing to drop mmap I/O latency to RAM speed
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals. (1) nest-runtime: adopt rkyv-style zero-copy archived structs as the in-memory view of mmap'd sections (chunk_ids, provenance, search_contract, hnsw/bm25 index nodes) so the reader casts repr(C) LE bytes to typed structs with zero parse cost on open, formalizing nest's existing mmap-cast pattern in nest-format reader.rs and nest-runtime materialize; nest's repr(C)/little-endian invariants already match rkyv's archived-layout discipline. (2) Bigger steal: the InstanceVersion + double-buffer + grace-period drain protocol as the foundation for nest's missing real-time edit / hot-reload. Keep the FROZEN .nest v1 container immutable but add an optional local atomic-version sidecar in nest-runtime so a rebuilt container is published and queried wait-free while old readers finish on the previous mmap; the 24-bit-checksum-in-version trick gives O(1) integrity gating per swap. Must stay offline/single-file: implement as an in-process atomic-swap layer, never a socket, and outside the frozen format. The packed-version u64 idiom also informs encoding size+checksum+epoch in one LE manifest/footer word.
repos.compression_relevance: Low and indirect. mmap-sync does not compress (pins rkyv 0.7 raw aligned archives, no entropy coder, no quantization), so it does not advance the 'compress more than everyone' north star directly. Its value is to the SERVE half: it shows the canonical zero-copy mmap layout that exposes decoded sections (and never-compressed embeddings scored straight off disk) as typed structs at tens of nanoseconds, and its version-word checksum is a model for compactly embedding integrity metadata. Enables fast/real-time edit and concurrent serving (stated mission goals) without touching the codec stack.
repos.perf_notes: i7-13800H: write 250.7 ns (3.96 Melem/s), read with WyHash checksum validation 40.1 ns (24.9 Melem/s), read without validation 26.7 ns (37.5 Melem/s). All atomics SeqCst (conservative; nest could relax to Acquire/Release on the read fast path). Single-writer/multi-reader only. tmpfs backing keeps latency at RAM speed; 39-bit size field caps a single buffer at 549 GB.
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause (Cloudflare standard OSS)

repos.one_liner: A schema-less, append-only, single-file binary storage engine whose payloads are 64-byte-aligned for cache/SIMD efficiency, indexed by an in-memory xxh3_64 -> offset map, recoverable by a backward-linked metadata chain, and read fully zero-copy straight off mmap.
repos.core_innovation: The "metadata-after-payload backward-linked chain" on-disk layout: each entry stores its payload first, then a trailing fixed metadata block (key_hash, prev_offset, crc32c). Because every entry points back to the previous entry's tail, the whole keyspace and index are reconstructible by scanning from EOF backward to byte 0, and any torn/incomplete tail write is auto-discarded by stopping at the last unbroken link. This gives crash-safe, index-free-on-disk recovery with a single sequential append being the only write path, and 64-byte payload alignment so reads are zero-copy reinterpretable as typed SIMD slices.
key_techniques: 64-byte payload alignment via pad = (A - (prev_tail % A)) & (A-1), A=64, so every payload start lands on a cacheline/SIMD boundary for safe &[u8]->&[f32] reinterpretation
trailing metadata block per entry: 8B xxh3_64 key hash + 8B prev_offset (absolute tail of prior entry) + 4B crc32c payload checksum, forming a backward-traversable linked chain
index-free-on-disk: in-memory DashMap<u64,u64> (key_hash -> offset) rebuilt by backward chain scan at open; newest-wins so updates/deletes are pure appends
1-byte tombstone (0x00 payload) plus same 20B metadata trailer for O(1) logical deletes without rewriting
torn-write recovery: load stops at last validly-linked+checksummed entry, truncating partial tails automatically
lock-free parallel reads off a shared Arc<Mmap>, Mutex/RwLock only guards remap-on-grow, AtomicU64 tail pointer
EntryHandle: zero-copy &[u8] view into the mmap region, optionally reinterpreted as Apache Arrow arrays via arrow feature for columnar typed access
explicit compaction replays newest-per-key into a fresh file to reclaim dead/tombstoned space
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) nest-format reader recovery: nest v1 has 4 SHA-256 surfaces and a pre-footer body, but recovery from a truncated/partially-written container is a weak spot for a single-file format. Adopt the backward "stop at last valid section" scan as an additive validate mode in nest-format/src/reader (surfaced via nest-cli `validate`): walk sections from the footer backward, verify each per-section checksum, and report the last intact section boundary without trusting the manifest. Additive (no format bump), hardens the offline single-file guarantee against torn writes. (2) nest-format/src/layout + nest-runtime hot path: enforce and verify 64-byte alignment on the embeddings section so the mmap'd f32/f16/int8 vectors can be reinterpreted as typed SIMD slices with zero bounds/alignment fixups before AVX2/NEON dot products. nest scores embeddings directly from mmap and must never zstd them; guaranteeing 64-byte payload alignment is the missing precondition that lets the simd dispatcher do aligned loads (vmovaps vs vmovups) without a copy. The pad formula pad=(64-(off%64))&63 drops straight into the writer's section placement and stays deterministic/reproducible.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. The engine does NO compression (raw bytes, schema-less), so it does not advance the "compress more than everyone" north star directly. Its compression relevance is structural: 64-byte alignment plus zero-copy typed reinterpretation is the precondition that lets you keep embeddings UNCOMPRESSED yet serve them at full SIMD speed (validating nest's "never zstd embeddings" choice), and the append-only newest-wins chain is a substrate for real-time edit (a north-star feature nest lacks) without rewriting the whole container. The companion rust-llkv project (Arrow columnar chunks over simd-r-drive EntryHandles) is the more compression-relevant idea: column-oriented chunking enables per-column encodings (dictionary, RLE, delta) which is where extreme compression of json/parquet/datasets actually comes from.
repos.perf_notes: xxh3_64 key hashing uses SSE2 (default x86_64) / AVX2 / NEON; benchmark cited at ~1M random 8-byte seeks in well under 1s. crc32fast (CRC32C, hardware SSE4.2 crc32 instr) for payload integrity, NOT SHA, much cheaper than nest's per-section SHA-256 but non-cryptographic; nest must keep SHA for its citation/integrity surfaces, but CRC32C is a candidate for a cheap fast-path liveness check during streaming edits. Reads are lock-free off Arc<Mmap>; only file-growth remap takes a lock. simd_copy accelerates the write-side memcpy into the append buffer. Datasets larger than RAM via mmap paging.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (per crates.io publication of simd-r-drive); verify before vendoring, compatible with permissive reuse.

repos.one_liner: A header-only C++17 CSV reader/writer that mmaps the whole file and lazily iterates cells via memchr-driven newline scans plus a branchy scalar quote state machine, hitting ~1 GB/s zero-copy without materializing the dataset.
repos.core_innovation: Treat the on-disk byte buffer as the only data structure: never copy, never pre-tokenize. Iteration is fully lazy and offset-based -- a RowIterator finds the next row with one memchr('\n') call, and CellIterator only computes a cell's [start,end) span at deref time, returning a string_view straight into the mmap. The parsed "table" is just two cursors over bytes you already paid to map; cell values are decoded (unescape/trim) on demand, so unread columns cost nothing.
key_techniques: memchr-based row scan: locate next \n in the mmap region with one libc SIMD-accelerated memchr call instead of a byte loop
Lazy offset-only cell boundaries: CellIterator stores start_/end_ and computes the next delimiter span on deref, returning string_view (zero allocation, zero copy)
Branchy scalar quote state machine: quote_opened flag + last_quote_location==i-1 test detects doubled-quote escapes; delimiter ignored while inside quotes
Compile-time dialect via templates: delimiter<','>, quote_character<'"'>, first_row_is_header<>, trim_policy -- monomorphized so the hot loop has no runtime config branches
mmap-the-whole-file zero-copy I/O via the bundled header-only mio wrapper (page-aligned, cross-platform POSIX/Windows, MIT)
Decode-on-demand value path: read_view() returns raw span; read_value() applies trim+unescape only when the caller wants the string
Naive append-only Writer: ostream_iterator + delimiter concatenation, no quoting/escaping by design (caller owns CSV-safety)
repos.nest_application: Two concrete lifts. (1) nest-runtime materialize path + nest-cli: adopt csv2's lazy-offset cursor model for any row/columnar section we mmap. Today nest scores embeddings off mmap; csv2 proves we can also serve text-table payloads (csv/tsv/dataset rows the north-star wants to ingest) as &str slices into the mapped file with zero decode until a row is cited, mirroring our chunks_canonical/chunks_original_spans span discipline. (2) Ingestion-side tokenizer in nest-python build: replace any byte-by-byte CSV/field scanner with the Rust memchr crate (already SIMD on AVX2/NEON, deterministic) for row splitting, plus a small monomorphized delimiter/quote state machine instead of regex -- speeds import of the PT-BR fake-news corpora and future parquet/json/yaml dataset fronts. The decode-on-demand idea also reinforces nest-format: store cheap text columns as raw offset spans (like chunks_original_spans) so zstd table sections decompress lazily per accessed cell rather than whole-section, leaving the embedding hot path untouched.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect. csv2 is a speed/zero-copy parser, not a compressor -- no entropy coder, no quantization, no columnar dictionary encoding, so it does not advance 'compress more than everyone' directly. Its value is structural: the lazy-offset, decode-on-demand discipline lets a zstd-compressed table section in nest-format be unpacked one cell/row at a time rather than wholesale, lowering working-set memory during ingest and preserving the mmap-friendly layout all of nest's encodings depend on. It teaches layout-for-compression, not a new codec.
repos.perf_notes: ~0.9-1.0 GB/s sustained cell iteration on an i9-11900KF (16 GB file in 16.5s; 11 GB / 262M rows in 10.8s). No explicit SIMD intrinsics in csv2 itself -- throughput comes from glibc memchr (hand-vectorized SSE/AVX), zero per-row/cell allocation, and template monomorphization stripping config branches from the inner loop. Footprint is essentially page cache for the mapped file plus two cursor structs; no parse tree, no row vector. Quote handling is fully scalar/branchy, so quote-heavy CSVs lose throughput -- a ceiling a true SIMD parser (simdcsv / Mison structural-index bitmaps) would beat.
repos.license: MIT (csv2 and the bundled mio mmap header are both MIT)

synthesis.summary: The seven repos cluster into two complementary disciplines nest must master to deliver its "compress AND serve json/yaml/parquet/datasets" north star: (1) zero-copy/mmap LAYOUT (serde borrowed-view codecs, FlatBuffers offset-tables + vtable dedup + FlexBuffers min-width packing, rkyv archived-struct casts via mmap-sync, simd-r-drive 64-byte alignment + backward-link recovery, csv2 lazy-offset cursors) and (2) SIMD STRUCTURAL PARSING (simdjson/simd-json two-stage parse: branch-free bitmask classification + prefix-XOR quote masking into a fixed-stride u64 tape). Grounding against the actual code: nest already has the right bones — decode_payload returns Cow (serde-style borrow vs copy), SECTION_ALIGNMENT=64 is declared in layout/mod.rs, Int8EmbeddingsView borrows rows zero-copy, and the simd dispatcher uses OnceLock+cpuid exactly like simdjson's runtime dispatch. The gaps the extracts target are real and verifiable in-tree: chunk_ids stores 71-byte ASCII "sha256:<64hex>" strings (sections/chunk_ids.rs) instead of 32 raw bytes; chunk_ids/canonical/spans are sequential length-prefixed strings with NO offset table so reaching chunk N is O(n) (sections/spans.rs, canonical.rs); materialize_f32_vectors allocates n*dim*4 per call even though a borrowed int8 view exists; and the bm25 tokenizer is a scalar per-char loop (bm25/tokenize.rs), the documented CJK/Thai gap. The highest-value, lowest-risk steals are pure-data-layout wins that move the size ratio with zero hot-path cost and respect the additive-only v1 contract (new encoding ids 4-255, new section ids 0x09+, never re-meaning an existing field). The tape/structural-index ideas are the strategic bridge to ingesting and sub-citing structured documents, but they are bigger and should land behind the layout wins.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: State of the art in serialization-parsing for an mmap-first embedded DB is a clean separation of "find the structure" from "interpret the values," with the structure stored once as a low-entropy, fixed-stride, position-independent offset table that is cheap to mmap, cheap to zstd, and supports O(1) random access. simdjson/simd-json define the parse frontier: a branch-free SIMD stage-1 classifies 64-byte chunks into structural/whitespace/quote bitmasks, resolves string interiors with a single prefix-XOR carry-less-multiply (parity bit carried across chunks), validates UTF-8 in the same pass at 2-6 GB/s, then emits a flat u64 tape (type-tag in high bits + offset/length payload, container links for O(1) skip) with strings in a separate length-prefixed blob; On-Demand defers per-field decode for 2-4x on partial reads. The layout frontier is set by FlatBuffers (vtable indirection with deduplicated vtables so N homogeneous rows cost one vtable; self-relative u32/u16 offsets making buffers position-independent and DAG-shareable; absent-field-as-default needs no presence bitmap) and FlexBuffers (per-value width tag narrowing every scalar to 8/16/32/64 bits + pooled strings/keys, often smaller than a typed format while keeping O(1) indexed access). serde sets the API frontier: an N+M data-model split with lifetime-parameterized Deserialize<'de> that returns &'de str/&[u8] borrowed straight out of the input, falling back to owned (Cow) only when escapes force it — monomorphized, no reflection, no intermediate Value tree. rkyv (via cloudflare mmap-sync) and simd-r-drive push the zero-copy-read extreme: cast repr(C) LE bytes to typed archived structs with no deserialize step, read in tens of nanoseconds, with 64-byte payload alignment so &[u8] reinterprets directly as SIMD &[f32]; mmap-sync adds a packed-u64 {index|size|checksum} version word for wait-free RCU publish/swap, and simd-r-drive adds a backward-linked metadata chain for index-free, torn-write-safe recovery. csv2 shows the lazy-offset endpoint: the mmap'd buffer IS the data structure, cells are [start,end) spans computed at deref, unread columns cost nothing. The consensus lesson for nest: keep canonical text byte-exact (content_hash stability), store all derived structure as separate fixed-stride little-endian offset/tape arrays (low-entropy, zstd-friendly, mmap-scannable), decode by borrowed reference, and gate any SIMD kernel behind cpuid with a deterministic scalar fallback.
top_innovations: FlatBuffers/FlexBuffers compact integer encoding for cold metadata: store sha256 as 32 raw bytes not 71-byte ASCII 'sha256:<64hex>' (~2.2x pre-zstd on chunk_ids), and min-width/delta+varint pack offsets, lengths and provenance ints. Pure entropy reduction, zero hot-path decode cost, fully deterministic — the single highest size/effort ratio in the category.

FlatBuffers uoffset offset-table layout for variable-length sections: prepend a u32 (or width-narrowed) offset array to chunk_ids/canonical/spans so cite/materialize jumps to chunk N in O(1) off the mapped page instead of the current O(n) sequential length-prefixed scan. Compression-neutral but the structural enabler for serving compressed corpora and nest://content_hash/chunk_id byte-span reopen.

serde borrowed-view codec discipline (Deserialize<'de> / visit_borrowed_str / Cow): make the section decode path return &'a [u8]/&'a str/&'a [f32] borrowed from mmap, copying only when zstd forces it. nest already does this for embeddings via decode_payload->Cow; extend it to text sections and kill the per-call n*dim*4 allocation in materialize_f32_vectors by threading a reused scratch buffer (serde DeserializeSeed pattern).

simdjson two-stage parse with a fixed-stride u64 tape + separate length-prefixed string blob: the on-disk representation for ingested json/yaml as a new RESERVED section (0x09+). Low-entropy offset arrays that zstd crushes, mmap-scannable, pointer-free, enabling sub-document citation (nest://content_hash/chunk_id#json_pointer) without re-parsing on the hot path.

simdjson/simd-json branch-free SIMD byte classification + prefix-XOR parity scan as a reusable region/delimiter kernel: powers a SIMD bm25 word-boundary tokenizer (fixing the scalar per-char CJK/Thai gap in bm25/tokenize.rs) and future CSV/JSONL delimiter scanning, wired through the existing avx2/neon/scalar dispatcher. Implement portable (no PCLMULQDQ dependency) to stay deterministic.

rkyv/mmap-sync archived-struct zero-copy reads: formalize nest's mmap-cast of repr(C) LE structs (header, section table, hnsw/bm25 nodes) as typed views with no parse step, tens-of-ns open. nest's repr(C)+LE invariants already match the archived-layout discipline.

simd-r-drive 64-byte payload-alignment guarantee + verification on read: nest declares SECTION_ALIGNMENT=64 but does not verify it on the embeddings section at open; verifying it is the missing precondition for aligned SIMD loads (vmovaps vs vmovups) with zero copy/bounds fixups on the dot-product hot path.

simd-r-drive backward-linked 'stop at last valid section' recovery scan as an additive nest-cli validate mode: walk sections from the footer backward, verify each per-section SHA-256, report the last intact boundary without trusting the manifest — hardens the single-file/offline guarantee against torn writes, no format bump.

mmap-sync packed-u64 version word {index|size|checksum} + double-buffer RCU swap as the substrate for nest's missing real-time edit/hot-reload: publish a rebuilt container and query it wait-free while old mmap readers drain, implemented as an in-process atomic-swap sidecar OUTSIDE the frozen format (never a socket).

FlexBuffers/FlatBuffers self-relative offsets + structural dedup (shared substrings/vtables): store a repeated source_uri in chunks_original_spans once and reference it by offset (most spans share one source doc), and resolve absent optional provenance fields to defaults instead of storing nulls.

nest_recommendations.idea: Store chunk ids as 32 raw SHA-256 digest bytes instead of the 71-byte ASCII string 'sha256:<64 hex>'. Reconstruct the 'sha256:' prefix and hex on decode. This is an additive encoding change to the chunk_ids section payload (or a new encoding id in the 4-255 reserved space), not a format-version bump, and is a pure function of inputs so determinism/reproducibility hold.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/chunk_ids.rs (encode_chunk_ids/decode_chunk_ids); add a 16/32-bit width tag in the 12-byte SECTION_PAYLOAD_PREFIX or a new SECTION_ENCODING_* id in layout/mod.rs. content_hash in reader/decode.rs must hash the canonical decoded representation so citations stay stable across the encoding switch.
nest_recommendations.impact: ~2.2x reduction on chunk_ids section before zstd, plus removal of the redundant per-id 'sha256:' prefix; direct entropy win toward 'compress more than everyone' on every corpus with zero hot-path cost.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a u32 (width-narrowed where possible) offset table at the head of variable-length sections (chunk_ids, chunks_canonical, chunks_original_spans) so reaching chunk N is O(1) off the mapped page instead of an O(n) sequential scan of length-prefixed strings. Offsets are self-relative/section-local and little-endian; offset deltas are low-entropy and zstd-friendly.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/{chunk_ids,canonical,spans}.rs encode/decode; consumed by crates/nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs and the cite path (nest-cli/src/cmd/cite.rs) to jump directly to chunk N for nest://content_hash/chunk_id reopen.
nest_recommendations.impact: Unlocks O(1) random-access materialize/cite off compressed corpora (currently must decode earlier chunks first); compression-neutral but a structural prerequisite for serving large compressed datasets and sub-citation.

nest_recommendations.idea: Eliminate the per-call n*dim*4 f32 allocation in the materialize/ANN path by threading a reusable scratch out-buffer through dequant (serde DeserializeSeed-style state param), and return borrowed &[f32]/&[i8] views where the dtype permits (raw f32 and int8 already borrow via Int8EmbeddingsView; only zstd/f16 conversions need to own).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs (materialize_f32_vectors reallocates vec![0.0f32; n*dim] every call) and crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs; mirror the encoding-driven borrow-vs-copy already in nest-format/src/encoding/mod.rs decode_payload (Cow).
nest_recommendations.impact: Removes hot-path allocation on repeated search/ANN-build calls, serving the light/cheap pillar; lets aggressive int8/f16 encodings cost zero runtime allocation, keeping the SIMD dot-product loop reading lanes straight from mmap.

nest_recommendations.idea: Replace the scalar per-char bm25 tokenizer with a SIMD word-boundary scanner: classify ASCII alnum vs separator bytes into a bitmask over 64-byte chunks (simdjson stage-1 style) for fast Latin splitting, with a scalar fallback for non-ASCII codepoints. Use a portable carry-less/parity scan (no PCLMULQDQ dependency) to stay deterministic.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/tokenize.rs (currently a char-by-char is_alphanumeric loop), wired through the existing crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/{avx2,neon,scalar}.rs OnceLock+cpuid dispatcher.
nest_recommendations.impact: Speeds bm25 build/query on large corpora (a documented throughput gap) and is the seam to later improve CJK/Thai segmentation; serves the cheap/light pillar without touching size ratio.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an additive backward 'stop at last valid section' recovery mode to validate: walk the section table from the footer backward, verify each per-section SHA-256, and report the last intact section boundary without trusting the manifest, so a torn/partially-written .nest is recoverable up to the last good section.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/reader/validate.rs and crates/nest-format/src/manifest/validate.rs, surfaced via crates/nest-cli/src/cmd/validate.rs. Additive, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump.
nest_recommendations.impact: Hardens the single-file/offline guarantee against crashes/torn writes (current weak spot for a single-file format with 4 SHA surfaces but no partial-recovery path); reuses existing per-section checksums.

nest_recommendations.idea: Verify (not just declare) 64-byte alignment of the embeddings section payload at reader open, and assert it so the SIMD dispatcher can use aligned loads. The pad formula pad=(64-(off%64))&63 is already implicit in SECTION_ALIGNMENT=64; add a read-side guard plus a padded/bounds-guarded tail so 64-byte SIMD scans never read past the mapped buffer.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/layout/mod.rs (SECTION_ALIGNMENT already 64, align_up exists) + reader open in crates/nest-format/src/reader/parse.rs; consumed by crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/{avx2,neon}.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: Precondition for aligned vmovaps loads and safe 64-byte structural scans off mmap with zero copy; validates the 'never zstd embeddings, score straight from disk' design and prevents read-past-end UB if SIMD structural scanning is added later.

nest_recommendations.idea: Refactor the Encoding enum into a small visitor-style codec registry where each encoding id (raw/zstd/float16/int8 and future delta/varint/bitpack/dictionary) implements one decode(&[u8])->Cow view method in its own <300-line file, keeping the additive 4-255 encoding-id space clean and extensible without rewriting every section reader.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/mod.rs (decode_payload match) and crates/nest-format/src/sections/codec.rs; one file per codec under encoding/.
nest_recommendations.impact: Makes the codec layer extensible — the prerequisite for adding delta/varint/bitpacking/dictionary codecs that push the compression frontier on chunk_ids/spans/provenance without touching readers; respects the 300-line/single-responsibility hygiene rule.

nest_recommendations.idea: Define a fixed-stride repr(C) u64 tape (type-tag in high bits + LE offset/length) plus a separate length-prefixed string/value blob as a new RESERVED section (id 0x09+) for ingested json/yaml structured documents, enabling pointer-free mmap reopen and sub-document citation (nest://content_hash/chunk_id#json_pointer) without re-parsing. Build it with a portable two-stage structural indexer at ingest time.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new module crates/nest-format/src/encoding/structure.rs + a new section file under crates/nest-format/src/sections/; ingest in nest-python build path (crates/nest-python/src/build_fn.rs) or a build-time path that may use serde_json/serde_yaml as a build-only dep (never in the frozen container).
nest_recommendations.impact: Strategic enabler of the 'compress AND serve json/yaml/parquet/datasets' north star: low-entropy offset tape zstd-compresses extremely well as a non-embedding section and is cheaply re-scannable; keeps canonical text byte-exact for content_hash. Higher risk, land after the layout wins.

nest_recommendations.idea: Deduplicate the repeated source_uri in chunks_original_spans: store each distinct uri once in a small string pool and reference it by offset/index from each span (most spans in a corpus share one source document), and resolve absent optional provenance fields to schema defaults instead of storing nulls (FlatBuffers vtable-default trick).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs (OriginalSpan currently inlines a full length-prefixed source_uri per chunk) and crates/nest-format/src/sections/provenance.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: Direct size reduction on spans/provenance when many chunks share a source uri (the common case for chunked documents); pure entropy reduction, deterministic, zero hot-path cost.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an in-process atomic-swap sidecar for real-time edit/hot-reload using mmap-sync's packed-u64 {active-index|size|truncated-checksum} version word + double-buffer RCU drain, so a rebuilt .nest is published and queried wait-free while old mmap readers finish. Keep the frozen v1 container immutable; the swap layer lives entirely outside the format and never opens a socket.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new module in crates/nest-runtime/src/ (e.g. swap.rs) layered over crates/nest-runtime/src/mmap_file.rs; surfaced to nest-python. Outside crates/nest-format entirely.
nest_recommendations.impact: Delivers the stated-but-missing real-time edit / concurrent-serving mission goal without compromising single-file/offline/deterministic guarantees; the version-word checksum gives O(1) integrity gating per swap.

compression_wins: chunk_ids: store 32 raw SHA-256 bytes instead of 71-byte ASCII 'sha256:<64 hex>' — ~2.2x shrink pre-zstd and removes the redundant repeated 'sha256:' prefix; verified concrete in sections/chunk_ids.rs.

Structural/offset/provenance integers: FlexBuffers-style minimum-width + delta+varint packing (offsets and lengths are monotonic/low-entropy) trims non-embedding overhead with zero hot-path decode cost, stacking on the zstd nest already applies to non-embedding sections.
chunks_original_spans: dedup the per-chunk source_uri into a single string pool referenced by offset — large win when many chunks share one source document (the common chunking case).

Ingested json/yaml as a fixed-stride u64 offset tape + separate length-prefixed blob: offset deltas are textbook low-entropy and zstd-crush far better than raw nested text, while canonical text stays byte-exact for content_hash stability.

Offset-table layout makes per-cell/per-chunk lazy zstd decode possible (csv2 decode-on-demand), so a compressed table/text section can be unpacked one chunk at a time instead of whole-section, lowering working-set memory during ingest and serve.

An extensible codec registry (one encoding id per file in the additive 4-255 space) is the prerequisite to later add delta/RLE/dictionary/bitpacking codecs — the column-oriented per-encoding path (rust-llkv/Arrow direction) is where extreme compression of parquet/datasets actually comes from.

Embeddings stay uncompressed by design (scored from mmap) — none of these wins touch the hot path; the 64-byte alignment guarantee is what KEEPS embeddings serveable at full SIMD speed while every cold section is squeezed.
watch_outs: Do NOT pull the serde crate into the frozen container: the format is repr(C) little-endian and must stay dependency-light and byte-deterministic. Steal the patterns (borrowed-view codec, encoding-driven Cow, N+M codec separation), not the dependency. serde_json/serde_yaml are acceptable only in nest-python or a build-time ingest path, never in the on-disk reader.

Do NOT use PCLMULQDQ/vmull_p64 carry-less multiply directly for the prefix-XOR trick if it could vary across CPUs — implement a portable parity/carry-less scan so structural indexing and tokenization stay bit-for-bit deterministic and reproducible (same chunks + model fingerprint => byte-identical file).

Any SIMD structural scanner needs input padding (SIMDJSON_PADDING) so 64-byte loads never read past the mmap buffer end; reading past the mapped region is UB. nest must pad the section tail or bounds-guard the final chunk — and never panic in library code (typed thiserror only).

Every new layout (offset tables, tapes, raw-digest chunk_ids, min-width ints, string dedup) must be additive within v1: use reserved encoding ids 4-255 and section ids 0x09+, and only bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION for a true v2 where an existing field changes meaning. content_hash must keep hashing a stable canonical decoded representation so the chunk_ids encoding switch and offset tables do not break existing citations.

FlexBuffers/min-width packing trades read speed for size via per-value width-tag dispatch — apply it ONLY to cold structural/metadata sections, NEVER the embedding hot path, which must stay fixed-stride aligned for SIMD.

rkyv (used by mmap-sync) pins a specific version and brings unsafe archived-cast machinery; reimplement the lightweight archived-struct cast directly on nest's existing repr(C)+LE structs rather than adding the rkyv dependency, to keep the small dependency-light core.

csv2 and FlatBuffers are C++/Apache-2.0 and simd-r-drive/simd-json are Rust Apache/MIT — all permissive and safe to reimplement, but reimplement the algorithms in pure safe-where-possible Rust rather than vendoring C++, to preserve the single-binary, no-FFI, offline posture.

mmap-sync's RCU swap is single-writer/multi-reader and tmpfs-oriented; the real-time-edit sidecar must stay in-process and never open a socket (offline by construction), live entirely outside the frozen .nest container, and handle crashed-reader drain without blocking the read path.

Keep SHA-256 for the four integrity/citation surfaces — CRC32C (simd-r-drive) and truncated WyHash (mmap-sync) are cheaper but non-cryptographic and only acceptable as a fast-path liveness check during streaming edits, never as a replacement for the citation/integrity hashes.

File hygiene: every new codec/section/tape module must stay under 300 lines (333 hard cap), single-responsibility — split a codec registry into one file per encoding rather than growing encoding/mod.rs.

categories.name: ann-index
categories.focus: approximate nearest neighbor indexes and libraries

repos.one_liner: FAISS is a C++/Python library of composable ANN indexes and vector codecs (PQ, additive quantizers, scalar quantization, IVF, HNSW) whose distinguishing feature is extreme lossy compression of vectors into short codes that remain searchable directly via SIMD lookup-table kernels, with a built-in two-stage approximate-then-rerank search contract.
repos.core_innovation: PQ4 FastScan: quantize each vector into M 4-bit product-quantization codes, lay the codes out in interleaved 32-vector blocks (bbs=32, 2 sub-quantizers per 32-byte block), quantize the per-query distance lookup tables to 8-bit integers, and evaluate distances with SIMD byte-shuffle instructions (AVX2 pshufb / NEON vqtbl) accumulating in 16-bit lanes -- a 16-entry LUT lives entirely in a vector register and 32 candidate distances are computed per pair of shuffles, with no RAM lookups on the hot path. Pair this with a mandatory exact rerank of the top k*k_factor candidates to recover the accuracy lost to 4-bit quantization. This is the same approximate-then-exact-rerank contract nest already enforces, applied to a far more aggressive code than int8.
key_techniques: PQ4 FastScan: 4-bit product quantization codes (16 centroids/subquantizer) packed in interleaved 32-vector blocks for register-resident SIMD shuffle lookups
8-bit-quantized lookup tables with formula A*(dist-B), 16-bit non-saturating accumulators, even/odd sub-quantizer split to avoid AVX cross-lane ops (SCANN-derived)
Additive quantizers: Residual Quantizer (greedy beam-search encoding) and Local Search Quantizer (simulated annealing); x = sum of M codebook entries, beat PQ accuracy at 64-128 bits
use_beam_LUT distance decomposition into precomputable norm/cross-product/query tables to avoid explicit residual computation during encoding
Scalar quantization tiers SQ8/SQ6/SQ4/SQfp16 as a simple per-dimension uniform codec (nest has int8/f16, missing 4-bit and 6-bit)
OPQ / random-rotation / Hadamard transform (O(d log d)) preprocessing to decorrelate dimensions before PQ, raising recall at fixed code size
Composable index-factory string grammar (e.g. OPQ16_64,IVF4096,PQ16x4fs,RFlat) describing transform + coarse quantizer + encoding + refine as one declarative recipe
RFlat/Refine/RefinePanorama two-stage retrieve-then-rerank with early pruning during the exact reranking phase
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) Add a PQ codec to nest-format encoding (a new RESERVED encoding id in 4-255, additive-only, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump): store learned codebooks plus 4-bit codes for the embeddings section. Codebooks are tiny (M*16*subdim f32) and codes are ~M*0.5 bytes/vector, beating int8's d bytes/vector by 4-16x -- directly serving the north-star goal on the largest section. repos.one_liner: A C++/Python random-projection-forest ANN index whose entire forest lives in one contiguous, headerless, raw-float32 blob that is mmapped read-only and shared across processes with zero deserialization.

Node count is recovered as `file_size / _s`; tree roots are recovered by scanning backward from EOF and collecting nodes whose `n_descendants == m` (the max). One union'd struct overloads three roles via a single discriminant (`n_descendants`): leaf (==1, vector in v[]), compact internal node (2..=_K, child item-ids packed where v[] would be), or split node (>_K, hyperplane normal in v[]). Headerless contiguous blob: n_nodes = file_size/_s, roots found by backward EOF scan for max n_descendants, roots copied into a trailing segment at build end
Single union'd Node struct discriminated by n_descendants: leaf(1)/compact-internal(<=_K ids inline)/split(hyperplane in v[]); _K=(_s-offsetof(Node,children))/sizeof(S)

Hand-written SIMD distance kernels: AVX _mm256_mul_ps/_mm256_add_ps + hsum256_ps_avx; AVX512 _mm512_fmadd_ps + _mm512_reduce_add_ps; Manhattan/Euclidean use _mm256_andnot_ps for abs
Angular metric stores L2-normalized vectors so cosine becomes sqrt(2-2cos); DotProduct metric reduced to cosine space via an extra dot_factor dimension per node
Hamming metric packs bits into 64-bit words and uses popcount primitives -- a compact binary-quantization candidate path
prefault flag: eager full read vs lazy on-demand page-faulting of the mmap, tuning cold-start latency vs RAM for partial scans
