repos.one_liner: A pure-Rust, dependency-light (no BLAS) ANN library implementing HNSW, SSG, Random-Projection-Tree, and Product-Quantization/IVFPQ indexes over a generic ANNIndex<E,T> trait, with packed_simd distance kernels and serde+bincode dump/load persistence.
repos.core_innovation: Product Quantization (PQ) with an Inverted-File coarse partition (IVFPQ) used as a lossy vector codec: split each D-dim vector into n_sub subvectors, k-means-train a codebook of 2^sub_bits centroids per subvector, and store each vector as n_sub small codes (e.g. 8 bits each) instead of D floats. This compresses embeddings ~8-32x while supporting Asymmetric Distance Computation (ADC): the query stays full-precision and distances to all centroids are precomputed into a lookup table, so scoring a stored code is just n_sub table lookups + adds. IVF adds a residual-quantization layer (each cluster PQ-encodes the residual to its coarse centroid) to cut quantization error.
key_techniques: Product Quantization: vector split into n_sub subvectors, codebook = 1<<sub_bits centroids per subquantizer trained by k-means over _train_epoch iterations; code width _sub_bytes=(sub_bits+7)/8
IVFPQ residual quantization: _n_kmeans_center coarse centroids, _ivflist: Vec<Vec<usize>> inverted lists, per-cluster PQIndex encoding the residual (_residual=coarse center), _search_n_center probes
Asymmetric Distance Computation via precomputed query-to-centroid distance tables (get_distance_from_vec_range): full-precision query vs quantized codes
Codes stored as packed Vec<u8> (_code_bytes=sub_bytes*n_sub); centroids as Vec<Vec<Vec<E>>> shaped [n_sub][n_center][sub_dim]
SerializableIndex trait with dump(path)/load(path) over serde derive + bincode 1.3 binary format
Generic ANNIndex<E,T> trait separating element/distance type E from external id type T; Metric enum {Dot, Euclidean, Manhattan, Cosine}
packed_simd_2 0.3.6 vectorized distance kernels with a BruteForce SIMD baseline and no BLAS dependency
build->dump offline-codec pipeline (k-means via rand 0.8) usable deterministically if seeded

The embeddings section stores a small trained codebook (n_sub x 2^bits x sub_dim f32 centroids) plus one n_sub-byte code per chunk, replacing the D f32/f16/int8 vectors. This is the biggest single lever for the 'compress more than everyone' north star: PQ8 on a 384-d MiniLM embedding is ~48 codes/vector vs 384 f32 (32x) or 384 int8 (8x), pushing the tiny preset below its current 0.283 size ratio. PQ/IVFPQ is THE classic lossy vector-compression scheme (8-32x over f32) and the most promising path beyond nest's current int8 (8x) embedding quantization. Store ZeroNode as a packed [u32; M*2] and UpperNode as [u32; M] arrays, all little-endian repr(C), so the graph section is a pure POD byte block that nest-runtime mmaps and walks with zero deserialization (no serde, no allocation), matching the offline/mmap hot-path constraint. The M-vs-M*2 split and u32::MAX padding give a constant, predictable section size that compresses well under zstd (the index section is NOT on the SIMD scoring hot path, so unlike embeddings it CAN be zstd-encoded, helping the tiny/hybrid presets shrink further). Port the deterministic SmallRng::seed_from_u64 + ml=1/ln(M) level assignment into nest-runtime::ann::HnswIndex to satisfy nest's seeded-determinism rule, and adopt the generational Visited { Vec<u8>, generation } pattern to avoid per-query allocation. The select_heuristic diversity pruning is what lets nest's tiny preset hit recall@10 0.992 at low degree; keep it. Crucially, nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank means the graph only needs to be a good candidate generator, so nest can push M lower than 32 (smaller index, more compression) and lean on rerank to recover precision -- a direct lever for 'compress more than everyone' without losing the real-cosine guarantee. Split across files to respect the <=300 line cap: types (node structs), build (seeded insert), search (descent + visited), and an encode/decode codec in nest-format.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct: the fixed-arity [u32; M] / [u32; M*2] node layout is a POD byte block with constant per-point size that zstd-compresses well and mmaps zero-copy; lowering M (safe because nest always exact-reranks) directly shrinks the 0x07 index section, improving the tiny preset's 0.283 size ratio without harming recall.
repos.perf_notes: No SIMD distance kernel exists (open issue #20 requests generalizing SIMD to n-length vectors); distance is user-supplied via the Point trait, so nest's existing AVX2/NEON dot-product dispatcher is strictly ahead and should NOT be replaced by anything here. Performance wins come from the cache-friendly flat Vec<ZeroNode> layout (sequential u32 reads, no pointer chasing), bounds-check elision over fixed arrays, generational visited (no clear cost), and rayon-parallel construction. Build is parallel (rayon + parking_lot RwLock on zero layer during insert); query is single-threaded beam search. ordered-float avoids NaN ordering hazards.

repos.one_liner: A Rust ANN library that ports Spotify's Annoy (forest of random-projection / random-hyperplane trees) onto LMDB memory-mapped key-value storage, adding incremental insert/delete, RoaringBitmap-filtered search, and optional 1-bit binary quantization of stored vectors.
repos.core_innovation: Binary quantization of stored vectors to exactly 1 bit per dimension (sign bit: x>0 -> 1, x<=0 -> 0) for 32x raw vector shrink, while keeping the split hyperplanes in float32 so ANN partition quality is preserved -- the "lossy storage, faithful structure" split is the transferable idea for extreme compression of embedding sections.
key_techniques: Forest of random-projection trees: each internal node stores a random hyperplane (from 2 sampled points' equidistant plane) splitting space into two subspaces; n_trees forest, search_k controls recall/latency tradeoff

Two node types on disk: split/internal nodes (float hyperplane normal + offset) and descendant/leaf nodes (item ids); deletion collapses a last-descendant node into a direct item link to cut node count and lookups
1-bit binary quantization: pack sign bits, reconstruct -1/+1 on the fly via bitmask + select (NEON vbslq_f32) so distance math runs on faked floats; default cosine over [0,1] vectors
Incremental indexing: insert/delete rewrites only the affected tree path (a few nodes) instead of rebuilding the whole forest, made cheap by LMDB copy-on-write Btree
LMDB-backed storage via heed: multi-reader concurrency while writing, u16 multi-index namespacing, mmap straight off disk
RoaringBitmap filtered search (Filtered-DiskANN style): restrict traversal to a candidate id subset to skip whole subtrees
Bachrach et al. 2014 transform: maps inner-product space to cosine space so dot-product search reuses cosine tree machinery
SIMD distance kernels borrowed from Qdrant for the float path
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals. (1) Compression: add a binary/sign-bit encoding to nest-format encoding ids (reserved 4-255) as a new embedding codec -- 1 bit/dim is 32x smaller than f32 and 4x smaller than nest's current int8 tiny preset, pushing the size ratio well below 0.283. nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank already covers the precision loss: the 1-bit vectors serve as a coarse ANN/prefilter (Hamming via XOR+popcount, a cheap new SIMD kernel in nest-runtime's dispatcher alongside AVX2/NEON dot), then the real f32/f16 vectors produce the true cosine score, so the search_contract ground-truth guarantee is untouched. Highest-value adaptation. (2) Index codec: arroy's random-projection-tree node format (float split node + id descendant node, deterministic under a seeded RNG) is a smaller, simpler alternative to nest's hnsw_index(0x07) and fits nest's <=300 LOC/file and deterministic constraints better than HNSW -- a candidate reserved section (0x09+) 'rptree_index'. Its collapse-on-delete trick informs future real-time edit support. Do NOT copy LMDB: it violates nest's single-file/offline/frozen-format constraints; nest must keep nodes as repr(C) little-endian structs inside its own section.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. 1-bit sign quantization is the single biggest lever arroy offers for "compress more than everyone": 32x over f32, 4x over nest's current int8 tiny preset. The key insight that makes it safe for nest is that nest already mandates exact-cosine rerank, so an aggressive 1-bit lossy code can be a pure prefilter without corrupting returned scores -- arroy itself had to keep hyperplanes in float precisely because it has no rerank stage. A new 'binary'/'sign1' embedding codec plus a tiny-binary preset is a concrete path to a sub-0.1 size ratio.
repos.perf_notes: Binary distance is XOR + popcount (Hamming), extremely CPU-friendly and SIMD-trivial vs float dot products; arroy reports ~7x faster indexing and ~6.5x disk reduction at 3072 dims (26 GiB -> 4 GiB), but note real-world space savings were diluted (~15% in one case) because tree/internal nodes are NOT quantized, only user vectors. Lesson for nest: quantize only the embeddings section (already the hot mmap path), leave index/structure full precision. arroy's search is acknowledged slower than Annoy/HNSW due to log(n) Btree lookups and non-aligned LMDB vectors -- nest avoids both via aligned repr(C) structs in one mmap'd file rather than LMDB.

repos.one_liner: VSAG is Ant Group's production C++ graph-ANN framework (HNSW/HGraph/IVF/SINDI) whose standout component is RaBitQ binary quantization, a randomized 1-bit-per-dimension codec with a provably unbiased distance estimator and a popcount-based SIMD hot path.
repos.core_innovation: RaBitQ: quantize each L2-normalized, centroid-centered, randomly-rotated vector to its sign bits (1 bit/dimension), then estimate the true inner product with an UNBIASED estimator (error O(1/sqrt(D)), asymptotically optimal) using only bitwise AND + popcount instead of float math or PQ lookup tables. The query is split into Bq bit-planes (default 4) so the dot product becomes a weighted popcount sum: result = 1*popcount(code&q1) + 2*popcount(code&q2) + 4*popcount(code&q3) + 8*popcount(code&q4). Unlike PQ it needs zero training/codebook learning and has a real theoretical error bound, which is exactly the guarantee a deterministic, sovereign database needs.
key_techniques: RaBitQ 1-bit binary quantization: random orthogonal rotation (Johnson-Lindenstrauss) then sign extraction -> D-bit code per vector
Unbiased distance estimator <o_bar,q>/<o_bar,o> with per-vector precomputed factor <o_bar,o> + per-vector norm + dataset centroid stored as f32 side metadata
Popcount bit-product distance: AND + popcount over bit-planes weighted by 2^j (AVX512VPOPCNTDQ / NEON CNT, 1-cycle ops, ~3x faster than PQ LUT)
Bq-bit query decomposition (default 4 bit-planes) trading accuracy vs speed without re-encoding the database
Extended/multi-bit RaBitQ: binary MSB code first for coarse estimate, ex-code refines incrementally; 4/5/7 bits -> 90/95/99% recall
FastScan SIMD layout: transposed bit-plane packing for batched quantizer scans
SQ4/SQ8 scalar quantization and fp16/bf16 SIMD operators as a tiered quantizer ladder
Automatic build-parameter generation from vector dimension and dataset scale
repos.nest_application: Add a new additive encoding id (reserve id=4 in the 4-255 range) `rabitq` in nest-format/src/encoding/rabitq.rs, mirroring the existing int8.rs layout: versioned u32 prefix, then per-vector side data (f32 norm + f32 <o_bar,o> factor + one shared f32 centroid block + the seeded rotation), then packed D-bit sign codes row-major. Because nest mandates an exact-cosine rerank in nest-runtime/src/search, RaBitQ only ranks the candidate SET; the returned score stays real cosine, so RaBitQ's ANN-proxy nature never violates the search contract. Add a dot_rabitq_popcount kernel to nest-runtime/src/simd (avx2.rs popcount/LUT, neon.rs vcnt, scalar.rs u64::count_ones) dispatched from simd/mod.rs alongside dot_f32_i8. Determinism is preserved by seeding the rotation from the model fingerprint (same chunks + model => byte-identical rotation => byte-identical codes), matching nest's reproducible-build and deterministic-hnsw rules. Wire into writer/encoding_choice.rs and a new bq/micro preset.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly serves the north star: RaBitQ is 1 bit/dimension = 32x smaller than f32 and 8x smaller than nest's current int8 embeddings, the single largest section in any vector container. It is the most aggressive embedding compression with a real error bound (not heuristic), so it can push nest's tiny preset below its current 0.283 size ratio while nest's mandatory exact rerank keeps recall@10 near-lossless. Clearest path to compress embeddings more than everyone without sacrificing deterministic/sovereign/single-file guarantees.
repos.perf_notes: RaBitQ distance estimation reduces to AND+popcount, ~1 cycle on Intel IceLake+/AMD Zen4+ via AVX512VPOPCNTDQ (NEON CNT on aarch64), benchmarks ~3x faster than PQ RAM table lookups at equal accuracy. Codes are D bits (vs PQ 2D default) so smaller AND faster. No training pass so encode time is comparable to scalar quantization. Popcount kernel is mmap-friendly: codes are dense contiguous bytes scored straight off disk like nest's current i8 hot path. Side metadata is tiny (few f32/vector + one shared centroid + deterministic rotation).

repos.one_liner: Knowhere is the C++ vector-search core of Milvus, a unified index/config factory wrapping a Zilliz-optimized FAISS fork plus hnswlib and DiskANN, exposing HNSW/IVF/DiskANN/IVF_RABITQ indexes with SQ1-SQ8, PQ, and 1-bit RaBitQ quantization over a templated fp32/fp16/bf16/int8/bin1 operand type system with AVX512-VPOPCNTDQ and ARM-SVE SIMD kernels.
repos.core_innovation: RaBitQ 1-bit quantization: random-orthogonal-rotate a centroid-normalized vector, take the sign of each dimension to get a D-bit code (1 bit/dim, no codebook), store 2 small per-vector float scalars, and recover a provably-unbiased cosine/distance estimate with O(1/sqrt(D)) error bound using only bitwise-AND + popcount against a 4-bit-decomposed query, then exact-rerank a refine_k-larger candidate pool with higher precision. This is the textbook recipe for "compress harder than int8 yet still return real cosine after rerank" that nest already half-implements.
key_techniques: RaBitQ: random orthogonal rotation + sign() = 1-bit-per-dim code, no stored codebook (1536-dim vector -> 192 bytes)
Two precomputed per-vector float scalars give an unbiased distance estimator with O(1/sqrt(D)) error bound
Asymmetric distance: data 1-bit, query in Bq=4 bit-planes; estimate = 1*popcount(code&q1)+2*popcount(code&q2)+4*popcount(code&q3)+8*popcount(code&q4)
AVX512 VPOPCNTDQ and ARM SVE popcount kernels for the bitwise hot path; ~3x faster than PQ LUT lookups
Incremental refinement: split code into MSB binary-code + ex-code, coarse estimate first then refine bits on demand
DiskANN dynamic PQ+Refine: doubles K each round to emulate range search, switches to PQ+Refine when >x% of bits set
centroid-relative normalization (global or per-cluster centroid) to improve local 1-bit encoding accuracy
templated operand type system (fp32/fp16/bf16/int8/bin1/sparse) with compile-time feature-flag typeCheck and MockData->fp32 promotion

This becomes a new preset below "tiny" -- call it "atom" -- pushing the 0.283 size ratio toward ~0.05-0.08 for the embedding bytes (1 bit/dim vs int8's 8 bit/dim). In nest-runtime, the simd dispatcher (currently AVX2/NEON/scalar dot) gains a bitwise-AND+popcount path (AVX2 has no native VPOPCNTDQ, so use the SSSE3/AVX2 nibble-LUT popcount or vcntq_u8 on NEON) to produce the 1-bit estimate cheaply, then -- critically -- nest's MANDATORY exact-cosine rerank stays exactly as is: the 1-bit codes are pure candidate generation, the returned score is still real cosine read from a small materialized f32/f16 refine set, preserving the search_contract guarantee that score is never an ann proxy. Keep determinism by seeding the rotation and using alphabetical/stable tie-breaks. Each nest-runtime file stays <=300 lines by isolating the codec (rabitq_codec.rs) from the popcount kernel (simd/popcount.rs).
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to the north star of "compress data more than everyone." RaBitQ is the single most compact published vector encoding that still supports search: 1 bit/dimension with NO codebook and a proven error bound, an 8x shrink over nest's current int8 embedding mode and ~32x over f32. Because nest already mandates an exact-cosine rerank, it gets RaBitQ's recall recovery essentially for free -- the risky part of 1-bit quantization (lossy scores) is already neutralized by nest's architecture. This is the highest-leverage compression idea available for the embeddings section.
repos.perf_notes: Bitwise-AND+popcount distance is ~3x faster than PQ LUT-in-RAM scans and runs near 1 cycle/word on VPOPCNTDQ hardware. On nest's targets: x86_64 AVX2 lacks VPOPCNTDQ so use the Mula nibble-shuffle popcount (pshufb LUT) for ~16-32 bytes/iter; aarch64 NEON uses vcntq_u8 + horizontal add, which is excellent. The 1-bit codes are tiny and mmap-friendly (192 bytes for a 1536-d vector), so far more candidates fit in cache, improving candidate generation before rerank. Asymmetric 4-bit query keeps full query info while data stays 1-bit. Memory: 2 extra f32/vector overhead (8 bytes) is negligible vs the bit savings.

repos.one_liner: A Python wrapper over FAISS that auto-selects and tunes a KNN index (the faiss factory string + nlist + PQ subquantizers + nprobe/efSearch) from nb_vectors, dimension, a strict memory budget, and a query-latency target, via threshold heuristics plus binary search against measured recall.
repos.core_innovation: A closed-form memory/compression cost model for Product Quantization (each vector costs pq + 8 bytes; compression ratio = 4*dim / (pq+8)) that lets you invert a target memory budget into a quantization scheme deterministically, then a learned OPQ rotation that decorrelates dimensions before PQ so the same byte budget buys higher recall. The compression target drives codec choice, not the other way around.
key_techniques: Product Quantization (PQ): split D-dim vector into m subvectors, each coded to one of 256 (8-bit) centroids learned by k-means; vector stored as m bytes; distance via asymmetric distance computation (ADC) over precomputed lookup tables
OPQ: a learned orthonormal rotation matrix applied before PQ (factory 'OPQ{m}_{y}', y=(min(dim//pq,6)+1)*pq) that minimizes quantization distortion by aligning subspaces to the PQ grid
PQ-budget inversion: choose m from pq_values=[256,128,64,48,32,24,16,8,4] such that (4*dim)/(pq+8) >= target_compression_ratio = 4*N*dim / max_memory_bytes
nlist heuristic: nb_clusters = 4*sqrt(N) rounded to nearest power of 2 (<1M); fixed ladders for larger N; switch to IVF{nlist}_HNSW32 coarse quantizer when nlist>=1000
k-means train-size heuristic: ~100 points/cluster (floor 31, range 30*nlist..256*nlist), 2^code_size*1000 for PQ codebooks
Two-phase greedy tuning: binary_search_on_param over nprobe/efSearch to find min param hitting 99% neighbor coverage, then maximize recall under a max_speed_ms wall-clock bound
Index-type decision tree by data scale: flat brute force <1000 vectors, no quantization <10000, IVF-Flat <1M, IVF-PQ/OPQ above, gated by a should_be_memory_mappable flag
Memory-mappable IVF index path: index built and served from disk via mmap with optional direct-map for reconstruction (~8 bytes/vec id overhead)
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) Add a PQ/OPQ embedding codec to nest-format encoding.rs as a new RESERVED encoding id (additive within v1): store per-vector m-byte codes plus a small codebook (new section 0x09+ or folded into search_contract). This is nest's path past int8's hard 4x ceiling toward 16-100x embedding compression (m=32 on a 768-dim f32 vector is ~96x). It does NOT break nest's 'score f32 from mmap on the hot path' rule because nest already runs a MANDATORY exact-cosine rerank: use PQ ADC tables in nest-runtime as the cheap ANN candidate generator (alongside hnsw), then rerank top-k against full-precision vectors so the returned score stays real cosine. PQ codes are mmap-friendly: ADC is a gather over a small in-cache codebook. (2) Port the budget->codec inversion and nlist=4*sqrt(N) power-of-2 heuristic into nest-python's builder so the user passes a target .nest size or recall floor and the builder deterministically solves codec+params, replacing the fixed exact/compressed/tiny/hybrid presets. The binary-search nprobe/efSearch tuner adapts directly to deterministic HNSW efSearch selection feeding search_contract. Keep determinism by seeding PQ/OPQ k-means and emitting codebooks in fixed order so same chunks+model => byte-identical file.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. PQ+OPQ is the single highest-leverage embedding compression technique nest lacks: it breaks the int8 4x ceiling and reaches 16-100x on the embeddings section, which is usually the largest part of a .nest file. nest's mandatory exact rerank in search_contract is exactly what makes lossy PQ safe (returned score stays real cosine), so this slots into the design instead of fighting it. The budget-driven codec inversion turns 'compress more than everyone' into a solvable optimization instead of fixed presets.
repos.perf_notes: PQ ADC computes a distance by summing m table lookups (one per subquantizer) from a 256*m precomputed query-distance table that fits in L1/L2; a gather+accumulate that is SIMD-friendly (faiss PQ4 fast-scan packs 32 codes and uses shuffle-based lookups). Per-vector storage is exactly m bytes (+8 byte id) vs 4*dim for f32. OPQ adds a one-time D*D matmul per query (negligible). Build cost is the tradeoff: k-means over training subvectors (~100 points/cluster) plus optional Spark distribution for >RAM data; autofaiss reports a 10GB index from a 1TB/200M-image corpus at 10ms query in ~3h.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A Rust+PyO3 flat-scan ANN index implementing Google Research's TurboQuant: a data-oblivious (training-free) quantizer that random-rotates unit vectors so every coordinate follows a known Beta/Gaussian marginal, then applies precomputed Lloyd-Max 2/4-bit scalar quantization plus a per-vector length-renormalization scalar, scored directly in the compressed domain with FastScan-style nibble-LUT SIMD (AVX-512BW/AVX2/NEON).
repos.core_innovation: Data-oblivious quantization: because a single fixed random orthogonal rotation makes each coordinate's distribution input-independent (Beta marginal converging to N(0,1/d)), the quantizer boundaries can be PRECOMPUTED once from (dimension, bit-width) alone -- no k-means, no codebook training, no per-corpus fit, no rebuild on insert. This collapses "good ANN compression" from a stateful trained artifact into a pure deterministic function of dim+bits, while a cheap per-vector scalar (||v|| / <u,x_hat>) restores inner-product unbiasedness that scalar quantization otherwise loses.
key_techniques: TurboQuant pipeline: normalize (store ||v|| as f32) -> fixed random orthogonal rotation -> 2/4-bit Lloyd-Max scalar quantization tuned for the Beta marginal -> bit-pack
Length-renormalized scoring: store ||v|| / <u, x_hat> per vector to debias the inner-product estimate at zero extra runtime cost (adapted from RaBitQ, SIGMOD 2024)
TQ+ per-coordinate calibration: fit one shift+scale per coordinate from empirical 5/95% quantiles on the FIRST add, then freeze, mapping data onto the canonical Beta marginal

FastScan-style SIMD scoring: rotate query once into codebook domain, score directly against packed nibbles using nibble-split lookup tables + u16 accumulators at 32-vector block granularity, no decompression of DB vectors
Runtime SIMD dispatch: AVX-512BW primary, AVX2 (x86-64-v3) fallback gated by is_x86_feature_detected!, hand-written NEON on ARM
Lazy deterministic init via std::sync::OnceLock for rotation matrix, Lloyd-Max centroids, and SIMD-blocked layout (one-time, lock-free reads after)
Filtered search honored inside the kernel: ID allowlist / slot bitmask drops non-allowed slots at heap-insert per 32-vector block, no over-fetch, no recall penalty
IdMapIndex: stable external u64 IDs surviving deletes with O(1) removal, persisted as .tvim alongside the flat .tq index
repos.nest_application: Add a new embedding codec in nest-format/src/encoding (alongside raw/zstd/f16/int8), reserving one of the additive encoding ids 4-255: a "turboquant2bit"/"turboquant4bit" codec that stores, in the embeddings section, (a) a header with dim+bitwidth (rotation+codebook fully derived from these, so nothing per-corpus persisted), (b) bit-packed quantized codes, (c) a per-vector f32 length-renorm scalar, and (d) per-vector ||v||. nest-runtime/src/simd gains a nibble-LUT FastScan kernel beside the existing AVX2/NEON dot-product dispatcher, scoring compressed codes straight off the mmap on the hot path -- exactly nest's "score embeddings directly from mmap, never decode" rule, which today blocks zstd on embeddings. The mandatory exact-cosine rerank in nest-runtime search stays unchanged and absorbs the small recall loss, so the returned score is still real cosine. This unlocks ~16x embedding compression (6144B f32 -> 384B at 2-bit for d=1536) vs int8's 4x, advancing the "tiny" preset and the compress-more-than-everyone north star. Determinism holds because the rotation is a fixed seeded function of dim+bits (compatible with nest's seeded-hnsw rule), so builds stay byte-identical. Keep each new file <=300 loc, typed thiserror, no panics.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. Embeddings are nest's largest incompressible section (zstd is banned on them because they're scored from mmap). TurboQuant breaks that wall: 16x embedding compression at 2-bit AND scoring in the compressed domain, so it compresses the one section nest currently cannot, without violating the no-decode-on-hot-path constraint. At 10M vectors it shrinks 31GB f32 to ~4GB. This is the single biggest available lever on nest's "most compact AI database in the world" goal, far beyond the current int8 (4x) tiny preset.
repos.license: MIT
repos.perf_notes: Hand-written kernels beat FAISS IndexPQFastScan by 12-20% on Apple M3 Max NEON and win most 4-bit configs by 1-6% on Intel Sapphire Rapids (within ~1% on 2-bit single-threaded). Recall at R@1 vs FAISS IndexPQ: +0.4 to +3.4pp on OpenAI d=1536/3072, slightly trailing (~1.2pp) on low-dim GloVe d=200 2-bit; high-dim recall converges to 1.0 by k=4. Lloyd-Max distortion within 2.7x of the Shannon rate-distortion lower bound. Flat scan (no graph/IVF), so O(N) per query -- best paired with HNSW for large N (nest already has hnsw_index 0x07; the two compose: HNSW for candidate gen, TurboQuant codes for compact storage + fast block scoring, exact rerank on top). OnceLock caches make repeated queries lock-free; rayon for parallel scan. Deps: ndarray, rayon, faer, rand.

repos.one_liner: A Mojo-first (with a Rust `squish_quant` extension, MIT-licensed) embedding-compression + HNSW library offering 7 quantization codecs (INT8, NF4, PQ, Binary, RQ, learned autoencoder, kurtosis-routed AutoQuantize) wrapped in a self-describing VQZ container with optional ZSTD/zlib second-pass.
repos.core_innovation: A "codec menu + rerank" architecture: store embeddings in one of several aggressive lossy quantizations (down to 1-bit binary at 32x), use cheap quantized-space distances (Hamming XOR+POPCOUNT, PQ asymmetric distance via precomputed lookup tables) as a coarse prefilter, then recover real accuracy with an exact rerank pass. The two highest-leverage codecs for nest are NF4 (8x, fixed information-theoretically-optimal 16-level codebook so it stays deterministic) and Binary+ADC PQ (16-32x), both layered UNDER a generic ZSTD second pass.
key_techniques: NF4: 4-bit normal-float with a fixed 16-value codebook at equiprobable N(0,1) quantiles (-1.0,-0.6962,...,0,...,0.723,1.0), per-block absmax scale, two codes packed per byte, decoded via a branchless decision tree
PQ with ADC (asymmetric distance computation): 96 subspaces x 256 centroids = 96 bytes/768-dim vec (32x); query distances precomputed into a 96x256 lookup table then summed per candidate
Binary 1-bit packing: sign(v) -> 8 dims/byte, Hamming distance via XOR+POPCOUNT (>=50M vec/s), used as coarse prefilter then exact-rerank to recover ~0.95 recall@10
Residual Quantization: 3-pass cascade where each pass quantizes the residual of the previous, ~0.98 cosine at 10x
NF4-mixed / outlier-aware: outlier dims stored as FP16, remaining dims as NF4
Kurtosis-routed AutoQuantize: pick codec (INT8/NF4/PQ/Binary) from per-tensor data statistics to hit a target_cosine/target_compression
VQZ container: 64-byte header (magic, version, blake2b checksum) + optional ZSTD/zlib second-pass OVER the already-quantized payload (INT8 4x then ZSTD ~1.6x ~= 6.4x)
assume_normalized fast path + fused single-pass NEON/AVX2 kernel: skip absmax scan for L2-normalized embeddings (~1.4x), eliminate the second L2 traffic pass for d<=4096
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add NF4 as encoding id 4 (PQ as id 5, binary as id 6) to nest-format's encoding codec set, applied ONLY to the embeddings section. Today nest stops at int8 (0.283 ratio, tiny preset); NF4 at 8x and PQ at 32x would push past competitors on the embedding bytes, the dominant payload. NF4's codebook is a FIXED constant table, so encode/decode stays byte-deterministic and additive (ids 4-255 reserved-in-v1, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump). nest-runtime: vectro proves embeddings can be scored in quantized space without full dequant -- add a binary-Hamming or PQ-ADC prefilter in nest-runtime's simd dispatcher to cut candidates cheaply, slotting UNDER nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank (rerank already guarantees the returned score is real cosine, so a lossy prefilter changes recall, never the contract). The fused single-pass / assume_normalized trick directly optimizes the existing AVX2/NEON kernels. Boundary to re-examine: nest's rule 'never zstd the embeddings (scored off mmap on the hot path)' -- vectro's ADC/Hamming path scores the QUANTIZED bytes directly, so a quantized-but-not-zstd'd embeddings section keeps mmap-direct scoring while still hitting 8-32x.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. Embeddings are nest's largest section; nest tops out at int8 (4x) while vectro ships NF4 (8x), PQ (32x), Binary (32x), RQ (10x), then stacks a generic ZSTD second pass (~6.4x compound for INT8 alone). Adopting NF4+PQ as embedding codecs is the single biggest lever to 'compress data more than everyone.' Codebooks are fixed/deterministic and the lossy distortion is absorbed by nest's mandatory exact rerank, so extreme compression is nearly free against the recall contract.
repos.perf_notes: Claimed INT8 ~12M vec/s (Mojo SIMD, d=768, '4.85x FAISS'); Python/NumPy fallback ~167-210K vec/s; Binary Hamming >=50M vec/s; VQZ save/load >=2GB/s. SIMD: NEON 32-wide unroll, AVX2 fused kernels, AVX-512-VNNI/SME2 stubbed, Apple AMX/Accelerate (vDSP_vsmsa) for d>=256, Rayon block-coarsening BLOCK=64 rows/task. Numbers are author marketing claims, unverified; the Hamming >=50M figure is plausible (XOR+POPCOUNT) and most relevant to a nest prefilter. Accuracy/size: INT8 4x cos>=0.9999, NF4 8x cos>=0.985, PQ-96 32x cos>=0.95, Binary 32x ~0.80 cos but >=0.95 recall@10 with rerank.

repos.repo: https://github.com/TusKANNy/kannolo (core codec engine in companion crate https://github.com/TusKANNy/vectorium)
repos.one_liner: A modular Rust (edition 2024, nightly portable-SIMD) HNSW + Product-Quantization ANN library whose real value for nest lives in its `vectorium` codec crate: a SIMD Stream-VByte sparse encoder with recursive-graph-bisection component reordering, an 8-bit PQ with SoA distance-table ADC, and cache-blocked batch-6 distance kernels.
repos.core_innovation: Compression is a codec trait, not an index feature: every vector encoder (PlainDense f32/f16, ScalarDense int8, ProductQuantizer 8-bit, DotVByteFixedU8 sparse) implements one VectorEncoder/QueryEvaluator interface so the same HNSW graph walks raw, quantized, or VByte-packed bytes interchangeably, and the graph is always BUILT on full-precision vectors while only the stored payload is compressed (why they beat Faiss up to 11x: quantization never pollutes graph topology, only storage size). The single most transferable trick is DotVByteFixedU8: sparse vectors are component-delta-gap + Stream-VByte byte-packed (1 control bit/element = 1 vs 2 bytes) over u64 words, values are int8 fixed-point, AND component indices are first remapped by a recursive graph bisection permutation learned offline so co-occurring terms get adjacent ids, shrinking the d-gaps VByte then encodes near-optimally.
key_techniques: DotVByteFixedU8 sparse codec: sort components, delta-gap, Stream-VByte (1 control bit/elem = 1 vs 2 bytes) packed into u64 words, int8 fixed-point values aligned at the tail for SIMD gather; decode via 256-entry compile-time swizzle mask LUT + simd_prefix_sum

Recursive graph bisection (rgbisect crate) learns a component->id permutation offline so frequently co-occurring dimensions become adjacent, minimizing VByte d-gaps; inverse permutation restores original ids on decode

8-bit Product Quantization: M subspaces (M%4==0), KSUB=256 centroids/subspace, 1 byte/code; per-subspace seedable k-means (25 iters, 10% sampling above 1M vecs); centroids stored SoA [M*dsub*KSUB] so the distance-table build auto-vectorizes
ADC asymmetric distance: precompute per-query distance table [KSUB*M] once, then score each code with 4 independent f32 accumulators over chunks_exact(4) via get_unchecked LUT gathers (4-way ILP)
Two-level PQ (coarse IVF u32 id + residual PQ codes + optional f16 residual norm) for ColBERT MaxSim, blocked [coarse_ids][pq_codes][norms] layout, const-generic Q unrolled SAXPY kernel
Cache-aware batch-6 distance kernels (dense dot/L2 and dense-sparse) with 6 independent accumulators plus explicit prefetch_with_range during the graph beam search to hide memory latency
CSR graph storage: flat neighbors:Box<[u32]> + offsets:Box<[usize]> compact form vs fixed-degree Optioned<u32> padded array for the growable builder, with optional local->external id mapping
fast-math algebraic_add/algebraic_mul intrinsics + std::simd gather/swizzle, and scalar code that auto-vectorizes by construction (SoA layouts, register-resident accumulators, single-write tiling)
repos.nest_application: Three additive grafts, all within format v1. (1) nest-format/src/encoding.rs: add a new encoding id for a `vbyte` codec (delta-gap + Stream-VByte + int8) ported from DotVByteFixedU8, applied to bm25_index(0x08) term postings and the chunk_ids section that nest already zstd-compresses; it never touches embeddings, honoring the 'never compress embeddings' rule. (2) nest-python build step + nest-runtime/src/bm25: add deterministic recursive-graph-bisection term reordering (alphabetical tie-break keeps builds byte-identical), store the term-id permutation in the bm25_index header, apply the inverse map at query time so postings d-gaps shrink before vbyte/zstd. (3) nest-runtime/src/simd + ann::HnswIndex: adopt the PQ ADC distance-table + batch-6 + prefetch pattern and add 8-bit PQ as a fourth embedding encoding (raw/f16/int8/pq). Because nest mandates an exact-cosine rerank, PQ is used ONLY for the ANN candidate shortlist while exact f32/f16 cosine still produces the returned score — exactly kannolo's build-on-full-precision philosophy — so PQ recall loss is fully masked and the size ratio drops far below the current tiny preset.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission. The DotVByte+RGB sparse codec is a textbook 'compress more than everyone' technique for BM25 postings and any inverted/sparse section; 8-bit PQ behind nest's mandatory exact rerank lets nest store embeddings at ~M bytes/vector (e.g. 4-16 bytes vs 1536 f32) for the ANN shortlist while still returning real cosine, slashing the size ratio below the current tiny preset (0.283) without breaking the recall guarantee. Both compress only non-embedding sections or ANN-only payloads, leaving the directly-mmap-scored f32/f16 embeddings untouched on the hot path.
repos.perf_notes: Beats Faiss up to 11.1x on HNSW build by building the graph on full-precision vectors, not quantized ones. Kernels lean on portable std::simd (nightly), fast-math algebraic_add/mul, SoA centroid layout for auto-vectorized table builds, batch-6 ILP with explicit prefetch, and 256-entry compile-time swizzle mask LUTs; PQ table build keeps 8 partial accumulators in registers across all dsub passes (single write per slot); ADC scoring uses 4-way unrolled get_unchecked LUT gathers. CAVEAT: requires Rust NIGHTLY (portable_simd, gen blocks) — nest targets stable edition 2024, so nest must reimplement the codec on stable using its existing AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatcher rather than std::simd. Graph uses u32 neighbor ids (max u32::MAX-1 nodes); CSR offsets are usize.
repos.license: MIT (both kannolo and vectorium) — clean for vendoring/porting. The recursive bisection pulls in the rgbisect / enhanced-graph-bisection crate; verify that crate's license before vendoring that specific piece.

synthesis.summary: The ann-index field has converged on one dominant pattern that nest is architecturally primed to exploit: aggressive lossy vector quantization (down to 1 bit/dim) used purely as a candidate generator, paired with an exact rerank that recovers real distances. Nest already enforces that exact-cosine rerank in search_ann/search_hybrid (search.rs: idx.search -> score_subset -> sort), so the "risky" part of extreme quantization (lossy scores) is already neutralized. That makes the embeddings section -- nest's largest, currently floored at int8/4x because it must be SIMD-scored from mmap -- the single highest-leverage compression target in the whole project. The state of the art splits cleanly: (a) CODECS for the embeddings bytes (RaBitQ 1-bit with an unbiased estimator and zero codebook; TurboQuant 2/4-bit data-oblivious quantization scored in the compressed domain; PQ4/OPQ trained product quantization; NF4 fixed-codebook 4-bit) and (b) GRAPH-LAYOUT efficiency for the HNSW section 0x07 (flat fixed-stride mmap-able records, uint40 neighbor ids, generational visited sets, Algorithm-4 diversity pruning to lower M). Nest's current HNSW uses Vec<Vec<u32>> adjacency, a fresh HashSet per layer_search, the _simple top-m selection, and a scalar cosine_dist loop that bypasses its own AVX2/NEON dispatcher -- all of which the surveyed libraries fix. The clear ranking for nest: RaBitQ-style 1-bit codec first (deterministic, error-bounded, popcount-cheap, 8x over int8), then route HNSW through the existing SIMD dispatcher + generational visited + Algorithm-4 (correctness/latency/recall with zero format risk), then a flat fixed-stride 0x07 layout with uint40 ids, then PQ/OPQ as a higher-accuracy mid tier. Three watch-outs dominate: never vendor nightly portable_simd (kannolo/turbovec) or unmaintained packed_simd (hora) against nest's stable edition-2024; never adopt LMDB/serde/bincode persistence (arroy/hora/instant-distance) against the single-file frozen repr(C) constraint; and keep every new codec deterministic by seeding rotations/k-means from the model fingerprint and using stable tie-breaks so builds stay byte-identical.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The category has settled on "compress hard, score in the compressed domain, rerank exact." Embedding codecs now reach 1 bit/dimension: RaBitQ (VSAG/Knowhere, SIGMOD 2024) random-rotates a centroid-centered unit vector, takes sign bits, and recovers an UNBIASED inner-product estimate with O(1/sqrt(D)) error using only AND+popcount over a 4-bit-decomposed query, needing zero codebook training and storing only ~2 f32 scalars/vector -- the rare 1-bit scheme with a real theoretical error bound (exactly what a deterministic, sovereign DB needs). TurboQuant (turbovec) makes the rotation data-oblivious so quantizer boundaries are a pure function of (dim, bits): no k-means, no per-corpus artifact, fully deterministic by construction, scored via FastScan nibble-LUT SIMD. FAISS PQ4 FastScan packs 4-bit product-quantization codes in interleaved 32-vector blocks and evaluates distances with register-resident pshufb/vqtbl shuffles (no RAM lookups), reaching ~280k QPS WITH rerank; OPQ/Hadamard rotations decorrelate dimensions to raise recall per byte. NF4 (vectro) is a fixed 16-level normal-float codebook (deterministic, 8x). On the graph side, hnswlib/USearch/instant-distance/rust-cv converge on a FLAT fixed-stride single-allocation layout (one base+offset index, zero pointer-chasing, mmap-able), uint40 (5-byte) neighbor ids to cut the dominant edge cost ~37.5%, generational/epoch-tagged visited sets to kill per-query HashSet allocation, and the Malkov-Yashunin Algorithm-4 diversity-pruning heuristic that raises recall at fixed degree -- letting M drop (smaller index) without losing recall, which compounds beautifully with a mandatory exact rerank. Annoy/arroy show random-projection forests compress far better under a generic second-pass entropy coder than HNSW (no back-edges), and a headerless self-describing flat-array layout (count = byte_len/stride) eliminates offset tables. kannolo/vectorium add the orthogonal lesson that index quality must be built on FULL-PRECISION vectors while only stored payload is quantized (why they beat FAISS up to 11x on build), plus Stream-VByte + recursive-graph-bisection reordering for sparse/BM25 postings. Universal contract across the strong libraries: the compressed code drives candidate generation only; an exact pass produces the returned score.
top_innovations: RaBitQ 1-bit quantization with an unbiased, error-bounded (O(1/sqrt(D))) estimator scored by AND+popcount and NO codebook -- 8x over nest's int8, 32x over f32, deterministic via a seeded rotation, and its lossy nature is fully absorbed by nest's already-mandatory exact-cosine rerank. The single highest-value steal (VSAG, Knowhere).

Build the ANN graph on full-precision f32 while storing a quantized payload -- quantization never pollutes graph topology, only size. Nest already snapshots f32 into HnswIndex.vectors via attach_vectors, so it gets this for free and can quantize the embeddings section arbitrarily hard without degrading recall (kannolo/vectorium).

Route HNSW traversal through the existing AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatcher instead of the scalar cosine_dist loop in ann/mod.rs, and replace the per-query HashSet<u32> in layer_search with a generational visited buffer (Vec<u8>+epoch tag) -- pure latency win, zero format change, stays deterministic (hnswlib VisitedListPool, instant-distance Visited, USearch SIMD).

TurboQuant data-oblivious quantization: rotation+quantizer boundaries are a pure function of (dim, bits) so nothing per-corpus is stored and builds are byte-identical by construction -- a determinism-native path to 2/4-bit codes scored in the compressed domain (turbovec).

Flat fixed-stride single-allocation graph layout with uint40 (5-byte LE) neighbor ids -- makes section 0x07 directly mmap-traversable as &[u8] with zero decode/alloc and shrinks the edge arrays ~37.5% vs u64 / drops Vec<Vec> overhead vs nest's current adjacency (hnswlib, USearch, instant-distance, rust-cv).

Malkov-Yashunin Algorithm-4 diversity neighbor selection (keep a candidate only if it is closer to the query than to any already-chosen neighbor) -- nest's mod.rs already flags this as planned Phase 2; it raises recall at fixed M, so the tiny/nano presets can LOWER M and shrink the index without losing recall@10 (instant-distance, hnswlib, rust-cv).

PQ4 FastScan: 4-bit product-quantization codes in interleaved 32-vector blocks scored by register-resident pshufb/vqtbl shuffle LUTs (no RAM lookups), ~280k QPS with rerank -- a higher-accuracy mid tier between int8 and 1-bit (FAISS).

Hamming/binary navigation: pack sign bits 64 dims/u64 and traverse the HNSW graph on XOR+popcount instead of float cosine, ~order-of-magnitude cheaper per hop, recall recovered by exact rerank (rust-cv hnsw, USearch b1x8, vectro Binary).

Stream-VByte (delta-gap, 1 control-bit/elem) + recursive-graph-bisection term reordering for BM25/sparse postings -- compresses the 0x08 inverted index well below raw u32 pairs while staying deterministic via alphabetical tie-break (kannolo/vectorium).

Budget-driven codec inversion: solve codec+params from a target .nest size or recall floor (PQ cost = m+8 bytes/vec; compression = 4*dim/(pq+8)) instead of fixed presets, turning 'compress more than everyone' into an optimization (autofaiss).

Store: u32 payload_version, a seeded rotation descriptor (seed derived from the model fingerprint -- store the seed, regenerate the rotation, or use a structured Hadamard rotate to avoid persisting a dense matrix), a shared centroid block, packed D sign bits row-major, plus the ~2 f32 side scalars per vector for the unbiased estimator. Score candidates via a new AND+popcount kernel, then feed the EXISTING exact-cosine rerank unchanged so the returned score stays real cosine.
