repos.one_liner: XTDB v2 is a bitemporal SQL database whose primary index is a distributed LSM tree of immutable Apache Arrow files, sharded by a 2-bit (branching-factor-4) HAMT trie over entity-id, where each file publishes min/max + bloom-filter metadata and a single collapsed "recency" scalar so the query engine can prune whole files before touching their columnar buffers.
repos.core_innovation: Collapse a multi-dimensional temporal coordinate (valid_time, system_time) into ONE monotone sortable scalar ("recency" = max T at which the row was believed valid for both valid-time=T and system-time=T), publish it as per-file metadata alongside min/max ranges and bloom filters, then prune entire immutable files at query time without decoding their payload. This is a generic "skip-index on a derived sort key + cheap per-file summary statistics" pattern, decoupled from temporality.
key_techniques: 2-bit HAMT trie (branching factor 4) over entity-id hash; trie path [3,2,1,0] = recursive prefix buckets that double as deterministic file shard names (210/211/212/213) and keep ~100MB files

LSM tree of append-only immutable files; compaction merge-sorts L0->L1->L2 and CONCATENATES bitemporal events instead of dropping versions; a file is 'superseded' only when its compacted output commits, making cache invalidation trivial
Per-file zone-map metadata: min/max for numeric columns + Bloom filters for non-numeric columns, used for predicate pushdown / file skipping before reading Arrow buffers
Recency heuristic: collapse (valid_time, system_time) into one sortable scalar so 'give me data newer than T' elides whole historical files
Survivor vs historical split at L1: current versions sharded by entity-id only; superseded versions sharded by entity-id AND recency, so hot current-state scans never touch cold history
Apache Arrow columnar layout chosen because remote/immutable storage already forbids in-place update, so columnar scan locality comes for free
Deferred leaf sorting: HAMT leaf stays unsorted until it exceeds 1024 bytes and is promoted to a branch, amortizing sort cost
repos.nest_application: Two steals, both anchored in nest-format. (1) ZONE-MAP/SUMMARY metadata per section, additively: extend the manifest entry in crates/nest-format/src/manifest and the section descriptors in crates/nest-format/src/sections so each section (chunks_canonical, provenance, future edit-log) carries cheap precomputed summaries -- for embeddings, per-block min/max per dimension or a coarse centroid; for text/provenance, a deterministic Bloom filter over tokens/source-ids. Then crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs and bm25 skip blocks whose Bloom filter cannot contain a query term and whose summary cannot beat the current top-k cosine bound, cutting SIMD dot products and mmap page faults without changing scored bytes (exact cosine rerank stays ground truth). Implement as a new RESERVED optional section 'section_zonemaps(0x09)' or new optional manifest fields -- additive, never a v2 bump. (2) RECENCY-SCALAR for nest's future real-time edit dimension: model each chunk version's (valid_from, ingested_at) as one monotone u64 'recency' stored in chunk_ids or a new edit-index section, kept sorted so 'serve current state' and 'as-of T' queries prune superseded chunk versions deterministically; the LSM survivor/historical split gives a coordination-free, single-file, append-only edit model that stays deterministic (seeded, alphabetical term order) and offline by construction.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. The zone-map/Bloom skip-index does not shrink the file but lets nest keep MORE data in one .nest container while staying fast, because cold blocks are never paged in or decoded -- it makes large-corpus single-file serving viable, the scaling axis of the 'compress AND serve whole databases' north star. The recency-collapse + LSM-concat compaction is the canonical compact way to store full edit history: one append-only sorted run that compacts and dedups instead of N snapshots, so historical versions migrate to deeper denser blocks that zstd (nest's existing non-embedding codec) compresses well. Bloom filters are themselves a compact (~10 bits/elem) probabilistic substitute for an exact term dictionary.
repos.license: Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL-2.0), file-level copyleft. Safe to read and reimplement the ideas, but do not vendor MPL source files into nest's permissive crates; reimplement the trie/zone-map/recency logic from scratch in Rust.
repos.perf_notes: Index lives on object storage and is cached across nodes (irrelevant to nest's single-file offline model -- adapt the file-skip idea, drop the distribution). Pruning works because Arrow buffers are columnar and contiguous, so a passed zone-map check yields a tight sequential scan; nest's mmap + SIMD dot-product hot path benefits identically -- skipping a block avoids both page faults and AVX2/NEON work. The ~100MB shard size and 1024-byte leaf-promotion threshold are tuning knobs worth mirroring as nest block sizes. Bloom false positives cost one wasted block scan, never a wrong answer; nest's mandatory exact rerank preserves correctness regardless.

repos.one_liner: An embeddable pure-Go in-memory key/value store that is ACID-durable via a single text append-only file (AOF) replayed on open, with copy-on-write B-tree indexes, pluggable Less comparators, GJSON path indexing, and an R-tree for spatial/k-NN queries.
repos.core_innovation: Durability and real-time edit on a single file without a WAL+pages engine: writes are serialized as a RESP/text command log appended to one AOF, live state is an in-memory B-tree, and crash recovery is just deterministic replay of the log in commit order. Compaction is a Shrink() that rewrites the file as the minimal set of `set` commands representing current state (an idempotent, replay-equivalent snapshot), triggered when the log grows past AutoShrinkPercentage. Transaction rollback needs no MVCC: each Tx records a rollbackItems map of the prior value (or tombstone) for every key it touches, and on abort re-inserts those prior values into the B-tree.
key_techniques: AOF as sole durability surface: each committed write appended as a RESP/text command (set/del/SETEX); recovery = replay in order, no page cache or WAL checkpoints
Shrink/compaction: rewrite AOF as minimal `set` snapshot of live state (idempotent, replay-equivalent), gated by AutoShrinkPercentage + AutoShrinkMinSize
Per-Tx rollbackItems map: store previous dbItem (or nil tombstone) per touched key; rollback re-applies them, commit flushes one buffered byte slice then fsyncs per SyncPolicy
Single-writer / multi-reader: one write Tx, many concurrent read Tx over stable snapshots, no read-side lock contention
Copy-on-write B-tree with path-hint Get/Set/Delete (SetHint/GetHint) to amortize repeated nearby lookups during bulk insert/replay
Pluggable Less comparator secondary indexes (IndexString/Int/Float/JSON/Rect/Desc), each a B-tree selected by key glob pattern (user:*)
GJSON zero-allocation path indexing of a JSON field (name.last) without deserializing the whole document; R-tree for Intersects() bbox and Nearby() k-NN
Configurable SyncPolicy (Never/EverySecond/Always) trading fsync frequency against a bounded data-loss window
repos.nest_application: nest's hard gap is that the .nest v1 container is frozen/read-only (mmap + SIMD scoring) with no edit path, yet the North Star demands real-time edit. Steal BuntDB's AOF+Shrink model as nest's mutation layer WITHOUT touching the frozen v1 body. Add a new optional binary append-only edit journal of typed records (add_chunk{content_hash,chunk_id,canonical_bytes,embedding}, del_chunk{chunk_id}) written by nest-runtime in a new journal.rs (<300 loc, single responsibility, little-endian repr(C), append-only -> matches additive-only + offline constraints). The reader overlays journal deltas in memory on top of the mmap base sections: base served from mmap, deltas merged at open. Adopt rollbackItems for transactional edits (record prior dbItem per touched chunk_id, re-apply on abort) staying typed-thiserror, never panicking. Adopt Shrink() as a nest-cli `compact` subcommand that rewrites base+journal into a fresh deterministic .nest v1 holding only live chunks, recomputing content_hash/file_hash so same live set => byte-identical output (matches nest determinism law). Separately steal the pluggable-Less secondary-index pattern for nest-runtime metadata filtering: a deterministic sorted index over provenance fields (source/lang/timestamp), mirroring bm25's alphabetical-order determinism rule.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. BuntDB does no entropy coding, so it is not a direct compression win. The value is that AOF+Shrink is the only way nest gains real-time edit while preserving single-file/deterministic guarantees, and the Shrink/compaction step is exactly where extreme compression re-enters: compaction is the moment to re-run zstd on non-embedding sections, re-quantize embeddings (int8/f16), drop dead chunks, and rebuild hnsw/bm25 to the smallest preset (tiny, 0.283 size ratio, recall@10 0.992). Without an edit-then-compact cycle nest can only compress at build time; with it nest can absorb edits cheaply (append) and periodically re-derive a minimal maximally-compressed container. Shrink idempotency (replay-equivalent minimal snapshot) is the conceptual twin of nest's reproducible build.
repos.perf_notes: In-memory B-tree O(log n) ops; reads lock-free across concurrent read Tx. Writes serialized (single writer), dominated by AOF append: EverySecond (default) buffers in memory and fsyncs once/sec (<=1s loss window), Always fsyncs per commit, Never defers to OS. Path-hint ops cut repeated comparisons during bulk replay. Cost: full dataset resident in RAM (pure in-memory) -- contrast with nest, which mmaps and scores off disk, so nest should keep base sections mmap-resident and hold only journal deltas in RAM, avoiding BuntDB's whole-dataset-in-RAM cost. GJSON indexing is zero-allocation over raw JSON bytes.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A statically-allocated, fully deterministic, single-file financial accounting database (Zig) whose entire on-disk state is a hash-chained tree of fixed 0.5 MiB grid blocks protected by out-of-band 128-bit AEGIS checksums, with an LSM "forest" over a WAL ring buffer and a 4-copy superblock root.
repos.core_innovation: Byte-for-byte physical determinism turns integrity into content-addressing: every block is referenced by {address, 128-bit checksum} in its parent, so corruption recovery is "fetch a block matching checksum X" with no error path, and repair is single-block (physical) rather than recomputing whole structures.
key_techniques: EWAH (Enhanced Word-Aligned Hybrid) run-length bitmap compression for the grid free-set: marker words encode runs of clean (all-0/all-1) words + literal dirty words, scannable/operable in place, guaranteed never >0.1% larger than raw bitset
Two-bitset free-set design (blocks_acquired + blocks_released) so deletions are deferred until a checkpoint is durable, giving crash-consistent reclamation without a full rewrite
AEGIS-128L as a (non-cryptographic-strength but fast) 128-bit checksum built on AES round instructions to saturate hardware AES on x86-64/aarch64; software fallback exists but is assumed unused
Out-of-band checksums: a block's checksum lives in its parent reference, not the block, defeating misdirected/torn writes and decoupling the checksum from the bytes it covers
Hash-chaining at every layer (WAL prepares chain, manifest log is a linked list of blocks, superblock chains predecessors) so a single root checksum authenticates all reachable state

4-redundant superblock root with a per-copy `copy` field excluded from the checksum, so all copies share one checksum yet stay individually addressable; recovery picks the newest root with >=2 matching copies
Static allocation from CLI-derived worst-case upper bounds: zero alloc/free after startup, so memory and on-disk sizing are an explicit deterministic function of declared limits
Deterministically scheduled, evenly-amortized LSM compaction (fixed work-per-op) so layout and latency are reproducible from a seed; LSM forest = many fixed-value-size trees keyed by stable tree_id
repos.nest_application: 1) nest-format hashing: TigerBeetle's out-of-band, content-addressed checksum model directly validates and sharpens nest's four-checksum scheme. Adopt the "checksum stored in the parent reference, not the bytes" rule for the manifest's per-section entries (layout.rs/manifest.rs/hashing.rs), and treat content_hash as a Merkle root over per-section content_hashes so a citation nest://content_hash/chunk_id can verify a single chunk against the root (partial verification without rehashing the whole file). 2) nest-format encoding: add an EWAH/word-aligned-hybrid bitset codec as a new RESERVED encoding id (>=4) or as an internal representation for sparse/boolean metadata -- e.g. a deletion/tombstone bitmap for real-time edit, an hnsw "live node" mask, or bm25 doc-presence sets -- giving near-free compression of sparse id-sets while staying scannable in place off mmap; deterministic by alphabetical/ascending id order, fits the <=300-line single-responsibility codec module. 3) nest-format additive section: the two-bitset (acquired/released) free-set is the blueprint for nest's missing edit story -- an additive section (0x09+) holding an EWAH live-set + released-set lets nest mark chunks deleted/superseded and reclaim space at the next deterministic rebuild without bumping to v2, preserving append-only + reproducible-build guarantees. 4) nest-runtime simd: evaluate AEGIS-128L (AES-NI / NEON AES) as an optional fast integrity check on the mmap hot path where SHA-256 is too slow for per-query re-verification -- keep SHA-256 as the canonical sovereign hash, expose AEGIS only as an internal fast-path detector of mmap corruption.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly relevant via EWAH: extreme, in-place-scannable compression of the sparse boolean id-sets nest will need for edit/tombstones/hnsw-liveness/bm25-presence, with a hard "never materially larger than raw" guarantee -- ideal for the smallest-on-disk mission. The deterministic/content-addressed-block model also reinforces nest's reproducible-build and partial-verification story, which underpins trustworthy aggressive compression. AEGIS is a perf, not a size, lever (fast re-verification of compressed mmap'd bytes).
repos.perf_notes: AEGIS-128L checksumming targets >GB/s by mapping onto AES round instructions on both x86-64 (AES-NI) and aarch64 (NEON crypto); software fallback exists but is assumed never used (an assert guards non-AES CPUs). Direct I/O (O_DIRECT) bypasses the page cache to avoid fsync/EIO cache-coherency bugs and to manage its own cache; fixed 0.5 MiB blocks double as network messages (zero re-encode between disk and wire). Static allocation means no GC/alloc jitter; compaction work is evenly spread per op to bound tail latency. EWAH bitsets are operated on in compressed form (no decompress step) which is the property nest needs for off-mmap scanning.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: An LSM-tree embedded key-value engine whose on-disk SST "block-based table" format combines prefix/delta-encoded sorted blocks with restart points, full/partitioned Bloom and Ribbon probabilistic filters, and trained-dictionary block compression to hit aggressive space-amplification targets.
repos.core_innovation: Decoupling the compressor's statistical model from the unit of access: RocksDB trains ONE ZSTD dictionary by sampling across many small blocks (buffer up to target_file_size, sample uniformly, run the ZDICT trainer to max_dict_bytes) and stores that single digested dictionary in a meta-block, so each 4KB block compresses against cross-block redundancy a per-block compressor can never see. The complementary idea is the Ribbon filter: replacing per-key Bloom hashing with a solved banded linear system over GF(2) that hits the same false-positive rate at ~30% fewer bits/key, trading one-time construction CPU for permanent space savings on long-lived data.
key_techniques: ZSTD trained dictionary: sample across blocks, run ZDICT trainer to max_dict_bytes, store one shared digested dictionary in a meta-block, compress each block against it
Ribbon filter: banded linear system over GF(2) solved by on-the-fly Gaussian elimination (Dietzfelbinger-Walzer), ~7 bits/key vs Bloom ~10 for equal FP, 128-bit band
Prefix/delta key encoding with restart points: store (shared_len, non_shared_len, non_shared_bytes), full key only every block_restart_interval=16, binary search over restarts
format_version=4 index delta encoding: reconstruct offset as prev_offset+prev_size+trailer, store only the size delta, ~4-5x smaller index blocks
Full/partitioned filter blocks: one filter per whole SST file instead of per-data-block, removing index lookup and address jumping on the query path
Footer-anchored layout parsed backwards from a fixed-size footer pointing to meta-index and index blocks
Cost-based filter selection: Ribbon for long-lived data, Bloom for short-lived, hybrid per-level
optimize_filters_for_memory: round filter sizes to reduce cache-line/page waste
repos.nest_application: Two steals into nest-format plus one into nest-runtime. (1) ZSTD trained-dictionary codec in crates/nest-format/src/encoding/zstd_codec.rs: today it calls plain zstd::encode_all at level 19 with NO dictionary. Add a build-time pass that trains ONE ZDICT dictionary over all text sections (chunks_canonical, chunks_original_spans, provenance) and compresses each against it; persist the digested dictionary in a new RESERVED section id 0x09+ or in the manifest. This attacks the exact pain point: many small, highly-similar chunks (the PT-BR fake-news corpus repeats names/boilerplate across articles) compress far better against a shared cross-chunk model than independently. Determinism holds because ZDICT is deterministic given identical sampled input and a pinned zstd version, so same chunks => byte-identical dictionary => byte-identical file. Purely additive via a new encoding id (4-255 reserved); old readers fail closed. Embeddings stay untouched for SIMD mmap scoring. Biggest single lever on 'compress more than everyone'. (2) Delta + restart encoding (format_version=4 trick) for chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans sections (crates/nest-format/src/sections/chunk_ids.rs, spans.rs): these are sorted u64 ids and (offset,len) spans that delta-encode almost perfectly; store only the size delta and reconstruct offsets, shrinking metadata overhead in the smallest 'tiny' preset. (3) Deterministic seeded Ribbon filter in nest-runtime alongside ann::HnswIndex and bm25 (crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/): ~30% smaller membership filter than Bloom at equal FP, stored in the optional bm25_index (0x08) region, as a fast offline pre-filter before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank, never violating the search contract.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission. Trained-dictionary ZSTD is the highest-ROI compression upgrade for nest: it converts cross-chunk redundancy (invisible to per-section zstd today) into bytes saved on every text section, improving every preset that uses zstd (compressed/tiny/hybrid) at zero recall cost since embeddings are excluded. Ribbon filters and delta/restart encoding of id and span sections cut index and metadata overhead, shrinking the smallest 'tiny' ratio (today 0.283) further. All three respect the FROZEN additive format (new reserved encoding/section ids only) and stay deterministic and offline.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 and GPLv2 dual-licensed. nest must NOT vendor RocksDB code: reimplement Ribbon clean-room from the public Dietzfelbinger-Walzer paper and use the zstd crate's native ZDICT bindings, to avoid GPL contamination of the small rust core.
repos.perf_notes: Ribbon construction ~140ns/key (4-5x Bloom ~32ns) with ~230 bits/key temporary build memory, but query only ~600ns vs Bloom ~500ns and steady-state ~7 vs ~10 bits/key; one-time offline build cost is fine for nest (python builds). ZSTD dictionary: in-memory digested form is larger than on-disk but decompresses faster; dictionary pin is one small meta-block. nest compresses whole sections (not 4KB blocks), so the dictionary gain is maximal precisely on many-small-similar-chunk corpora. Level 19 plus a trained dictionary stacks cleanly.

repos.one_liner: An in-process columnar analytical database with a single-file, block-based storage engine that applies per-segment adaptive lightweight compression (RLE, bitpacking, FOR, delta, dictionary, FSST for strings, ALP for floats) chosen automatically by a sampling-based Analyze phase.
repos.core_innovation: Per-segment adaptive compression cascade: each fixed-size column segment is independently analyzed by cheaply sampling the data, every candidate codec estimates its own compressed size via a uniform Analyze/Compress interface, and the smallest-estimate codec wins -- so the engine picks the best lightweight scheme per data block rather than committing to one global codec, all while keeping the data scannable in place without a heavyweight LZ pass.
key_techniques: FSST string compression: a 255-entry static symbol table mapping frequent 1-8 byte substrings to single-byte codes, ~2-3x on text with random-access per-string decode (no block decompression); dictionary offsets stored via delta+bitpacking

ALP float compression: PseudoDecimal path uses one shared exponent e + factor f per 1024-value vector to map doubles to ints then Frame-of-Reference + bitpacking; falls back to cutting low-variance front bits and bitpacking the remainder; outliers stored as exceptions
FastLanes 1024-value bitpacking with the Unified Transposed '04261537' layout over a virtual MM1024 register so scalar code auto-vectorizes to any SIMD width (AVX2/AVX512/NEON) with no intrinsics
Frame-of-Reference (FOR): store min value + bitpacked offsets per 1024-value block; ideal for dates/timestamps/clustered ints
Delta encoding feeding into FOR+bitpacking for monotonic sequences
Constant + RLE encoding for low-cardinality / repeated runs (store value once, or value+run-length pairs)
Uniform CompressionFunction interface (InitAnalyze/Analyze/FinalAnalyze size estimate then InitCompress/Compress/Finalize) enabling cheap sampling-based codec selection per segment
Block-based single file: 256KB blocks, main header + two alternating DatabaseHeaders for atomic ping-pong checkpoint, free list of reclaimable blocks, metadata blocks pointing to row groups/segments
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals into nest-format/src/encoding. (1) FSST as a new RESERVED encoding id (4-255 slot) for the canonical text sections (chunks_canonical, chunks_original_spans, provenance): 2-3x on text like zstd but with per-string random-access decode straight off mmap, so nest can cite/materialize a single chunk's bytes without inflating a whole zstd frame; pairs naturally with nest://content_hash/chunk_id byte-span reopen. (2) ALP + FastLanes-style transposed bitpacking as the principled successor to nest's crude int8/float16 embedding quantization: ALP is lossless and the FastLanes 04261537 layout means one scalar decode kernel auto-vectorizes to AVX2 and NEON, collapsing nest-runtime's three SIMD paths into one portable kernel. Most important architecturally: adopt DuckDB's per-section Analyze-and-pick pattern in the nest writer so each section's codec is chosen by a deterministic sampling estimate (seeded/ordered to stay reproducible) instead of fixed per-preset encodings -- directly serving 'compress more than everyone' by letting tiny/compressed presets pick the smallest codec per section while keeping byte-identical determinism.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central: DuckDB is the reference design for cheap, scannable, lossless lightweight compression. FSST gives random-access text compression (better fit than zstd for nest's cite/materialize path), ALP gives lossless float compression that could shrink embeddings better than naive float16/int8 without recall loss, and the per-segment adaptive selection is exactly the 'pick the smallest encoding automatically' machinery nest's north star needs. Caveat: nest scores f32 directly from mmap on the hot path, so any embedding codec must keep cheap/random decode -- FastLanes bitpacking decodes fast enough to fit, plain zstd does not (which is why nest already bans zstd on embeddings).
repos.perf_notes: FSST ~= LZ4 ratio (3x on TPCH l_comment) but decodes individual strings; analyze samples 25% of row-group vectors to estimate size. ALP is 2-4x faster decompress than older Patas/Chimp at ~2x better ratio, avg 2.08x on FCBench vs 1.47x for Bitshuffle+Zstd. FastLanes claims >100 billion ints/sec decode; the transposed interleaved layout speeds even scalar decode by exposing ILP, and the same source auto-vectorizes across Intel/AMD/Apple/AWS. All codecs operate on 1024-value vectors keeping working sets in L1/registers.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: An embedded, page-based B+Tree key-value/analytical engine (single-file, multi-database, mmap'd) whose headline innovation is SIMD-accelerated integer-key compression inside B+Tree leaf KeyLists, plus analytical aggregates that run directly over compressed pages.
repos.core_innovation: Store sorted integer key columns as delta-coded, block-bit-packed streams (SIMD-BP128 / VarIntGB / StreamVByte / MaskedVByte) and operate on them WITHOUT full decompression: binary search, range scans, and analytical aggregates (SUM/COUNT/AVG) run directly over the packed blocks. Decode kernels are vectorized via per-control-byte SSE shuffle-mask lookup tables (StreamVByte) and per-block fixed-bit-width unpacking (SIMD-BP128), hitting 4-8 billion ints/sec. This is the 'compress columnar data AND serve it from the same compact bytes' pattern, co-authored by upscaledb's own Christoph Rupp with Daniel Lemire.
key_techniques: SIMD-BP128 binary packing: split a sorted column into blocks of 128 ints, compute max bit-width b for the block, pack 128 ints into b 128-bit SSE words; decode via fixed shift/mask SIMD kernel (best case 1 bit/key, ~32x shrink)
Delta (differential) coding of sorted keys before packing so only small gaps are stored; reconstruct via vectorized prefix-sum (cumulative add)

StreamVByte: separate control stream (2 bits per int = byte length 1/2/3/4) from data stream; decode 4 ints/iteration via a 256-entry SSE pshufb shuffle-mask table indexed by the control byte (co-authored by Rupp)
VarIntGB / Group Varint: one control byte per group of 4 ints for branch-free length lookup; MaskedVByte for vectorizing classic varint streams
Frame-of-Reference (FOR) and patched PFOR / SIMD-FastPFOR: subtract a per-block reference value, bit-pack residuals, store rare exceptions out-of-band for fast random access
Per-block bit-width header lets binary search skip to the target block, decode only that block, then scan in-register
Analytical aggregates (SUM/COUNT/AVG) computed in B+Tree context across many packed keys at once without materializing records (millions/call)
Transparent record/journal compression (snappy/zlib/lzf) plus CRC32 page verification and AES page encryption layered under one page abstraction
repos.nest_application: Add a fourth integer codec family to nest-format/src/encoding alongside raw/zstd/float16/int8: a delta+bit-packing codec (SIMD-BP128-style blocks of 128, or StreamVByte) for INTEGER sections, specifically chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans (offset/length pairs are monotone or near-monotone and delta-code to ~1-4 bits each, far below zstd on small-int arrays). Reserve a new encoding id in the additive 4-255 v1 range (no version bump). The decode kernel slots into nest-runtime's existing SIMD dispatcher (AVX2/NEON/scalar fallback already present) as a new vectorized unpack path: NEON tbl, AVX2 pshufb shuffle-mask tables. Critically for the hot path, StreamVByte's 'operate-in-register' property lets the runtime reconstruct span offsets during materialize() and resolve nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations without decompressing whole sections, mirroring upscaledb's binary-search-on-compressed trick. Keep it deterministic (fixed block size 128, sorted input nest already mandates) so reproducible-build byte-identity holds. Do NOT apply to embeddings (they stay raw/f16/int8 scored straight from mmap), exactly as nest already forbids zstd on embeddings.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to 'compress more than everyone'. nest leans on zstd for non-embedding sections, but zstd is weak on arrays of small/monotone integers, which is exactly what chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans (span offset+length pairs) are. Delta + SIMD bit-packing reaches 1-4 bits/integer (vs zstd's byte-granular framing overhead on short int runs), shrinking structural sections while DECODING faster than memcpy. It is a true compress-and-serve codec: the runtime searches the packed bytes directly off mmap, preserving the offline/single-file/no-materialize hot path. Rare codec that improves both size and speed at once, which is precisely nest's mission.
repos.perf_notes: Reference simdcomp decodes binary-packed ints at ~0.3 cycles/int (>8 billion/sec on Skylake); StreamVByte decode can exceed memcpy (up to 2x faster than varint-G8IU). SIMD-BP128 saves up to 2 bits/int over prior vectorized schemes; whole-DB benchmark showed ~40% faster queries AND ~10x compression vs uncompressed B+Tree. Decode cost scales with bit-width (fewer bits = faster), so delta-coded near-sorted data is both smallest and fastest. Blocks of 128 ints map onto 128-bit registers (SSE/NEON 128-bit lanes), portable to nest's AVX2/NEON dispatch; AVX2 runs two 128-bit lanes. Per-block bit-width metadata is tiny (1 byte/block).
repos.license: upscaledb itself is GPLv3 / commercial dual-license (AVOID vendoring its code). The underlying algorithm libraries are permissive and safe to learn/port: lemire/simdcomp and lemire/streamvbyte are Apache-2.0, and StreamVByte is explicitly patent-free; permissive Rust ports exist (streamvbyte by Marshall Pierce / Trevor McCulloch, bazhenov/svbyte). Reimplement from the papers and Apache refs, not from the GPL upscaledb source.

synthesis.summary: This cohort (datahike, datascript, xtdb, buntdb, tigerbeetle, rocksdb, duckdb, upscaledb) converges on a handful of patterns that map almost 1:1 onto nest's three biggest open gaps: real-time edit on a frozen single-file container, deeper compression of non-embedding sections, and large-corpus serving without paging cold data. The two highest-leverage steals are RocksDB's cross-block trained ZSTD dictionary (the single biggest size lever for nest's many-small-similar-chunk PT-BR corpus, where per-section zstd today cannot see cross-chunk redundancy) and the upscaledb/Lemire delta + SIMD bit-packing family (StreamVByte / SIMD-BP128) for the integer sections chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans, which are exactly the small/monotone arrays zstd handles poorly and which nest can search/materialize directly off mmap. DuckDB contributes the architectural pattern that should govern all of this: a deterministic Analyze-and-pick codec selection per section instead of fixed per-preset encodings, plus FSST for random-access text compression that fits the cite/materialize path better than zstd frames. For the edit pillar, BuntDB's AOF+Shrink and datahike/datascript's content-addressed structural-sharing tree both show the same answer: never mutate frozen v1 bytes; append a typed journal (new reserved section 0x09+) overlaid in memory at open, with a deterministic `compact` that re-derives a minimal maximally-compressed container (the exact moment to re-run the trained dictionary and re-quantize). TigerBeetle's EWAH bitset and out-of-band content-addressed checksums, plus XTDB's per-file zone-maps + recency scalar, give the supporting machinery: compact scannable tombstone/liveness sets, a Merkle-root content_hash enabling single-chunk citation verification, and block-level skip-indexes so a large .nest stays fast. Every recommendation below respects nest's hard constraints: additive-only within v1 (reserved encoding ids 4-255, section ids 0x09+), embeddings stay raw/f16/int8 scored straight from mmap (never zstd), deterministic/seeded, offline by construction, typed thiserror (never panic), and <=300 lines per source file.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The state of the art for embedded edit+realtime engines is a layered stack: (1) an append-only/immutable substrate where edits never rewrite existing bytes -- either an AOF command log replayed on open (buntdb), an LSM of immutable files (rocksdb, xtdb), or a copy-on-write content-addressed tree where an edit touches ~log_b(N) nodes and unchanged nodes are shared by hash (datahike/datascript). (2) Content-addressing as integrity AND dedup: node/block id = hash(contents), so identical sub-structures across versions/corpora collapse to one physical block (datahike SHA-512, tigerbeetle 128-bit AEGIS with the checksum stored out-of-band in the parent reference, defeating torn/misdirected writes). (3) Lightweight, scannable, per-segment-adaptive compression that decodes faster than memcpy and is operated on without full decompression: DuckDB's cascade (RLE/FOR/delta/dictionary/FSST/ALP) chosen by a sampling Analyze phase; RocksDB's cross-block trained ZSTD dictionary + Ribbon filters (~7 vs ~10 bits/key) + delta/restart key encoding; upscaledb's SIMD-BP128/StreamVByte delta-bitpacking at 4-8 billion ints/sec; tigerbeetle's EWAH run-length bitmaps operated on in compressed form. (4) Cheap per-block summary statistics for skip/prune: zone-maps (min/max), Bloom/Ribbon membership filters, and a collapsed monotone "recency" scalar so temporal/current-state queries elide whole cold files before touching payload (xtdb). (5) Temporal model as append-only facts with an assertion/retraction flag and tx ids, so time-travel (as-of/history) is a filter, never a mutation (datahike datoms in EAVT/AEVT/AVET covering indexes; xtdb bitemporal recency). The unifying lesson for nest: compression, integrity, dedup, and edit are not separate subsystems -- content-addressed immutable blocks + adaptive lightweight codecs + per-block skip metadata deliver all four at once, and a periodic deterministic compaction is where extreme compression re-enters after cheap appends.
top_innovations: Cross-block trained ZSTD dictionary (rocksdb): train ONE ZDICT dictionary by sampling across all text chunks, compress each section against it. Captures cross-chunk redundancy (repeated names/boilerplate in PT-BR fake-news articles) that nest's current per-section zstd::encode_all at level 19 cannot see. Deterministic given pinned zstd + sorted input. Highest single ROI on 'compress more than everyone', zero recall cost (embeddings excluded).

Delta + SIMD bit-packing for integer sections (upscaledb / lemire simdcomp+streamvbyte, Apache-2.0/patent-free): SIMD-BP128 or StreamVByte over chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans reaches 1-4 bits/int on monotone/near-monotone arrays vs zstd's byte-granular framing overhead, AND decodes faster than memcpy with operate-in-register random access for citation/materialize -- a rare codec that improves size and speed simultaneously.

DuckDB per-section Analyze-and-pick codec selection: a deterministic sampling estimate chooses the smallest codec per section instead of fixed per-preset encodings. Turns nest's presets from hardcoded choices into an automatic 'pick smallest' machine while preserving byte-identical determinism (seeded/ordered sampling).

FSST random-access text compression (duckdb, MIT): 255-entry static symbol table, ~2-3x on text like zstd but decodes a single string without inflating a whole frame -- a strictly better fit than zstd for nest's nest://content_hash/chunk_id cite/materialize path.

AOF + Shrink edit model (buntdb, MIT): append typed edit records to a journal overlaid in memory at open; never touch frozen v1 bytes; a deterministic compact() re-derives a minimal container. The cleanest way to add the real-time-edit pillar while preserving single-file/deterministic guarantees, and compact is exactly where re-compression (trained dict, re-quantize, drop dead chunks, rebuild to tiny preset) happens.

Per-block content-addressed structural sharing (datahike/datascript, EPL -- learn not vendor): block id = hash(contents) so duplicate chunks/embeddings/index-nodes across versions or similar corpora dedup to one physical block; an edit rewrites only ~3 dirty nodes. Dedup-as-compression for multi-version/multi-corpus .nest files.

EWAH run-length bitmap codec (tigerbeetle, Apache-2.0): in-place-scannable compression of sparse boolean id-sets with a hard 'never >0.1% larger than raw' guarantee -- ideal for nest's coming tombstone/liveness/doc-presence sets, scannable off mmap without decompression.

Zone-map + Bloom/Ribbon skip metadata per block (xtdb, rocksdb): cheap per-block min/max + membership filter lets search.rs and bm25 skip blocks that cannot beat the current top-k cosine bound or contain a query term, cutting SIMD dot products and mmap page faults so a large single .nest stays fast. Exact rerank keeps correctness regardless of false positives.

Out-of-band content-addressed checksums + Merkle-root content_hash (tigerbeetle, datahike): store a block's checksum in its parent reference; make content_hash a Merkle root over per-section/per-block hashes so a citation can verify a single chunk against the root without rehashing the whole file (partial verification).

Recency-scalar / append-only fact log for temporal (xtdb, datahike): collapse (valid_from, ingested_at) into one monotone u64 'recency' kept sorted, and model edits/retractions as append-only [chunk_id, op, tx] facts so 'serve current state' and 'as-of T' become a deterministic filter over tx ids -- the temporal pillar with no mutation of frozen sections.

nest_recommendations.idea: Trained ZSTD dictionary codec for text sections. Add a new RESERVED encoding id (e.g. SECTION_ENCODING_ZSTD_DICT=4) in layout/mod.rs; in writer, train ONE ZDICT dictionary over chunks_canonical + chunks_original_spans + provenance via the zstd crate's ZDICT bindings, compress each against it, and persist the digested dictionary either as a new optional section (0x09) or a manifest field. Reader gains a decode arm in encoding/mod.rs decode_payload that loads the dict then decompresses. Embeddings untouched.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new zstd_dict_codec.rs), layout/mod.rs (new encoding id + reserved section), writer/encoding_choice.rs + writer/build.rs (train+emit), reader/decode.rs (decode arm)
nest_recommendations.impact: Highest single compression lever. Cross-chunk redundancy in the PT-BR corpus (repeated names/boilerplate) becomes bytes saved on every text section in compressed/tiny/hybrid presets at zero recall cost. Old readers fail closed on the unknown encoding id (additive-safe).

nest_recommendations.idea: Delta + SIMD bit-packing codec for integer sections. Add encoding id 5 (e.g. SECTION_ENCODING_DELTA_BP) and a delta_bitpack.rs codec (blocks of 128, per-block bit-width header) for chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans. chunk_ids are sha256: strings today -- pair this with storing ids as raw u64 hashes (or delta-coded sorted ints) so they delta-code to ~1-4 bits. Span (byte_start,byte_end) pairs are near-monotone and delta-code well. Decode kernel slots into the existing SIMD dispatcher (avx2 pshufb / neon tbl / scalar) for operate-in-register reconstruction during materialize().
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new delta_bitpack.rs), sections/chunk_ids.rs + sections/spans.rs (encode/decode integration), crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/ (vectorized unpack path)
nest_recommendations.impact: Shrinks structural sections below zstd while decoding faster than memcpy; directly tightens the tiny preset (today 0.283) and speeds citation/materialize. Improves size AND speed.

nest_recommendations.idea: Per-section Analyze-and-pick codec selection. Replace the fixed per-preset SectionEncoding choice with a deterministic sampling Analyze pass: for each non-embedding section, cheaply estimate compressed size under each candidate codec (raw / zstd / zstd+dict / delta-bitpack / fsst) and emit the smallest. Seed/order the sampling so output stays byte-identical across builds.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/writer/encoding_choice.rs (turn enums into an estimator), writer/build.rs (selection loop)
nest_recommendations.impact: Converts presets from hardcoded codecs into an automatic 'pick smallest per section' machine -- the core 'compress more than everyone' machinery. Preserves determinism via ordered sampling.

nest_recommendations.idea: FSST codec for random-access text. Add encoding id 6 (SECTION_ENCODING_FSST) with a 255-entry symbol table for chunks_canonical, giving ~2-3x like zstd but per-string decode straight off mmap so materialize/cite resolves one chunk without inflating a whole zstd frame.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new fsst.rs), sections/canonical.rs (decode integration), crates/nest-runtime materialize path
nest_recommendations.impact: Better fit than zstd for the nest://content_hash/chunk_id byte-span reopen path; competitive ratio with random access. Complements (not replaces) the trained dict where whole-section scan dominates.

nest_recommendations.idea: Append-only edit journal + deterministic compact. New nest-runtime journal.rs (<300 loc, little-endian repr(C), typed thiserror) holding add_chunk{content_hash,chunk_id,canonical_bytes,embedding} / del_chunk{chunk_id} records appended after the frozen v1 body or as a sidecar; reader overlays journal deltas in memory at open (base served from mmap). Per-Tx rollbackItems map for transactional abort. New nest-cli `compact` subcommand rewrites base+journal into a fresh deterministic .nest holding only live chunks, recomputing all four hashes and re-running the trained dict + re-quantization + index rebuild to the tiny preset.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/journal.rs (new), reader overlay in nest-format/src/reader/, crates/nest-cli/src/cmd/ (new compact.rs)
nest_recommendations.impact: Unlocks the real-time-edit north-star pillar without bumping v2 or mutating frozen sections; compact is where extreme re-compression re-enters after cheap appends. Same live set => byte-identical output (determinism law holds).

nest_recommendations.idea: EWAH liveness/tombstone bitset codec. Add an EWAH word-aligned-hybrid bitset as encoding id 7 (or an internal representation) for a deletion/tombstone bitmap, an hnsw live-node mask, and bm25 doc-presence sets. Operated on in compressed form off mmap; deterministic by ascending id order; <=300-line single-responsibility module.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new ewah.rs), used by the edit-log section and crates/nest-runtime/src/ann + bm25 liveness masks
nest_recommendations.impact: Near-free, in-place-scannable compression of the sparse boolean id-sets edit/tombstones need, with a hard 'never materially larger than raw' guarantee. Enables soft-delete before the next compaction.

nest_recommendations.idea: Per-block zone-map + Ribbon/Bloom skip section. New optional section_zonemaps (0x09): per-block embedding coarse centroid or per-dim min/max, plus a deterministic Ribbon filter (~30% smaller than Bloom at equal FP, clean-room from the Dietzfelbinger-Walzer paper) over bm25 terms / provenance source-ids. search.rs and bm25 skip blocks whose summary cannot beat the current top-k cosine bound or whose filter cannot contain a query term, before issuing SIMD dot products. Exact cosine rerank stays ground truth so false positives never cause wrong answers.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/manifest + sections (new section_zonemaps), crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs (block-skip in score_all), crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/
nest_recommendations.impact: Lets one .nest hold far more data while staying fast -- cold blocks never paged or scored. The scaling axis of 'compress AND serve whole databases'. Ribbon also shrinks the membership filter itself.

nest_recommendations.idea: Merkle-root content_hash for partial verification. Restructure hashing so content_hash is a Merkle root over per-section (and eventually per-block) content_hashes, and store each section's checksum in the manifest/parent reference (tigerbeetle out-of-band rule). A citation nest://content_hash/chunk_id can then verify a single chunk against the root without rehashing the whole file.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/writer/build.rs (footer_hash/content_hash computation), layout/section_entry.rs + manifest (checksum placement), reader/validate.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: Enables single-chunk integrity verification (cheap citation trust) and is the precondition for per-block content-addressed structural sharing/dedup in a future edit region. Reinforces reproducible-build story.

nest_recommendations.idea: Recency-scalar temporal index for as-of queries. Store each chunk version's (valid_from, ingested_at) collapsed into one monotone u64 'recency' in the edit-log/journal section, kept sorted; model retractions as append-only [chunk_id, op, tx] facts. 'Serve current state' and 'as-of T' become a deterministic filter over tx ids; a survivor/historical split keeps hot current-state scans off cold history.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/journal.rs (recency + fact tuples), search.rs (as-of filter before scoring)
nest_recommendations.impact: Adds the temporal/time-travel pillar deterministically without mutating frozen sections; historical versions compact into denser blocks that the trained dict compresses well.

nest_recommendations.idea: ALP + FastLanes-style transposed bitpacking as the principled embedding quantization successor and SIMD-path unifier. Evaluate ALP (lossless float) and the 04261537 transposed bitpacking layout so one scalar decode kernel auto-vectorizes across avx2/neon/scalar -- potentially collapsing nest's three SIMD dot paths into one portable kernel while shrinking embeddings better than naive f16/int8 without recall loss. Gate strictly on keeping cheap random decode for the mmap hot path.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new alp.rs, embedding-only), crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/ (unified kernel evaluation)
nest_recommendations.impact: Could improve embedding size at zero recall cost and reduce SIMD-path maintenance surface. Higher risk: must not break direct-from-mmap f32 scoring.

compression_wins: Trained cross-chunk ZSTD dictionary on chunks_canonical/spans/provenance: captures repeated names/boilerplate across PT-BR articles that per-section level-19 zstd cannot see today. Biggest single lever; improves every zstd-using preset (compressed/tiny/hybrid) at zero recall cost since embeddings are excluded.

Delta + SIMD bit-packing (SIMD-BP128/StreamVByte) on chunk_ids and chunks_original_spans: 1-4 bits/integer vs zstd's byte-granular framing overhead on short monotone int arrays; directly shrinks the tiny preset's structural overhead while decoding faster than memcpy.

FSST on canonical text: ~2-3x ratio with per-string random-access decode -- compresses the cite/materialize path's working bytes without forcing whole-frame inflation, a better space/latency tradeoff than zstd frames for citation reopen.
EWAH run-length bitmaps for tombstone/liveness/doc-presence sets: near-free compression of sparse boolean id-sets with a hard never->0.1%-larger guarantee, scannable in compressed form off mmap.

Ribbon filters instead of Bloom in the bm25/zonemap region: ~7 vs ~10 bits/key at equal false-positive rate -- ~30% smaller membership index, compact probabilistic substitute for an exact term dictionary.

Per-block content-addressed structural sharing / dedup: duplicate chunks, embeddings, and index nodes across versions or similar corpora collapse to one physical block, so a multi-version or multi-corpus .nest pays once -- dedup-as-compression for whole evolving repos/databases.

Per-section Analyze-and-pick codec selection: always emits the smallest available codec per section (raw/zstd/zstd+dict/delta-bitpack/fsst), squeezing every section to its best lightweight scheme instead of a fixed per-preset choice.

Compaction-time re-compression cycle: cheap appends absorb edits, then a deterministic compact re-runs the trained dict, re-quantizes embeddings (int8/f16), drops dead chunks, and rebuilds indexes to the smallest preset -- so edited corpora periodically re-derive a minimal maximally-compressed container instead of bloating.
ALP lossless float compression for embeddings (evaluate carefully): potential shrink below naive f16/int8 with no recall loss, only if random decode stays cheap enough for the mmap SIMD hot path.

LSM-concat recency compaction for history: store full edit history as one append-only sorted run that compacts/dedups instead of N snapshots, so old versions migrate to denser deeper blocks that the trained dict compresses well -- compact way to store full temporal history.
watch_outs: Never zstd/dictionary-compress or heavyweight-encode the embeddings section: it is scored f32/f16/i8 directly from mmap on the hot path. Any embedding codec MUST keep cheap random decode (ALP/FastLanes may qualify; zstd and FSST do not). nest already correctly bans zstd on embeddings -- preserve that invariant in every new codec.

Licensing traps: datahike/datascript are EPL-1.0 (weak-copyleft) -- learn the content-addressed tree and IStorage ideas, do NOT vendor Clojure source. upscaledb is GPLv3 -- reimplement from papers; use the Apache-2.0/patent-free lemire/simdcomp and streamvbyte (and the permissive Rust ports) instead. rocksdb is Apache/GPLv2 dual -- clean-room Ribbon from the public paper, use the zstd crate's native ZDICT bindings, never vendor rocksdb. xtdb is MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft) -- reimplement trie/zone-map/recency. buntdb, duckdb, tigerbeetle are MIT/MIT/Apache-2.0 (safe to adapt). The small permissive Rust core must stay uncontaminated.

Determinism is a hard law: ZDICT must be pinned to a fixed zstd version and fed sorted/identical sampled input; the Analyze-and-pick sampler must be seeded/ordered; EWAH/Ribbon/delta-bitpack must use fixed block sizes and ascending id order. Any nondeterminism breaks 'same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file' and reproducible builds.

Additive-only within v1: only consume reserved encoding ids 4-255 and section ids 0x09+; old readers must fail closed (UnsupportedSectionEncoding / MissingRequiredSection) on unknown ids. Do NOT bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION unless an existing field changes meaning (a true v2). The edit journal and zone-maps must be optional sections, not changes to the frozen six.

No panics in library code: all new codecs and the journal must return typed thiserror NestError/RuntimeError, including on malformed/truncated/adversarial inputs (mirror the existing negative_zstd/negative_int8/negative_fp16 test discipline). Ribbon/Bloom false positives must never produce wrong answers -- the mandatory exact cosine rerank is the safety net; keep it unconditional.

Offline + single-file by construction: konserve-style pluggable KV backends, xtdb object-storage/distribution, rocksdb remote caching, and buntdb's whole-dataset-in-RAM model all violate nest's model. Adapt only the on-disk/in-process algorithm; drop distribution; keep base sections mmap-resident and hold only journal deltas in RAM (do not load the whole corpus into memory).

File-hygiene cap: each new codec (zstd_dict, delta_bitpack, fsst, ewah, alp) and journal.rs must stay <=300 lines (333 hard cap), single-responsibility. The Analyze-and-pick estimator and Ribbon construction are the most likely to bloat -- split estimator/codec cleanly.

Build-CPU cost asymmetry is acceptable but bounded: Ribbon construction is ~4-5x Bloom, ZDICT training and FSST table-building add a build pass, ALP/transposed-bitpacking add kernel complexity. nest builds in Python offline so one-time build cost is fine, but it must not regress the runtime hot path or the deterministic-build reproducibility guarantee.

Quantization/lossy interactions with content_hash: content_hash is over decoded canonical sections and must stay STABLE across encodings for non-quantized sections. Lossy embedding codecs (int8 today, ALP-exception paths tomorrow) already make content_hash encoding-dependent for embeddings -- keep the documented rule that content_hash equality holds only for non-quantized sections, and do not let a new text codec accidentally change decoded bytes.

CJK/Thai tokenizer gap compounds with bm25 skip-filters: a Ribbon/Bloom term filter built on the current word-segmented tokenizer inherits its degradation on CJK/Thai. Do not let the skip-filter silently drop candidates for those languages -- ensure the filter is advisory (skip only) with exact rerank as backstop, and flag the tokenizer as the real fix.

categories.name: fulltext-search
categories.focus: full-text and lexical search engines (inverted index, BM25, edge cases)

repos.one_liner: Java full-text search library whose default codec compresses inverted-index postings with delta-coded, block-bit-packed integers (FOR/PForDelta over 128-doc blocks), stores term dictionaries as a shared-prefix/suffix FST (now Trie), and accelerates top-k BM25 with Block-Max WAND skipping over impact-block skip lists.
repos.core_innovation: Sorted integer lists (doc ids, freqs) are never stored raw: they are delta-encoded then bit-packed in fixed 128-value blocks using Frame-Of-Reference (FOR for docs, Patched-FOR/PForDelta for freqs/positions), with a VInt/group-varint tail. This single idea -- decompose a monotone integer column into delta + per-block minimal-bit-width packing -- is the workhorse that shrinks postings 4-10x while keeping SIMD-friendly fixed-width decode.
key_techniques: Delta (gap) encoding of sorted doc-id postings before any packing
FOR / PForDelta: 128-value blocks bit-packed with PackedInts at the minimal bitsPerValue, with outliers patched separately
byte-aligned bitsPerValue rounding (to 8/16/32) tuned by acceptableOverheadRatio for fast random-access decode
VInt / group-varint tail encoding for the sub-128 remainder of each postings list
FST (minimal acyclic subsequential transducer, Mihov/Maurel) for term dict with BOTH prefix and suffix sharing; recently a byte-keyed Trie in blocktree
BlockTree / burst-trie term dict: in-memory FST/Trie index over on-disk variable-length term blocks (25-48 terms) sharing a common prefix
Block-Max WAND: per-block max impact (pruned (tf,dl) pairs) in hierarchical skip lists (8/64/512/4096) to skip decoding whole blocks during top-k
int8/int4 scalar quantization with per-vector confidence-interval calibration, two int4 values packed per byte
repos.nest_application: Target nest-runtime bm25/codec.rs and bm25/index.rs (the 0x08 section). Today to_bytes() writes each posting as raw little-endian (u32 doc, u32 tf) -- 8 bytes/posting, zero compression -- and search() does exhaustive-OR over every posting. Adapt three layers additively: (1) replace per-term postings encoding with delta-coded doc ids + deterministic bit-packing of 128-doc blocks at minimal byte-aligned bitsPerValue plus a varint tail; tf gets its own bit-packed block. This is a pure encoding change to section 0x08 (bump only BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION, NOT NEST_FORMAT_VERSION, since the section is optional/additive), cutting the bm25 section several-fold -- directly serving the compress-more-than-everyone north star and shrinking the hybrid preset. (2) Replace the raw length-prefixed alphabetical term list with shared-prefix front-coding (store common-prefix-len + suffix per term; already alphabetical so deterministic) -- a small no-new-dependency win before a full FST. (3) Add per-block max-impact metadata so search() does Block-Max WAND skipping instead of exhaustive OR, cutting search-text latency; the mandatory exact-cosine rerank in nest's search contract is unaffected since BMW only reorders/skips candidate generation. All three preserve repr(C) little-endian, determinism (alphabetical terms, seeded), and never-panic typed errors.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central: postings delta+block-bitpacking is the canonical lossless compression for the exact integer column nest currently stores raw (u32 doc, u32 tf) in section 0x08, plus front-coding/FST for term strings. Both shrink bm25_index and the hybrid preset with zero recall loss and zero new dependencies -- squarely the compress-more-than-everyone mandate.
repos.perf_notes: FOR/PForDelta in 128-value blocks is SIMD-friendly: fixed-width packing lets a vectorized unpack decode a whole block branch-free (Lucene uses its vector API); nest can decode with scalar shifts now and add an AVX2/NEON unpack later via its existing simd dispatcher. Byte-aligned bitsPerValue trades a few bits for faster random access -- relevant since nest mmaps and decodes on the hot path. Block-Max WAND cuts top-k query time to ~10-20% of exhaustive OR in production reports but degrades faster as k grows. int4 quantization halves int8 storage (8x vs f32) at ~30% slower scoring when bit-packed.
repos.license: Apache License 2.0 (permissive; format/algorithms free to clean-room reimplement in Rust, no copyleft contamination)

repos.one_liner: A Lucene-class Rust full-text search library whose inverted index stores posting lists as interlaced 128-doc blocks of delta-encoded, SIMD-bitpacked doc ids and bitpacked term frequencies, fronted by an FST term dictionary and a Block-Max-WAND skip list.
repos.core_innovation: 128-doc block posting lists with delta+SIMD-bitpacking and a Block-Max-WAND skip list, fronted by an FST term dictionary.
key_techniques: 128-doc block posting layout: delta+bitpacking on doc ids, bitpacking on term frequencies, interlaced to avoid pointer chasing
minimal per-block bit-width b = ceil(log2(max+1)); value = min + fetch_bits(num_bits*i..)
VInt fallback for the incomplete trailing block (1-127 docs)
SIMD bitpacking (BitPacker4x SSE3 128-int, BitPacker8x AVX2 256-int, scalar fallback) at ~5-7 billion int/s
FST term dictionary (BurntSushi fst): term -> TermOrdinal, ordinal mod block size locates one TermInfo block to decode
skip list with per-block fieldnorm_id + max_term_freq enabling Block-Max-WAND top-k pruning
fast-field columnar codecs: bitpacking + GCD divisor + linear/blockwise-linear interpolation over a min_value baseline
LZ4/Zstd block-compressed document store kept separate from the index
repos.nest_application: Rewrite nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs (and the Posting/TermEntry model in index.rs) to replace the current raw fixed-width u32 (doc, tf) pair encoding with tantivy-style 128-doc blocks: per term, delta-encode the already-doc-sorted posting doc ids and bitpack at minimal per-block width, bitpack the parallel tf block, and VInt the trailing partial block. This is a pure section-0x08 payload codec change behind BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION (bump it; section id and additive v1 format are untouched), so it respects the FROZEN container. Term order stays alphabetical (already deterministic) -- optionally front the term-string region with an fst-crate FST to shrink it and get prefix lookups. Keep a scalar bitpacking kernel in nest-runtime/src/simd to honor the offline/repr(C)/LE/no-panic constraints (only vendor the bitpacking crate if its scalar fallback is acceptable). Add a per-block max_term_freq plus doc_length-derived bound to enable Block-Max-WAND in bm25/index.rs::search, cutting the full-posting scan that today touches every Posting. Keep files under the 300-line cap by leaving the block codec in codec.rs and putting WAND in a new wand.rs.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct. Today nest spends a flat 8 bytes per posting (u32 doc + u32 tf) plus u32 doc_lengths, the dominant cost in the bm25_index section. Delta+bitpacking typically collapses doc ids to 4-8 bits each on dense corpora and tf to 2-4 bits (most tf are 1-2), a 4-8x shrink of the dominant posting array, advancing the 'compress more than everyone' north star for the hybrid/tiny presets. The zstd wrapper over the now-bitpacked section adds little extra -- bitpacked integers are already near entropy-optimal, so this is real structural compression, not just a general codec pass.
repos.perf_notes: bitpacking crate hits ~5.3-7 billion int/s compress and ~5.5-6.5 billion int/s decompress (SSE3/AVX2); delta decode ~5 billion int/s. A scalar fallback exists and is selected at runtime, so determinism + portability hold (nest can ship a scalar kernel matching its existing SIMD-dispatch pattern). Block-Max-WAND turns BM25 from O(all postings) into early-terminating top-k, helping amortize the ~300-500ms search-text python boot overhead by making the scan negligible. Bitpacked blocks decode straight off mmap (fetch_bits over a block) with no per-value branching, matching nest's mmap-and-score hot path.

repos.one_liner: A from-scratch C++ in-memory typo-tolerant lexical search engine whose inverted index is an Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) over tokens with Frame-of-Reference bit-packed posting lists, pointer-tagged compact lists for short postings, incremental trie-Levenshtein fuzzy traversal, and relevance encoded as a single sortable 64-bit integer.
repos.core_innovation: Posting lists are compressed with Frame-of-Reference (FOR) bit-packing: each block stores a min base m, then packs (value - m) deltas at the minimal bit-width b = required_bits(M - m) for that block. This is a self-contained, branch-light integer codec that compresses sorted doc-ids and token positions to near entropy while still allowing random access (at(i)) and binary search (lower_bound) directly on the packed bytes without full decompression -- exactly the "compress AND still serve from the packed form" property nest needs on its scoring hot path.
key_techniques: Frame-of-Reference (FOR) bit-packing: per-block min base + adaptive bit-width b=required_bits(M-m) over delta-from-min, sized via for_compressed_size_bits() (lib for.h)

compact_posting_list_t: interleaved [num_offsets, off1..offn, id] records in a single uint32 flex-array for short lists, avoiding per-list block overhead
Low-bit pointer tagging (ptr|1) to distinguish compact vs full posting list at zero extra storage; IS_COMPACT/RAW_PTR/COMPACT_PTR macros mask the LSB
Relevance packed into one 64-bit int via bit-shifts (word-presence high bits, then unique-word count, typo cost, proximity, exact match, position, synonym) so ranking is a single integer compare
Adaptive Radix Tree node4/node16/node48/node256 upgrading node type as fanout grows, leaves holding sorted_array ids + offset_index + raw offsets

Trie-Levenshtein fuzzy search: descend ART carrying parent's DP cost-row, compute child row from insert/delete/substitute min, prune subtrees by max-word-length and length-delta bound; O(k*nodes) not O(terms)

repos.one_liner: A C++ full-text + columnar search engine whose Manticore Columnar Library (MCL) compresses attributes with per-block adaptive encoding (const / table-dictionary / delta+bitpack / generic) plus min-max zone maps and a PGM learned secondary index, while full-text postings use VLN (variable-length number) delta encoding and the docstore stores original text in LZ4-compressed fixed-size blocks.
repos.core_innovation: Per-block adaptive codec selection: data is cut into fixed-size blocks (a few hundred to ~1024 rows) and for EACH block independently the encoder picks the cheapest scheme from a small menu - const (1 value when all equal), table/dictionary (store a <256-entry value table + small indices when low cardinality), delta+bitpack (FastPFOR-style: subtract a base, bitpack residuals to minimal bit-width), or generic raw fallback - and writes a tiny per-block min-max header so a scan can skip the whole compressed block without decoding when the filter range cannot match. VLN (varint) delta encoding of doc-ids and positions in inverted postings (.spd doclists, .spp hitlists)
PGM-index (Piecewise Geometric Model): learned piecewise-linear key->position index, dominates B-tree space by orders of magnitude

repos.one_liner: A C full-text/secondary-index engine for Redis whose inverted index is a custom block-structured posting list using delta+varint gap coding with pluggable per-schema encoder variants, backed by a HyperLogLog-driven adaptive numeric range tree.

Pluggable encoder family by IndexFlags: DocIdsOnly, FreqsOnly, FieldsOnly, Full - write only fields the schema needs

TF*docRank pre-folded into stored hit score so only IDF applied at query time (cheaper BM25/TF-IDF)

HyperLogLog (6-bit precision ~13% error) for per-node cardinality, depth-dependent split threshold 16<<(depth*2) capped 2500

separated document-length stream: doclen stored once per doc in its own postlist-like structure, never repeated per term-posting

Immutable append-only segment model enabling content-addressing and aggressive caching

The remote/IPFS Directory is OUT of scope (nest is offline-by-construction, never opens a socket), but its block-addressable philosophy validates nest's mmap-and-skip design and could later inform a zstd block index for the canonical text section so one chunk decompresses without inflating the whole section.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission for "compress more than everyone": bm25_index (0x08) is nest's least-compressed section - raw 8 bytes per posting plus uncompressed UTF-8 terms. Delta+bitpacked postings typically cut posting bytes 3-6x and an FST term dictionary cuts dictionary bytes further while adding prefix/range query capability. Because postings are read by the lexical path (not the SIMD dot-product hot path), they can be compressed freely, unlike embeddings - pure upside for the hybrid and tiny presets.
repos.license: Summa itself is AGPL-3.0 (do not vendor its source). The reusable building blocks are permissive and re-implementable: the fst crate (BurntSushi) is MIT/Apache-2.0; delta/varint/zigzag, SIMD bitpacking, and Block-Max WAND are public algorithms and Tantivy itself is MIT. Reimplement from algorithm descriptions, do not copy AGPL code.
repos.perf_notes: SIMD bitpacking decodes fixed 128-doc blocks branch-free, pairing with nest's existing AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatcher in nest-runtime; the same dispatch pattern can host a bitpack decode kernel. Block-Max WAND turns full-posting scans into skips, cutting the per-query work that currently dominates search-text. The 32KB-chunk + prefetch caching is irrelevant to nest (the OS page cache already demand-pages the mmapped file), so skip it. FST lookups are O(query-term-length) automaton walks over far less memory than a HashMap, friendly to mmap-off-disk.

repos.repo: toshi-search/Toshi (thin REST/Raft server over the Tantivy search library; the transferable codecs live in Tantivy + its tantivy-columnar / bitpacker / sstable / fst subcrates)
repos.one_liner: Toshi is an Elasticsearch-style HTTP/Raft frontend over Tantivy, whose value to nest is Tantivy's segment codec stack: FST term dictionaries, BP128 delta+bitpacked posting blocks with VInt remainders, 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorms, and an auto-selecting columnar fast-field codec (constant/GCD/bitpacked/blockwise).
repos.core_innovation: Block-wise posting-list compression: split each posting list into fixed 128-doc blocks, delta-encode doc_ids within a block, bitpack each block to the minimum bit-width needed (num_bits derived from the block max), and VInt-encode the final partial block; pair this with a per-term skip header so you can binary-search blocks and decode only the block you need. Tantivy generalizes the same min+num_bits bitpacking idea to columnar data and auto-picks the cheapest codec (constant when all values equal, GCD when they share a divisor, plain bitpacked otherwise) at serialize time, so the file always carries the smallest representation without the reader needing to know which was chosen.
key_techniques: BP128: per-block (128 docs) delta-encode doc_ids then bitpack at block-local num_bits = bits(max_delta); store one num_bits byte + block min
VInt (LEB128-style variable-byte) for the trailing partial block under 128 elements, avoiding a wasted full-width block
Per-term skip list / block headers (first doc_id + byte offset per block) enabling block-skip and future block-max WAND without decoding the whole list
FST (finite-state transducer, fst crate) term dictionary: term -> TermOrdinal -> TermInfo, giving shared-prefix term compression and ordered prefix/range iteration
1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm encoding: doc length compressed to a single byte (small values exact) instead of a raw u32 doc_length
Columnar auto-codec selection: probe constant / GCD / bitpacked, emit whichever is smallest, recorded in column metadata so decode stays uniform
min_value + bitpacked-residual columnar layout giving O(1) random access (min + fetch_bits(num_bits*id..)) directly off mmap
BlockedBitpacker: bitpacking in 128-element blocks so each block adapts its bit-width to local value range
repos.nest_application: Target nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs + index.rs, which today serialize section 0x08 as raw fixed-width pairs (Posting{doc:u32, tf:u32} = 8 bytes/posting, no deltas) plus doc_lengths as raw u32. Adapt three Tantivy codecs, all deterministic and additive within format v1 (no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump since the 0x08 payload is internal, gated by BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION 1->2): (1) replace each term's postings with sorted-doc delta + BP128-style block bitpacking (block num_bits byte + bitpacked deltas + VInt tail), cutting the dominant posting cost roughly 2-6x on real corpora; (2) replace per-doc doc_lengths: Vec<u32> with a single min+num_bits bitpacked column (the columnar trick), typically 1-2 bytes/doc instead of 4, or go further with the 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm; (3) optionally replace the alphabetical term list + 4-byte length prefixes with a front-coded / shared-prefix term block (the FST idea in its simplest sorted-prefix form) to shrink the dictionary. Keep tf as a parallel bitpacked stream. All structures stay seeded/sorted so builds remain byte-identical, and the existing exact-cosine rerank means BM25 stays a candidate generator so lossy fieldnorm quantization is safe. A small bitpacker (min + num_bits + LE u64 word packing) is ~60-100 LOC, under the 300-line file cap, and reusable later for HNSW neighbor-id lists (section 0x07) and future columnar metadata.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on the north star. The BM25 index is currently one of nest's least-compressed sections (8 bytes/posting, 4 bytes/doc, fully raw). Block delta+bitpacking plus a bitpacked doc-length column is a proven, lossless, mmap-friendly win that shrinks section 0x08 several-fold while preserving exact-rerank correctness; the same min+num_bits columnar bitpacker is the reusable primitive for compressing any integer-id section (HNSW edges, chunk-id maps) under nest's hot-path mmap constraint.
repos.perf_notes: BP128 / blocked bitpacking is SIMD-friendly: Tantivy decodes 128-doc blocks with SSE2-vectorized bitpacking (the bitpacking crate has AVX2/SSE paths; a scalar word-at-a-time unpack is the portable fallback, matching nest's existing AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatch philosophy). Decode is branch-light and cache-friendly because each block is contiguous; random access via min+fetch_bits is a single memory fetch per value. Bitpacking touches far fewer bytes than raw u32 arrays, so the mmap/page-cache footprint and cold-read I/O both drop, which matters more than raw CPU for nest's off-disk model. Determinism holds: bit-width is a pure function of the sorted data, so identical input yields byte-identical packed output.
repos.license: Toshi: MIT. Tantivy and subcrates (bitpacker, columnar, sstable, fst): MIT. fst crate (Andrew Gallant): Unlicense/MIT. All permissive and vendorable; nest can cleanly reimplement the algorithms without pulling the heavy tantivy dependency, keeping the rust core small and offline.

repos.one_liner: A sub-millisecond, sharded, real-time full-text + vector search engine in Rust (Apache-2.0) whose lexical core stores posting lists as roaring-bitmap-compressed doc-id sets with delta+VINT-encoded term positions, ranked by BM25F/BM25F_Proximity via Document-at-a-Time traversal with improved Block-Max WAND, MaxScore, galloping and SIMD set intersection, served from one on-disk format in either RAM or mmap mode.
repos.core_innovation: A production lexical index whose byte layout is identical in RAM and on mmap'd disk (switchable via an AccessType flag), so the inverted index is served straight off the file exactly like nest's embeddings already are. The winning combination of compact-AND-fast: roaring-bitmap posting lists (doc-id sets) + a separate delta-compressed VINT position stream + Block-Max WAND skip metadata, traversed Document-at-a-Time so no large intermediate result sets ever materialize.
key_techniques: Roaring bitmaps for posting lists: per-65536-doc-chunk hybrid array/bitmap/run containers, giving compressed doc-id sets that allow hardware SIMD AND/OR directly on the compressed form (no full decode)
SIMD vector intersection and union of compressed bitmap posting lists on both x86-64 (AVX2) and AArch64 (NEON), the same two-arch dispatch nest already runs for dot products
Galloping (exponential) intersection for skewed posting-list size ratios, complementing SIMD merge for balanced lists
Improved Block-Max WAND + MaxScore: per-block max-impact upper bounds let top-k pruning skip whole blocks whose best possible BM25 cannot enter the heap
Document-at-a-Time (DAAT) traversal scoring one doc fully across all query terms, bounding memory vs Term-at-a-Time accumulators
Term positions delta-compressed then VINT (variable-byte) encoded as a SEPARATE stream from doc-ids, enabling phrase/proximity (BM25F_Proximity) without bloating the doc-id bitmaps
Zstandard-compressed JSON document store (docstore.bin) decoupled from index files (index.bin doc-ids+positions, index.json meta, delete.bin tombstones)
Tombstone-based real-time delete (delete.bin, recoverable until compaction) so every doc is searchable immediately, before/during commit
repos.nest_application: nest already ships an optional bm25_index section (0x08) in nest-runtime::bm25::Bm25Index. Steal three layers into it additively (0x08 internals can evolve without a NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump): (1) in nest-format/src/sections + encoding, replace any plain doc-id list inside 0x08 with roaring-bitmap-encoded posting lists plus a SEPARATE delta+VINT position stream; this is the single biggest size win for the lexical section and keeps it serveable straight off mmap, matching nest's read-from-disk discipline. (2) in nest-runtime::bm25, add Block-Max WAND + MaxScore top-k pruning with per-block max-impact bounds stored alongside each posting list; this slashes query cost and is safe because bm25 only needs to surface candidates for reciprocal-rank fusion before nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank. (3) reuse nest-runtime's EXISTING simd dispatcher (AVX2/NEON/scalar) for bitmap AND/OR intersection, so adding integer set-ops is incremental, not a new subsystem. Preserve determinism by keeping alphabetical term order and a single non-sharded global-stats index. The zstd JSON docstore maps onto nest's already-zstd-encoded chunks_canonical, so that piece is already solved and serves only as validation.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission for "compress more than everyone" on the lexical/text path. Roaring bitmaps are a near-optimal compressed encoding for sparse-to-dense doc-id sets (array containers for sparse terms, bitmap for dense, run containers for contiguous runs) and routinely beat plain VINT/delta posting lists while STILL supporting SIMD set ops without full decode, so compression and serve-speed are not in tension, exactly nest's requirement. The separate delta+VINT position stream keeps proximity ranking from inflating the doc-id bitmaps. For nest's bm25_index (0x08) this is the highest-leverage size reduction for the text index, complementing (not touching) the embeddings hot path which stays raw f32/f16/int8 for direct SIMD scoring.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (permissive). Roaring bitmap is itself a published standardized format with permissive Rust crates (e.g. roaring-rs), so nest can reimplement or vendor without GPL contamination. WARNING: do NOT adopt SeekStorm's sharding; it makes BM25 scores non-deterministic and non-comparable across shards (per-shard avg doc length, df, posting-list length, load-balanced non-deterministically), which would break nest's byte-identical reproducible builds. Keep a single deterministic index with global stats and alphabetical term order; steal the encoding, pruning, and SIMD set-ops only.
repos.perf_notes: Claims sub-millisecond queries and ~20x Lucene throughput; reported ~40,000 docs/sec indexing on 5M-doc Wikipedia, and 4-6x faster indexing / 3x shorter query latency from intra-query shard parallelism. SIMD intersection runs on x86-64 AVX2 and AArch64 NEON, the same targets nest already supports. Index latency and size grow linearly with doc count while RAM stays roughly constant in mmap mode, enabling billion-scale indices. nest should take the per-document deterministic single-index path, not the shard topology.

repos.one_liner: A lightweight schema-less search backend in Rust that pairs a RocksDB inverted index (term -> packed 32-bit IID arrays) with a per-bucket memory-mapped BurntSushi-fst Finite-State Transducer for typo-tolerant autocomplete, returning external identifiers rather than documents and running in a few MB of RAM.
repos.core_innovation: Decouple the ranked inverted index from the lexical/fuzzy lookup layer: postings live in a compact KV index (term -> packed u32 ids), and a separate immutable memory-mapped FST holds only the vocabulary for prefix/Levenshtein expansion, with all term/document identity collapsed to 32-bit ids so raw strings never sit on the hot path.
key_techniques: OID<->IID 32-bit id indirection so postings are u32 arrays not strings (30-40% vs 64-bit)
9-byte radix key [idx<1B>|bucket<4B>|route<4B>] of XxHash32 hashes, little-endian
Term-To-IIDs postings as raw little-endian u32 arrays; IID-To-Terms reverse map for GC
Immutable mmap'd BurntSushi fst::Set per bucket, lexicographic insertion required
FST consolidation tasker: buffer word push/pop, periodic sorted-merge rebuild to fresh on-disk FST
fst_levenshtein automaton for typo tolerance + FST prefix scan for autocomplete, as exact-match fallback
Language-aware lexer: stopword-count for long text / n-gram guess for short text, ISO-639-3 stopword stripping, word-level only
RAM write-buffering + RocksDB atomic delete_range() flush to minimize SSD write amplification
repos.nest_application: nest-format gets a redesign target for the optional bm25_index (0x08) section: store postings as the term -> sorted u32 chunk-ordinal arrays exactly like Sonic's Term-To-IIDs, with terms keyed by a deterministic hash (nest already mandates alphabetical term order, which doubles as the FST/lexicographic-insertion guarantee).
