The chunk-ordinal indirection mirrors OID<->IID: nest already has chunk_ids, so the bm25 section only needs to carry u32 ordinals + per-term doc-freq, never raw strings, and these arrays are highly zstd-friendly (zstd is allowed on non-embedding sections, so delta+zstd over sorted u32 postings is a direct extreme-compression win). nest-runtime's bm25::Bm25Index can mmap these postings straight off disk (Sonic proves mmap'd lexical lookup at a few MB RAM) and feed the existing reciprocal-rank-fusion + mandatory cosine rerank path. Crucially, nest can add an OPTIONAL FST/vocabulary blob (a new RESERVED section id 0x09+, additive-only) built with the BurntSushi fst crate to deliver typo-tolerant and prefix SUGGEST over chunk vocabulary, run as a Levenshtein/prefix automaton in nest-runtime, then resolve expanded terms back into the BM25 postings before rerank. This addresses nest's known CJK/word-segmentation gap path (language-aware lexer + ISO-639-3 stopword tables) and gives nest-cli search-text a fuzzy mode. The immutable consolidation model (rebuild FST from sorted merge) fits nest's frozen/deterministic-build ethos perfectly: build it once in python, freeze it, mmap in rust.
repos.compression_relevance: Direct: collapsing terms and documents to 32-bit hashed ids and storing postings as sorted little-endian u32 arrays (Sonic's 30-40% saving over 64-bit ids) is exactly the kind of dictionary+integer-indirection that makes the bm25_index section tiny; sorted u32 postings are ideal for delta-encoding + zstd (already permitted on non-embedding sections), so this could shrink the lexical index dramatically while staying mmap-scorable. The FST itself is a state-of-the-art compressed vocabulary representation (shared prefixes/suffixes via minimal DFA), aligning with nest's compress-more-than-everyone north star.
repos.perf_notes: ~1M messages indexed in 20MB KV + 1.4MB FST on disk, peak 28MB RAM; ~4000 PUSH/s (275us avg) and ~1000 QUERY/s (880us avg) single-thread, queries parallelize across CPUs. FST is mmap'd so vocabulary access is page-cache served, not heap-resident. Achilles heel: FST is immutable and must be fully rebuilt on vocabulary change (consolidation batched at intervals), which is fine for nest's frozen build-once model. Word-level only (no positional/phrase index) to keep the FST shallow.
repos.license: MPL-2.0 (Mozilla Public License 2.0)

repos.one_liner: A static-site full-text search engine that replaces a traditional inverted index with one approximate-membership Xor filter per document, serialized with bincode and compiled into a tiny dependency-free WASM blob.
repos.core_innovation: Invert the cost model of lexical search: instead of one global term->postings inverted index, store one tiny per-document approximate-set-membership filter (Xor filter) keyed on that document's token set, then answer a query by probing every document's filter for each query term and ranking by the count of term hits. This trades exact recall and term-frequency scoring for a drastically smaller, append-friendly index where each document's lexical footprint is a fixed ~9-10 bits per unique token rather than full postings lists.
key_techniques: Xor8 filter (xorf crate): ~9.84 bits per key, ~0.39% FPR, fingerprint = u8; membership test is f == B[h0(x)] XOR B[h1(x)] XOR B[h2(x)]

3-hash peeling construction: assign each key to one of three slots via reverse topological order over a hypergraph so the xor of three table cells reproduces the fingerprint (single static build, no incremental inserts)
BinaryFuse8 successor filter: ~9.0 bits/key, denser slot packing, faster build than classic Xor8, same xor-of-three-fingerprints probe
per-document filter granularity: one filter per doc instead of a global inverted index; query = AND of terms, rank by number of filters containing each term (score = hit count)
bincode binary serialization of the Vec of (metadata, filter) tuples, with serde derive on the filter structs
build-time stop-word stripping to shrink the keyspace plus brotli/gzip post-compression (~1KB/doc compressed)
explicit rejection of tries (10x larger) in favor of probabilistic filters; abandoned prefix search because it bloated the binary
repos.nest_application: Add an optional ultra-compact lexical mode to nest-runtime's bm25::Bm25Index path and a new encoding inside the existing bm25_index section 0x08 (still v1, additive). Build a deterministic Xor8/BinaryFuse8 filter per chunk over the chunk token set (seeded hashing + alphabetical term order to preserve determinism), serialize the filter arrays as little-endian repr(C), stored one filter per chunk_id parallel to chunk_ids. nest-format gains a 'bm25-membership' codec variant: where full BM25 postings+tf are too big, the membership-only filter gives lexical pre-filtering at ~9 bits/unique-token/chunk. In nest-runtime search-text, run the Xor probe over all chunk filters as a cheap candidate generator (AND query terms, score by hit count) feeding RRF, then the mandatory exact-cosine rerank still produces real scores, so approximation is confined to candidate generation and never leaks into returned scores, matching nest's search_contract. Unlocks a 'tiny+lexical' preset where lexical search adds only kilobytes.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission. A per-chunk Xor8/BinaryFuse8 filter encodes lexical membership at a fixed ~9-10 bits per unique token with no length-dependent postings or varint gaps, an order of magnitude smaller than full BM25 postings+term frequencies, and it compounds with nest's existing zstd on non-embedding sections. It is the smallest way to keep a lexical/keyword channel alive in the 'tiny' preset, shrinking the bm25_index footprint while still enabling hybrid search.
repos.license: MIT (tinysearch); xorf crate MIT/Apache-2.0; BinaryFuse algorithm (Graf/Lemire) permissively published
repos.perf_notes: Xor/BinaryFuse probes are three random table reads plus two XORs and one compare per term: branch-light, cache-bound, data-parallel across chunks. Construction is O(n) via peeling but build-time only (python side), so the Rust hot path stays read-only over mmap. Filters can be probed in place from the mmapped 0x08 section with zero deserialization if laid out as flat little-endian arrays. Xor8 FPR ~0.39% is acceptable because the mandatory exact-cosine rerank removes false positives.

repos.one_liner: A Rust+WebAssembly static-site full-text search engine that builds a single self-contained binary `.st` index file (MessagePack-serialized inverted "prefix map") which a WASM blob loads in the browser to do instant prefix search with positional excerpt highlighting, no server.
repos.core_innovation: The entire search index is a single self-describing versioned binary artifact that bundles BOTH the inverted index AND the displayable content (excerpts + char offsets) so the search runtime needs nothing but the one file to return rendered, highlighted results offline. The index is keyed by BTreeMap<String, Container> (a "prefix map") where each Container is self-sufficient: from one container you derive every result for a query, and prefix queries with no exact container resolve through aliases (BTreeMap of alias-target -> score) that redirect to the nearest indexed term. The on-disk structure directly serves the query without a separate scoring pass over the corpus.
key_techniques: Inverted index as BTreeMap<String, Container> 'prefix map' (deterministic, alphabetically ordered keys) instead of a hashmap, so iteration/serialization is stable
Self-contained Container: results: BTreeMap<EntryIndex, SearchResult> + aliases: BTreeMap<AliasTarget, Score>, so prefix/partial matches alias to indexed terms with a discounted score

Excerpts stored INLINE in the index with word offset, field (title vs contents), and char-range annotations, so the runtime returns ready-to-render highlighted snippets without touching original documents
MessagePack binary serialization via rmp-serde (compact tag-length-value, no JSON key repetition) for the .st payload
Self-describing versioned container: length-prefixed version string (e.g. 'stork-3.0.0') precedes payload; VersionedIndex::try_from dispatches to V2/V3 parsers for additive format evolution
Scoring via MATCHED_WORD_SCORE base plus configurable title_boost multiplier and exact-vs-prefix discount, precomputed at build time and stored, not recomputed at query time
rust-stemmers (Snowball) + unicode-segmentation + stopword normalization at BUILD time so query-time matching is cheap and the index conflates 'tries'->'try', 'Power'->'power'
excerpts_per_result=0 build switch that strips inline excerpts to shrink the index 20-50% (filter-only mode), trading display payload for size
repos.nest_application: Three steals for nest-format's optional bm25_index section (0x08). (1) Adopt Stork's BTreeMap<term, Container> postings layout: nest already mandates 'bm25 alphabetical term order' for determinism, so a BTreeMap-backed self-contained per-term container is a drop-in that satisfies determinism by construction and serializes stably. (2) Adopt the alias/prefix-redirect trick in nest-runtime/bm25 to add cheap prefix and stemmed-variant matching to nest's word-segmented tokenizer (a known gap) without storing full substring postings: store only canonical terms plus an alias table mapping prefixes/stems to canonical term ids with a discount score; this directly mitigates nest's CJK/Thai tokenizer degradation by letting non-exact segments alias to the nearest indexed term. (3) Precompute per-doc term scores (Stork's build-time MATCHED_WORD_SCORE + boost model) so the bm25 candidate pass in nest-runtime is a pure lookup before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank, keeping the hot path allocation-light. Keep nest's own serialization (repr(C), little-endian, zstd on non-embedding sections) -- borrow the data-structure shape, NOT rmp-serde. For extreme compression: Stork's excerpts_per_result=0 'filter-only index' maps to a nest preset flag that drops any cached snippet/offset payload from bm25_index and reconstructs spans on demand from chunks_original_spans, shrinking the optional section 20-50% while citations stay intact.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real for nest's bm25 section, not the embedding hot path. Two transferable size ideas: (a) the alias/prefix-redirect table avoids materializing substring/prefix postings (Stork's docs note full substring indexing bloats the file), giving prefix search at a fraction of postings size; (b) the excerpts_per_result=0 'strip display payload, keep only the filter' mode is a clean precedent for a nest preset that drops cached snippets and reconstructs spans from chunks_original_spans, a 20-50% cut on bm25_index. Stork's actual codec (MessagePack, no entropy coder, no compression crate -- relies on the host server's gzip) is BELOW nest's bar: nest already zstd-compresses non-embedding sections, which beats raw MessagePack, so nest should NOT adopt rmp-serde. Borrow index shape and the two size tricks; nest's existing zstd + repr(C) encoding dominates Stork's on-disk format.
repos.license: Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: Stork's claim to fame is sub-millisecond browser-side search by loading the whole index into WASM linear memory and doing direct BTreeMap lookups (O(log n) key lookup + container iteration), no network round-trips after the initial index download. No SIMD, no bitpacked postings, no roaring bitmaps -- deliberately simple: build-time precomputation (stemming, scoring, excerpt extraction) trades index size for query-time CPU. Entire index resident in WASM heap, which is why >~megabyte corpora and <3-char queries get slow and the 2.0 line moved to sharded indexes (load one chunk at a time) to bound resident memory. Lesson for nest: precompute at build, keep the query path a pure lookup; but Stork's lack of bitpacked/delta-encoded postings is exactly where nest can do better.

repos.one_liner: An in-memory full-text search library whose "contextual index" replaces query-time TF-IDF with a pre-scored lexical dictionary that buckets postings by an integer relevance score (resolution), making multi-term intersections near-constant-time.
repos.core_innovation: Pre-score at index build, not query time: instead of storing one posting list per term and computing BM25/TF-IDF on the fly, FlexSearch stores `map[score_bucket][term] = [doc_ids]` where the bucket index IS the quantized relevance. Relevance is collapsed into a small integer in [0, resolution) computed from three distances (document position, partial/token distance, and contextual term-pair distance within a bidirectional window of depth d). Querying becomes: walk buckets from highest score to lowest and intersect/union the small doc-id arrays, so scoring is "already done" and ranking is just bucket order. This trades a tiny, bounded score space for eliminating per-hit float math, and it makes the score field itself compressible (a 4-bit/1-byte ordinal instead of an f32).
key_techniques: Resolution-bucketed inverted index: term -> array of `resolution` buckets, each holding doc-id lists; bucket index = quantized integer relevance (default resolution 9), so score is an ordinal not a float

Contextual pre-scoring: bidirectional moving 2-pointer window of configurable `depth` pre-computes term-pair proximity scores at build time; bidirectional flag collapses (a,b)/(b,a) pairs to halve memory
Three-distance scoring model (document distance + partial distance + contextual distance) deliberately replacing TF-IDF, yielding an integer score
complexity = resolution - threshold: a `threshold` floor prunes low-score buckets entirely from storage and from intersection, bounding both index size and query cost

Latin encoder ladder (Exact -> Normalize -> Balance -> Advanced -> Extra -> Soundex) giving ~7% to ~70% term-dictionary shrinkage via progressive phonetic normalization, collapsing many surface forms to one key
Tokenizer memory-factor taxonomy (strict 1x, forward nx, reverse 2n-1x, full n(n-1)x, tolerant 2(n-2)+2x) making the size/recall tradeoff explicit and selectable
fastupdate secondary register for O(1) delete via reverse doc->term map, plus cleanup() to compact empty slots
Fast-boot serialization: export/import the already-pre-scored dictionary so rehydration does zero recompute
repos.nest_application: Apply to nest-runtime crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25 (index.rs + codec.rs) and section 0x08. (1) CODEC WIN, additive: today codec.rs writes `Posting{doc:u32, tf:u32}` (8 bytes/posting) and search.rs recomputes BM25 floats at query time. Adopt FlexSearch's bucketing: precompute each posting's BM25 contribution at build time, quantize it into N ordinal buckets (e.g. 16, 4 bits), and store the inverted list grouped by bucket. The 4-byte tf becomes a 4-bit ordinal, shrinking section 0x08 roughly 30-40%, and doc-id lists per bucket are monotonically sortable so they zstd-delta-compress far better than interleaved (doc,tf). This stays within the 0x08 section and is gated by BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION (bump the payload version, not NEST_FORMAT_VERSION, since 0x08 is optional and additive). (2) SPEED WIN: search becomes bucket-descending iteration with early termination once top-k is filled from high buckets, removing the per-posting idf/denom float loop in index.rs:106-114; nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank then dominates less. Keep determinism via alphabetical term order (already done) plus fixed bucket boundaries. (3) TOKENIZER/CJK GAP: port the Latin normalization ladder into bm25/tokenize.rs as deterministic encoder presets (raw -> normalize-diacritics -> phonetic) to collapse surface forms and shrink the term dictionary; this directly attacks the documented bm25 tokenizer gap. (4) RRF fusion in fusion.rs already wants ranks, not raw scores, so an ordinal bucket score is a natural fit. Optional `context.depth` proximity could later be a reserved 0x09+ section.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly relevant. Quantizing the per-posting score from an f32/u32 into a small integer ordinal (resolution buckets) is the same move nest already makes for embeddings (f32 -> int8); applied to the bm25 0x08 section it cuts posting size ~30-40% before zstd, and grouping doc-ids by bucket produces monotonic, delta-friendly runs that zstd compresses much better than interleaved (doc,tf) pairs. The threshold prune further shrinks the index by dropping low-relevance postings entirely. This advances the north-star "compress more than everyone" on the lexical-index section specifically, with no recall loss on the top buckets and the exact-cosine rerank still guaranteeing real scores.
repos.perf_notes: FlexSearch reports ~50M single-term queries/sec vs 3.9k-23k for competitors, attributed entirely to pre-scored buckets eliminating query-time scoring and shrinking intersection sets. Memory scales mainly with context depth (depth 1 ~12.5MB, depth 2 ~21.5MB on Gulliver's Travels corpus); bidirectional pair-collapsing reduces it (17.9MB vs 19.0MB at depth 2). Pure JS, single-thread hot path, with optional Web Worker sharding. For nest the relevant takeaway is that ordinal scores make both storage smaller and the scan branch-predictable; no SIMD needed since the hot path becomes integer bucket iteration plus sorted-list intersection.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A pure-Rust Okapi BM25 toolkit (MIT, ~1.2M downloads) that turns text into precomputed sparse-vector embeddings via a pluggable tokenizer, with three composable layers: Embedder (text to sparse vec), Scorer (inverted-index query scoring), and SearchEngine (in-memory CRUD search).
repos.core_innovation: Treat BM25 as a precomputed sparse embedding so query-time scoring is a sparse dot product reusing the same vector primitive as dense embeddings.
key_techniques: Okapi BM25 with k1/b/avgdl params; b=0 cleanly disables length normalization (good for short, uniform chunks)
avgdl auto-fit from corpus statistics (with_fit_to_corpus) so the only stateful param is computed deterministically from the data
Sparse embedding format: TokenEmbedding { index, value } pairs, only non-zero dims stored, directly ingestible by Qdrant/Pinecone/Milvus
Hash-based token IDs (token hashed to u32/u64) instead of a term dictionary, eliminating the string->id map at the cost of possible collisions
Pluggable Tokenizer trait; DefaultTokenizer pipeline = deunicode normalization + unicode-segmentation word boundaries + stop-words removal + rust-stemmers Snowball stemming
Three-layer split Embedder/Scorer/SearchEngine, each usable independently, generic over token-id (TokenEmbedder trait) and doc-id (Document<T>)
Optional feature flags: language_detection (whichlang), parallelism (rayon batch fit), default_tokenizer toggle to drop text-proc deps
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime/src/bm25.rs (Bm25Index) should adopt the precomputed-sparse-weight model: store, in the 0x08 bm25_index section, per-chunk postings as (term_id:u32_le, weight:f16_or_quantized) sorted by alphabetical term order (nest's determinism rule already requires this), plus a small header of {k1,b,avgdl,doc_count}. This converts BM25 scoring into a sparse dot product that nest's existing SIMD dispatcher can run straight off mmap, exactly mirroring the dense f32 cosine hot path, so hybrid preset RRF fusion needs no separate scoring engine. Steal the Tokenizer trait shape into nest-runtime so the word-segmented tokenizer becomes swappable (addresses the known CJK/Thai gap) without an additive format change. Borrow deunicode+unicode-segmentation+rust-stemmers+stop-words as the default pipeline. Do NOT adopt hash-based token IDs: nest needs deterministic alphabetical term ordering and reopenable citations, so keep an explicit sorted term dictionary in-section (a sorted Vec<&str> with delta/front-coded prefix compression) to stay collision-free and byte-reproducible.
repos.compression_relevance: Medium-high: storing BM25 as precomputed sparse weights lets the 0x08 section be zstd-compressed (it is a non-embedding section, so nest's codec rules permit it) and the postings quantized (f16 or int8 weights) and front-coded/delta-coded on term_id, shrinking the lexical index dramatically versus a full inverted index with float positions. The hash-id trick is a compression idea (drop the term dictionary entirely) but conflicts with nest's determinism/citation guarantees, so nest should instead front-code the term dictionary to recover most of that space without collisions.
repos.perf_notes: Pure-Rust, no_std-friendly enough to compile to WebAssembly (proven by bm25-demo). Sparse representation keeps memory proportional to non-zero terms. Optional rayon parallelism only for batch corpus fitting; query scoring is single-pass over postings. No SIMD kernel of its own (nest would add SIMD via its existing dispatcher). In-memory only, no on-disk serialization in the upstream crate, so nest must design the on-disk 0x08 layout itself.
repos.license: MIT

synthesis.summary: Across 16 lexical engines (Lucene, Tantivy/Quickwit/Toshi/Summa, Meilisearch, Typesense, Manticore/MCL, RediSearch, Xapian, SeekStorm, Sonic, tinysearch, Stork, FlexSearch, Michael-JB/bm25) the field has converged on one canonical, near-entropy posting codec and one canonical term-dictionary structure, both of which nest is currently NOT using. nest's bm25 section (0x08) today (verified in crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs:14-39) writes every posting as a raw fixed 8 bytes (u32 doc + u32 tf), raw u32 doc_lengths (4 bytes/doc), and length-prefixed UTF-8 terms with a 4-byte length prefix each; index.rs::search (lines 101-115) does exhaustive term-at-a-time OR touching every posting. This is the single least-compressed, least-optimized section in the whole container and is squarely on the 'compress more than everyone' critical path for the hybrid and tiny presets. The state of the art replaces all three layers losslessly and deterministically: (1) postings = delta-gap doc ids + per-128-block minimal-bit-width bitpacking (FOR/PForDelta/BP128) with a varint tail, typically collapsing 8 bytes/posting to 1-2 bytes; (2) term dictionary = an FST (shared prefix AND suffix minimization, BurntSushi `fst` crate, MIT/Unlicense) that also unlocks prefix/range/typo lookup for free; (3) doc lengths = 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm or a min+bitpacked column. Query-side, Block-Max WAND / MaxScore turns the O(all postings) OR into early-terminating top-k by storing per-block max-impact bounds. Every one of these is a pure internal payload change inside the already-reserved 0x08 section gated by BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION (currently 1 in index.rs:8), needs NO NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump, stays deterministic (terms already sorted alphabetically, bit-widths are pure functions of the data), decodes branch-free off mmap (matching nest's embedding hot-path discipline), and is recall-safe because BM25 is only a candidate generator before nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The settled lexical-index stack is: FST term dictionary (term -> ordinal, mmap zero-copy, O(term-len) lookup, free prefix/range/Levenshtein scan) over 128-doc posting BLOCKS where doc ids are delta-encoded then bitpacked at each block's local minimal bit-width b=ceil(log2(max_gap+1)), term-freqs bitpacked in a parallel block stream, with a VInt/varint remainder for the trailing partial block and rare terms (df<128). A per-block skip list (last_doc_id, byte offset, max_term_freq, fieldnorm bound) drives Block-Max WAND / MaxScore dynamic top-k pruning so query cost scales with surviving blocks, not corpus size (production reports ~10-20% of exhaustive-OR time). Doc lengths compress to 1 byte via BM25 length-saturation (log-quantized fieldnorm). Roaring bitmaps (array/bitmap/run containers per 64k chunk, ~1.25 bits/doc dense) are the alternative posting encoding when SIMD set-intersection on the compressed form matters (SeekStorm, Meilisearch). The whole index is immutable, self-describing, byte-range addressable and served straight off mmap with no decompression of the whole section (Quickwit/Summa prove block-addressable lexical search; Sonic proves mmap'd FST vocab at a few MB RAM). bitpacking decode hits 5-7 billion int/s SIMD with a clean scalar fallback (the `bitpacking` crate, Tantivy's subcrate, MIT). Manticore/MCL adds per-block ADAPTIVE codec selection (const / dictionary-when-<256-uniques / delta+bitpack / raw, chosen by cheapest cost per block) plus min-max zone maps for skip-without-decode. The frontier extremes: tinysearch's per-document Xor8/BinaryFuse8 filters (~9 bits/unique-token, no postings at all) for an ultra-tiny lexical channel, and FlexSearch's build-time ordinal-bucket pre-scoring (score becomes a 4-bit ordinal, not an f32). All the reusable building blocks are permissively licensed (Tantivy/fst/bitpacking/roaring/xorf all MIT or Apache); the GPL/AGPL/SSPL daemons (Typesense, Xapian, Manticore daemon, Quickwit, Summa, RediSearch) are reference-only but their algorithms are public-domain IR and safe to clean-room in Rust.
top_innovations: Delta-gap + per-128-block minimal-bit-width bitpacking of doc ids with varint tail (FOR/PForDelta/BP128) - the universal posting codec, 4-8x lossless shrink of nest's raw 8-byte postings, deterministic, branch-free mmap decode
FST term dictionary (BurntSushi fst, MIT/Unlicense) - shared prefix+suffix minimization compresses vocab and unlocks prefix/range/Levenshtein lookup, closing the typo and CJK/Thai gaps
Block-Max WAND / MaxScore top-k pruning - turns the exhaustive term-at-a-time OR into early-terminating DAAT, recall-safe before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank
1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm - 4x shrink of the raw u32 doc_lengths array, lossless-enough under BM25 saturation
Separated doc-length stream + sorted-term front-coding - near-free dictionary shrink and a simpler stepping stone before a full FST
Per-block adaptive codec selection (const/dict/delta-bitpack/raw) + min-max zone maps (MCL) - exploits local uniformity zstd misses, reusable across all integer-id sections
Per-document Xor8/BinaryFuse8 membership filter (~9 bits/unique-token) - a kilobyte-scale lexical channel for a tiny+lexical preset, false positives killed by rerank
Build-time ordinal-bucket pre-scoring (FlexSearch) - tf becomes a 4-bit ordinal, doc ids group into delta-friendly runs, replaces per-posting float math
Roaring-bitmap posting lists with SIMD set-ops on the compressed form - near-optimal for sparse-to-dense doc-id sets, reuses the AVX2/NEON dispatcher
BM25-as-sparse-embedding (Michael-JB/bm25) - scoring becomes a sparse dot product reusing nest's SIMD dispatcher exactly like the dense cosine path

nest_recommendations.idea: Replace raw (u32 doc, u32 tf) postings with delta-gap doc ids + per-128-doc-block minimal-bit-width bitpacking + a varint tail; tf as a parallel bitpacked block. Postings are already doc-sorted (index.rs:69), so gaps are positive and small. Bump BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION 1->2 ONLY (index.rs:8); no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION change. Keep the decode kernel scalar (word-at-a-time shifts) to honor portability/never-panic, with an optional AVX2/NEON unpack later via the existing simd dispatcher.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs (rewrite to_bytes/from_bytes postings loop, lines 33-37 and 72-77); put the bitpack/unpack primitive in a new crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/bitpack.rs (~80-120 LOC, under the 300-line cap); update the layout doc-comment in bm25/mod.rs:10-28.
nest_recommendations.impact: Highest single win. Collapses the dominant posting array from 8 bytes/posting to ~1-2 bytes (4-8x) on the PT-BR corpus, shrinking section 0x08 and the hybrid/tiny presets several-fold with zero recall loss. Bitpacked ints are near entropy-optimal so it composes with (does not fight) the existing zstd-on-non-embedding pass.

nest_recommendations.idea: Quantize doc_lengths from raw u32 to a 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm (BM25 length-saturation makes the loss negligible and the exact-cosine rerank absorbs it), stored as a flat little-endian byte column. Optionally generalize to a min+num_bits bitpacked column for an exact-but-compact alternative.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs (doc_lengths write at lines 22-24 and read at 55-58); decode the quantized length back in index.rs::search where dl is read (line 109). Document the quantization table in bm25/mod.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: 4x shrink of the per-doc length array (4 bytes -> 1 byte) with no measurable ranking change after rerank. Small but free and clean.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add Block-Max WAND / MaxScore top-k pruning: store per-128-block max_term_freq (and a doc-length-derived BM25 upper bound) in the posting skip header, then make search iterate Document-at-a-Time skipping blocks that cannot enter the top-k heap, instead of the current exhaustive term-at-a-time OR over every posting.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: new crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/wand.rs (keep WAND out of index.rs to stay under 300 lines, as the extracts suggest); rewrite the scoring loop in crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/index.rs::search (lines 101-115). Block metadata is written in codec.rs alongside the bitpacked blocks.
nest_recommendations.impact: Cuts search-text query work to a fraction of corpus size, directly attacking the known latency gap. Recall-safe: BM25 only generates candidates for rrf_union (fusion.rs) before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank, so skipping/reordering candidates never changes returned scores.

nest_recommendations.idea: Replace the length-prefixed alphabetical term blob with an FST (BurntSushi `fst` crate, MIT/Unlicense, pure-Rust, no_std-friendly) built from the already-sorted terms, mapping term -> u32 term-ordinal. Deterministic by construction over sorted input. Stage it AFTER the postings codec so the two land independently.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs term loop (write lines 28-32, read 60-70) and the terms HashMap in index.rs (lines 32, 59, 78); add `fst` to crates/nest-runtime/Cargo.toml. Consider a separate bm25/dict.rs module to respect the file-size cap and single-responsibility rule.
nest_recommendations.impact: Compresses the vocabulary via shared prefix+suffix (beats front-coding) and unlocks prefix/range/typo lookup for free, closing nest's typo-tolerance and CJK/Thai gaps. Only new dependency in the set, but it is the canonical, vetted, permissive choice used by 5 of the 16 engines.

nest_recommendations.idea: Before (or instead of) the FST dependency, front-code the alphabetical term dictionary: store shared-prefix-length-with-previous-term + suffix bytes instead of a full 4-byte length prefix + full UTF-8 per term. Nearly free since terms are already sorted, zero new dependency.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/codec.rs term write (lines 28-32) and read (lines 60-70).
nest_recommendations.impact: Meaningful dictionary shrink on natural-language PT-BR vocab with no new crate; a clean stepping stone that de-risks the FST decision and is reversible.

nest_recommendations.idea: Generalize the bitpack primitive into a reusable per-block adaptive integer codec (const / dictionary-when-<256-uniques / delta+bitpack / raw, chosen per block by cheapest cost, with a tiny repr(C) LE min-max header) as a NEW additive encoding id in the reserved 4-255 range, applied to non-embedding integer sections only (postings, chunk_ids, spans), NEVER embeddings.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new module, mirror the int8.rs/float16.rs/zstd_codec.rs pattern; register an id beside SECTION_ENCODING_* in layout/mod.rs:59-62) and wire into writer/encoding_choice.rs SectionEncoding enum; decode in encoding/mod.rs::decode_payload (lines 44-55). Min-max zone maps enable skip-without-decode in the bm25 search path.
nest_recommendations.impact: Exploits local uniformity that a single global zstd pass misses (const/dict blocks collapse to a few bytes), and becomes the shared primitive for every integer-id section in the container, advancing compress-more-than-everyone beyond just bm25.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an optional ultra-compact 'membership-only' bm25 codec variant: a deterministic per-chunk Xor8/BinaryFuse8 filter (xorf crate, MIT/Apache) over the chunk token set, stored as flat little-endian arrays one filter per chunk_id, probed in place off mmap with zero deserialization. Used as a cheap candidate generator (AND query terms, score by hit count) feeding RRF; the exact-cosine rerank removes the ~0.39% false positives.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: a new codec variant selected inside section 0x08 (gated by BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION) in crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/; build-side filter construction in nest-python (O(n) peeling is build-time only). Feeds the existing fusion.rs rrf_union path.
nest_recommendations.impact: Enables a 'tiny+lexical' preset where the keyword channel costs only ~9 bits/unique-token/chunk (kilobytes total) instead of full postings, keeping lexical search alive in the smallest preset. Lossy candidate-gen only, never leaks into returned scores.

nest_recommendations.idea: Upgrade the tokenizer into a swappable pipeline with deterministic normalization presets (raw -> diacritic-fold -> Snowball stem -> optional CJK/Thai n-gram/bigram segmentation), keeping the current behavior as the default preset so builds stay byte-reproducible. Pair with FST Levenshtein lookup for typo tolerance. The exact-cosine rerank means tokenizer changes only affect candidate recall, not final scores.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/tokenize.rs (currently a single fixed function, lines 8-28); introduce a Tokenizer trait shape and presets while preserving the default. Both build (index.rs:42) and query (index.rs:97) must use the identical preset for determinism.
nest_recommendations.impact: Closes the documented CJK/Thai word-segmentation gap and adds typo/prefix search; FST-driven normalization also collapses surface forms, shrinking the dictionary. Must be opt-in per preset to preserve byte-identical reproducible builds.

compression_wins: Postings: delta-gap doc ids + per-128-block minimal-bit-width bitpacking + varint tail replaces raw 8 bytes/posting (u32 doc + u32 tf) -> ~1-2 bytes/posting, a 4-8x structural shrink of the dominant array in section 0x08. Near entropy-optimal so it stacks with the existing zstd-on-non-embedding pass for residual gains.
tf stream: most term frequencies are 1-2, so a parallel bitpacked tf block needs ~2-4 bits each vs the current full 4-byte u32 (8-16x on the tf column alone).

Doc lengths: 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm replaces raw u32 doc_lengths -> 4x shrink (4 bytes -> 1 byte per doc), lossless-enough under BM25 length saturation and fully absorbed by the exact-cosine rerank.

Term dictionary: FST (shared prefix+suffix minimization) or front-coding (shared-prefix-len + suffix) replaces full 4-byte-length-prefixed UTF-8 per term -> large vocabulary shrink on natural-language PT-BR terms, with FST also delivering prefix/typo lookup for free.

Per-block adaptive codec (const / dict<256 / delta+bitpack / raw) collapses locally-uniform integer regions to a handful of bytes that a single global zstd pass misses, applicable to postings, chunk_ids, spans, and future HNSW edge lists alike.
Ordinal-bucket pre-scoring turns the per-posting tf into a 4-bit ordinal and groups doc ids into monotonic delta-friendly runs, which then zstd-compress far better than interleaved (doc,tf) pairs.

Xor8/BinaryFuse8 per-chunk filters give a whole lexical channel at a fixed ~9 bits/unique-token with no postings/varints, an order of magnitude under full BM25, enabling a tiny+lexical preset measured in kilobytes.

Roaring bitmap posting lists (array/bitmap/run containers, ~1.25 bits/doc dense) are near-optimal for sparse-to-dense doc-id sets and still SIMD-intersectable on the compressed form, an alternative size win for dense terms. Net effect: section 0x08, today the least-compressed section in the container, becomes one of the most-compressed, advancing the compress-more-than-everyone north star specifically on the hybrid and tiny presets.
watch_outs: SeekStorm's sharding makes BM25 scores non-deterministic and non-comparable across shards (per-shard avgdl, df, posting lengths, load-balanced non-deterministically). This would break nest's byte-identical reproducible builds and global-stats ranking. Steal only the encoding/pruning/SIMD-set-ops; keep a single deterministic non-sharded index with global stats and alphabetical term order.

License hygiene: Typesense (GPL-3.0), Xapian (GPL-2.0+), Manticore daemon (GPL-3.0), Quickwit (AGPL-3.0), Summa (AGPL-3.0), RediSearch (RSALv2/SSPLv1, not OSI-open) must NOT be vendored or copied. Their algorithms (FOR, delta+varint, BMW, range trees, trie-Levenshtein) are public IR and safe to clean-room in Rust. Only depend on the permissive building blocks: fst (MIT/Unlicense), bitpacking (MIT), roaring-rs (Apache/MIT), xorf (MIT/Apache), the Michael-JB bm25 ideas (MIT).

Any FST or quantization change to section 0x08 must stay an INTERNAL payload change gated by BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION (index.rs:8, currently 1), NOT a NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump: 0x08 is optional/additive and its section meaning is unchanged. Bumping the frozen format version for an internal codec swap would violate the additive-only v1 rule.

Determinism must be preserved end to end: bit-widths must be a pure function of the sorted data, FST built over already-alphabetical terms (canonical), bucket boundaries fixed, hashing seeded. Do NOT adopt hash-based token IDs (Michael-JB/bm25, Sonic) for the canonical dictionary: collisions plus non-stable ordering break byte-reproducibility and reopenable nest:// citations. Keep an explicit sorted term dictionary.

Lossy tricks (fieldnorm quantization, ordinal-bucket scores, Xor-filter false positives, tokenizer normalization changes) are only safe because BM25 is a candidate generator before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank. They must NEVER leak into the returned score and must NOT touch the embedding hot path (embeddings stay raw f32/f16/int8 for direct SIMD scoring per nest's codec rules). Do not apply stream/columnar compression to embeddings.

SIMD bitpacking is optional, not required: ship a scalar word-at-a-time unpack first (matches the existing avx2/neon/scalar dispatcher and the never-panic + portability constraints), add vectorized unpack later. Do not introduce a hard dependency on a crate whose scalar fallback is unacceptable or which can panic in library code.

Skip the remote/IPFS/network Directory ideas (Summa, Quickwit object-store, Sonic RocksDB, SeekStorm RAM-vs-mmap server) and the 32KB-chunk HTTP caching: nest is offline-by-construction and never opens a socket; the OS page cache already demand-pages the mmapped file. Borrow only the block-addressable on-disk layout philosophy.

Respect file hygiene: keep the block codec in codec.rs/bitpack.rs, WAND in wand.rs, FST dict in dict.rs, each single-responsibility and under the 300-line cap (333 hard). Do NOT adopt rmp-serde/MessagePack (Stork) or Toshi/Summa server frontends: nest's existing repr(C) LE + zstd-on-non-embedding already beats raw MessagePack and the server layers are out of scope.

FlexSearch/Stork/tinysearch are in-memory or WASM-heap-resident designs that get slow above ~1MB corpora or on short queries; borrow their build-time-precompute and ordinal/filter size tricks, not their resident-memory query model. nest's mmap-and-skip discipline is already superior.

categories.name: embeddings-models
categories.focus: embedding and representation models (text + image, including tiny/static)

repos.one_liner: CLIP is a contrastively-trained dual-encoder (ViT/ResNet image tower + 12-layer Transformer text tower with byte-level BPE) that projects both modalities into one shared L2-normalized embedding space (embed_dim 512 for ViT-B/32) where cosine similarity, scaled by a learned temperature, is the native cross-modal metric.
repos.core_innovation: The unit-hypersphere embedding convention plus a single shared text/image space, which turns SIMD dot product into exact cosine and makes int8 quantization nearly lossless.
key_techniques: L2 normalization to unit hypersphere so cosine(a,b) == dot(a,b) for unit vectors
Shared cross-modal embedding space: text and image projected to identical embed_dim (512), one index serves both
Byte-level BPE tokenizer with a 256-entry byte<->unicode bijection that skips whitespace/control bytes, vocab 49408, gzipped rank-ordered merges file
Regex pre-tokenization (contractions, unicode letter runs \p{L}+, single digits \p{N}, symbol runs) before applying merges
Per-word BPE merge cache keyed on input token to avoid recomputation
Learned temperature logit_scale = exp(log(1/0.07)) (~100x) as a stored scalar that rescales raw cosine into calibrated logits
End-of-text token position used as the pooled text feature (deterministic single-vector reduction)
repos.nest_application: nest-format: document/enforce L2-normalized embeddings in search_contract + store optional temperature scalar in provenance (additive, content_hash-safe). nest-runtime: adopt byte-level BPE (byte<->unicode bijection + frozen ranked merges section) in bm25::Bm25Index to fix the CJK/Thai tokenizer gap deterministically. Unlocks: exact cosine via raw SIMD dot product, near-lossless int8 compression, and a path toward shared text+image vectors for the 'fast image similarity' north-star.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to extreme compression: L2-normalized unit vectors are the precondition that makes int8 (and even lower-bit) embedding quantization nearly lossless because every component lies in [-1,1] with a globally bounded scale, so a single symmetric quantization scale per vector or per file suffices -- maximizing nest's compression ratio while keeping the int8 tiny preset's 0.992 recall. It also lets cosine == dot product, so no extra magnitude bytes ever need storing.
repos.perf_notes: Inference is GPU/PyTorch-heavy and out of scope for nest's runtime (nest never runs models). The transferable cheap part is purely the post-encoder convention: a single L2 normalize (one pass) at build time, and a static byte-BPE lookup tokenizer with O(word_len^2) merges + per-word cache. Both are deterministic, allocation-light, and fit nest's offline mmap serving model. embed_dim 512 f32 = 2KB/vector raw, 512B at int8.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A scalable client/server (gRPC, HTTP, WebSocket) for producing CLIP text+image embeddings and cross-modal rank scores, with swappable PyTorch / ONNX Runtime / TensorRT inference backends and DocArray protobuf transport.
repos.core_innovation: Decoupling the CLIP model into two independently-runnable towers behind a single L2-normalized shared embedding space, served through a portable ONNX Runtime backend so the same image-aligned text encoder (including XLM-RoBERTa-based multilingual M-CLIP) runs anywhere without the full PyTorch/CUDA stack. For nest the load-bearing idea is "the embedding model is a portable ONNX graph + a vocab, not a server" plus the cross-modal exact-score rerank pattern.
key_techniques: ONNX Runtime backend: CLIP towers exported to a single .onnx graph run on CPU via onnxruntime with no PyTorch/CUDA dependency (TensorRT/JIT optional accelerators)
Two-tower shared embedding space: separate text and image encoders projecting into one L2-normalized 512/640/768/1024-dim space so cross-modal cosine is meaningful
M-CLIP multilingual: XLM-RoBERTa / LaBSE text tower aligned/distilled to the frozen CLIP image space, giving non-English (PT-BR, CJK) text image-aligned vectors
/rank cross-modal re-ranking: cheap candidate gather then exact joint CLIP-score (softmax of logit_scale * cosine) rerank, returning a real score not an ANN proxy
minibatch_size (default 32) encode batching decoupled from num_worker_preprocess (4) CPU preprocessing workers: separate preprocessing parallelism from the encode kernel
DocArray columnar protobuf serialization of ndarrays with streaming on-disk format and configurable ndarray_type/dtype for large batch transfer
repos.nest_application: nest-python build path: adopt the ONNX Runtime CPU backend pattern so nest's embedding step is a portable .onnx graph + tokenizer instead of a torch dependency, keeping builds deterministic and shrinking the model payload shipped with the demo corpus. Adopt an M-CLIP-style XLM-RoBERTa/LaBSE multilingual text tower as a default text model fingerprint written into provenance: this fixes the documented bm25 CJK/Thai degradation at the embedding layer and matches the PT-BR fake-news datasets, all into the existing embeddings section. In nest-runtime the /rank pattern is conceptually identical to nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank after hnsw/bm25 RRF, validating that design; a logit_scale*cosine softmax could be an optional scoring mode in search_contract. The image tower (ViT-B/32 exported to ONNX) is the concrete route to the mission's "fast image similarity": image vectors land in the same embeddings section and are scored by the existing SIMD dot-product dispatcher with zero new codec, since L2-normalized CLIP image embeddings cosine-search identically to text. Fully additive: no format bump, only embeddings + provenance(model fingerprint).
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect for raw bytes-on-disk compression. clip-as-service has no entropy coder, no embedding quantization, and no on-disk index; it never compresses embeddings (mirroring nest's rule that embeddings stay raw for hot-path scoring). The compression-adjacent wins are second-order: a portable ONNX text+image model shrinks the build-side dependency/model payload vs a torch install, and a single shared 512-dim image-aligned space lets images and text reuse one embeddings section and one SIMD kernel instead of a separate image codec, keeping the format minimal. CLIP's native fp16 weights also confirm nest's float16 embedding preset is safe for these vectors.
repos.perf_notes: Documented ~800 QPS on an RTX 3090 default config; throughput is GPU-bound and irrelevant to nest's CPU/mmap runtime. Transferable perf lessons: the preprocessing/encode split (num_worker_preprocess=4 vs minibatch_size=32), and that ONNX Runtime CPU inference of a ViT-B/32 tower is viable for batch indexing on commodity hardware. CLIP embeddings are L2-normalized so nest's cosine==dot-product fast path applies directly, and image and text vectors share the exact same SIMD dot kernel (AVX2/NEON/scalar) with no per-modality branch.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: BERT is a bidirectional transformer encoder for contextual text embeddings, but its independently-reusable artifact is the WordPiece tokenizer: a greedy longest-match-first subword segmenter over an ordered string-to-id vocabulary, fronted by a CJK-aware basic tokenizer.
repos.core_innovation: Vocabulary-driven subword segmentation that is language-agnostic and OOV-robust: a fixed vocab of word pieces (with a "##" continuation marker) plus a deterministic greedy-longest-match loop turns any string, including unsegmented CJK/Thai, into a stable bounded-size token set without a whitespace assumption and without ever emitting an out-of-vocab token (worst case falls back to single chars / [UNK]). The CJK pre-pass that inserts spaces around every Han codepoint makes ideographic scripts tokenize per-character instead of collapsing into one giant token.
key_techniques: WordPiece greedy longest-match-first: for each word, scan end index downward from full length, take longest substring (## prefixed when start>0) present in vocab, advance start, repeat; is_bad -> [UNK] if no prefix matches
Vocab as OrderedDict / sequential id map (token string -> u32 id) giving O(1) lookups plus a stable inverse id->token table
## continuation prefix preserves word-boundary info while sharing subword pieces across words
BasicTokenizer pre-pass: NFD accent stripping, control-char removal, whitespace normalization, lowercasing, punctuation isolation (split both sides of every punct char)
_tokenize_chinese_chars: insert spaces around CJK codepoints (U+4E00-9FFF, U+3400-4DBF, extension blocks) so ideographs become single-char tokens despite absent whitespace
max_input_chars_per_word guard (default 200) to bound worst-case segmentation cost
Deterministic data-only design: entire tokenizer is a frozen vocab.txt plus a pure function, no model weights needed to run it
repos.nest_application: Replace nest-runtime/src/bm25/tokenize.rs (currently a word-split-on-non-alphanumeric splitter that, per nest's own known-gaps note, degrades on CJK/Thai because space-less scripts collapse into one dropped/huge token) with a two-stage pipeline mirroring BERT: (1) a basic-tokenizer pass that lowercases, NFD-strips accents (already partial for PT-BR), isolates punctuation, and inserts boundaries around CJK codepoint ranges so Han/Thai segment per-character; (2) an optional WordPiece-style greedy-longest-match over a small frozen vocab. The on-disk BM25 codec (bm25/codec.rs) needs ZERO format change: terms stay UTF-8 strings written length-prefixed and sorted alphabetically, so determinism and the additive-format constraint hold and section 0x08 layout is byte-identical. If a learned subword vocab is later shipped, store it as a new additive optional section in the 0x09+ reserved range (or fold into search_contract) so the runtime stays offline and builds stay reproducible. This unlocks correct multilingual lexical recall (CJK/Thai/Korean) for the hybrid preset's BM25-via-RRF leg, closing a named gap without touching the frozen header or the embedding hot path.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. WordPiece is a vocabulary-substitution scheme yielding fewer, shared subword units than character or naive word tokenization, which shrinks the BM25 term dictionary and postings (fewer unique terms, shared pieces) -- classic dictionary coding. But it does not touch the embedding bytes that dominate .nest size, so it improves multilingual search quality far more than the compress-more-than-everyone north star. Treat the CJK-aware basic tokenizer as the must-have piece and WordPiece as a quality/size win for the lexical index only.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (code). Subword vocabs are training-produced, but the greedy-match algorithm and CJK char-range logic are trivially reimplementable in clean-room Rust; only the algorithm is adapted, not the vocab.txt artifact.
repos.perf_notes: Pure CPU, allocation-light, single-pass per word; greedy match is O(word_len^2) worst case but bounded by max_input_chars_per_word and dominated by hashmap lookups. No SIMD needed; runs in the rust runtime with no socket/model dependency, preserving offline-by-construction. Memory cost is the frozen vocab hashmap (tens of KB to a few MB by vocab size), mmappable if stored as a section.

repos.one_liner: A PyTorch framework for dense/sparse/cross-encoder text+image embeddings whose most transferable assets are three post-hoc compression techniques: scalar(int8)/binary embedding quantization with float32 rescoring, Matryoshka (front-loaded truncatable dimensions), and Model2Vec static distillation (attention-free token lookup tables).
repos.core_innovation: Compress-then-rescore as a search contract: store embeddings in a lossily quantized form (binary 1-bit or int8) for cheap candidate retrieval over Hamming/int8 distance, then rerank the small candidate set against a higher-fidelity query representation so the FINAL score is near-full-precision. This decouples on-disk storage cost from result quality, exactly nest's "ann/bm25 always run a mandatory exact cosine rerank" philosophy generalized to the codec layer.
key_techniques: Binary quantization: sign-threshold normalized float32 at 0 -> 1 bit/dim, np.packbits into bytes (1024d -> 128 bytes, 32x), retrieve by popcount Hamming distance (~2 CPU cycles)
Scalar int8 quantization: per-dimension min/max calibration buckets map float32 -> int8 (-128..127), 4x shrink, affine dequant for rescoring
Asymmetric rescore: fetch rescore_multiplier*top_k binary candidates, rescore with float32 query vs stored quantized doc vectors; recovers ~96% (binary) / ~99% (int8) recall
Matryoshka (MRL): train so information is front-loaded; truncate 1024->512 (1.5% drop) or ->256 (0.6% drop) by slicing the prefix, no re-encode
Model2Vec distillation: forward each vocab token through teacher once, PCA the token-embedding matrix (denoises even w/o dim reduction), then SIF weight w=1e-3/(1e-3+proba)
Zipf-rank proxy: vocab is frequency-sorted so rank substitutes for corpus frequency -> IDF-like downweighting of stopword tokens with zero corpus access
Static inference: EmbeddingBag token lookup + mean pooling, no attention, ~100k sents/sec CPU, model ~30MB (potion-base-32M) down to 1.8MB (potion-base-2M)
Tiered store: binary for first-stage memory-resident search, int8 on disk for rescore (cited 200GB->5GB RAM / 52GB disk)
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals. (1) nest-format encoding layer: add MRL-style truncation metadata to the embeddings section and search_contract so a 'matryoshka' preset stores only the front D dims (e.g. 256 of 768) deterministically, shrinking the embeddings section ~3x with ~0.6% recall loss; stacks on existing int8/f16 codecs for compounding compression. (2) nest-runtime search path: generalize the EXISTING mandatory exact-cosine rerank into a two-fidelity store -- keep an optional binary (1-bit packed, popcount-Hamming) shadow of embeddings as a new RESERVED-id codec for first-stage candidate gen, then rerank with the int8/f32 vectors already mmapped; binary Hamming is a tiny NEON/AVX2 popcount kernel that fits the SIMD dispatcher and never touches Python. (3) nest-python build side: implement a Model2Vec-style static distiller (PCA-normalize + Zipf/SIF reweight via vocab rank) so nest ships a sub-30MB deterministic CPU encoder bundled offline, killing the ~300-500ms python boot for search-text and giving sovereign single-file embedding with no transformer download. int8 per-dim min/max calibration should be stored in provenance for reproducible, byte-identical dequant.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. Binary quantization is 32x on the embeddings section (the part nest deliberately leaves uncompressed for hot-path scoring) -- the asymmetric rescore trick is the ONLY way to compress embeddings without breaking nest's "score is real cosine" guarantee, since the lossy form is used only for candidate generation. Matryoshka truncation gives a free orthogonal ~3x. With Model2Vec's PCA denoising they push the 'tiny' preset (currently 0.283 ratio, int8) materially lower while preserving recall@10 ~0.99.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (sentence-transformers); Model2Vec is MIT (MinishLab) -- both vendor-friendly for nest's build-side python and rust runtime.
repos.perf_notes: Binary Hamming = packed-bit XOR + popcount, ~2 CPU cycles/comparison, ideal for a small std::arch popcnt/vcnt SIMD kernel (scalar fallback trivial via u64::count_ones). int8 dot product is the existing nest path. Static encoder ~107k sents/sec single-thread CPU (397x all-mpnet), pure table lookup + mean, deterministic and reproducible -- aligns with nest's seeded/deterministic-build constraint. Model2Vec PCA-then-int8 reaches 25% of original size with no quality loss, evidence quant+dim-reduction compose without recall collapse.

repos.one_liner: A retrieval toolkit (MIT) whose flagship BGE-M3 model emits, from one shared XLM-RoBERTa encoder, three aligned representations per text -- a 1024-d dense vector, a learned sparse lexical-weight dict (ReLU over a linear head per token id, max-pooled on repeats), and ColBERT-style per-token multi-vectors -- combined at query time by a weighted hybrid score.
repos.core_innovation: Learned sparse lexical weights as a {token_id: float} dictionary that is a drop-in upgrade over BM25 term frequencies: w_t = ReLU(W_lex . H[i]) per contextual token, scored as s_lex(q,d) = sum over shared tokens of w_q,t * w_d,t. It is a sparse vector keyed by tokenizer vocab id (~250k dims, almost all zero) that is cheaper, more compressible, and more semantic than a raw text index, and it fuses with dense cosine via a fixed weighted sum -- exactly the hybrid contract nest already runs.
key_techniques: Learned sparse lexical weights: w_t = ReLU(W_lex . H[i]) per token, max-pool weight on repeated token ids, drop special tokens (CLS/SEP)
Sparse score s_lex = sum_{t in q intersect d} w_q,t * w_d,t over two token-id->weight dicts (set-intersection sparse dot product / merge-join)
Storage as parallel ascending-sorted (token_id:u32, weight:f32) arrays per doc -- trivially int8/f16 quantizable and zstd-friendly via delta+varint over ascending ids
ColBERT late interaction: s_mul = (1/N) sum_i max_j (E_q[i] . E_d[j]^T), per-query-token MaxSim over row-normalized doc-token vectors
Weighted hybrid fusion: score = w1*dense + w2*sparse + w3*colbert (e.g. [0.4,0.2,0.4]) alongside/instead of reciprocal-rank fusion
Self-knowledge distillation: combined hybrid score used as teacher to train each single mode (training-side; explains why fixed fusion weights are stable)
Matryoshka dimensionality + quantization knobs on the dense head for size-vs-recall tradeoffs
MCLS (multiple CLS tokens) to embed up to 8192-token long inputs without long-text fine-tuning
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add an OPTIONAL learned-sparse section in the reserved id space (0x09+, additive within v1) storing per-chunk ascending (token_id:u32, weight) pairs; quantize weights to int8/f16 and zstd the section (it is scored by integer merge-join, not a SIMD dot off mmap, so zstd is safe here unlike embeddings). nest-runtime/src/bm25: generalize the existing Bm25Index into a SparseIndex whose postings hold learned weights instead of tf-idf; the merge-join s_lex = sum w_q*w_d replaces BM25 term scoring while reusing the deterministic ordering and the existing reciprocal-rank fusion in bm25/fusion.rs. nest-format/src/sections/contract.rs (search_contract) plus the manifest gain a fusion descriptor (mode = rrf | weighted_sum and deterministic w1/w2/w3) so the hybrid path is self-describing and cross-checked at open. The mandatory exact-cosine rerank stays ground truth -- sparse only changes candidate generation, preserving nest's 'returned score is real cosine' guarantee. nest-python build_fn computes BGE-M3 lexical_weights at build time; rust does only the integer merge-join at serve time, so the runtime stays offline and model-free.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct. Learned sparse weights compress the lexical index far below storing original text or a classic inverted index: each doc is a short list of (u32 token_id, quantized weight) pairs, weights int8/f16-quantize cleanly and ascending token-id streams zstd well (delta + varint). This replaces nest's word-segmented BM25 tokenizer -- a known gap that degrades on CJK/Thai -- with language-agnostic subword ids, so it both shrinks the index AND fixes a correctness gap. It lets nest carry semantic keyword search in a fraction of the bytes of raw text, advancing the 'compress more than everyone while still serving' north star.
repos.license: MIT (toolkit + BGE-M3 weights). Only the on-disk format and scoring ideas are adapted, not the weights; ColBERT late-interaction concept originates from Stanford ColBERT (separate, but the idea is unencumbered).
repos.perf_notes: Sparse scoring is a sorted merge-join over two integer-keyed posting lists -- branchy, not SIMD, but cheap (a few hundred shared tokens) and runs off mmap with no float kernel; int8 weights keep the intersection in cache. ColBERT MaxSim is O(N_q*N_d*dim) per pair and is the costly mode -- nest should use colbert as an optional rerank-only signal, never a candidate generator, to stay light; the cheap (dense + learned-sparse) pair is the practical hybrid. Sparse vocab is ~250k but stored sparsely, so per-doc cost scales with unique tokens/doc, not vocab.

repos.one_liner: A family of decoder-only LLM-based text embedding/reranker models (0.6B/4B/8B, dims 1024/2560/4096) using causal last-token (EOS) pooling, instruction-prefix conditioning, and Matryoshka Representation Learning so a single vector can be truncated to as few as 32 dims and re-normalized with minimal retrieval loss.
repos.core_innovation: Matryoshka Representation Learning makes embedding dimensionality a near-lossless, deterministic compression knob via nested-prefix-trained vectors that stay valid under truncate-then-renormalize.
key_techniques: Matryoshka Representation Learning: nested-prefix loss front-loads importance so vec[:d] for d in {32,64,128,256,512,768,1024} is independently usable
Truncate-then-renormalize: slice the first d dims then L2-normalize so dot product == cosine remains exact on the prefix
Last-token (EOS) causal pooling: final hidden state aggregates the whole sequence under the causal mask (no [CLS]), with left/right padding handling
Instruction-prefix conditioning: 'Instruct: {task}\nQuery: {q}' template steers the same weights per task, +1-5% with no retraining
L2-normalized output vectors as the contract so similarity is a plain dot product
Per-model fixed full dim (1024/2560/4096) advertised as the MRL ceiling
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add an MRL-aware dimension-truncation codec/manifest field on the embeddings section. The Python builder (nest-python) records the model's full dim plus a chosen mrl_dim (e.g. 256 of 1024); it truncates each vector to the prefix and re-L2-normalizes before writing, storing mrl_dim and full_dim in the embeddings section header / search_contract. nest-runtime's SIMD dot-product kernels already score raw f32/f16/int8 straight from mmap, so they need only honor the smaller per-vector stride from the manifest; the exact-cosine rerank still returns true cosine because vectors are renormalized on the truncated prefix. This stacks multiplicatively with the existing tiny preset (int8): a 256-of-1024 MRL prefix at int8 is 4x (dims) * 4x (int8 vs f32) = ~16x smaller embeddings than f32-1024, while exact rerank guarantees the returned score is real cosine on the stored prefix. Add a CLI flag (nest-cli build/stats) to surface mrl_dim and the size/recall tradeoff. Determinism is preserved: truncation is a pure deterministic slice, so same chunks + same model fingerprint + same mrl_dim => byte-identical file. Stays additive (new manifest field + reserved encoding id), single-file, offline.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to the 'compress more than everyone' north star. MRL adds a compression axis nest does not yet exploit: the embedding-dimension axis, independent of and multiplicative with the value-precision axis (int8/f16) nest already has. Qwen reports truncating 4096->1024 keeps ~95% retrieval while cutting storage 75%; for nest's tiny preset, a 256-of-1024 int8 layout could roughly quarter the dominant on-disk cost (embeddings are usually the largest section) at small recall cost, and because the format mandates exact-cosine rerank, the headline score stays honest. It also shrinks the HNSW index footprint since graph vectors are shorter.
repos.perf_notes: Truncation is a contiguous prefix slice, so per-vector memory stride shrinks linearly with mrl_dim and the existing AVX2/NEON dot-product kernels run unchanged on the shorter stride (fewer SIMD lanes per vector => proportionally faster scoring and smaller mmap working set). No new entropy coder or transform needed; cost is one L2 renorm per vector at build time only. Shorter vectors also reduce HNSW distance-eval cost and index size. The models themselves are heavy (0.6B params, BF16, 32K ctx, RoPE), but nest only consumes their float outputs, so the model weight is irrelevant to the runtime; only the build-time embedder cares.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (Qwen3-Embedding model weights and repo)

repos.one_liner: A dataset-free distillation method that collapses a sentence-transformer into a static token-embedding lookup table, so encoding a sentence becomes tokenize + table-lookup + mean-pool (no forward pass), shrinking models up to 50x and running up to 500x faster on CPU.
repos.core_innovation: Encoding is reduced from a neural forward pass to a pure memory operation: a frozen [vocab x dim] static embedding matrix indexed by token ids, averaged per sentence. The matrix is post-processed offline with PCA (which normalizes/whitens the embedding space, giving ~2.8% gain even with no dim reduction) plus SIF/Zipf per-token weights (w = 1e-3/(1e-3+p), p approximated from token rank via Zipf's law since vocabularies are frequency-sorted), then optionally quantized to int8/f16 with no measurable quality loss. The whole model is just three files: model.safetensors (the matrix), tokenizer.json, config.json.
key_techniques: Static embedding matrix as a [vocab~32K x dim] lookup table; encode = tokenize -> gather rows -> mean-pool -> optional L2 normalize
PCA whitening of the distilled matrix as a quality step even at full dimensionality (decorrelates/normalizes the space), enabling cheap dimensionality reduction on top
SIF/Zipf per-token weighting: w = 1e-3/(1e-3+p) with p derived from token vocabulary rank (frequency-sorted), folded into the matrix offline so query time stays a plain gather+mean
int8 and float16 scalar quantization of the embedding matrix (25% and 50% of f32 size) with negligible recall loss because vectors are L2-normalized and PCA-conditioned
safetensors on-disk format: single 'embeddings' tensor (f32/f16/i8) + zero-copy mmap load, dtype and dim read from tensor shape, normalize flag in config.json
token_mapping array for vocabulary quantization (remaps original token ids to a reduced row set) plus optional per-token weights array
median-token-length pre-trim and unk-token filtering to bound tokenization cost
official Rust impl (model2vec-rs) proving the entire encode path runs with no Python, only safetensors + tokenizers crate
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) Builder-side codec for nest-format: add a deterministic 'static-embed' build mode in nest-python that distills/loads a model2vec matrix and produces embeddings via tokenize+lookup+mean-pool with PCA+SIF baked in offline. This makes nest's embed step dataset-free, ~500x cheaper on CPU, and fully deterministic (no GPU/transformer nondeterminism) -- directly serving the reproducible-build guarantee (same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file). (2) Validate and strengthen nest's int8 codec: model2vec confirms PCA-whitened + L2-normalized vectors quantize to int8 at ~25% size with no measurable loss, which is exactly nest's 'tiny' preset (int8, 0.283 ratio, recall@10 0.992) -- so nest should add an optional offline PCA/whitening pass before int8 packing in nest-format's encoding module to lift the int8 codec quality at the same byte cost. The static matrix itself (~32K x 256 int8 ~= 8MB) could ship as an optional dictionary/section to support on-device re-embedding of edited chunks without a server. model2vec-rs (MIT, safetensors + tokenizers) is a near drop-in reference for the nest-runtime side if nest wants to embed query text natively offline, closing the search-text 300-500ms python boot gap.
repos.compression_relevance: High but indirect: model2vec compresses the MODEL not the stored vectors, yet its PCA-whitening + SIF reweighting conditions the embedding space so int8/f16 scalar quantization loses ~nothing -- the precise lever nest needs to make its 'tiny' int8 codec safe and possibly push to lower-bit packing. It also enables a sovereign offline re-embed path (no 500MB transformer), keeping the single-file footprint tiny. It does not add a new entropy coder, but it is strong evidence for nest's quantization presets and a path to compressing the embedding-generation dependency itself to ~8-30MB.
repos.license: MIT (code and POTION models; authors Stephan Tulkens & Thomas van Dongen, Minish Lab)
repos.perf_notes: ~500x faster CPU encode than the parent sentence-transformer; distillation ~30s on CPU, dataset-free. Models 8MB (smallest on MTEB) to ~30MB f32; int8 = 25% size, f16 = 50% size, both ~no quality loss. Encode is memory-bound (gather + mean over ~dozens of rows), trivially SIMD/multiprocessing-friendly (multiprocessing kicks in >10K sentences). safetensors load is zero-copy mmap, matching nest's mmap philosophy. Only hard runtime dep on the Python side is numpy; the Rust port needs only safetensors + tokenizers.

repos.one_liner: SetFit is a prompt-free few-shot text-classification framework that fine-tunes a Sentence-Transformer body via contrastive Siamese pair training (CosineSimilarityLoss) then fits a tiny logistic-regression head on the resulting frozen embeddings, plus a contrastive knowledge-distillation path that compresses a teacher into a much smaller student.
repos.core_innovation: The transferable idea is contrastive knowledge distillation: a large teacher embedder's geometry is transferred into a tiny student embedder using cheap unlabeled in-domain text turned into positive/negative pairs (and the teacher's own similarity scores as soft targets via ContrastiveDistillationDataset). This decouples the model that PRODUCES the on-disk vectors from the model the user originally chose, so the same corpus can be re-embedded into a smaller, faster, dimension-reduced vector space whose neighbor ordering is preserved -- exactly the lever nest needs to shrink the embeddings section (its largest, non-zstd-compressible payload) without changing the search contract.
key_techniques: Contrastive Siamese fine-tuning with CosineSimilarityLoss on same-class=positive / diff-class=negative pairs
Combinatorial pair amplification: from N labeled sentences generate O(N^2) pairs (8+8 -> 28 pos + 64 neg = 92), controlled by num_iterations=R
Two-stage decoupling: frozen Sentence-Transformer body produces embeddings, cheap LogisticRegression / differentiable SetFitHead does classification
ContrastiveDistillationDataset: teacher similarity scores become soft regression targets for the student (DistillationTrainer), reported ~123x inference speedup
Mean-pooling of token embeddings into a single fixed-width sentence vector (the unit of storage)
Body-swap multilinguality: any compatible ST checkpoint replaces the encoder without changing the pipeline
repos.nest_application: nest steals contrastive distillation as an offline, Python-side (nest-python build path, not the rust core) re-embedding step: ship a small distilled student embedder fingerprint so a corpus can be re-encoded into a lower-dimension vector space (e.g. 768 -> 256) before the embeddings section is written. This shrinks nest's single largest section -- which the format deliberately never zstd-compresses because nest-runtime/src/simd scores it straight from mmap -- in a way zstd/float16/int8 cannot, since it cuts the float COUNT not just the per-float width, and stacks multiplicatively with the existing int8 codec in nest-format/src/encoding. The provenance/search_contract sections record the student model fingerprint so determinism holds (same chunks + same student => byte-identical file); content_hash stays stable because it hashes decoded canonical text, not vectors. The teacher-vs-student recall delta is validated by the mandatory exact-cosine rerank already in nest-runtime/src/search.rs, so a lossy smaller embedder still returns true cosine over whatever vectors are stored. Optionally expose a build-time preset in nest-cli (a 'nano' preset = distilled-256-dim + int8 + hnsw) below the current 'tiny' preset. The contrastive-pairs-from-unlabeled-text trick also gives nest a cheap way to domain-adapt the student to its PT-BR fake-news demo corpus without labels.
repos.compression_relevance: Direct and high: embeddings are nest's biggest and least-compressible section (raw f32 is incompressible by zstd, and nest forbids zstd on it anyway for hot-path mmap scoring). Distillation attacks the only remaining axis -- the dimensionality/count of floats -- via a smaller student embedder, which composes with int8/float16 width reduction multiplicatively. A 768->256 distill is a 3x cut on top of int8's ~4x, plausibly pushing below the current tiny preset 0.283 size ratio while the exact-cosine rerank guards recall. Cleanest path toward 'compress more than everyone' for vector payloads.
repos.perf_notes: Reported 30s training on 8 examples/class (V100, ~$0.025); distillation yields ~123x inference speedup of student vs teacher. Bodies are standard ST checkpoints (MPNet ~110M, RoBERTa-Large ~355M). All cost is training/build-time; the rust runtime is unaffected and gains pure win (fewer/smaller floats per dot-product, fewer cache lines touched by the SIMD kernels in nest-runtime/src/simd).
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A thin Rust port of sentence-transformers that runs DistilUSE/DistilBERT multilingual sentence-embedding models through libtorch (tch-rs/rust-bert), producing fixed-size embeddings via masked mean pooling plus a dense+tanh projection.
repos.core_innovation: The exact, reproducible embedding-head pipeline that turns per-token transformer outputs into one sentence vector: attention-mask-weighted mean pooling (sum of masked token embeddings divided by the clamped mask count) followed by a Dense linear+tanh projection. This is the canonical post-encoder math every sentence-transformer uses, and matching it bit-for-bit is what makes embeddings reproducible and model-aligned.
key_techniques: masked mean pooling: input_mask_expanded = mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(emb); (emb*mask).sum_dim(1) / mask.sum_dim(1) so padding tokens contribute zero
Dense embedding head: x.apply(linear).tanh() projecting hidden dim (768) to the model output dim, the learned reduction that defines the final vector space
dual tokenizer backends behind one API: HF tokenizers (wordpiece/BPE) and rust_tokenizers (sentencepiece), selectable as SBertHF vs SBertRT
batched forward over Vec<String> with rayon CPU parallelism sized by num_cpus
tch-rs/libtorch tensor ops (sum_dim_intlist, unsqueeze, expand_as, clamp) as the f32 compute kernel; output_attentions=true config flag exposes mask-aware tensors
offline model conversion via prepare_distilbert.py into a libtorch-loadable weights directory (Apache-2.0)
repos.nest_application: nest-python is the embedding producer and MUST replicate this exact pooling+dense head so nest-runtime cosine scores are meaningful. Concretely: in nest-python's embedding build path, after running the encoder, apply the identical masked-mean formula (sum(token*mask)/clamp(sum(mask),1e-9)) then the model dense linear+tanh (or L2-normalize) head, and record the precise pooling mode plus dense weights identity inside the provenance section's model fingerprint. This locks determinism: same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical embeddings. For nest-runtime, knowing the head is mean-pool+tanh (NOT L2-normalized by default here) clarifies that the SIMD dot-product hot path needs an explicit normalization assumption in search_contract; nest should pin 'embeddings are L2-normalized at build time' so the AVX2/NEON dot product equals true cosine with no per-query norm. The dual-tokenizer split (wordpiece vs sentencepiece) is also a direct fix for nest's bm25 CJK/Thai gap: adopting a sentencepiece-style subword tokenizer in nest-runtime bm25::Bm25Index removes the word-segmentation degradation while keeping deterministic alphabetical term ordering.
repos.compression_relevance: Low and indirect. The repo has no entropy coder, quantization, or on-disk compression (embeddings are dense f32 tensors from libtorch). Its relevance to compress-more-than-everyone is upstream: pinning the exact pooling+dense head plus an explicit L2-normalize step is the precondition that makes nest aggressive embedding quantization (int8/float16 in tiny/compressed presets) safe -- once vectors are unit-norm, int8 scalar quantization preserves cosine recall (nest already reports recall@10 0.992 at 0.283 ratio). Without the deterministic normalized head, lossy embedding compression cannot be validated against a stable ground truth.
repos.license: Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: Runs on libtorch f32 via tch-rs 0.15 (heavy hundreds-of-MB native dependency, not embeddable -- nest must NOT vendor this; reference-only for the math). CPU batching via rayon scaled by num_cpus. DistilUSE multilingual covers 13 languages, STS2017 score 80.1, output dim ~512 (768 hidden then dense projection). No SIMD kernel of its own; vector math delegated to libtorch BLAS. No quantization, no mmap, no custom on-disk format -- model is a plain converted libtorch weights directory.

repos.one_liner: A Rust port of Hugging Face transformers built on the tch-rs libtorch bindings (with optional ONNX Runtime via ort), whose sentence_embeddings pipeline reproduces the Sentence-Transformers modules.json chain (Transformer -> Pooling -> optional Dense -> optional Normalize) to turn token sequences into fixed Vec<f32> embeddings.
repos.core_innovation: The exact, masking-correct reimplementation of the Sentence-Transformers post-processing chain in Rust: attention-mask-weighted mean pooling, optional dense projection, and L2 normalization, driven declaratively by the model's own modules.config.json so the embedding is bit-faithful to the upstream Python model.
key_techniques: Mask-weighted mean pooling: multiply token states by expanded attention mask, sum_dim over seq axis, divide by clamped mask-sum (min 1e-9) so padding never dilutes the mean
Alternative pooling modes in one struct: CLS (select(1,0)), max (masked_fill_ padding to -1e9 then max_dim), and mean-sqrt (divide by sqrt(mask_sum))
Declarative module chain parsed from modules.json/sentence_bert_config.json with enforced order (pos0 Transformer, pos1 Pooling, pos2-3 optional Dense/Normalize) via SentenceEmbeddingsModuleType enum
Dense post-projection layer (nn::Linear + activation) that can reduce embedding dimensionality before storage
L2 normalization making cosine similarity reduce to a plain dot product
tch-rs convert_model.py path: PyTorch .bin weights converted to a libtorch-loadable tensor store, cached under RUSTBERT_CACHE
rust-tokenizers multi-threaded WordPiece/BPE tokenization decoupled from the model
repos.nest_application: nest never runs inference (python builds embeddings), so do NOT vendor tch/libtorch. The steal is narrow and goes into nest-python's build path plus nest-format provenance: (1) record the resolved Sentence-Transformers module chain (pooling mode, dense in/out dims, normalize bool) into the provenance section and search_contract as the model fingerprint, so two builds with the same chain are provably byte-identical and a consumer can verify the embeddings were L2-normalized. (2) If normalize=true is recorded in search_contract, nest-runtime's simd dispatcher can drop the per-vector norm in cosine rerank and run a pure dot product against the int8/f16 mmap'd embeddings section (the hot path), since cosine == dot for unit vectors. (3) The mask-weighted mean-pool semantics document exactly what a 'chunk embedding' means, hardening the deterministic contract; it is reference-level guidance, not Rust code to import into the small core.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect. rust-bert has no entropy coder, quantization, or on-disk compression to steal.
