The only compression-adjacent lever is the optional Dense projection layer, which is the upstream mechanism for shipping lower-dimensional embeddings (e.g. 384->256): fewer dims directly shrinks nest's embeddings section, the largest tiny-preset payload. Recording normalize=true also lets the runtime store and score embeddings without keeping norms, marginally tightening the format.
repos.perf_notes: Inference throughput is entirely libtorch/ONNX-bound (CPU or CUDA via .with_device()); no custom SIMD kernels, no quantized inference. Heavyweight C++ runtime dependency, opposite of nest's small-core/offline philosophy. The post-processing tensor ops (mean/max pool, normalize) are trivial and would be plain scalar/ndarray loops if ever ported.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A C++ library for linear-bag-of-words text classification and subword word embeddings whose real gem for nest is its model-compression pipeline (fastText.zip): product quantization of the embedding matrix plus greedy coverage-based feature pruning, shrinking 400MB+ models to single-digit MB with near-zero accuracy loss.
repos.core_innovation: Product Quantization of the embedding matrix: subvector k-means with 256 centroids (1-byte codes) plus decoupled scalar-quantized norms and asymmetric lookup-table scoring, enabling sub-byte-per-dimension storage scored without full decode.
key_techniques: Product quantization: per-subvector-position k-means (k=256 -> 8-bit codes), dsub=2 subvector dim, decouples norm (qnorm: scalar-quantize the L2 norm separately from the direction codes)

Greedy coverage-based feature pruning: keep the n-gram with highest L2 norm that covers each training doc, then top up by norm until a target feature budget is hit - retains only high-information rows before quantizing
Asymmetric distance computation: query stays full-precision; build a per-subvector lookup table of query-vs-256-centroids dot products, then scoring a code is m table lookups + adds (no decode)
Character n-gram subwords (3-6 chars, with < > word-boundary markers) hashed into a fixed bucket array for OOV-robust representations
FNV-1a hashing trick: n-grams mapped via h=2166136261, XOR+multiply by 16777619, mod bucket(=2M) into a fixed-size row table; n-gram rows placed after word rows to avoid word/ngram index collision
Hierarchical softmax over a Huffman tree of labels (frequent labels get shorter codes) for O(log k) classification
repr-stable little-endian binary model format (dictionary + hyperparams + quantized matrices) loadable by mmap
repos.nest_application: Add a new embeddings codec encoding=4 ('pq') in crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new pq.rs sibling to int8.rs, registered in encoding/mod.rs and writer/encoding_choice.rs) using a reserved id in the 4-255 additive range - no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump. On-disk layout mirrors int8.rs prefix conventions: u32 payload_version, u32 dsub, the k-means codebook (m_subspaces * 256 * dsub f32 centroids, deterministic via seeded k-means to honor the reproducible-build constraint and alphabetical/seeded tie-breaks), per-vector scalar norm (reuse int8 norm machinery), then n*(dim/dsub) u8 centroid-index codes. In crates/nest-runtime the SIMD dispatcher gains a PQ scoring path: build the asymmetric lookup table (query dotted against the mmapped codebook with the existing AVX2/NEON/scalar dot kernels) once per query, then score every candidate as dim/dsub byte-indexed table lookups + adds straight off mmap - then feed into the MANDATORY exact-cosine rerank path so the returned score stays true cosine (PQ is only the ANN coarse filter, never the final score, exactly matching nest's search_contract). This makes a new 'nano' preset below tiny: at dsub=2 the embeddings section is ~half of int8 (approaching 0.14 size ratio territory) directly advancing 'compress more than everyone' while staying single-file/offline/deterministic. Optionally port the greedy coverage pruning into the python builder (nest-python/build path) to drop low-norm chunks/rows before encoding.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. PQ is THE classic technique for pushing vector storage below 1 byte/dimension - it is what nest's current int8 codec (1 byte/dim, 4x) leaves on the table. At dsub=2,k=256 PQ stores 1 byte per 2 dims (8x base, ~16x vs f32 on the embedding bytes) with recall recoverable via the mandatory exact rerank. fastText.zip demonstrated ~250x model shrink (427MB -> 1.7MB) with negligible accuracy loss, validating that PQ + norm-decoupling + pruning is the highest-leverage path to beat everyone on embedding compression.
repos.perf_notes: PQ scoring is cache- and SIMD-friendly: build one query lookup table (m_subspaces x 256 f32) using nest's existing AVX2/NEON dot kernels against the mmapped codebook, then each candidate costs dim/dsub u8-indexed loads + f32 adds - no float decode on the hot path, fits nest's score-off-mmap model. Codebook (m*256*dsub*4 bytes, e.g. dim=384,dsub=2 -> ~600KB) is tiny, stays hot in L2. Caveat: k-means training is the only added build-time cost and must be seeded for byte-identical deterministic builds; keep it in python builder, not rust library.
repos.license: MIT License (facebookresearch/fastText)

repos.one_liner: GloVe is a log-bilinear word-embedding model trained on a global word-word cooccurrence matrix, shipped as a 4-stage C toolchain (vocab_count -> cooccur -> shuffle -> glove) whose real engineering value is its external-memory sparse-matrix pipeline that sorts/merges/shuffles billions of records on a tiny RAM budget.
repos.core_innovation: External-memory construction of a giant sparse keyed dataset: fixed-size POD records (CREC = {int word1; int word2; real val}) are streamed to disk in sorted runs, then combined with a min-heap k-way merge that ACCUMULATES values for duplicate (word1,word2) keys during the merge pass, so deduplication/aggregation costs nothing extra and peak RAM is bounded by a single overflow buffer regardless of total data size. The same fixed-record discipline enables a two-phase external Fisher-Yates shuffle. This is the canonical recipe for building large derived index sections on a resource-constrained machine.
key_techniques: CREC fixed-size POD record {int word1; int word2; float val} written via raw fwrite(sizeof(CREC)) with no per-record framing -- pure densely-packed binary array
Hybrid dense/sparse storage: a dense bigram_table indexed by lookup[w1-1]+w2-2 for frequent pairs (product of frequency ranks < max_product), sparse overflow buffer cr[] for the long tail
Overflow-to-disk: when cr[] hits overflow_threshold, qsort by (word1,word2) and flush a sorted run to a temp file, bounding peak RAM
k-way merge of sorted temp files via a min-heap priority queue (merge_files), emitting globally ordered records and accumulating val for equal keys in one streaming pass (merge_write)
Frequency-rank remapping: words encoded as integer ranks (most frequent = small id) so the hot dense region is the small-id corner -- an implicit Zipf-aware layout
AdaGrad per-parameter adaptive LR with gradient clipping over a flat W array of vocab*(dim+1) floats (dim + 1 bias), context vectors offset by vocab*(dim+1)
Weighting function f(x) = (x/x_max)^alpha for x<x_max else 1, alpha=0.75, x_max=100 -- sublinear down-weighting of rare cooccurrences
Two-phase external Fisher-Yates shuffle: shuffle within array_size (2e6) record chunks to temp files, then merge-shuffle ~array_size/num records from each chunk; budget set by -memory
repos.nest_application: Steal the external-memory sparse pipeline into nest-format's writer/build path (NOT the embedding model -- nest already produces embeddings from a real model). Concretely: (1) when building the optional bm25_index (0x08) inverted postings and any future graph-search edge section, use GloVe's CREC pattern -- a repr(C), little-endian, fixed-width POD posting/edge record {u32 term_id; u32 doc_id; f32 weight} written as a packed array, sorted into runs, then combined with a min-heap k-way merge that accumulates duplicate keys in one pass. This builds indexes for corpora larger than RAM on a minimal-budget machine while preserving determinism (alphabetical/sorted term order maps directly onto GloVe's sorted-merge ordering, so determinism falls out for free). (2) Adopt frequency-rank id remapping so dense postings cluster at small ids, improving zstd ratio on the non-embedding index sections (encoding already covers 0x07/0x08). (3) Reuse the two-phase external Fisher-Yates only if a build step ever needs shuffled sampling order, with a seeded RNG to honor deterministic builds. Each module stays under the 300-line cap as a single-responsibility unit (e.g. nest-format/src/build/external_merge.rs). The model/AdaGrad/weighting math is reference-only.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. GloVe itself does NOT compress (raw f32 vectors, unframed binary; released vectors are large uncompressed files). Its relevance to nest's compress-more-than-everyone north star is the BUILD side: the sorted-run + k-way-merge-with-accumulation pattern is how you construct large index sections (bm25 postings, graph edges) deterministically on a tiny RAM budget, and frequency-rank id remapping makes those non-embedding sections more compressible by zstd (small clustered ids -> better entropy coding). It does not help embedding compression (nest already uses float16/int8 there).
repos.perf_notes: Pure sequential disk IO with fixed-size records: no parsing, fwrite/fread of sizeof(CREC) blocks, trivially mmappable and vectorizable. Min-heap merge is O(N log k) for k temp files. Peak RAM bounded by the overflow_threshold/array_size buffer, set explicitly by -memory. CREC is 12 bytes (2x int32 + float32) -- nest should mirror with a repr(C) packed 12-byte record. The dense bigram_table avoids hashing for the hot Zipfian corner. No SIMD in GloVe's IO path; the AdaGrad inner loop is scalar over dim. Determinism caveat: GloVe's shuffle uses rand_long() (not reproducibly seeded by default), so any nest adaptation must seed the RNG to honor the deterministic-build constraint.
repos.license: Apache License 2.0

repos.one_liner: The original C implementation of word2vec: trains static word embeddings (CBOW / skip-gram) with negative sampling and hierarchical softmax, and ships utilities (distance, word-analogy) that linear-scan a flat float32 matrix with precomputed L2-normalized vectors so a dot product equals cosine.
repos.core_innovation: Normalize-at-load + flat-contiguous-matrix + brute-force dot product so cosine is a single FMA loop -- nest's exact-cosine ground truth, minus the per-query normalization cost.
key_techniques: L2-normalize every vector once at load so dot(q,v) == cosine, removing per-query sqrt/division from the scan loop
Flat row-major contiguous matrix M[word*size + dim] with no per-vector object header -- ideal mmap target, stride = size*sizeof(real)
Top-N nearest neighbor via insertion into sorted bestd[40]/bestw[40] arrays (no heap allocation, branch-predictable shift) instead of a full sort
Negative-sampling unigram table: precompute a 1e8-entry array filled proportional to count^0.75, then sample neighbors/negatives by a single random index lookup (O(1) frequency-weighted sampling)
Sigmoid lookup table: EXP_TABLE_SIZE=1000 precomputed values over [-MAX_EXP=6, +6], index = (f+6)*(1000/12), replacing exp() with a table read
Huffman-tree hierarchical softmax giving each word a variable-length binary code (MAX_CODE_LENGTH=40), frequent words get short paths -- a frequency-optimal prefix code
Vocabulary hash: 30M-slot open-addressing table, polynomial rolling hash (*257 per char), linear probing, rebuild when load factor > 0.7
Tiny self-describing text header `vocab_size layer1_size\n` then either ASCII floats or raw fwrite of float32 rows (binary flag) -- minimal format, no index
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime/src/search + simd dispatcher: adopt the normalize-at-build invariant. Store embeddings L2-pre-normalized in the embeddings section (a one-time deterministic transform recorded in provenance/search_contract) so the SIMD AVX2/NEON kernel runs a pure dot product with zero per-query normalization, and the mandatory exact rerank after hnsw/bm25 becomes a bare FMA scan -- faster hot path, byte-identical determinism preserved. The bestd[40]/bestw[40] sorted-insert pattern maps directly onto nest-runtime's top-k collection for small k (avoid a BinaryHeap; a fixed sorted array is branch-predictable and allocation-free). For the int8 'tiny' preset, pre-normalizing before int8 quantization tightens the value range and improves recall@10. The count^0.75 unigram-table trick is reusable in nest-runtime/bm25 or any future negative-sampling / frequency-weighted sampler as an O(1) deterministic (seeded) sampler. The flat M[words x dim] row-major layout validates nest-format's contiguous embeddings section as the correct mmap shape; the 'vocab_size dim\\n' header is the minimalist ancestor of nest's manifest.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: the L2-normalize-then-quantize ordering directly helps nest's int8/float16 codecs -- normalized vectors have a bounded, predictable per-dimension range, so int8 scale/zero-point is tighter and recall loss at the 0.283 'tiny' ratio shrinks. The count^0.75 / Huffman-code ideas are frequency-optimal coding lessons (short codes for frequent symbols) that generalize to entropy-coding the non-embedding sections. word2vec itself does NO embedding compression (raw float32), so it is a baseline to beat, not a source of a codec.
repos.perf_notes: Brute-force linear scan is O(words*dim) per query with a tight inner FMA loop over contiguous memory -- cache-friendly, trivially SIMD/AVX-vectorizable, exactly nest's exact-cosine path. Normalization moved to load (one-time) means the query loop has no sqrt/div. Lookup tables (sigmoid 1000-entry, unigram 1e8-entry) trade memory for branch-free O(1) compute. No threading in distance.c (single-thread scan); training uses lock-free Hogwild-style multithreaded SGD. float32 throughout, no quantization -- memory-bound at scale, which is why nest's int8/f16 + hnsw matter for anything large.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: Top2Vec is a topic-modeling pipeline that places documents AND words in one shared embedding space, then derives topics geometrically: UMAP-reduce doc vectors, HDBSCAN-cluster the dense regions, take each cluster's centroid as a "topic vector," and cosine-rank the nearest word vectors to label it; search is served by an optional hnswlib HNSW index over the same vectors.
repos.core_innovation: The single most transferable idea is the joint document+word embedding space combined with the "centroid-as-query" trick: because words and documents are embedded with the same model into the same metric space, a cluster centroid (mean of member doc vectors) is itself a valid query vector, and the n nearest WORD vectors to it become a free, human-readable label for that cluster of chunks. No separate keyword extraction, no supervised step, no extra index types are needed: one cosine kernel over one vector pool produces clustering, topic labels, and semantic search. This turns "what is this corpus / cluster of chunks about" into pure linear algebra over vectors nest already stores.
key_techniques: Joint doc+word embedding: embed corpus words alongside chunk text with the same model so word and chunk vectors are cosine-comparable in one pool
Centroid topic vectors: topic = arithmetic mean of member doc vectors in ORIGINAL full-dim space, not the UMAP-reduced space
Cosine-rank labeling: rank n-nearest word vectors to a centroid to auto-generate topic keywords
UMAP for clustering-prep only (n_neighbors=15, n_components=5, metric=cosine, min_dist=0.0) to densify sparse high-dim vectors before clustering
HDBSCAN density clustering (min_cluster_size=15, metric=euclidean, cluster_selection_method=eom) that emits noise/outliers instead of forcing assignment; topic count emerges from density, no preset k
Hierarchical topic reduction: iteratively merge nearest topic centroids to collapse N topics to a requested smaller count
Optional hnswlib HNSW index (M / ef_construction / ef_search, space=cosine/ip/l2, incremental add_items) over the same vectors for fast doc/word ANN
repos.nest_application: Two additive moves, both reusing the existing SIMD cosine kernel and embeddings section, no heavy deps. (1) nest-runtime: a new offline `topics` module (~250 loc, single-responsibility, under the 300-line cap) that streams centroids over the already-mmapped embeddings section and, for labeling, cosine-ranks nearest chunk/term vectors via the existing simd dispatcher + exact rerank path used by `search`. Clustering should be a deterministic, seeded, dependency-light scheme (seeded k-means or fixed-threshold greedy cosine agglomeration) to honor nest's deterministic/never-panic/offline-by-construction rules instead of vendoring UMAP/HDBSCAN (Numba/SciPy stacks that break single-file/offline). The centroid-as-query trick fits nest's contract: a topic vector is just another query, so exact-cosine ground truth still holds. (2) nest-format: an OPTIONAL additive section in the RESERVED 0x09+ range, e.g. topics_index(0x09), holding repr(C) little-endian records {topic_id, inline f16/int8 centroid or offset into embeddings, member chunk_id ranges, top-k label term ids}; it is covered by the existing per-section SHA-256 checksum and folds into content_hash via decoded canonical bytes, preserving determinism and the four integrity surfaces. Centroids are NOT on the hot scoring path, so they MAY be zstd-compressed (unlike embeddings). nest-cli gains a thin `topics` subcommand mirroring the existing 8-subcommand clap surface. Unlocks: corpus summarization, cluster-scoped/faceted "search within topic", graph-search seeds (centroids as nodes), and auto-labels for citations.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. (a) Centroids are a coarse codebook: store K topic centroids plus per-chunk topic_id (1-2 bytes) and keep each embedding as centroid + small residual -- the IVF/PQ residual idea reached via Top2Vec's centroid geometry -- shrinking the embeddings section (the largest in tiny/compressed presets) below flat int8, composing with nest's existing int8/f16 codecs. (b) Reordering chunks by topic_id places semantically similar embeddings adjacent, improving byte-locality and the zstd ratio on the NON-embedding sections (chunks_canonical, provenance) that ARE zstd-eligible. (c) Auto-generated label terms double as a tiny corpus dictionary that can seed a zstd custom dictionary for chunks_canonical. Net: a path toward "compress more than everyone" by exploiting redundancy ACROSS chunks (codebook + residual + locality), not just within each chunk.
repos.perf_notes: Centroid computation is a single streaming mean over the embeddings section (one mmap pass, O(N*d), SIMD-summable). Cosine-ranking labels reuses nest's AVX2/NEON/scalar dot-product dispatcher -- no new kernel. The expensive/fragile upstream parts (UMAP via Numba, HDBSCAN, hnswlib build) are training-time, heavyweight, and non-deterministic by default; do NOT vendor them into the rust runtime -- push optional clustering to the python BUILD side (nest-python / build pipeline) where SciPy-class deps are acceptable, and keep the rust serve path to deterministic centroid math plus existing HNSW (0x07) and cosine rerank. hnswlib's M/ef_construction/ef_search and incremental add_items already overlap nest's seeded ann::HnswIndex, so nothing new there. Memory: K centroids at d dims is negligible (K << N); residual quantization is the only footprint lever and it strictly shrinks the file.
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause

repos.one_liner: A Rust inference server for embedding/reranking transformers (BERT/XLM-R/GTE/ModernBERT/Qwen) with a candle + ONNX-Runtime backend, token-based dynamic batching, and four pooling heads (CLS, mean, last-token, SPLADE) exposing dense and sparse embeddings plus cross-encoder rerank scores.
repos.core_innovation: SPLADE: reuse the MaskedLM vocab-projection head, apply log(1+relu(logits)) then max-pool over tokens to get a vocabulary-sized, ~99%-zero learned sparse embedding whose nonzeros are (term_id, weight) pairs usable for inverted-index retrieval and trivially compressible.
key_techniques: SPLADE head: Linear+GELU -> LayerNorm -> decoder Linear to vocab -> relu -> log1p -> amax over sequence (max-pool) = vocab-sized sparse vector
Sparse encoding: filter nonzeros into (index:u32, value:f32) pairs, CSR-style offsets/indices/values layout
Token-based dynamic batching capped by --max-batch-tokens (16384) not request count, for variable-length inputs
Pooling head abstraction (CLS/mean/last-token/SPLADE) auto-detected from 1_Pooling/config.json
Dual backend (candle native Rust + ONNX Runtime) behind one pooling interface; safetensors + ONNX weight loading
Cross-encoder rerank head emitting one real relevance score per pair as a final exact rerank stage
repos.nest_application: Add a third index section alongside hnsw(0x07) and bm25(0x08): a SPLADE-style learned-sparse index, e.g. splade_index(0x09) in nest-format (sections.rs + new encoding path), built in nest-python at build time by running a ForMaskedLM model with the log(1+relu) max-pool head. Store each chunk's sparse vector as deterministic alphabetical/ascending term-id (index:u32 LE, value:f16/int8) pairs (CSR: offsets[] + indices[] + values[]), which respects nest's additive v1 reservation (0x09+ reserved), little-endian, repr(C) rules. nest-runtime gains a splade::SparseIndex that scores queries via sparse dot-product over an inverted index, then feeds candidates into the EXISTING mandatory exact-cosine rerank (search contract preserved: SPLADE/bm25 are ANN proxies, cosine stays ground truth) and fuses with bm25 via the existing reciprocal-rank fusion. This is a strict upgrade over the current word-segmented bm25 tokenizer (the known CJK/Thai gap): SPLADE term expansion is model-learned and vocabulary-based, so it degrades far less on non-space-delimited languages. Crucially for the north star, a SPLADE vector is ~99% zeros, so CSR + zstd (allowed on non-embedding sections) compresses it dramatically better than a dense f32 embedding, letting a 'sparse' preset ship retrieval quality near dense embeddings at a fraction of the bytes.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct. A SPLADE vector is a learned sparse vector that is ~99% zeros, so stored as CSR (sorted term-id deltas + quantized weights) it is an order of magnitude smaller than a dense f32 embedding while remaining a strong retrieval signal. Delta-coding ascending term ids (varint or fixed u32) plus int8/f16 weights, then zstd on the whole section (permitted because sparse indices are not on the SIMD dot-product hot path), pushes nest's size ratio well below the current tiny preset for text-dominant corpora. It also unlocks 'compress-and-still-search' for the bm25 replacement path.
repos.perf_notes: Sparse dot-product retrieval scales with nonzeros per query (tens to low hundreds of terms), not embedding dimension, so it is cache-friendly and avoids dense vector scans; well suited to nest's mmap-off-disk model. Dense pooling (mean/cls/max) is expressed as framework tensor reductions; on CPU these map cleanly to nest's existing AVX2/NEON dot-product dispatcher for the exact-cosine rerank stage. Dynamic batching is a server-side throughput trick (offline nest does not need the queue) but the per-token budget idea informs batched build-time embedding in nest-python. License: Apache-2.0 (note: TEI's own server has a custom HFOIL license on newer releases; only the algorithmic SPLADE/pooling math is being reused, not their code).
repos.license: Apache-2.0 for older code; newer TEI releases carry a custom HFOIL source-available license. Only the SPLADE/pooling math (public research, SPLADE paper) is adapted, not TEI source, so nest stays clean.

synthesis.summary: The embeddings-models corpus splits cleanly into two layers for nest, which only consumes float outputs (never runs inference): (1) a build-side production layer (CLIP, BERT/WordPiece, sentence-transformers, BGE-M3, Qwen3-Embedding, Model2Vec, SetFit, rust-sbert, rust-bert, word2vec, GloVe) that pins the post-encoder convention and ships cheap deterministic encoders; and (2) a storage/scoring layer that is the real prize for the 'compress more than everyone' north star. The collective state of the art is converging on one contract that nest already half-implements: produce L2-normalized unit vectors so cosine == dot product (CLIP, word2vec, all ST models), then aggressively compress the embeddings section along FOUR orthogonal, multiplicative axes -- value precision (f16/int8, already in nest), dimensionality (Matryoshka truncate-then-renormalize: Qwen3/BGE/ST), sub-byte vector quantization (fastText product quantization, ~8x), and representation sparsity (SPLADE/BGE-M3 learned-sparse, ~99% zeros, zstd-friendly) -- with quality guarded by exactly nest's existing pattern: a lossy form for candidate generation plus a mandatory exact-cosine rerank that makes the returned score honest. nest's int8 'tiny' preset (0.283 ratio, recall@10 0.992) is mid-pack; PQ + MRL + sparse stack multiplicatively below it toward ~0.10-0.14. The biggest correctness gap (word-segmented BM25 that collapses on CJK/Thai) is fixed for free at the tokenizer layer (BERT CJK basic-tokenizer) and superseded at the index layer (SPLADE/BGE learned-sparse on subword ids). The model-production gap (300-500ms python boot, torch dependency) is closed by Model2Vec static distillation, a sub-30MB lookup-table encoder with an official MIT Rust port, giving sovereign offline re-embedding. Everything maps to additive-only changes: new encoding IDs in the free 4-255 range, new optional sections at 0x09+, and new manifest/search_contract fields, with zero NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: Convergent contract across the field: encoders emit L2-normalized vectors on the unit hypersphere so cosine(a,b) == dot(a,b) (CLIP's logit_scale temperature, word2vec normalize-at-load, every sentence-transformers Normalize module, Qwen3/BGE truncate-then-renormalize). This single convention -- which nest must PIN in search_contract as 'normalize=l2' -- is the precondition that makes everything downstream cheap: pure SIMD dot product with no per-query sqrt/div, and near-lossless int8 because every component lies in a bounded [-1,1] with one symmetric per-vector scale. On top of that base, four independent compression axes have matured: (A) VALUE PRECISION -- f16 (2x) and int8 (4x), both validated as ~lossless on normalized+PCA-whitened vectors (Model2Vec, sentence-transformers); nest already ships these. (B) DIMENSIONALITY -- Matryoshka Representation Learning front-loads information so vec[:d] is independently valid after renormalize; Qwen reports 4096->1024 keeps ~95% recall at 75% storage cut, ST reports 1024->256 at 0.6% drop; a pure deterministic prefix slice, multiplicative with (A). (C) SUB-BYTE QUANTIZATION -- fastText product quantization (k=256 subvector k-means -> 1-byte codes, dsub=2 -> 1 byte per 2 dims = 8x base, norm decoupled, asymmetric LUT scoring with no decode on the hot path) plus binary 1-bit quantization (sign-threshold + popcount-Hamming, 32x, ST asymmetric rescore recovers ~96% recall). (D) SPARSITY -- SPLADE (TEI) and BGE-M3 learned-sparse emit vocab-sized ~99%-zero vectors stored as CSR (sorted term-id deltas + int8/f16 weights), an order of magnitude smaller than dense f32, scored by integer merge-join, and zstd-compressible because they are off the float hot path. The unifying retrieval discipline is compress-then-rescore: the lossy/sparse/ANN form does candidate generation only, then a higher-fidelity rerank produces the final score (CLIP /rank, ST asymmetric rescore, BGE weighted fusion, TEI cross-encoder) -- structurally identical to nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank after hnsw/bm25 RRF, which validates nest's design and means nest can adopt ALL of these as candidate generators without weakening its 'returned score is real cosine' guarantee. On the production side, the trend is away from heavy torch towards portable artifacts: a model is 'an ONNX graph + a vocab' (clip-as-service) or, more radically, 'a [vocab x dim] static lookup table' (Model2Vec: tokenize + gather + mean-pool, no forward pass, ~500x faster CPU, 8-30MB, PCA-whitened + SIF/Zipf-weighted, int8-quantizable, with an official Rust port needing only safetensors + tokenizers). Multilingual quality (the PT-BR/CJK/Thai concern) is solved at two layers: BERT's CJK-aware basic tokenizer (insert boundaries around Han codepoints, NFD accent strip, punctuation isolation) fixes lexical tokenization, and M-CLIP/XLM-R/LaBSE text towers plus SPLADE/BGE subword sparsity fix it semantically.
top_innovations: Product Quantization with asymmetric LUT scoring (fastText.zip): subvector k-means (k=256 -> 1-byte codes, dsub=2) stores 1 byte per 2 dims (~8x base, ~16x vs f32) with norm decoupled; query builds a per-subvector lookup table once, then each candidate is dim/dsub byte-indexed loads + f32 adds with NO float decode on the hot path -- a perfect fit for nest's score-off-mmap SIMD model and the single highest-leverage embedding-compression steal. Demonstrated 250x model shrink (427MB->1.7MB) with negligible loss.

Matryoshka Representation Learning truncate-then-renormalize (Qwen3-Embedding, BGE-M3, sentence-transformers): embedding dimensionality becomes a near-lossless deterministic compression knob (slice prefix, L2-renormalize) that is multiplicative with int8/f16/PQ and also shrinks the HNSW index. 256-of-1024 at int8 = ~16x vs f32-1024. A pure deterministic slice, so byte-identical builds hold.

Compress-then-rescore as the universal search contract (sentence-transformers binary/int8, CLIP /rank, BGE fusion, TEI cross-encoder): store a lossy/sparse form for cheap candidate generation, rerank survivors at higher fidelity so the FINAL score is honest. This is nest's existing mandatory exact-cosine rerank generalized to the CODEC layer -- it is the ONLY safe way to compress embeddings while keeping 'returned score is real cosine', and it licenses adopting PQ, binary, and sparse all as candidate generators.

Learned sparse vectors (SPLADE in TEI, lexical_weights in BGE-M3): a vocab-sized ~99%-zero vector of (token_id, weight) pairs that is a semantic, language-agnostic, drop-in upgrade over BM25 tf-idf, stored as CSR (delta-coded ascending term ids + int8/f16 weights), zstd-compressed (off the float hot path), and scored by integer merge-join. Simultaneously shrinks the lexical index AND fixes nest's CJK/Thai BM25 gap with subword ids.

Model2Vec static distillation (MinishLab): collapse a sentence-transformer into a [vocab x dim] lookup table so encoding = tokenize + gather + mean-pool (no forward pass), PCA-whitened + SIF/Zipf-weighted offline, int8-quantizable, 8-30MB, ~500x faster CPU, dataset-free, deterministic, with an official MIT Rust port (safetensors + tokenizers). Gives nest a sovereign offline single-file embedder that kills the 300-500ms python boot and the torch dependency.

L2-normalize as a pinned build-time invariant (CLIP, word2vec, all ST Normalize heads): store embeddings pre-normalized so the SIMD dot equals true cosine with zero per-query sqrt/div, AND normalize-before-quantize tightens the int8 scale range to lift recall at the same byte cost. The precondition that makes every other compression axis safe to validate against a stable ground truth.

Binary quantization with popcount-Hamming first stage (sentence-transformers): sign-threshold normalized f32 to 1 bit/dim (32x), packbits, retrieve by XOR + popcount (~2 CPU cycles, a tiny AVX2 popcnt / NEON vcnt kernel), then asymmetric rescore against int8/f32 recovers ~96% recall. The cheapest possible first-stage candidate gate, fully inside nest's SIMD dispatcher.

BERT CJK-aware basic tokenizer + WordPiece greedy-longest-match: a data-only, model-free, deterministic pure function (insert boundaries around Han/CJK codepoint ranges, NFD accent strip, punctuation isolation, then greedy ## subword match over an ordered vocab) that fixes nest's named CJK/Thai BM25 degradation with ZERO bm25 codec change -- terms stay UTF-8 length-prefixed alphabetical, section 0x08 byte-identical.

PCA-whitening before quantization (Model2Vec, sentence-transformers): decorrelate/normalize the embedding space offline (a build-time matrix multiply) so int8/binary/PQ lose ~nothing; ~2.8% gain even at full dim. A pure build-side conditioning pass that strengthens every nest codec at the same byte cost.

Contrastive distillation to a smaller-dimension student (SetFit, BGE self-distillation): re-embed a corpus into a lower-dim space (768->256) whose neighbor ordering is preserved, attacking the float COUNT (not just width) -- the one axis zstd/int8 cannot touch -- multiplicative with int8, guarded by exact rerank. A 'nano' preset below tiny.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add Matryoshka dimension-truncation as a build-time codec: nest-python slices each f32 vector to a chosen mrl_dim prefix and re-L2-normalizes before writing; store full_dim + mrl_dim in the embeddings section header and mirror into search_contract. Runtime needs only honor the smaller per-vector stride from the manifest -- existing AVX2/NEON/scalar kernels and the int8 view run unchanged on the shorter row. Exact rerank stays true cosine because vectors are renormalized on the prefix.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add encoding=4 'pq' (product quantization) as a new embeddings codec in the free 4-255 additive range, sibling to int8.rs. On-disk layout mirrors int8.rs prefix conventions: u32 payload_version, u32 dsub, seeded-k-means codebook (m_subspaces*256*dsub f32 centroids), per-vector scalar norm (reuse int8 norm machinery), then n*(dim/dsub) u8 codes. Runtime SIMD dispatcher builds the asymmetric query LUT (query dotted vs mmapped codebook via existing dot kernels) once per query, scores each candidate as dim/dsub byte-indexed adds off mmap, then feeds the mandatory exact-cosine rerank -- PQ is only the ANN coarse filter, never the final score. Enables a 'nano' preset (~0.14 ratio) below tiny. k-means MUST be seeded in the python builder for byte-identical builds.

Candidate generation only; exact-cosine rerank stays ground truth. Replaces the word-segmented BM25 (fixes CJK/Thai) AND shrinks the lexical index.

nest_recommendations.idea: Pin 'normalize=l2' as a checked invariant in search_contract and document/enforce L2-normalized embeddings: nest-python L2-normalizes (and for int8, normalizes BEFORE quantizing to tighten the per-vector scale range). The on-disk BM25 codec needs ZERO change -- terms stay UTF-8 length-prefixed sorted alphabetical, section 0x08 byte-identical, determinism preserved. Clean-room reimplement the algorithm + CJK ranges (not vocab.txt).

Recovers ~96% recall via asymmetric rescore; never touches Python; the binary form is candidate-gen only so 'score is real cosine' holds.

Optionally store CLIP's logit_scale temperature scalar in provenance (additive, content_hash-safe) for a calibrated logit scoring mode in search_contract. nest_recommendations.impact: medium

compression_wins: Product quantization (encoding=4, dsub=2, k=256) stores 1 byte per 2 dims = ~8x over raw f32 and ~2x over the current int8 codec, scored off mmap via asymmetric LUT with no float decode and guarded by exact rerank -- the single biggest lever to push embeddings (the largest, non-zstd-compressible section) toward a ~0.14 ratio and beat int8's 0.283 tiny preset. fastText.zip evidence: 427MB->1.7MB (250x) at negligible loss.

Matryoshka dimension truncation is multiplicative with value-precision: 256-of-1024 prefix (4x on dims) at int8 (4x on width) = ~16x smaller embeddings than f32-1024, a pure deterministic prefix slice with ~0.6-5% recall cost, also shrinking the HNSW index footprint since graph vectors are shorter. The one compression axis (float COUNT) that zstd/f16/int8 cannot touch.

Learned-sparse (SPLADE/BGE) CSR sections are ~99% zeros: stored as delta-varint ascending term ids + int8/f16 weights then zstd'd (safe because off the SIMD hot path), they carry semantic keyword search in an order of magnitude fewer bytes than dense f32 or a raw text index -- a text-dominant corpus can ship retrieval quality near dense at a fraction of the bytes, advancing compress-and-still-search.

Binary 1-bit quantization is 32x on the embeddings section (1024d -> 128 bytes) as a first-stage candidate gate; asymmetric rescore against the int8/f32 vectors recovers ~96% recall, so the 32x form is used only for candidate generation and the final score stays real cosine.

PCA-whitening + L2-normalization BEFORE quantization is a free quality multiplier: it conditions the space so int8/binary/PQ lose ~nothing (Model2Vec reaches 25% of original size with no measurable loss; ~2.8% gain even at full dim), letting nest push to lower-bit packing at the SAME byte cost and lifting recall at the 0.283 tiny ratio.

Contrastive distillation to a smaller-dimension student (768->256) attacks the float COUNT directly and composes multiplicatively with int8 (~3x on top of ~4x), plausibly pushing a 'nano' preset below the current 0.283 tiny ratio, with the exact-cosine rerank guarding recall against the lossier embedder.

Codebook + residual via topic/IVF centroids (Top2Vec geometry): store K centroids + per-chunk topic_id (1-2 bytes) + small residual, exploiting redundancy ACROSS chunks; reordering chunks by topic_id also places similar embeddings adjacent, improving byte-locality and zstd ratio on the zstd-eligible sections (chunks_canonical, provenance). Auto-generated label terms double as a zstd custom dictionary seed for chunks_canonical.

Frequency-rank id remapping (GloVe/word2vec/Model2Vec Zipf) on bm25/sparse postings clusters dense entries at small ids, directly improving zstd entropy coding on the non-embedding index sections at zero quality cost.
watch_outs: NEVER zstd the embeddings section: it is scored directly from mmap on the SIMD hot path, so any whole-section entropy coding breaks score-off-disk. PQ/binary/MRL/int8 are fine because they are FIXED-stride codecs read by stride, not stream-decompressed. Sparse/CSR sections (0x09) and centroid/topic sections ARE zstd-eligible precisely because they are scored by merge-join, not a float dot off mmap -- keep that boundary sharp.

Do NOT vendor torch/libtorch (rust-sbert tch-rs, rust-bert) or candle/ONNX-Runtime servers into the small rust core: these are hundreds-of-MB native deps that violate single-file/offline/small-core. Inference stays build-side in nest-python; the runtime only consumes floats. The ONLY runtime-embeddable encoder is Model2Vec (model2vec-rs: safetensors + tokenizers, MIT), and even that should be a gated feature, not core.

k-means (PQ codebook), PCA rotation, HDBSCAN/UMAP clustering, and any sampling shuffle are nondeterministic by default and will break byte-identical builds. PQ k-means and topic clustering MUST be seeded; UMAP/HDBSCAN (Numba/SciPy, fragile, non-deterministic) must stay python build-side and never enter the rust runtime -- use seeded k-means or fixed-threshold greedy cosine agglomeration for any in-runtime clustering. GloVe's default rand_long() shuffle must be reseeded if adapted.

Adopting a learned subword/WordPiece/SPLADE vocab changes the BM25/sparse term space, so determinism requires the vocab be FROZEN and its fingerprint recorded in provenance/search_contract; the greedy-match algorithm and CJK ranges are clean-room reimplementable, but a shipped vocab.txt artifact bloats the single file and is training-produced -- prefer the model-free CJK basic tokenizer as the must-have and treat WordPiece/SPLADE vocab as optional.

Honor the additive-only v1 constraint precisely: PQ/binary go in encoding ids 4-255 (4 is the next free), sparse/topic/splade go in section ids 0x09+; new manifest/search_contract fields are fine, but do NOT change the meaning of any existing field (mrl_dim/full_dim must be additive optional, not a redefinition of dim) or you force a true v2 NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump.

Keep every new rust module single-responsibility and <=300 lines (333 hard cap): PQ codec, popcount-Hamming kernel, SparseIndex, external_merge, and CJK tokenizer each need their own file; do not fold PQ scoring into the existing simd/mod.rs (already ~144 lines) past the cap.

ColBERT late-interaction (BGE-M3 multi-vector MaxSim) is O(N_q*N_d*dim) and storage-heavy (per-token vectors) -- use it only as an optional rerank-only signal if ever, NEVER as a candidate generator or a default, to keep the runtime light; the practical hybrid is dense + learned-sparse.

Never weaken the mandatory exact-cosine rerank: PQ, binary, sparse, and distilled-student vectors are ALL lossy and must remain candidate generators only. The returned score must always be real cosine recomputed against the highest-fidelity stored vectors, or nest loses its 'score is real cosine' guarantee.

logit_scale temperature scaling (CLIP) and weighted-sum fusion (BGE) introduce calibration scalars that, if folded into the stored/returned score, would make scores model-dependent and break cross-encoding score stability -- keep them as an OPTIONAL self-describing scoring mode in search_contract, never the default, so the default returned score stays plain cosine.

Image/CLIP support must not introduce a per-modality SIMD branch or a separate image codec: only L2-normalized 512-d vectors in the shared embeddings section qualify (they cosine-search identically to text). Anything requiring a distinct distance or layout would fork the hot path and violate the minimal-format goal.

categories.name: tokenizers
categories.focus: tokenization (the front of every embed + a compression primitive)

repos.one_liner: A Rust-core tokenization library (Python/Node/Ruby bindings) implementing BPE, WordPiece, Unigram and WordLevel behind a five-stage normalizer -> pre-tokenizer -> model -> post-processor -> decoder pipeline, with full original-span alignment tracking and a single self-describing tokenizer.json serialization.
repos.core_innovation: Reversible byte-level alphabet (GPT-2 scheme): the 256 raw bytes are bijectively remapped to printable Unicode codepoints so any byte stream - CJK, Thai, emoji, binary, JSON, PDF text - is losslessly tokenizable by a learned subword vocabulary with zero UNK and zero out-of-vocab loss, turning a learned merge table into a reversible variable-length dictionary code over arbitrary bytes.
key_techniques: Byte-level BPE: bijective 256-byte to printable-Unicode map (byte_level.rs) so the model alphabet is closed and tokenization is fully reversible/lossless on any input

BPE merge_word: Word as Vec of (symbol, prev, next) linked-array plus a BinaryHeap of Merge candidates keyed by (rank, pos); merges lowest-rank pair first with deterministic tie-break (leftmost), O(n log n) per word
merges stored as HashMap<(u32,u32), (rank:u32, new_id:u32)> - pair-rank lookup, not string compares; vocab as HashMap<String,u32> plus reverse Vec for id_to_token

Unigram model: Viterbi forward-DP over a lattice of all substrings present in vocab, scored by log-probabilities, returns minimum-cost (most-probable) segmentation; trained via EM with iterative pruning
LRU word-result cache (cache.rs) + per-thread cache (PR 2028) to memoize BPE output per pre-token, +47-62% on parallel workloads
byte_fallback (SentencePiece trick): unknown chars decomposed to <0xNN> byte tokens so vocab stays small but coverage is total
Full alignment/offset tracking: every token carries (start,end) byte offsets back into the ORIGINAL string even through destructive (NFKC/lowercase/strip) normalization
Single self-describing tokenizer.json via serde: one file carries normalizer+pre_tokenizer+model(vocab,merges)+post_processor+decoder, version-tagged, reconstructs the exact pipeline
repos.nest_application: Three concrete lifts. (1) Replace the word-segmented bm25 tokenizer in nest-runtime/src/bm25 with a byte-level pre-tokenizer + tiny deterministic BPE/Unigram model: kills the known CJK/Thai degradation gap, stays deterministic (alphabetical-equivalent merge-rank order), needs no extra section. (2) Add a learned-BPE codec for the text-bearing sections: train a per-file BPE/Unigram vocab over chunks_canonical, store the merge table as a new RESERVED encoding id (4-255) in nest-format/src/encoding, and emit token-id streams instead of raw UTF-8 - this is dictionary compression that composes with zstd and is the single most mission-relevant idea for compress-more-than-everyone on repetitive corpora; vocab+merges become a deterministic part of content_hash. (3) Steal the offset-alignment model to harden chunks_original_spans: nest already maps canonical->original; the (start,end)-through-normalization technique is the proven design for keeping nest://content_hash/chunk_id byte-exact after lossy normalization. Mirror the single tokenizer.json idea: keep the tokenizer config inline in the manifest so the file stays self-describing and offline.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central: a learned BPE/Unigram vocabulary IS a variable-length dictionary code, and the byte-level alphabet makes it lossless and reversible on arbitrary bytes (text/json/yaml/pdf-text). Token-id streams shrink repetitive corpora before zstd, and Unigram-Viterbi gives provably minimum-cost segmentation. The merge table is the entropy-model that beats generic zstd on structured/repetitive data - the core lever for the compress-more-than-everyone north star. Caveat: must never be applied to the embeddings section (hot-path SIMD scoring needs raw f32/f16/int8 off mmap), only to text-bearing sections.
repos.perf_notes: Rust core tokenizes ~1GB/CPU-min (<20s/GB cited). Hot path is merge_word with the BinaryHeap; LRU + per-thread cache memoize per pre-token (single-thread flat, +47-62% at 88+ threads). Merge lookups are integer (u32,u32) HashMap probes, no string compares. Build-time win: BPE::Builder no longer formats strings in hot loop (~45% faster from_file on Llama-3). No SIMD in the tokenizer itself; parallelism is rayon over the batch. Memory: vocab+merges are plain HashMaps, fits easily; tokenizer.json for large LLM vocabs (128k-256k) is a few MB.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: Language-agnostic subword tokenizer that trains a unigram-LM (or BPE) vocabulary by EM + Viterbi over a lattice and ships the whole model (pieces, float scores, byte-fallback, NFKC normalizer FST) self-contained in one protobuf, decoded at runtime via a Darts double-array trie.
repos.core_innovation: A tokenizer is a self-contained, deterministic compression codec: a vocabulary of variable-length pieces with floating-point scores plus a single best-path (Viterbi-over-lattice) decoder segments arbitrary text losslessly into ID streams. The whole model (vocab + scores + normalization rules + byte-fallback) is one frozen byte-stable blob, and the hot-path lookup structure is a double-array trie that holds 80k+ pieces in ~2 MB instead of ~83 MB. This is exactly the deterministic, single-file, compress-text primitive nest needs, sitting in front of (or instead of) zstd for the canonical-text section.
key_techniques: Unigram LM training: suffix-array-seeded large vocabulary, then EM (E: forward-backward/Viterbi expected piece counts, M: update piece probabilities) with loss-ranked pruning by shrinking_factor=0.75 until target size -- inverse of BPE's grow-by-merge

Viterbi best-path segmentation over a lattice where each piece is an arc scored by log unigram prob; O(n) memory by storing only best_path score+backpointer per char position (lattice nodes recognized then discarded, no node pool)
Darts double-array trie: 4 parallel arrays base[]/check[]/value[]/score[], transition next=base[node]+byte validated by check[next]==node; collapses 256-pointer-per-node tries to ~2 MB for 80k pieces
first_byte_max_len[256] table for early trie-traversal termination (2x on CJK where most byte continuations are invalid)
byte_fallback: OOV chars decompose into 256 raw BYTE-type pieces (Type=6) so the model is total/lossless over any input, never emitting <unk>
Self-contained proto2 ModelProto: repeated SentencePiece{piece, float score, Type} plus NormalizerSpec, all behavior-changing params embedded for reproducible portable artifact
precompiled_charsmap: NFKC normalization compiled into a second double-array trie + '\0'-delimited rewrite string, layout [u32 trie_len][trie][normalized], so normalization is a data table not code
U+2581 meta-symbol marks whitespace so detokenization is a pure string replace -> fully reversible round-trip
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals. (1) New section + codec for extreme text compression: add a frozen unigram-LM tokenizer model as an optional v1 section (reserved id 0x09+) and a new encoding id (range 4-255) that stores chunks_canonical as Viterbi-segmented piece-ID streams instead of raw/zstd bytes. Python (nest-python) trains the EM model offline; nest-format/src/encoding/ gets a unigram_codec.rs holding the read-only double-array trie + scores and running O(n)-memory Viterbi decode; the ID stream is then varint/range-coded and optionally zstd'd. Because IDs index a shared vocab, this beats per-chunk zstd on short repetitive corpora and is deterministic (seeded EM + stable tie-break) so byte-identical builds hold. Segmentation is reversible so content_hash over decoded canonical text stays stable. (2) Fix the known CJK/Thai bm25 gap: replace the word-split tokenizer at crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/tokenize.rs with subword Viterbi segmentation from the same shipped model, giving script-agnostic BM25 terms (alphabetical term order preserved for determinism). The Darts double-array trie fits nest's repr(C), little-endian, mmap, never-panic constraints: it is just integer arrays read straight off disk.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to compress-data-more-than-everyone. A shared subword vocabulary turns canonical text into dense small-integer ID streams; on repetitive/structured corpora (news, JSON keys, code) this routinely cuts entropy-coder input vs raw bytes, and stacking range/zstd on the ID stream compounds it. Unlike a general byte compressor the model is trained ON the corpus so it captures domain-specific morphemes, and byte_fallback guarantees losslessness on any input. The double-array trie keeps the decoder tiny and mmap-resident, fitting the light/portable mandate.
repos.perf_notes: ~50k sentences/sec segmentation, ~6 MB runtime footprint (vocab ~1.5 MB + trie ~2 MB + score/hash arrays). Inference is O(n*L) time, O(n) memory (L = max piece len 16-32 bytes). Hot path is pointer-light integer indexing into base/check, ideal for mmap. SIMD upside is modest: community ARM64 port used CRC32 only for model-load hashing, not Viterbi; trie traversal is lookup/branch-bound not a dot-product kernel, so it does not contend with nest's AVX2/NEON cosine path. Stack-allocated Viterbi buffers (cap ~8192 chars) with heap fallback keep allocation off the hot path.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A fast Rust-core byte-level BPE (byte pair encoding) tokenizer whose vocabulary is a flat HashMap<Vec<u8>, Rank> mapping byte sequences to compact integer merge-priority ranks, driving a regex pre-split plus greedy lowest-rank merge loop that is reversible, lossless, language-agnostic, and deterministic.
repos.core_innovation: BPE as a deterministic, reversible, lossless byte-to-integer compression code: pre-split text with a fixed unicode-property regex, then greedily merge adjacent byte-pairs in strict ascending "rank" order (rank = global merge priority loaded from a tiny on-disk vocab), so the same input always yields the same shorter integer-ID stream and decode is a pure HashMap<Rank, Vec<u8>> concat. Tokenization is itself compression (fewer, denser symbols than raw UTF-8 bytes), it is byte-level so it never fails on arbitrary/CJK/Thai/binary input, and it is bit-exact reproducible from a frozen vocab file.
key_techniques: byte-level BPE: vocab is HashMap<Vec<u8>, Rank> (rank = merge priority, lower merged first); decode is HashMap<Rank, Vec<u8>>
greedy lowest-rank merge on parts: Vec<(start, rank)>; O(mn) linear-scan-for-min for pieces <100 bytes, BinaryHeap<Merge> O(m log n) for large pieces (_byte_pair_merge_large)
Rank::MAX sentinel marks unmergeable pairs; get_rank closure looks up piece[parts[i].0..parts[i+3].0] slices in the encoder map

fixed unicode-property regex pre-tokenization (fancy_regex), e.g. cl100k splits on \p{L}++ runs, \p{N}{1,3}+ digit groups, contraction suffixes, whitespace runs; bounds merges and guarantees determinism
compact .tiktoken vocab format: one line = base64(token_bytes) + ' ' + ascii(rank) + newline; loaded into the map and SHA-256 verified against expected_hash
special tokens in a separate special_tokens_encoder map plus separate regex so merges never cross sentinel boundaries
FxHashMap over std HashMap (5-10% win); thread-local cloned regexes indexed by thread-id to avoid lock contention; no SIMD, GIL released for parallelism
the token set itself acts as the cache (no separate memoization); hot subwords are already vocab entries
repos.nest_application: Add a byte-level BPE tokenizer in nest-runtime::bm25 to replace the word-segmented tokenizer (the documented CJK/Thai gap): BPE pre-split plus merge yields language-agnostic subword terms while keeping bm25's required alphabetical/deterministic term order. Ship the frozen vocab as a new optional additive section (reserve a v1 id in 0x09+, e.g. bpe_vocab) encoded exactly as tiktoken's base64(bytes)+rank lines, then zstd-compressed via nest's existing non-embedding codec path; stays single-file, offline, per-section SHA-256 checksummed. The merge loop is pure-safe Rust (parts Vec + sentinel, no panics, thiserror on missing vocab), ~150-200 loc so it fits the 300-line rule, and seedless-deterministic so it preserves reproducible builds. Strategically, also expose a nest-cli/nest-format codec that stores chunks_canonical as BPE token-ID streams (a denser integer code than raw UTF-8) feeding a future entropy-coded text section; content_hash stays stable because it hashes decoded canonical bytes, not the encoding.
repos.compression_relevance: High and on-mission. BPE is compression by construction: it turns multi-byte UTF-8 runs into single small integers, and a BPE token stream is a strictly denser, dictionary-coded representation that downstream zstd/entropy coding compresses further. It is the natural front-end for an extreme text-compression pipeline (BPE IDs to rANS/range coder), and being byte-level plus deterministic it respects nest's lossless, reproducible, language-agnostic guarantees. Directly closes the known CJK/Thai bm25 tokenizer gap.
repos.license: MIT License
repos.perf_notes: 3-6x faster than HuggingFace tokenizers on 1GB GPT-2 text. Pure scalar Rust, no SIMD. Two merge paths: linear O(mn) for short pieces (<100 bytes, common after regex split), BinaryHeap O(m log n) for rare long pieces. FxHashMap and thread-local regex clones are the main micro-opts; parallelism comes from releasing the Python GIL, not rayon. Memory is dominated by the vocab map (cl100k ~100k entries, o200k ~200k entries); the .tiktoken file is a few MB of base64 lines, very zstd-friendly.

repos.one_liner: A fast C++ (with Python pyonmttok bindings) reversible tokenization library that combines Unicode-aware pre-segmentation with BPE/SentencePiece subword encoding, reversible joiner/spacer markup, and vocabulary-restricted recursive OOV splitting.
repos.core_innovation: Fully reversible, lossless tokenization: every segmentation decision (joins, spaces, case, script changes) is encoded as in-band modifier characters (joiner U+FFED, spacer U+2581, case markups, protected-region brackets) so the original text reconstructs byte-exactly from the token stream. This separates a reversible surface encoding from the compression model, exactly the property nest needs for a tokenizer-backed compression codec.
key_techniques: BPE merge table as two hash maps: _codes (concatenated pair string -> merge rank/priority, lower rank applied earlier) for O(1) priority lookup, and _codes_reverse (pair -> its two constituent tokens) to undo merges

Greedy min-rank merge loop: precompute scores for all adjacent pairs (rank or INT_MAX), repeatedly merge lowest-rank pair, incrementally update only the two neighbor scores, stop when best_score==INT_MAX
Vocabulary-restricted recursive_split: OOV tokens decomposed by reversing BPE merges via _codes_reverse until every piece is in-vocab or atomic, giving a deterministic bounded token vocabulary
Reversible joiner/spacer in-band markup (U+FFED joiner, U+2581 spacer) for lossless detokenization without storing original spans separately
case_feature / case_markup: factor casing out as a separate channel (C/L/U/M/N tags or soft uppercase-region markers) so the subword model sees lowercase only, shrinking effective vocab
Protected sequences (U+FF9F brackets) and placeholders that bypass tokenization entirely for exact passthrough of opaque spans
Unicode-type pre-segmentation (aggressive mode) via ICU: split on script/character-type change and digit boundaries, deterministic and language-aware
BPE-dropout: stochastically skip merges during training for subword regularization
repos.nest_application: Adapt the reversible-encoding plus BPE-merge-table pattern into nest-format as a new additive encoding id (in the reserved 4-255 space) for the chunks_canonical(text) section: ship a frozen deterministic BPE merge table (two flat little-endian arrays mirroring _codes and _codes_reverse, repr(C)) plus a token-id stream, replacing raw/zstd text bytes with subword token ids that zstd then compresses better (smaller alphabet, repeated merges). The reversible joiner/spacer markup is the key piece: it lets nest reconstruct exact canonical text from token ids, preserving content_hash stability and chunks_original_spans round-tripping. The vocabulary-restricted recursive_split gives a deterministic, seed-free, bounded token vocabulary satisfying nest's determinism constraint. Separately, case_feature/case_markup factoring is stealable for nest-runtime bm25::Bm25Index reversible case normalization, and the Unicode-type/script-change pre-segmenter is a concrete fix for the known bm25 CJK/Thai word-segmentation gap. Keep C++/ICU out: reimplement the merge loop in safe Rust (no panic, typed thiserror) in a sub-300-line module under crates/nest-format/src/encoding/.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly relevant. Subword tokenization is an entropy-reduction front-end: replacing UTF-8 byte runs with token ids over a small learned vocabulary shrinks the symbol alphabet and exposes long repeated merges, so a downstream zstd pass on token ids compresses text notably better than zstd on raw bytes, while reversible markup keeps it lossless and content_hash-stable. The vocabulary cap bounds dictionary size for tiny-preset goals. This is a complementary codec layer ahead of nest's existing zstd path for the text sections only (never embeddings).
repos.perf_notes: C++11 core with ICU for Unicode; encoding is O(chars x merges) per word with no word->subword cache (computed fresh per request, so a Rust port should add a word-keyed LRU cache). Hash-map lookups O(1); merge loop updates neighbor scores incrementally rather than recomputing all pairs. Single-threaded per token; Python overhead amortized via the pyonmttok C extension. No SIMD in the tokenizer hot path (branchy string work), so nest gains nothing for its SIMD dot-product path here, only for the build-time text codec.
repos.license: MIT

synthesis.summary: Across HF tokenizers, SentencePiece, tiktoken, and OpenNMT Tokenizer the field has converged on one shape that is almost custom-built for nest's north star: a tokenizer is a self-contained, frozen, deterministic, reversible compression codec. The shared primitives are (a) a byte-level alphabet (GPT-2/tiktoken bijective 256-byte<->printable-Unicode map, or SentencePiece byte_fallback emitting <0xNN>) that makes ANY input -- CJK, Thai, emoji, JSON, YAML, PDF-text, binary -- losslessly tokenizable with zero UNK; (b) a learned variable-length dictionary code, either grow-by-merge BPE (HashMap<(u32,u32)->rank> integer-pair merges, greedy lowest-rank) or shrink-by-prune Unigram-LM (Viterbi best-path over a lattice scored by log-probs, O(n) memory); (c) reversible surface markup (U+2581 spacer / U+FFED joiner / case channel) so detokenization is a pure string op and the round-trip is byte-exact; (d) compact mmap-resident lookup structures (SentencePiece Darts double-array trie holds 80k pieces in ~2MB vs ~83MB of pointer tries, just integer base[]/check[]/value[] arrays read straight off disk); (e) full (start,end) offset alignment back into the ORIGINAL string surviving destructive NFKC/lowercase/strip normalization; and (f) one version-tagged self-describing artifact (tokenizer.json / ModelProto) carrying the entire pipeline. The crucial reframing for nest: token-id streams ARE compression -- they replace multi-byte UTF-8 runs with dense small integers BEFORE zstd, and because the dictionary is trained ON the corpus it captures domain morphemes (PT-BR news, JSON keys, code) that generic zstd cannot model. Stacking range/zstd on the id stream compounds the win. This is the single most mission-relevant external category for 'compress more than everyone' on text-bearing sections, and it simultaneously closes the documented CJK/Thai bm25 gap with the same shipped model. Hard caveat repeated by every extract: NEVER apply to the embeddings section -- the hot-path SIMD cosine kernel scores raw f32/f16/int8 straight off mmap and tokenization would destroy that.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The state of the art is a unified pipeline normalizer -> pre-tokenizer -> model -> post-processor -> decoder, where the 'model' is a learned variable-length dictionary over a CLOSED byte-level alphabet, serialized as a single frozen self-describing artifact and decoded by a tiny integer-indexed structure. Two training philosophies, one runtime shape. BPE (tiktoken, HF, OpenNMT) grows a vocab by greedily merging the lowest-rank adjacent byte-pair; merges are stored as integer (u32,u32)->rank HashMaps (no string compares), decode is HashMap<rank,Vec<u8>> concat, fully deterministic and seedless. Unigram-LM (SentencePiece, HF) starts from a large suffix-array-seeded vocab and prunes by EM (shrinking_factor 0.75) until target size; segmentation is Viterbi over a lattice storing only best-path score+backpointer per char position (O(n) memory, recognized-then-discarded lattice nodes), giving provably minimum-cost segmentation. Losslessness on arbitrary bytes is universal via byte-level bijection (tiktoken/GPT-2) or byte_fallback to 256 raw-byte pieces (SentencePiece type=6) -- zero out-of-vocab loss, the property nest's lossless/reversible/content_hash-stable guarantees demand. Reversibility is achieved with in-band markup (U+2581 whitespace meta-symbol, U+FFED joiner, case channel) so the original reconstructs byte-exactly. The runtime lookup is the Darts double-array trie (base/check/value/score parallel arrays, transition next=base[node]+byte validated by check[next]==node, plus first_byte_max_len[256] early termination) -- 80k pieces in ~2MB, pointer-light integer indexing ideal for repr(C)+LE+mmap+never-panic, and it does NOT contend with the AVX2/NEON dot-product path (trie traversal is branch-bound, not a SIMD kernel). Perf is excellent and build-time only: tiktoken 3-6x faster than HF on 1GB GPT-2 text, HF ~1GB/CPU-min (<20s/GB), SentencePiece ~50k sentences/sec with ~6MB footprint, all pure scalar Rust/C++ with no SIMD in the tokenizer. Offset-alignment tracking (every token carries (start,end) byte offsets into the original even through destructive normalization) is the proven design for span-exact citations. Determinism is native: BPE merge-rank order and Unigram seeded-EM + stable tie-break (leftmost) make builds reproducible, which maps cleanly onto nest's bm25 alphabetical-term-order and seeded-hnsw discipline.
top_innovations: Byte-level closed alphabet (tiktoken/GPT-2 bijective 256-byte<->Unicode map; SentencePiece byte_fallback type=6 pieces): makes tokenization lossless and reversible on ANY input with zero UNK -- the non-negotiable property that lets a learned dictionary code satisfy nest's lossless/content_hash-stable/language-agnostic guarantees, and the direct fix for the CJK/Thai bm25 gap.

Token-id stream as dictionary compression front-end: a learned BPE/Unigram vocab turns multi-byte UTF-8 runs into dense small integers BEFORE entropy coding, and because it is trained ON the corpus it models domain morphemes (PT-BR news, JSON keys, code) that generic zstd cannot. The single most mission-relevant idea for compress-more-than-everyone on text-bearing sections.

SentencePiece Darts double-array trie: 80k pieces in ~2MB (vs ~83MB pointer tries) as plain integer base[]/check[]/value[]/score[] arrays read straight off mmap -- a perfect repr(C)+LE+never-panic decoder that keeps the tiny/portable mandate and never touches the SIMD cosine path.

Unigram-LM Viterbi best-path segmentation: O(n)-memory minimum-cost (most-probable) segmentation over a lattice, provably better symbol assignment than greedy BPE for compression, with seeded-EM determinism so byte-identical builds hold.

Reversible in-band markup (U+2581 spacer / U+FFED joiner / case channel from OpenNMT+SentencePiece): detokenization is a pure string replace, so token-id codec round-trips byte-exact and content_hash over decoded canonical text stays stable -- no separate span storage needed for reconstruction.

Integer (u32,u32)->rank merge tables (tiktoken/HF): pair-rank HashMap lookups, no string compares, seedless-deterministic greedy lowest-rank merge -- a ~150-200 loc pure-safe Rust merge loop that fits the 300-line file rule and the no-panic constraint.

Offset/alignment tracking through destructive normalization (HF (start,end) byte offsets surviving NFKC/lowercase/strip): the proven design to harden chunks_original_spans so nest://content_hash/chunk_id stays byte-exact after lossy normalization.

Single self-describing version-tagged artifact (tokenizer.json / proto2 ModelProto carrying normalizer+model+decoder): mirror inline in nest's manifest so the file stays self-describing, offline, and reconstructs the exact pipeline with no external dependency.

Word-result LRU + per-thread cache (HF cache.rs, +47-62% on parallel workloads; OpenNMT lacks it and pays per-request): memoize per pre-token at build time so the BPE/Viterbi hot loop is amortized over repetitive corpora.

precompiled_charsmap (SentencePiece NFKC compiled to a double-array trie + rewrite string, layout [u32 trie_len][trie][normalized]): normalization-as-data-table not code, a frozen deterministic LE blob that fits nest's data-over-code, reproducible-build philosophy.
