compression_wins: Token-id streams over a corpus-trained vocab replace multi-byte UTF-8 runs with dense small integers BEFORE zstd; on repetitive/structured corpora (PT-BR news, JSON keys, YAML, code) this lowers entropy-coder input vs raw bytes and the gain COMPOUNDS when zstd/range-codes the id stream -- the core lever for compress-more-than-everyone on text sections, and it composes with the existing zstd codec rather than replacing it.

Unigram-LM Viterbi gives provably minimum-cost (most-probable) segmentation, so the id assignment itself is information-theoretically tighter than greedy BPE -- fewer/denser symbols for the same lossless reconstruction.

Training the vocab ON the file's own corpus captures domain-specific morphemes (Portuguese inflections, dataset-specific tokens, repeated JSON schema keys) that a generic byte compressor like zstd cannot model, beating zstd-on-raw-bytes on exactly the structured/repetitive data nest targets.

The vocab cap (e.g. shrink-by-prune to a small target size) bounds dictionary size, so the per-file tokenizer section stays small (SentencePiece 80k pieces ~2MB trie) and the net size ratio improves for the tiny/micro presets rather than regressing.

Range/rANS coding the id stream (a natural next layer on top of dense ids) is the documented endgame BPE-ids -> entropy-coder; nest can stage this as encoding id 4 = tokenized, then later 5 = tokenized+range, all additive within v1.

Same shipped model serves double duty: the bytes spent on the tokenizer section are amortized across BOTH the text-compression codec AND the bm25 subword terms, so the marginal cost of closing the CJK/Thai gap is near zero once the codec ships.

Byte-level closed alphabet guarantees losslessness on json/yaml/pdf-text/binary, extending the compress-everything mandate (text, json, yaml, parquet, pdf, audio/video metadata) to a single reversible codec path without per-format special-casing.
watch_outs: NEVER tokenize the embeddings section. Every extract flags this: the hot path is SIMD cosine scoring raw f32/f16/int8 straight off mmap; token-id encoding would destroy random-access vector layout and the AVX2/NEON dot-product kernel. Enforce a hard guard that encoding id 4 (tokenized) is rejected for the embeddings section in decode_payload / writer.

Determinism is the make-or-break constraint. EM training (Unigram) is iterative and tie-breaks matter; you MUST seed EM and use a stable leftmost tie-break (BPE is naturally seedless/deterministic, prefer it if EM determinism is hard to pin). Without bit-exact reproducibility the same chunks + same model fingerprint will NOT produce a byte-identical file, breaking nest's core guarantee.

content_hash hashes DECODED canonical bytes -- the token-id codec MUST round-trip byte-exact (reversible markup, byte_fallback for any OOV) or citations and the STABLE-across-encodings content_hash guarantee break. Add a roundtrip assertion in the codec tests mirroring zstd_roundtrip_preserves_bytes.

Reject the C++/ICU dependency stacks. SentencePiece (proto2) and OpenNMT (ICU) bring heavy deps that violate the small-core, sovereign, offline, no-external-runtime mandate. Reimplement the merge loop / Viterbi / double-array trie in pure safe Rust (no panic, typed thiserror), each module <=300 loc (333 hard cap), single-responsibility.

Format additivity: only use RESERVED encoding ids (next free is 4; raw/zstd/f16/int8 occupy 0-3) and section ids 0x09+ (0x07/0x08 taken). Do NOT bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION (still 1) unless an existing field changes meaning -- a tokenizer section/encoding is purely additive and stays v1.

Per-file vocab adds bytes; on small or non-repetitive corpora the tokenizer section can cost more than it saves. Gate the codec behind a preset/heuristic (only emit when corpus size and repetitiveness clear a threshold) so default builds never regress in size, and always keep raw/zstd as the fallback encoding.

Keep the tokenizer config inline in the manifest, not as a companion file, or the single-file/self-describing/offline guarantee breaks. The tokenizer descriptor must also be folded into content_hash inputs so it is deterministic and tamper-evident.

bm25 requires alphabetical term order for determinism; subword segmentation changes the term set, so verify the sort still yields a stable, reproducible posting layout (the codec.rs already sorts terms by string -- subword terms must remain valid UTF-8 strings to keep that path).

Tokenizer perf is build-time, not serve-time, so do NOT add SIMD to the tokenizer (trie traversal is branch-bound, no dot-product) -- it would waste effort and the cited ARM port only used CRC32 for model-load hashing, not Viterbi. Keep the serve hot path purely mmap + SIMD cosine.

The ~150-200 loc merge loop and the Viterbi+trie decoder must split across files to respect the <=300 line rule (e.g. trie.rs, decode.rs, codec.rs) rather than one monolith; mirror the existing bm25/{index,codec,tokenize,fusion} single-responsibility split.

categories.name: model-runtime
categories.focus: inference runtimes and tensor libraries for on-device embedding

repos.one_liner: Cross-platform ML inference runtime whose CPU math library (MLAS) executes weight-only quantized matmuls via the MatMulNBits operator: block-wise sub-byte (int4/int8) weights with separate per-block scale/zero-point tensors, fused dequant-and-dot SIMD kernels (SQNBitGemm) dispatched per CPU feature level.
repos.core_innovation: Block-wise (group-wise) weight quantization: instead of one scale per whole vector, the contraction axis is cut into fixed-size blocks (e.g. 16/32/64/128 elements), each block gets its own f16 scale (and optional zero-point), and sub-byte codes are bit-packed (two int4 nibbles per byte) into a [N, k_blocks, blob_size] layout. The decisive companion idea is the FUSED kernel: SQNBitGemm unpacks nibbles, applies the per-block scale, and accumulates the dot product inside one SIMD pass, so the dequantized weights never materialize in memory. Accuracy stays high at int4 because each small block tracks local dynamic range, killing the single-outlier problem that ruins per-vector scaling.
key_techniques: Block-wise / group-wise quantization: one scale per K-block (block_size power-of-2, >=16), not per whole vector
Sub-byte bit-packing: two int4 codes packed per byte, blob_size = block_size/2; generalizes via blob_size = block_size/packed_size
Separate parallel tensors: packed weights, _scales (one f16 per block), optional _zero_points; dequant = (q - zp) * scale
[N, k_blocks, blob_size] block-major layout so each block's codes are contiguous for streaming SIMD unpack
MLAS SQNBitGemm fused dequantize+dot kernel: nibble unpack + scale + MAC in one SIMD pass, no materialized fp weights
Runtime CPU feature dispatch ladder: scalar -> NEON/dotprod -> AVX2+FMA -> AVX512-VNNI, picking widest kernel
accuracy_level knob: accumulate dot products in fp32/fp16/bf16/int8 to trade recall vs speed
Symmetric (int4, implicit zp=0) vs asymmetric (uint4, explicit zp) modes; RTN/GPTQ/HQQ scale-selection calibration
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add a new int4 embeddings encoding (an additive encoding id in the RESERVED 4-255 range, leaving the FROZEN v1 header untouched) modeled on crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs. Today int8.rs uses scale_kind=0 = ONE f32 scale per whole vector; introduce scale_kind=1 = block-wise: split each dim-length row into fixed blocks (e.g. 64), store one f16 scale per block (reuse the existing float16 codec), and bit-pack two int4 codes per byte in a block-contiguous [n, dim/block, block/2] layout. This same block-wise scheme should ALSO be retrofitted onto the existing int8 path as scale_kind=1 to recover accuracy int8 currently loses to per-vector outliers. nest-runtime: add a fused dequant+dot kernel beside crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/{neon,avx2,scalar}.rs that streams nibbles, applies the per-block f16 scale, and accumulates cosine straight off mmap, never expanding to f32 in RAM, mirroring SQNBitGemm. Determinism holds because round-to-nearest-even max-abs per block is fully reproducible; split pack/unpack from the kernel to stay under the 300-line cap. The mandatory exact-cosine rerank in search.rs already absorbs quantization error, so int4 can drive the candidate stage while ground-truth scores stay real cosine. This unlocks a new "nano" preset roughly halving the tiny preset's 0.283 embedding footprint (int4 = 4 bits + ~0.25 bits/dim f16 scale at block 64 vs int8's 8 bits/dim) -- the single biggest remaining lever on nest's compress-more-than-everyone north star, since embeddings are the one section that CANNOT be zstd-compressed.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. Embeddings are nest's largest incompressible section (zstd is banned on the hot path), so the only way to shrink them is better quantization. Block-wise int4 roughly halves bytes-per-dim vs the current int8 codec (~4.25 vs 8 bits/dim including the per-block f16 scale) while the per-block scale plus mandatory exact-cosine rerank protect recall. Pushing the tiny/nano preset below the 0.283 size ratio is the most concrete near-term win on the 'compress data more than everyone' goal.
repos.license: MIT
repos.perf_notes: SQNBitGemm fusion is the perf crux: nibble unpack + per-block scale + multiply-accumulate happen in one SIMD pass so dequantized weights never hit memory, keeping the matmul memory-bandwidth bound. MLAS dispatches at runtime across a feature ladder (NEON/dotprod, AVX2+FMA+F16C, AVX512-BW/VNNI, AMX) -- the int8 VNNI dot path (vpdpbusd) does 4 int8 MACs per lane and maps cleanly onto nest's simd/mod.rs dispatcher. Block size trades footprint vs accuracy (smaller block = more scales = bigger but more accurate); block_size 64-128 is the typical sweet spot. f16 scales (not f32) keep scale overhead near 0.25 bits/dim at block 64.

repos.one_liner: ONNX is a protobuf-defined interchange format for ML graphs whose TensorProto/external-data subsystem is a battle-tested spec for serializing quantized tensors (int4/int8/float8/MX microscaling) as raw, page-aligned, mmap-friendly byte blobs referenced by location/offset/length.
repos.core_innovation: The MX microscaling block-quant scheme: shared 8-bit power-of-two block exponent (FLOAT8E8M0) over sub-byte (int4/fp4) packed elements, decoupling a cheap shared scale from per-element mantissa for near-int8 quality at int4 size; standardized on disk as raw_data nibble-packing plus page-aligned mmap-able external byte ranges.
key_techniques: MX microscaling: 32-element blocks share one FLOAT8E8M0 power-of-two scale, per-element int4/fp4 mantissa, 2-stage dequant
int4/uint4 packed 2 nibbles/byte two's-complement; bf16/fp8 bit-cast to unsigned before serialize
raw_data little-endian native blob as single bulk serialization path bypassing protobuf overhead
External data: (location, offset, length, SHA1 checksum) referencing a flat weight sidecar by byte range
Page-aligned offsets (4KB / 64KB Windows) via round-up formula to enable zero-copy mmap of initializers
size_threshold gate: only tensors >= threshold spill to raw/external, small ones inline
Opset/version gating: new dtype force-upgrades consumer opset so readers know required capability
Named float8 variant zoo (E4M3FN, E5M2, FNUZ) as explicit encodings, not one lossy float8
repos.nest_application: Two additive grafts in nest-format/src/encoding/ (use a reserved encoding id 4-255, no v2 bump). (1) New block-scaled sub-byte embedding codec generalizing int8.rs: replace its per-vector f32 scale with int4 nibbles packed 2/byte plus a shared power-of-two u8 (E8M0-style) scale per 32-dim block; ~halves embeddings vs int8 while block scales recover int4-flat recall, pushing the 'tiny' preset below 0.283. Keep raw (never zstd embeddings) and fuse block dequant (single exponent add/shift) into the SIMD dot kernel in nest-runtime/src/simd before f32 accumulate, under AVX2/NEON. (2) Don't copy ONNX external-data (nest's single-file 64-byte-aligned section table in reader/parse.rs already beats the sidecar model); instead steal the size_threshold gate idea into writer/encoding_choice.rs so tiny sections skip block-quant overhead, and keep the per-section SHA-256 checksum discipline that mirrors ONNX's per-tensor checksum.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. MX block-scaling + int4 packing is the single highest-leverage path to push the embeddings section (the dominant byte cost in a vector DB) below int8 without the recall collapse of flat int4. It targets the exact 'compress more than everyone' north star and the 'tiny' preset, is implementable as an additive encoding id within frozen v1, and keeps embeddings raw/SIMD-scored from mmap. The float8 variant taxonomy (E4M3 vs E5M2 vs E8M0-scale) is the proven design space to copy rather than reinvent.
repos.perf_notes: raw_data + page-aligned external offsets exist specifically for zero-copy mmap of large weights (nest already does this with 64-byte SECTION_ALIGNMENT, single-file). E8M0 block-scale dequant is one exponent add/shift per block (32 elems), cheap to fuse into an AVX2/NEON dot-product kernel before f32 accumulation. int4 packing halves embedding bytes vs int8; block scaling restores the recall flat-int4 loses. No native NumPy dtype for int4/fp8 (uses ml_dtypes), so the packing/unpacking is hand-rolled bit ops -- nest would implement the same in Rust.
repos.license: Apache-2.0

repos.one_liner: A dependency-free C/C++ tensor library for on-device inference whose real innovation is its block-quantization codec family (legacy Qn_0, K-quants with double-quantized super-block scales, and i-quants with shared codebook grids) packed into the mmap-aligned GGUF on-disk format and dequantized straight from disk by AVX2/NEON kernels.
repos.core_innovation: Hierarchical "double quantization" inside fixed-size super-blocks: a tensor is split into 256-value super-blocks, each holding one or two fp16 master factors (d for scale, dmin for offset), and within that, eight 32-value sub-blocks whose own scale and min are stored as 6-bit integers relative to the master factors. This piecewise-affine scheme captures both global and local dynamic range at ~4.5 bits/weight (Q4_K) instead of fp16's 16, with metadata overhead amortized across 256 values, and every block is a self-contained repr(C) record dequantizable in isolation directly off mmap'd memory.
key_techniques: Q4_K super-block: struct{ fp16 d; fp16 dmin; uint8 scales[12] (6-bit packed scales+mins for 8 subblocks); uint8 qs[128] (4-bit nibble quants) } over 256 values = 4.5 bpw
Double-quantization: per-32 sub-block scale/min stored as 6-bit ints reconstructed as d*scale_idx and dmin*min_idx, so only two fp16 master values per 256 weights
block_q8_0: struct{ fp16 d; int8 qs[32] } symmetric per-32 int8 with one fp16 scale = direct upgrade to nest's flat int8 codec
block_q6_K split-bit packing: ql[128] low 4 bits, qh[64] high 2 bits, int8 scales[16], one fp16 d (6.5625 bpw)
i-quants (IQ2_XXS, 2.0625 bpw): vector codewords indexed into shared lookup grids (iq2xxs_grid, 64-bit packed entries) so weights cost log2(grid) bits not raw bits
GGUF format: magic 0x46554747, u32 version, tensor-info table (name,dims,type,u64 offset), every tensor 32-byte aligned for SIMD-loadable mmap, little-endian default
Block-local self-containment: no cross-block state, enabling zero-allocation streaming dequant and random access to any super-block from disk
Importance-matrix (imatrix) quantization: error minimized against per-channel activation importance not raw MSE, so bits go where they matter
repos.nest_application: Steal the K-quant super-block scheme as a new ENCODING ID (format reserves ids 4-255 inside v1, so this is additive, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump) applied ONLY to the embeddings section in nest-format (crates/nest-format/src/encoding.rs plus a new block-codec module under the 333-line cap). Today nest's hottest, largest section uses flat float16 or per-vector int8 and is deliberately left out of zstd because it is scored from mmap on the hot path. A Q4_K-style codec (256-dim super-blocks: fp16 d/dmin + 6-bit subblock scales + 4-bit quants) cuts embeddings from 16 bpw to ~4.5 bpw, ~3.5x shrink of the dominant section, while preserving the invariant: each repr(C) little-endian super-block is self-contained and dequantized inline by the existing nest-runtime SIMD dispatcher (AVX2/NEON/scalar) during the dot product, so vectors stay scored directly from mmap with no decompress-to-heap step. The mandatory exact-cosine rerank in nest-runtime's search path stays ground truth since the codec only changes candidate-vector storage; pair it with a 'nano' preset (Q4_K embeddings + zstd text + hnsw) targeting a size ratio well under tiny's 0.283. Determinism holds: fix super-block size at 256, quantization is a pure function of input (no seed), emit blocks in tensor order so same chunks+model fingerprint give byte-identical files. block_q8_0 is the lower-risk first step: a drop-in higher-quality replacement for nest's int8 codec (one fp16 scale per 32 dims vs per-vector), shippable immediately. Note: K-quants require the quantized dim be a multiple of 256 (768=3*256, 1024=4*256 are fine; 384 is not, so fall back to block-32 Q8_0 for non-multiples).
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central to the north star. Embeddings are nest's largest section and the only one excluded from compression; K-quant/i-quant block codecs are the proven way to take that section from 16 bpw to 4.5 (Q4_K) or ~2 (IQ2_XXS) while keeping it scoreable in place off mmap. This is the single biggest available win on the 'compress more than everyone' axis without touching the frozen layout, since it slots in as an additive encoding id. The 6-bit-scale double-quantization trick is the key insight: spend metadata bits hierarchically so per-subblock precision is nearly free across 256 values.
repos.perf_notes: Blocks are designed for zero runtime allocation and SIMD: Q4_0/Q8_0 use 32-value blocks aligned for one AVX2 256-bit / NEON 128-bit load; K-quants use 256-value super-blocks so dequant-and-dot fuses without spilling. GGUF mandates per-tensor 32-byte alignment so mmap'd block arrays start on SIMD boundaries. Dequant is a multiply-add against the fp16 master scale, cheap relative to the dot product, so the codec adds little hot-path cost. Constraint: K-quants need dim a multiple of 256 else fall back to block-32 Q8_0.
repos.license: MIT

synthesis.summary: Across onnxruntime/MLAS, onnx, and ggml the field has converged on one decisive technique for shrinking on-device embeddings: block-wise (group-wise) sub-byte weight quantization with a small per-block scale, packed in a self-contained repr(C) layout and dequantized fused-inline during the SIMD dot product so dequantized values never materialize in RAM. ggml's K-quants (Q4_K: 256-value super-blocks, fp16 d/dmin masters + 6-bit double-quantized sub-block scales + 4-bit quants = 4.5 bpw) and onnx's MX microscaling (32-elem blocks, shared FLOAT8E8M0 power-of-two exponent + int4 mantissa) are the two reference designs; MLAS SQNBitGemm is the reference fused dequant+dot kernel. This category is nest's single biggest unexploited lever, because embeddings are the one section banned from zstd (they are scored directly from mmap on the hot path), so the only way to shrink them is better quantization. nest is unusually well-positioned: its int8.rs payload ALREADY carries a scale_kind field (currently only 0 = per-vector), encoding ids 4-255 are reserved inside frozen v1, and search.rs already runs a mandatory exact-cosine rerank that absorbs quantization error so an int4 candidate stage keeps ground-truth scores. The one real blocker is an internal detail: mmap_file.rs materializes EVERY dtype to a full n*dim*4 f32 buffer whenever an HNSW index is present (materialize.rs), so today's int8 already loses its in-place-scoring advantage for tiny/hybrid presets, and a 4-bit codec inherits and worsens that problem unless the ANN distance path is taught to read packed blocks directly.
top_innovations: ggml Q4_K hierarchical double-quantization: 256-value super-blocks each carry two fp16 masters (d, dmin) and eight 32-value sub-blocks whose own scale/min are 6-bit ints relative to the masters, reaching 4.5 bpw vs nest's current 8 bpw int8 while a self-contained repr(C) record stays dequantizable in isolation off mmap. The key insight is spending metadata bits hierarchically so per-sub-block precision is nearly free amortized across 256 values.

MLAS SQNBitGemm fused dequant+dot: nibble-unpack + per-block-scale + multiply-accumulate happen in one SIMD pass so dequantized weights never hit memory, keeping the matmul memory-bandwidth bound. This is exactly the kernel shape nest's simd/mod.rs dispatcher needs for a 4-bit path, and it is what makes block-quant cheaper than it looks on the hot path.

onnx MX microscaling (E8M0 shared block exponent): a 32-element block shares one 8-bit power-of-two exponent, so dequant is a single exponent add/shift per block (no fp16 multiply), the cheapest possible block-scale to fuse into a NEON/AVX2 dot kernel before f32 accumulation. Near-int8 quality at int4 size.

Block-wise scaling as the fix for int8's per-vector-outlier loss: MLAS/ggml both show one scale per K-block (16/32/64) instead of per whole vector kills the single-outlier problem that crushes per-vector resolution. This retrofits onto nest's EXISTING int8 path as scale_kind=1 to recover accuracy at the same or near-same size, independent of any int4 work.

ggml block_q8_0 (one fp16 scale per 32 dims): the lowest-risk concrete artifact, a drop-in higher-quality, smaller-scale-overhead replacement for nest's per-vector-f32-scale int8 (4 bytes/vector of scale -> 2 bytes/32 dims), shippable as scale_kind=1 with minimal new kernel surface.

ggml i-quants (IQ2_XXS, ~2.06 bpw): vector codewords indexed into a shared lookup grid so weights cost log2(grid) bits, not raw bits, the longer-term path to push well below 4 bpw, at the cost of a shipped codebook and a gather in the kernel.

onnx size_threshold gate: only spill tensors above a threshold to block-quant; small sections keep flat layout. Cheap idea to steal into writer/encoding_choice.rs so tiny corpora don't pay block-scale overhead.

Deterministic round-to-nearest-even max-abs-per-block quantization: a pure function of input with no seed, so block-quant preserves nest's byte-identical reproducibility guarantee for free (unlike GPTQ/imatrix calibration which depends on a calibration set).

GGUF/ONNX page-and-SIMD-aligned block layout: every block/tensor starts on a 32-byte (GGUF) / 4KB (ONNX) boundary for zero-copy mmap. nest's 64-byte SECTION_ALIGNMENT already satisfies this; the lesson is to keep super-blocks an integer multiple of the SIMD load width and the section aligned so the first block does too.

ml_dtypes / hand-rolled nibble packing: int4/fp8 have no native numpy or Rust dtype, so all three projects hand-roll two's-complement nibble pack/unpack, confirming nest must own this in Rust and split pack/unpack out of the kernel file to stay under the 300-line cap.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The de-facto standard for compact on-device embeddings is fixed-size block (group) quantization with a small per-block scale, three design points along a bpw/quality curve: (1) symmetric int8 with one scale per 32-element block (ggml block_q8_0, ~8.5 bpw) as the safe, recall-preserving baseline; (2) int4 with a per-block scale, either an fp16 scale (MLAS MatMulNBits, ~4.25 bpw at block 64) or a shared power-of-two E8M0 exponent (onnx MX, ~4.25 bpw at block 32), as the sweet spot, where block scaling recovers the recall that flat per-vector int4 loses; (3) hierarchical double-quantization (ggml Q4_K, 4.5 bpw) which adds a second quantization level (6-bit sub-block scales relative to fp16 super-block masters) to track both global and local dynamic range across 256 values; and (4) codebook/i-quant schemes (IQ2_XXS, ~2 bpw) for the aggressive frontier. The universal implementation pattern is: self-contained repr(C) little-endian block records, SIMD-aligned, two int4 nibbles packed per byte, dequantized fused-inline inside the dot-product SIMD pass (MLAS SQNBitGemm) across a runtime CPU-feature dispatch ladder (scalar -> NEON/dotprod -> AVX2+FMA+F16C -> AVX512-VNNI, with VNNI's vpdpbusd doing 4 int8 MACs/lane). Block size trades footprint vs accuracy: smaller block = more scales = bigger but more accurate, with 32-128 the consensus sweet spot and fp16 scales keeping overhead near 0.25 bits/dim at block 64. A hard structural constraint from ggml: K-quants require the quantized dimension be a multiple of 256 (768, 1024 fine; 384 not), so a block-32 fallback (q8_0/q4 block-32) is mandatory for off-size models. Accuracy-recovery calibration (GPTQ/HQQ/imatrix) is the one part nest should NOT copy wholesale: it depends on a calibration corpus and breaks determinism; plain RTN max-abs-per-block is reproducible and, behind nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank, sufficient.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add block-wise int8 as scale_kind=1 in the EXISTING int8 codec (one fp16 scale per 32-dim block, ggml block_q8_0 shape), reusing the float16 codec for the scale. Lowest-risk first step: recovers recall int8 loses to per-vector outliers and shrinks scale overhead from 4 bytes/vector to 2 bytes/32 dims, with NO new encoding id and NO format-version bump.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs: branch on the already-present scale_kind field (add INT8_SCALE_KIND_BLOCK32=1 next to INT8_SCALE_KIND_PER_VECTOR=0); layout [u32 ver][u32 scale_kind=1][f16 scales: n*(dim/32)][i8 bodies]. Int8EmbeddingsView gains block_scale(i, block); parse() currently rejects kind!=0 so old readers stay safe. Runtime: simd/mod.rs score_int8_section and search.rs score_all/score_subset Int8 arm apply per-block scale.
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an int4 block-scaled embeddings codec as RESERVED encoding id SECTION_ENCODING_INT4=4 + new dtype string 'int4_b64', modeled on int8.rs: split each dim-length row into 64-elem blocks, one f16 scale per block (reuse float16 codec), bit-pack two int4 codes per byte in block-contiguous [n, dim/64, 32] layout. ~4.25 bpw vs int8's 8, roughly halves the dominant section. Additive within frozen v1; the exact-cosine rerank keeps returned scores real cosine even though int4 drives candidates.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: New file crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int4.rs (split pack/unpack from kernel to stay under 300 lines); wire into encoding/mod.rs (export + decode_payload passthrough since int4 bytes ARE canonical) and expected_embeddings_size; add SECTION_ENCODING_INT4=4 to layout/mod.rs; add EmbeddingDType::Int4 in writer/encoding_choice.rs and DType::Int4 in runtime mmap_file.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a fused dequant+dot SIMD kernel (dot_f32_i4) beside avx2/neon/scalar that streams nibbles, applies the per-block f16 scale, accumulates cosine in f32 in one pass, never expanding the row to f32 in RAM (the SQNBitGemm pattern). Add score_int4_section and a DType::Int4 arm to score_all/score_subset.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/{avx2,neon,scalar}.rs (new dot_f32_i4 fn each, mirroring dot_f32_i8); simd/mod.rs new dispatch fn + score_int4_section; crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs add the Int4 match arms. Keep nibble unpack helpers in a small simd/pack.rs to respect the 300-line cap.
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Fix the materialize-to-f32 leak so block-quant actually pays off for tiny/hybrid. Today mmap_file.rs::open materializes the WHOLE embeddings section to an n*dim*4 f32 buffer (materialize.rs) whenever an HNSW section is present, to feed the ANN graph. A 4-bit codec would be expanded to f32 in RAM, defeating compression on exactly the preset (tiny = int8+hnsw) that needs it most. Teach the ANN distance path to score against packed blocks via the new fused kernel (or at minimum keep f16, not f32, as the materialized form).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs and crates/nest-runtime/src/ann/{search.rs,mod.rs} (HnswIndex::attach_vectors / distance fn); have the graph hold a borrowed packed view + scale table and call the simd fused dot instead of holding a dense f32 Vec. Also shrinks resident RAM for the existing int8 tiny preset.
nest_recommendations.impact: high
draws_from: ggml block-local self-contained random access off mmap

nest_recommendations.idea: Ship a 'nano' preset (int4 block-64 embeddings + zstd text + hnsw) targeting a size ratio well below tiny's 0.283, since embeddings are the dominant incompressible bytes. Gate on dim being block-compatible (multiple of 64; a future Q4_K-256 variant needs multiple of 256) and fall back to block-32 int8 otherwise, matching ggml's K-quant dimension constraint.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: Preset selection lives above the format crate (nest-python build path / CLI). Wire EmbeddingDType::Int4 through writer/encoding_choice.rs and the manifest dtype string; document the preset and recall@10 where tiny (0.283) is documented. Add a writer-side guard that rejects/falls-back when dim % block != 0.
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Steal onnx's size_threshold gate: only apply block-quant overhead to embeddings sections above a byte threshold; tiny corpora keep flat float16/int8 so a handful of vectors don't pay per-block scale metadata. Keep per-section SHA-256 discipline (mirrors ONNX per-tensor checksum) untouched.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/writer/encoding_choice.rs (or writer/payload.rs where embedding dtype is chosen): add a min-bytes gate before selecting Int4/block-int8.
nest_recommendations.impact: low

nest_recommendations.idea: Defer i-quant / codebook (IQ2_XXS ~2 bpw) and any GPTQ/imatrix calibration. They are the frontier but (a) imatrix needs a calibration corpus and breaks byte-identical determinism, and (b) i-quants ship a lookup grid and add a gather to the hot kernel. Record as a v2-era research line, NOT a near-term graft; plain RTN max-abs-per-block int4 already lands the biggest win deterministically.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: Roadmap note only (kdb/research synthesis). If ever pursued, the codebook would be a new reserved encoding id with the grid embedded in the embeddings payload prefix; determinism would require shipping the exact grid, not deriving it from data.
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

compression_wins: Block-scaled int4 embeddings at block 64 = ~4.25 bpw (4 bits + ~0.25 bits/dim for the f16 scale) vs the current int8's 8 bpw, roughly HALVES nest's largest incompressible section and is the single biggest available lever on 'compress more than everyone', since embeddings are banned from zstd. On a 768-dim corpus that is ~3072 -> ~1632 bytes/vector for the embeddings body+scales.

A 'nano' preset (int4 block-64 + zstd text + hnsw) should push the total file size ratio meaningfully below tiny's 0.283, because the embeddings section dominates total bytes and is exactly what int4 targets; the mandatory exact-cosine rerank is expected to hold recall@10 near tiny's 0.992.

Block-scaled int8 (scale_kind=1, block 32) shrinks scale overhead from 4 bytes per vector to 2 bytes per 32 dims while ALSO recovering recall lost to per-vector outliers, a free accuracy+size win on the existing int8/tiny path with no new encoding id and no format bump.

ggml Q4_K (256-dim super-blocks, fp16 d/dmin + 6-bit sub-block scales + 4-bit quants = 4.5 bpw) is the higher-quality variant for 768/1024-dim models (3x256, 4x256), trading ~0.25 bpw over flat int4 for noticeably better local-dynamic-range tracking, a strong second codec once the int4 path exists.
Longer term, i-quant codebooks (IQ2_XXS ~2.06 bpw) could quarter embeddings vs int8, but only behind a shipped grid and gather kernel; flagged as frontier, not near-term.
Reusing the existing float16 codec for the per-block scales means scale storage costs no new code and stays deterministic, so the compression win comes with near-zero new format surface.
watch_outs: DETERMINISM: do NOT copy GPTQ/HQQ/imatrix calibration, they depend on a calibration corpus and would break nest's byte-identical 'same chunks + same model fingerprint => identical file' guarantee. Stick to pure round-to-nearest-even max-abs-per-block (a deterministic function of input, no seed), which preserves reproducibility for free.

IN-PLACE SCORING LEAK (already present): mmap_file.rs::open + materialize.rs expand EVERY dtype, including int8, to a full n*dim*4 f32 buffer whenever an HNSW section exists, to feed the ANN graph. Shipping int4 without fixing this means the codec halves DISK size but tiny/hybrid presets still hold a dense f32 copy in RAM, contradicting the 'scored directly from mmap, no decompress-to-heap' invariant. The ANN distance path must score packed blocks (or at least keep f16) before int4 delivers its promise.

DIMENSION CONSTRAINTS: ggml K-quants require dim be a multiple of 256 and even simple int4 block-64 needs dim % 64 == 0. Demo/PT-BR models may use 384 or other off-sizes; the writer MUST guard and fall back to block-32 int8 (or flat f16) rather than silently producing a malformed/padded section.

300/333-LINE CAP + SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: a fused dequant kernel plus nibble pack/unpack plus a new codec will blow the line cap in one file. Split pack/unpack (encoding/int4.rs + a tiny simd/pack.rs) from the dot kernels (avx2/neon/scalar.rs), exactly as ggml separates quantize/dequantize/vec_dot.

NEVER PANIC: all new parse paths (nibble unpack, block-count math, scale-table bounds, dim%block checks) must return typed thiserror NestError/RuntimeError, never unwrap/panic, mirroring Int8EmbeddingsView::parse size checks. Unchecked nibble indexing into an mmap'd slice is a panic/UB risk on a malformed file.

ADDITIVE-ONLY FROZEN V1: int4 must take a RESERVED encoding id in 4-255 and a NEW dtype string; do NOT change the meaning of any existing field. scale_kind=1 on the int8 path is safe because the field already exists and old readers reject unknown kinds (parse() guards kind!=0). Bumping NEST_FORMAT_VERSION is reserved for true v2 only.

OFFLINE/SINGLE-FILE: reject ONNX's external-data/sidecar model outright, nest's whole point is one self-contained file; the only thing to steal there is the size_threshold gate idea, not the byte-range-into-another-file mechanism. No codec may pull a codebook or scale table from outside the .nest container.

LITTLE-ENDIAN repr(C): block records (scales then nibbles) must be little-endian and the section must stay 64-byte aligned so the first block lands on a SIMD boundary; keep super-block size an integer multiple of the SIMD load width or the fused kernel will mis-stride on the tail block.

RERANK FIDELITY NUANCE: int4's low precision is only acceptable BECAUSE search.rs runs a mandatory exact-cosine rerank over candidates, but that rerank reads the SAME int4 vectors, so the 'real cosine' is real-cosine-of-the-quantized-vector, not of the original f32. For exact ground truth a corpus needs an f32/f16 preset; document that nano trades a small absolute-score fidelity for size, and keep exact/compressed as the recall-max options.

repos.one_liner: A Python/JS LLM-orchestration framework whose retrieval layer contributes two reusable, format-agnostic ideas: a content-hash record-manager indexing API for incremental dedup/sync of a vector store, and a content-hash-keyed embedding cache namespaced by model fingerprint.
repos.core_innovation: The "record manager" indexing API: every derived document carries a deterministic hash of (canonical content + metadata), plus a source_id and write timestamp. Re-indexing computes hashes, skips any hash already present (dedup), deletes stale hashes that share a touched source_id (incremental cleanup), and can scope cleanup to seen sources (scoped_full). This turns a write-once vector store into an idempotent, incrementally-syncable one keyed purely on content hashes, with no re-embed of unchanged content. It pairs with CacheBackedEmbeddings, which keys the embedding KV-cache on hash(text) prefixed by a model-name namespace so a model change invalidates cleanly.
key_techniques: Record-manager dedup: store per-chunk content_hash + source_id + write_time; skip-if-hash-present, delete-stale-by-source_id
Three cleanup policies: incremental (delete superseded chunks of touched sources continuously), full (delete anything not in this run's universe), scoped_full (in-memory set of seen source_ids)
source_id_key grouping so all chunks derived from one source document update/delete atomically
force_update flag to invalidate the index on embedding-model change without changing content
CacheBackedEmbeddings: cache key = namespace(model fingerprint) + hex(SHA-256(text)); only cache misses hit the embedder
Configurable key encoder (sha1/blake2b/sha256/sha512) trading collision-resistance vs speed
SemanticChunker: embed sentences, split where cosine distance between consecutive embeddings exceeds a percentile/stddev/IQR/gradient breakpoint
RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter: ordered separator hierarchy [paragraph,line,word,char] recursive descent until under chunk_size, then greedy merge with bounded overlap
repos.nest_application: nest-format already computes content_hash (decoded canonical sections, stable across encodings) and per-chunk chunk_ids; this is exactly LangChain's record-manager key. Add an optional section (reserved id 0x09+, additive within v1) holding a sorted manifest of {chunk_content_hash -> source_id, original_span_ref} so a future `nest update`/`nest merge` in nest-cli can do incremental edits: re-embed ONLY chunks whose content_hash is absent, copy embeddings/spans for unchanged hashes byte-for-byte from the old mmap, and drop chunks whose source_id was touched but hash vanished. This delivers the mission's missing real-time edit while preserving determinism (sorted hash order = byte-identical output for identical inputs) and zero-cost dedup. Mirror CacheBackedEmbeddings as a deterministic on-disk python-side cache in nest-python keyed by namespace(model fingerprint already in provenance) + SHA-256(chunk_canonical_text) so rebuilds and cross-corpus dedup never re-embed identical text. For compression: identical-chunk dedup across files plus span-deduped storage shrinks multi-document/whole-repo .nest containers (north-star use case) by collapsing repeated boilerplate to one physical chunk+embedding referenced by many spans.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: content-hash dedup collapses repeated/boilerplate chunks (and their fp32 embeddings, the largest section) to one physical copy referenced by many spans -- the biggest lever when packing whole repos/datasets/databases into one container. The embedding cache avoids recompute, not bytes, but cross-file hash dedup is a genuine size win for multi-document containers. Semantic chunking yields more self-similar chunks that zstd compresses better in non-embedding sections.
repos.perf_notes: Record manager is normally SQLite-backed (SQLRecordManager) but the algorithm is just a hash set + source_id index -- nest can implement it as a sorted in-file manifest scanned at build time, no DB, no socket, offline by construction. Hash cost is one SHA-256 per chunk (nest already does this for content_hash, near-zero marginal cost). LangChain's incremental cleanup has O(redundant) cost when a source's chunks span batches; nest builds the whole corpus in-process so a single batch avoids it. Time-based cleanup races are irrelevant since nest builds are single-shot and deterministic, not clock-driven.

repos.one_liner: A Pregel/BSP graph-execution runtime for stateful LLM agents whose durable-execution layer persists state as immutable, append-only checkpoints with content-deduplicated channel blobs keyed by per-channel version numbers.
repos.core_innovation: Version-keyed blob deduplication for append-only state history: each checkpoint stores only a tiny channel_versions int-map plus references; the actual serialized channel values live in a separate blobs table keyed by (channel_name, version). A new checkpoint that touches one channel bumps only that channel's version and writes one new blob; all unchanged channels keep pointing at existing blob bytes. This stores a full mutation/edit history with near-zero duplication of unchanged state, instead of rewriting the whole snapshot per step.
key_techniques: Pregel/BSP super-step loop: Plan (select actors whose subscribed channels changed) -> Execute (run nodes in parallel, writes invisible until step end) -> Update (apply reducers) -> Checkpoint; transactional/atomic per super-step

Channel abstraction with typed update functions: LastValue (single value/step), BinaryOperatorAggregate (associative reducer applied eagerly at write time), Topic (pubsub accumulate/dedup), DeltaChannel (reducer applied lazily on reconstruction from persisted writes)
Immutable append-only checkpoint store: INSERT per super-step keyed by composite (thread_id, checkpoint_id); never UPDATE in place; enables time-travel and resume
channel_versions monotonic version map + get_next_version() (default integer sequence from 1, overridable) used as the dedup key for blobs
Separate blobs table mapping (channel, version) -> serialized bytes so unchanged channels are referenced, not copied, across checkpoints
Pending/task-level writes: outputs of completed nodes in a failed super-step are persisted as task writes so resume skips already-done work (fault-tolerant partial progress)
JsonPlusSerializer: ormsgpack primary binary encoding with extended-JSON fallback for complex types (pydantic, datetime, enums); pluggable SerializerProtocol, optional EncryptedSerializer (AES)
Security lesson: CWE-502 RCE via constructor-style deserialization in the JSON fallback path; fixed with a strict module/class allow-list (LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK)
repos.nest_application: Adapt the (channel,version)->blob dedup model into nest-format to unlock nest's "real-time edit" north-star without breaking the FROZEN v1 single-file/deterministic guarantees. Concretely: add an OPTIONAL additive section (reserved id 0x09+) that is an append-only edit log, where each logical chunk/embedding is content-addressed by its existing per-section SHA-256 (nest already has section checksum + content_hash). A new edit appends only new/changed chunk and embedding blobs; unchanged chunks are referenced by their existing content hash rather than recopied. The current chunk_ids/chunks_canonical/embeddings sections become the version-0 base, and a small version map (analogous to channel_versions, repr(C) LE-u64 ids) records which blob hash is live per chunk. This gives nest incremental/versioned containers and cheap snapshots while keeping deterministic byte-identical rebuilds, and it compounds compression: dedup-before-encode means zstd/int8/f16 only ever encode the delta. nest-runtime's reader resolves the live version map at mmap time so SIMD dot products still run straight off the latest blobs with no copy. Borrow the get_next_version() integer-sequence determinism (seeded/monotonic) to keep the additive log reproducible, and adopt the allow-list deserialization lesson: nest must never deserialize arbitrary types from a container (typed thiserror, fixed section decoders only), avoiding LangGraph's CWE-502 class of bug by construction.
repos.compression_relevance: High. Version-keyed content-addressed blob dedup is a compression primitive: storing edit/version history of a corpus by referencing unchanged content-hashed chunks instead of recopying them is exactly the structural (cross-snapshot) dedup nest needs to "compress more than everyone" once it supports real-time edit and whole-repo/database ingestion, where most of a new version is unchanged. It composes with nest's existing zstd/int8/f16 codecs (dedup first, then encode the delta) and reuses nest's existing SHA-256 content_hash as the dedup key.
repos.perf_notes: Checkpoint store is INSERT-only (append-only), trading write amplification of metadata for immutability and time-travel; channel blobs are written once per version and shared, so steady-state writes are O(changed channels) not O(state size). Serialization uses ormsgpack (C, fast) with orjson fast paths. No SIMD/quantization in LangGraph itself (it is a Python orchestration layer, not a vector engine); the transferable value is purely the on-disk dedup/versioning data model, not any kernel. Known operational pain point in their Postgres saver is checkpoint bloat from append-only writes, which nest avoids by keeping the log inside one mmap-friendly additive section rather than per-row DB inserts.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A Python RAG/agent data framework whose core abstraction is the Node (a chunk with typed relationships, metadata, and a content/text hash id) wired into a swappable StorageContext (docstore + index_store + vector_store), with retrieval strategies including hierarchical multi-resolution chunking, auto-merging retrieval, and reciprocal-rank fusion hybrid search.
repos.core_innovation: The HierarchicalNodeParser + AutoMergingRetriever pair: documents are parsed into a multi-resolution tree of chunks (e.g. chunk_sizes [2048,512,128] tokens) where every child stores a PARENT relationship to a coarser node; only leaf nodes are embedded/searched, and at query time the retriever counts how many sibling leaves under a common parent were hit -- if a majority threshold is crossed it recursively replaces those leaves with the single larger parent node. This decouples embedding/search granularity (fine) from returned/materialized granularity (coarse); the parent-child relationship graph is the load-bearing data structure.
key_techniques: HierarchicalNodeParser: one document -> N levels of chunks (2048/512/128 tokens) with explicit child->parent references
Node relationship enum: SOURCE / PARENT / CHILD / PREVIOUS / NEXT links forming a chunk DAG via RelatedNodeInfo (target node_id + hash)
AutoMergingRetriever majority-threshold merge: if > threshold of a parent's children are retrieved, recursively collapse children into the parent node
Leaf-only embedding: only finest chunks are vector-indexed; coarser nodes live in the docstore and are fetched by id, not embedded
Reciprocal-rank fusion (RECIPROCAL_RANK mode, k=60.0, score += 1/(k+rank+1)) to merge vector + BM25 lists without an external model
Content-hash node ids (id = hash of text) giving stable dedup keys across retriever lists during fusion
StorageContext split into docstore / index_store / vector_store so relationship graph and embeddings persist independently
fsspec-backed JSON persistence so the same index serializes to local FS, S3, R2 unchanged
repos.nest_application: Add an optional RESERVED section (id 0x09+, additive within format v1) named chunk_hierarchy to nest-format/src/sections/: a repr(C), little-endian array of (child_chunk_id u32 -> parent_chunk_id u32, level u8) edges plus per-parent child-count, hashed as its own integrity surface. The python builder emits the tree; only leaf chunks get rows in embeddings/hnsw_index, matching nest's existing leaf-search model. In nest-runtime/src/search.rs, add a post-rerank auto-merge pass: after the mandatory exact-cosine rerank, count retrieved leaves per parent and, above a deterministic majority threshold, swap them for the parent before materialize() resolves chunks_original_spans. This reuses chunk_ids + chunks_original_spans already in the frozen format and stays offline/deterministic. Compression angle: parent canonical text need NOT be stored -- a parent's chunks_canonical is reconstructed by concatenating its children's chunks_original_spans against the source, so the hierarchy gives coarse-context retrieval at ~9 bytes/edge of graph and zero extra text bytes, directly serving 'compress more than everyone' while adding multi-resolution retrieval. Do NOT re-steal RRF: nest already has it in crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/fusion.rs (k=60).
repos.compression_relevance: High and non-obvious: the parent-child edge table is ~9 bytes per edge, and because a parent's text is fully derivable from its children's existing chunks_original_spans, the multi-resolution hierarchy adds coarse-context retrieval with near-zero additional text/embedding bytes (no parent text stored, no parent embedding stored). It turns one stored leaf layer into multiple retrievable resolutions -- improving recall-context per byte rather than spending bytes, a pure structural win for the compression north star.
repos.perf_notes: The auto-merge pass is O(retrieved_k) hashmap counting after rerank, negligible vs the SIMD dot products; no extra disk reads since parent text is reconstructed from already-mmapped spans. Leaf-only embedding keeps the embeddings section (the hot mmap-scored part nest never compresses) strictly minimal: coarser context costs no embedding rows. llama_index itself is pure Python and not perf-relevant -- the value is the algorithm and data model, not its implementation.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: A Rust CLI for document parsing (LlamaParse API) plus local, API-free semantic line search built on model2vec static embeddings (potion-multilingual-128M, distilled from bge-m3), simsimd SIMD cosine kernels, and an embedded qdrant-edge IVF_PQ index with a persistent on-disk workspace embedding cache.
repos.core_innovation: Replacing a neural embedding model with a precomputed static token-vector lookup table (model2vec/POTION): distill a transformer into per-token vectors via PCA + frequency weighting, then embed any text by mean-pooling its token vectors. This makes embedding generation pure table lookup + averaging (no matmul, no GPU, no network, fully deterministic), exactly the offline/sovereign/reproducible property nest needs to own its embedding step.
key_techniques: model2vec static embeddings: forward-pass vocab through sentence transformer (bge-m3), mean-pool output positions per token, PCA to 256 dims, Zipf weighting using vocab rank as frequency proxy (IDF-like downweighting of frequent tokens)
POTION/Tokenlearn post-training: re-regularize with PCA + SIF weighting w=1e-3/(1e-3+proba) for accuracy boost over plain Zipf
Uncontextualized inference: embed = mean of constituent token vectors (single gather + average, no attention, no forward pass at query time)
simsimd 6.5.1 SIMD cosine/dot kernels (AVX2/NEON/SVE) for similarity scoring
qdrant-edge embedded IVF_PQ: inverted-file coarse quantization + product quantization of residuals, serverless in-process ANN
persistent workspace embedding cache in ~/.semtools/workspaces/ via serde serialization with automatic re-embed when source documents change
per-line search with configurable context window (--n-lines) and --max-distance cosine threshold instead of fixed-size chunking
repos.nest_application: Two distinct steals. (1) nest-python (or a tiny nest-runtime module): vendor a model2vec-style static embedder as an offline, deterministic, zero-dependency embedding backend. A potion token-vector table (vocab x 256 f32, nest-encoded as int8+zstd) ships inside or beside the .nest file; provenance.model_fingerprint becomes the table hash. Embedding = tokenize + gather + mean-pool, giving byte-identical builds with no network and no PyTorch, matching nest's deterministic/reproducible/sovereign guarantees and removing a heavy external dependency. (2) nest-format + nest-runtime/ann: add IVF-PQ as a new optional encoding tier for the embeddings section (new reserved encoding id 4-255 and/or section id 0x09+, additive within v1). Product quantization (m subvectors, 256-centroid k-means codebook per subspace, 1 byte/subvector) compresses 256-d f32 ~16-32x vs raw and far below the current int8. Because nest already mandates an exact-cosine rerank after ANN, PQ distances are only a candidate funnel and the returned score stays real cosine, satisfying search_contract; seed k-means to keep it deterministic like the seeded-hnsw rule.
repos.compression_relevance: Very high. The IVF-PQ/product-quantization tier directly advances the compress-more-than-everyone north star: PQ encodes a 256-d float vector in ~8-16 bytes (m x 1 byte) vs 256 bytes raw f32 or 64 bytes int8, a 16-32x cut on the embeddings section (usually the largest). With nest's mandatory exact rerank, recall stays high while stored vectors shrink dramatically, going deeper than the tiny preset's int8. Separately, the static-embedding table is itself highly compressible (int8+zstd on a vocab x 256 matrix) and replaces a multi-GB neural model with a few-MB lookup table, shrinking the whole embedding toolchain footprint.
repos.license: MIT (run-llama/semtools and model2vec-rs); potion-multilingual-128M weights MIT (MinishLab); simsimd Apache-2.0; qdrant-edge Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: model2vec inference is reportedly up to ~500x faster than the source transformer with a ~15-50x smaller model; embedding is bandwidth-bound table gather + mean, ideal for CPU-only offline use. potion-multilingual-128M: 256 dims, 101 languages, ~90.9% of LaBSE quality, distilled from bge-m3. simsimd 6.5.1 ships AVX2/NEON/SVE cosine kernels aligning with nest's AVX2/NEON/scalar dispatcher (could cross-check or replace hand-rolled SIMD). IVF_PQ keeps the ANN index small and CPU-resident for serverless search. Caveat: like nest's bm25, model2vec tokenization quality on CJK/Thai depends on the underlying tokenizer (bge-m3 sentencepiece gives decent multilingual coverage).

repos.one_liner: A Python LLM/RAG orchestration framework whose pipelines are serializable component DAGs (now with cycles), with a pure-Python InMemoryDocumentStore that holds an incrementally-maintained BM25 inverted index (BM25Okapi/BM25L/BM25Plus) and does dense retrieval via a single numpy matmul, persisting everything to a single JSON file.
repos.core_innovation: The incrementally-maintained, in-memory BM25 inverted index (mutable corpus stats updated per write/delete) is the transferable idea: it turns nest's frozen bm25 build into something that supports live edits.
key_techniques: Incremental BM25 statistics: per-doc Counter(token)->freq + doc_len stored alongside doc; global _freq_vocab_for_idf (df map) and running _avg_doc_len updated on every write/delete instead of full reindex
Three BM25 scoring variants behind one interface: BM25Okapi vs BM25L vs BM25Plus, where L/Plus add a delta term (+delta in numerator/idf) to stop long-document over-penalization; tunable k1/b/epsilon
Configurable tokenizer as a single regex (r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b') captured in config, making tokenization a serialized, reproducible parameter
Dense retrieval as one BLAS call: stack all doc embeddings into a 2D array, scores = np.dot(query, embeddings.T) then top-k - identical math to nest's SIMD dot-product fan-out

to_dict/from_dict component contract: every component (incl. document store, retriever) serializes to a plain dict of construction params (e.g. store IP+db name, not the live client), enabling deterministic rebuild
Single-file persistence: save_to_disk/load_from_disk dump the whole store (config + documents + stats) to one JSON file
Pipeline-as-data: the entire orchestration graph (components + typed input/output connections) serializes to YAML and round-trips, with deserialize callbacks for component rewriting
repos.nest_application: Steal the incremental BM25 maintenance model for nest-runtime crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25.rs: keep the on-disk bm25_index(0x08) as the frozen cold start, but add an in-memory delta layer holding per-chunk term-frequency maps, a global df map, and a running avg_doc_len so live edits (insert/delete chunk) update scores without a full Python rebuild - this directly unlocks the north-star "real-time edit + fast search" without breaking the frozen container (the persisted 0x08 stays additive/deterministic, alphabetical term order preserved). Secondly, adapt the BM25L/BM25Plus delta-smoothing formula into the existing Bm25Index scoring path as a config flag in search_contract (nest-format) so recall on long/heterogeneous chunks improves; keep alphabetical term order for determinism. Thirdly, mirror the to_dict/from_dict contract as nest's reproducibility surface: the search_contract section already fingerprints config, and Haystack confirms that capturing tokenizer-regex + bm25 params + similarity-fn as serialized scalars is exactly what makes builds replayable - validates nest's content_hash design. Low compression relevance: this is index/orchestration plumbing, not an entropy coder; nest already beats Haystack on storage (Haystack stores raw JSON + full-precision f32 embeddings with zero quantization, whereas nest has zstd/f16/int8/hnsw).
repos.compression_relevance: Low/indirect. Haystack does no compression or quantization at all (save_to_disk is plain JSON, embeddings kept as full-precision f32 in a numpy array), so it offers nothing for the 'compress more than everyone' goal directly - nest is already far ahead here. Its relevance is to the adjacent north-star pillars (real-time edit, fast BM25/hybrid search), not to the entropy/quantization frontier.
repos.license: Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: Dense retrieval is a single numpy.dot (BLAS) over the full stacked embedding matrix then top-k - O(N*d) brute force, no ANN in the in-memory store (ANN is delegated to external vector DBs); fine at small N, does not scale, and is exactly the brute-force path nest already replaces with SIMD + HNSW. BM25 scoring is pure-Python over Counters (slow vs a compiled Rust scorer). No SIMD, no mmap, no quantization. Whole-store-in-RAM model; persistence is a full JSON rewrite, not append/mmap, so it has no zero-copy or partial-load story.

repos.one_liner: Dify is a Python LLM-app orchestration platform whose RAG subsystem (api/core/rag) is a modular multi-strategy retrieval pipeline: pluggable vector stores, an "economical" jieba+TF-IDF inverted keyword index, and a hybrid retriever that fuses semantic and keyword results via either a neural reranker or a transparent weighted-score formula.
repos.core_innovation: The "weight_rerank" fusion: instead of always needing a neural cross-encoder, Dify computes final = w_vec*cosine(query_emb, chunk_emb) + w_kw*tfidf_cosine(query_tokens, chunk_tokens), where the keyword side is a self-contained TF-IDF-cosine (IDF = log((1+N)/(1+df)) + 1, TF*IDF vectors, cosine between query and chunk term vectors) and the vector side is raw cosine. It is a deterministic, dependency-free, two-knob alternative to a black-box reranker that still yields one comparable score per chunk.
key_techniques: weighted-score hybrid fusion: final = w_vec*cosine + w_kw*tfidf_cosine, two tunable weights
TF-IDF-cosine keyword reranker: smoothed IDF log((1+N)/(1+df))+1, TF*IDF vectors, query/chunk cosine, fully deterministic and neural-free
economical inverted keyword index: keyword->set(chunk_ids) table built by jieba TF-IDF top-k extraction + subtoken expansion + stopword filtering
two-tier quality modes: 'economical' (inverted keyword index, no embeddings) vs 'high-quality' (embeddings+ANN), a build-time size/cost switch
RerankRunner factory: RERANKING_MODEL vs WEIGHTED_SCORE behind one interface; community RRF 1/(k+rank) as a scale-free rank fusion
pluggable vector-store abstraction: uniform retrieval interface across 16+ backends decoupling index format from query path
TopK dynamically bounded by the consumer context budget instead of a fixed constant
jieba (CJK-aware) tokenization for the keyword side
repos.nest_application: Adapt weighted-score fusion into nest-runtime's search path as a third hybrid mode beside RRF. nest today fuses bm25::Bm25Index and ann::HnswIndex via reciprocal-rank fusion then mandatory exact-cosine rerank; add a `weighted` fusion in crates/nest-runtime/src/search computing final = w_vec*exact_cosine + w_kw*normalized_bm25 with two deterministic config weights, giving an interpretable blended score. The exact-cosine rerank invariant still holds because cosine is one term, and it stays offline/deterministic (no neural reranker, no socket). Separately, mirror Dify's economical/high-quality split as a nest-cli + nest-format preset: an "economical" build shipping ONLY chunks + bm25_index(0x08) (no embeddings, no HNSW), zstd on non-embedding sections, for keyword-amenable corpora. The keyword->chunk_ids inverted-table layout is also a reference for making bm25_index(0x08) self-describing. All additive: existing section ids, frozen v1 layout untouched.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. Biggest lever is the "economical" build: an embeddings-free keyword-only .nest (chunks + bm25_index(0x08), zstd) would beat the tiny preset's 0.283 ratio for keyword-amenable corpora because int8 embeddings dominate file size, while the TF-IDF/BM25 inverted table is tiny and zstd-friendly. The weighted-score fusion adds no bytes but keeps that lighter index recall-competitive. RRF (1/(k+rank)) is also a config-only, storage-free fusion improvement.
repos.license: Modified Apache License 2.0 (Dify Open Source License: Apache 2.0 plus conditions on multi-tenant/SaaS commercial use and logo/branding). The math (TF-IDF cosine, weighted fusion, RRF) is not protectable, so a clean-room Rust reimplementation is fine.
repos.perf_notes: Fusion is a handful of float ops per candidate, run after ANN/BM25 gather, so negligible added latency on nest's hot path; the vector term IS exact cosine, so it reuses nest's SIMD dot-product kernels (AVX2/NEON/scalar). Dify's jieba keyword tokenizer is CJK-aware, directly relevant to nest's known gap (word-segmented BM25 tokenizer degrades on CJK/Thai); nest could adopt a jieba-style or unicode-segmentation tokenizer, but must pick an offline, small-footprint, deterministic segmenter to preserve reproducibility (jieba's dictionary is large).

repos.one_liner: A Python multi-agent LLM framework whose DocChatAgent implements a RAG retrieval pipeline that fuses semantic + BM25 + fuzzy rankings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (c=60), then applies deterministic post-rank reordering (diversity, lost-in-middle periphery) and optional cross-encoder/LLM relevance extraction.
repos.core_innovation: Rank-only Reciprocal Rank Fusion as the hybrid-search combiner: scores from heterogeneous retrievers are discarded and replaced by 1/(rank_i + 60) summed across methods. Because it consumes only ordinal rank, it fuses score spaces that are not comparable (cosine vs BM25 vs edit-distance) with zero normalization, zero tuning, and is fully deterministic given deterministic input rankings -- exactly what nest already guarantees for its hnsw and bm25 indices.
key_techniques: Reciprocal Rank Fusion: combined = sum_methods 1/(rank + c), c=60.0, sort desc; rank-only so no score normalization needed
Three-way fusion of semantic(vector) + BM25Okapi + fuzzy(thefuzz partial_ratio) rankings rather than the usual two-way
rank_to_periphery: deterministic anti-'lost-in-middle' reorder splitting by index into odds + reversed(evens) so top hits land at both list ends (1..9 => 1 3 5 7 9 8 6 4 2)
rank_with_diversity: greedy MMR-style selection picking the passage with min mean cosine similarity to already-selected set
n_neighbor_chunks context-window expansion via stored window_ids metadata: re-stitch adjacent original chunks around a hit
cross-encoder rerank with logistic squashing 1/(1+exp(-score)) using ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (mutually exclusive with RRF)
RelevanceExtractorAgent: LLM extracts verbatim relevant sentences by numbering, returns NO_ANSWER when nothing matches (post-retrieval filter)
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime/search: nest already runs hnsw + bm25 and fuses bm25 via reciprocal-rank fusion before the mandatory exact-cosine rerank. Steal two concrete upgrades. (1) Generalize the RRF fuser in the hybrid path to a rank-only sum_methods 1/(rank+60) over N>=2 ordered lists with c exposed in the search_contract section of nest-format (additive, no version bump), so a future third signal (fuzzy/edit-distance term match, helping the known CJK/thai bm25 gap) drops in without touching the codec; keep determinism via the existing alphabetical/seeded ordering. (2) Add rank_to_periphery as a pure-integer, deterministic final reorder in nest-runtime::search::materialize (odds + reversed(evens)) -- ~15 lines, no ML, no float, panic-free, well under the 300-line file cap -- improving downstream LLM answer quality on the returned chunk list at zero index/storage cost. The n_neighbor_chunks idea maps directly onto nest's chunks_original_spans: store left/right neighbor chunk_ids so a hit can re-materialize its original window from the mmap.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-none for raw byte compression: langroid has no on-disk format, entropy coder, or quantization -- it is an orchestration layer that outsources storage to Qdrant/LanceDB/Chroma. Indirect relevance: the n_neighbor_chunks/window_ids pattern argues for storing only neighbor chunk_id pointers (a few varints) instead of duplicating overlapping context text, which trims redundancy in chunks_canonical and supports nest's 'compress more than everyone' goal by deduplicating chunk overlap.
repos.perf_notes: All steal-worthy pieces are cheap: RRF is O(total_hits) integer/float adds; rank_to_periphery is an O(k) index permutation with no allocation beyond the output vec; both run after the hot-path exact-cosine rerank, so they add negligible latency and are SIMD-irrelevant. langroid itself is pure Python with per-method latency dominated by network calls to external vector DBs and LLM relevance extraction (the relevance_extractor adds an LLM round-trip per passage and is the main latency sink, defaultable to None) -- nest gains the math, not the runtime cost.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: An opinionated, YAML-configured LangGraph RAG engine (quivr-core) paired with MegaParse, a "lossless" document-to-markdown ingestion tool that combines layout models with vision-LLM table reconstruction, plus a deterministic iterative token-budget context-reduction algorithm.
repos.core_innovation: The MegaParse ingestion contract: normalize any source document (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX) into a single canonical, hierarchy-preserving markdown representation BEFORE chunking/embedding, by routing each region through a layout model (~90% table segmentation) and falling back to a vision LLM that crops hard tables and reconstructs them as markdown. The canonical text is the thing you chunk, hash, and serve -- decoupling messy source bytes from a stable normalized representation.
key_techniques: MegaParse two-tier table extraction: layout-model segmentation (unstructured/doctr) for ~90% of tables, vision-LLM (gpt-4o/claude-3.5) crop-and-reconstruct fallback for complex tables -> markdown

Hierarchy-aware partition->chunk: split on document-format semantic units (headers, TOC, sections) first, only fall back to text-splitting (\n\n) when an element exceeds max chunk size (the 'unstructured' chunking model)
Deterministic combine_documents: assign sequential metadata['index']=0,1,2... to chunks so retrieved fragments can be re-ordered and mapped back to source position
retrieve_full_documents_context: rank by similarity score + chunk frequency, then reconstruct full-document context up to the highest chunk index per knowledge item (chunk->full-doc expansion)

reduce_rag_context: iterative arithmetic context fitting with an 85% security factor -- drop oldest chat-history pairs first, then drop chunks from the longest task, recomputing token count until it fits max_context_tokens
dynamic_retrieve: saturation-driven retrieval that multiplies k/top_n per iteration (max 3) until enough relevance-thresholded chunks are found
ContextualCompressionRetriever pattern: base vector retrieval ALWAYS followed by a pluggable reranker (Cohere/Jina) with IdempotentCompressor no-op fallback
YAML-declared RetrievalConfig/WorkflowConfig/NodeConfig as a portable, declarative description of the whole search pipeline
repos.nest_application: nest-python ingestion + nest-format: adopt a MegaParse-style 'canonicalization-before-chunk' stage so PDF/DOCX/PPTX are first normalized to deterministic markdown, then that normalized text becomes chunks_canonical(text) while raw source byte spans feed chunks_original_spans -- this directly strengthens nest's content_hash STABILITY guarantee (hash the normalized canonical form, not the encoding-dependent source) and makes the 'compress and serve PDF/parquet/datasets' north-star tractable. The chunk->full-doc index reconstruction (combine_documents/retrieve_full_documents_context) maps cleanly onto nest's chunks_original_spans + nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation reopen: store the sequential chunk index and parent-doc id so a hit can rehydrate the surrounding original span. The reduce_rag_context 85%-factor iterative trimming is a tiny deterministic, panic-free pure-integer algorithm that belongs in nest-runtime materialize as a 'fit retrieved chunks into a token/byte budget' helper (drop-lowest-score-first, recompute, stop when under budget) -- offline, no LLM call, fully reproducible. The ContextualCompressionRetriever 'always rerank' pattern validates nest's existing mandatory exact-cosine rerank as the correct architecture.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: MegaParse's normalize-to-canonical-markdown step is a precondition for extreme compression of heterogeneous formats -- you cannot deduplicate/zstd/entropy-code PDF or parquet effectively until you have lifted them into a single normalized text/structure representation. Canonicalizing before hashing also makes content_hash stable across source encodings (already a nest goal) and exposes far more cross-document redundancy for zstd on non-embedding sections. The chunk->full-doc index lets nest store one canonical body once and reference spans rather than duplicating overlapping chunk text. No new entropy coder or quantization scheme is offered here -- this repo is pure Python RAG glue, not a codec.
repos.perf_notes: Pure-Python, langgraph/asyncio orchestration; no SIMD, no custom on-disk format, vectorstores are delegated to PGVector or Faiss. Heavy paths (vision-LLM table reconstruction, Cohere/Jina rerank) are network/GPU-bound external API calls -- antithetical to nest's offline-by-construction constraint, so only the ALGORITHMS (budget trimming, chunk indexing, hierarchy chunking) are stealable, not the runtime. dynamic_retrieve caps at 3 iterations; reduce_rag_context is O(n) per trim pass over chunks. No memory-mapping, no zero-copy; everything is in-RAM Python objects.
repos.license: Quivr: Apache-2.0. MegaParse: Apache-2.0 (with the caveat that MegaParse Vision and the unstructured/llama-parse backends pull in their own external model/API dependencies).

repos.one_liner: A Node.js/Express provider-agnostic RAG + agent platform that ingests documents, chunks them with an embedder-aware TextSplitter, caches embeddings deterministically by UUID v5 content hash, and queries one of ~10 pluggable vector DBs (default LanceDB/Arrow) with cosine distance normalized to a 0-1 similarity and optional native reranking.
repos.core_innovation: A deterministic content-addressed embedding cache keyed by chunk content + embedder identity (UUID v5), which makes re-ingestion skip already-computed vectors.
key_techniques: UUID v5 namespaced-hash cache keys over chunk text + embedder identity, stored as per-file JSON vectors
Embedder-aware TextSplitter sizing chunks to min(user setting, model max token length) with char overlap
Self-describing chunks via <document_metadata> headers (title/published/source) prepended before embedding
distanceToSimilarity: normalize cosine/L2 distances to a uniform 0-1 similarity
Retrieve-then-rerank with NativeEmbeddingReranker for precision over raw ANN recall
Single storage directory that fully reconstructs all state (sqlite + lancedb + vector-cache + documents JSON)
Common VectorDatabase interface abstracting ~10 backends
Agent Intelligent Skill Selection to prune tools and cut token usage up to 80%
repos.nest_application: Build a deterministic embedding cache in nest-python's builder backed by nest-format hashing: key = SHA-256(canonical_chunk_text || model_fingerprint), value = stored f32 embedding. On rebuild the builder reuses cached vectors instead of re-running the model, giving fast incremental rebuilds while keeping byte-identical output (preserves the reproducible-build contract). Also adopt distanceToSimilarity-style explicit 0-1 normalization of the exact-cosine rerank score in nest-runtime/search.rs so returned scores are uniform across raw/f16/int8 encodings, and formalize per-chunk provenance headers tying chunks_original_spans + provenance into nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations in nest-format/sections.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect. anything-llm does no compression or quantization (it stores raw f32 vectors via LanceDB/Arrow and delegates everything to external DBs), so it offers nothing for nest's extreme-compression north star directly. Its value is build-time/operational: the deterministic embedding cache removes recompute cost during the encode/quantize loop, which is what makes aggressive re-encoding experiments (int8, f16, future codecs) cheap to iterate. It validates nest's content-hash determinism as a cache primitive, not as a size reducer.
repos.perf_notes: All-JS/Node runtime; no SIMD, no quantization, no on-disk compression of its own. LanceDB (Rust/Arrow columnar, mmap-friendly) provides the fast local path and is reported "blazing fast on low-end hardware" with ~100% of users on it. Embedding cache is the main perf lever -- it eliminates redundant embedding API/model calls. Vectors stored as raw f32, so memory/storage scales linearly with corpus and dimension (no float16/int8 like nest).
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: RAGFlow is a layout-aware RAG engine (DeepDoc parser + template chunking) backed by the Infinity AI-native database, which serves a four-way hybrid search (dense vector via HNSW+LVQ, sparse vector, BM25 full-text, and ColBERT tensor/late-interaction) fused by RRF / weighted-sum / tensor reranking.
repos.core_innovation: Two-stage Local Vector Quantization (LVQ) for HNSW: instead of plain per-vector affine int8, first subtract the corpus mean and quantize the mean-centered residual (stage 1, used for graph construction and traversal), then quantize the second-order residual of that difference (stage 2, used only in the final similarity refinement). Because every vector is offset by the same global mean and scaled per-vector, the nearest-neighbor ordering is preserved, so the HNSW graph can be built and traversed entirely on the compressed stage-1 codes -- no full-precision vectors kept in RAM -- cutting memory bandwidth and footprint while recall stays intact. Complementary idea: ColBERT multi-vector reranking with binary quantization, where each float becomes one bit (1/32 size) and MaxSim is computed with Hamming distance, also ranking-preserving.
key_techniques: LVQ: subtract global corpus mean, then per-vector scalar-quantize the residual; build/traverse HNSW on stage-1 codes only
Two-stage residual quantization: stage-1 codes for traversal, stage-2 residual codes for final-score refinement
ColBERT late-interaction: per-token multi-vector (tensor) doc representation, MaxSim = sum over query tokens of max token-to-token similarity
Binary quantization of tensors: 1 bit/float (1/32 size), MaxSim via Hamming distance, ranking-preserving
Tensor-array chunking for >128-token docs: split, one tensor per chunk, aggregate MaxSim across chunks
Three fusion modes: RRF (rank-based, k=60), Weighted Sum (score-normalized), and tensor/ColBERT rerank as finer verification
EMVB tensor index (ColBERTv2 improvement): centroid pre-filtering + SIMD-accelerated MaxSim used as a retriever not just a reranker
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals. (1) LVQ in nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs + nest-runtime/src/ann + simd: today int8.rs does plain per-vector affine quant (scale=max_abs/127, no mean) and ann/mod.rs keeps a full f32 `vectors: Vec<f32>` snapshot in RAM for HNSW. Add a new additive embeddings encoding id (e.g. 4, RESERVED-safe within v1) int8_lvq: store one global f32 mean[dim] in the payload prefix, then per-vector scale + i8 residual codes, plus an optional stage-2 residual blob. Then ann/build.rs and ann/search.rs traverse on the i8 codes (reuse the existing dot_f32_i8 SIMD kernel) instead of the f32 snapshot, deleting the `vectors: Vec<f32>` RAM cost and shrinking the tiny preset below 0.283 while keeping recall via the exact-cosine rerank that already runs. (2) Weighted-sum fusion: bm25/fusion.rs only has rrf_union; add weighted_sum_union(a_scores, b_scores, alpha) with min-max score normalization as a second hybrid mode behind a search_contract flag (~30 deterministic lines, no new section). (3) ColBERT tensor rerank as a new optional section id 0x09 (tensor_index) + a nest-runtime rerank stage: store per-chunk multi-vectors binary-quantized (1 bit/float), compute MaxSim with Hamming-popcount as an optional final reranker after the mandatory exact-cosine pass, unlocking offline token-level semantic reranking with no GPU.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. LVQ is a strictly better embedding codec than nest's current int8: mean-centering + per-vector residual scale preserves NN order so the HNSW graph runs on compressed codes, eliminating the full-f32 in-RAM snapshot and pushing the tiny preset's 0.283 size ratio lower at equal recall@10 (0.992). Binary tensor quant is a 32x compressor for a new modality (multi-vector reranking) that is itself ranking-preserving via Hamming MaxSim. Both fit nest's compress-more-than-everyone-while-staying-offline/deterministic/single-file north star.
repos.perf_notes: Infinity benchmarks: HNSW+LVQ ~0.1ms query latency, 15K+ QPS on million-scale vectors; BM25 ~1ms / 12K+ QPS over 33M docs. LVQ win is reduced memory bandwidth (smaller codes streamed during graph walk) plus random-access friendliness suited to graph search. ColBERT rerank gives ~100x throughput of cross-encoder rerankers at comparable nDCG; binary-quantized MaxSim via Hamming/popcount maps to popcnt (x86_64) / vcnt (NEON), both already in nest's simd dispatcher. EMVB adds centroid pre-filter + SIMD MaxSim. Practical reranking range is top-100; top-1000 gives no nDCG gain at big latency cost.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (both ragflow and infinity) -- permissive, safe to vendor/learn from for nest.

repos.one_liner: Jina is a gRPC/HTTP/WebSocket microservice framework for multimodal AI serving whose real reusable asset is its data layer DocArray, with a columnar DocVec store that stacks all per-document tensors into one contiguous tensor and serializes via a typed protobuf schema (DenseNdArrayProto = raw buffer bytes + shape + dtype).
repos.core_innovation: The DocVec columnar layout: instead of storing N documents row-wise (each carrying its own embedding object), DocVec transposes the array so every schema field becomes a column, and all tensor fields across documents are stacked into ONE contiguous backing tensor; each Document becomes a zero-copy view (like tensor[i]) into that column.
