This is exactly nest's "embeddings as one packed matrix scored straight off mmap" idea, generalized into a data model with a typed protobuf wire format (DenseNdArrayProto: bytes buffer + repeated uint32 shape + string dtype) that cleanly separates the dense numeric payload from its shape/dtype metadata.
key_techniques: DocVec columnar transpose: per-field columns, all tensor fields stacked into one contiguous tensor for batch/SIMD-friendly access
Document-as-view: BaseDoc holds no data, it is a numpy/torch-style view[i] into the shared column buffer (zero-copy slicing)
DenseNdArrayProto encoding: split tensor into raw `bytes buffer` + `repeated uint32 shape` + `string dtype`, decoupling dense payload from metadata

DocVecProto with 4 typed column maps (tensor_columns / doc_columns / docs_vec_columns / any_columns) routing dense tensors, nested docs, doc-arrays, and heterogeneous scalars to format-appropriate codecs
Deferred tensor backend selection: dtype/shape metadata lets the same bytes deserialize to numpy/torch/tf at read time without re-encoding
Pluggable protocol x compression matrix (protobuf|pickle) x (lz4|bz2|lzma|zlib|gzip) via self-describing `name.$protocol.$compress` filenames
Recursive nesting: a BaseDoc field becomes a nested DocVec column, enabling columnar storage of structured/multimodal records
repos.nest_application: Two concrete adaptations. (1) nest-format: adopt DenseNdArrayProto's split-metadata discipline for any future non-embedding tensor section (image-similarity feature matrices, audio frames) -- store raw little-endian buffer + explicit (shape, dtype/encoding-id) descriptor in the section manifest, never interleaving metadata into the hot dense bytes; this keeps the AVX2/NEON dot-product kernel pointed at a clean contiguous matrix like nest's existing embeddings section, and the deferred-backend trick maps onto nest's float16/int8 encoding ids (same bytes, reader picks decode path). (2) nest-format sections + manifest: borrow DocVec's 4-way column routing as the design rule for the planned multi-modal expansion (text/json/yaml/parquet/pdf/audio/video) -- a typed-column manifest where each logical column declares its codec (zstd for text/json columns, raw-mmap f32/f16/int8 for dense tensor columns, bm25 for tokenized text), so the writer routes each column to its best codec while the reader still mmaps tensor columns directly. This is the columnar analogue of nest's current per-section encoding, uses RESERVED section ids 0x09+ additively, and unlocks "compress structured datasets/parquet/repos" without breaking single-file/offline/deterministic guarantees. nest-runtime hot path is untouched because tensor columns stay raw contiguous f32/f16/int8.
repos.compression_relevance: Medium-indirect. Jina/DocArray does NOT do extreme compression -- embeddings hit the wire as a raw f32 buffer (DenseNdArrayProto.buffer), and "compression" is just an outer general-purpose codec pass (lz4/zlib/lzma) over the serialized blob, the opposite of nest's policy of never general-compressing embeddings. The transferable compression-relevant idea is structural, not entropic: the columnar transpose groups like-typed, like-dtype values together, the precondition for high-ratio compression of NON-embedding data (delta/dictionary/RLE on an id column, zstd on a homogeneous text/json column) and for keeping dense tensor columns in one clean contiguous block that int8 quantization and mmap-scoring exploit. Informs nest's dataset/parquet column-compression roadmap; offers no new entropy coder.
repos.perf_notes: DocVec's contiguous column tensor is built for batch inference and vectorized ops -- the same memory shape nest relies on for SIMD dot products; zero-copy Document views avoid per-doc allocation. DocArray got ~240% faster JSON serialization by moving the validation core to Pydantic v2 (Rust pyo3), confirming the build-in-python/serve-in-Rust split nest already uses via nest-python. Jina/DocArray ships no SIMD distance kernels of its own; vector search is delegated to external Document Indexes (HNSWLib/Qdrant/Weaviate/Elastic), so there is nothing to steal on the ANN/SIMD side -- nest's hand-rolled HnswIndex + mandatory exact cosine rerank is already ahead.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (both jina and docarray)

repos.one_liner: A cloud-native (Cloudflare Workers + pgvector/D1) "memory engine" for LLMs that unifies RAG, user profiles, and a temporally-aware knowledge graph behind one API, using Matryoshka (MRL) truncatable embeddings, AST-aware (cAST/tree-sitter) code chunking, and RRF hybrid search with cross-encoder reranking under ~200ms.
repos.core_innovation: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL): one embedding model emits vectors whose dimensions are ordered by importance, so a 3072-dim vector can be truncated to a 256/512-dim prefix (then L2-renormalized) and still preserve most recall. This turns embedding dimensionality into a graceful, model-backed lossy compression knob and enables coarse-to-fine two-pass search (cheap truncated dims for candidate recall, full dims only to rerank survivors).
key_techniques: Matryoshka Representation Learning: order-by-importance dims, truncate to prefix (e.g. 3072->512->256), then L2-renormalize the slice so cosine stays calibrated in the smaller subspace
Coarse-to-fine two-pass retrieval: recall top-N (e.g. 200) with truncated low-dim vectors, then rerank that shortlist with full-dim exact cosine
Post-truncation lightweight scalar quantization of the renormalized slice (stacks on top of dim reduction)
AST-aware chunking (cAST): tree-sitter parses source into an AST and splits on function/class/method boundaries, line-based fallback for unsupported languages
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) for vector+keyword hybrid: score = sum 1/(k+rank), k=60; ~91% recall@10 before any reranker
Optional ColBERT/cross-encoder rerank only on top 20-50 candidates, added after benchmarking shows RRF alone misses recall target
Eval rigor: hard negatives (500 same-repo distractor files) + IoU>=0.3 relevance threshold to avoid trivially-easy retrieval benchmarks
Temporal layer: fact contradiction-resolution (overwrite stale facts) and recency-decay deprioritization over the knowledge graph
repos.nest_application: MRL is the single biggest steal and maps cleanly onto nest's frozen-but-additive format. (1) nest-format: add an MRL-aware dimension layout to the embeddings section. Store the full f32/f16 vectors AND record a manifest field `mrl_prefix_dims` (e.g. [256,512,full]); because dims are importance-ordered, a truncated prefix is just the first K contiguous floats already on disk, so an MRL-trained model lets the `tiny` preset drop to a 256-dim int8 prefix for the hot scan with near-zero recall loss. This is additive (new optional manifest field / reuses existing embeddings section bytes, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump) and deterministic. (2) nest-runtime: add a coarse-to-fine path in search.rs alongside the existing exact-rerank contract. Pass 1 runs the SIMD dot-product (AVX2/NEON) over the truncated prefix straight off mmap to gather candidates; Pass 2 reuses nest's MANDATORY exact-cosine rerank over the full-dim vectors. This fits nest's existing 'ann proxy then real cosine rerank' contract perfectly and cuts the hot-loop bytes-touched by 6-12x with no new index type. (3) The L2-renormalize-the-slice trick is the load-bearing correctness detail: store a per-prefix renorm scale (or renormalize at materialize time) so truncated cosine stays honest. Secondary steal: AST-aware chunking belongs in nest-python's builder as a tree-sitter-backed chunker so chunks_canonical respects code structure (better chunk_ids/spans), with line-based fallback. RRF is already nest's hybrid model, so it is reference-only confirmation that k=60 and exact rerank are the right defaults.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly on-mission. MRL prefix-truncation is a graceful, model-supported lossy compressor for the embeddings section, which is nest's largest and the only section that cannot be zstd-compressed (it is scored from mmap on the hot path). It is orthogonal to and stacks with nest's existing f16/int8 quantization: dim-reduction (3072->256 ~= 12x) times int8 (4x) compounds, and the two-pass coarse search means the smaller prefix is what the hot SIMD loop actually reads, so it improves BOTH size ratio (toward beating the 0.283 tiny preset) AND search throughput while the mandatory full-dim exact rerank preserves real-cosine ground truth.
repos.perf_notes: Supermemory reports end-to-end retrieve+rerank routinely under 200ms using MRL truncation plus lightweight quantization; RRF alone reaches ~91% recall@10. For nest: a 256-dim int8 prefix vs a 3072-dim f32 full vector is ~48x fewer bytes touched per candidate in Pass 1, which is pure win for cache-resident SIMD dot products off mmap (AVX2/NEON). The key footgun is that truncated prefixes occupy a smaller subspace and inflate/jitter cosine, so each slice must be L2-renormalized (scale by 1/||prefix||) before scoring; nest should bake this into the writer or materialize path to keep determinism.
repos.license: MIT (supermemory main repo and code-chunk are MIT-licensed); MRL itself is a published technique (Kusupati et al.), not encumbered, and tree-sitter is MIT.

repos.one_liner: A ~80-line TypeScript/Next.js edge-runtime "personalized Perplexity" that fuses Brave/Bing web results with user-scoped memories pulled from the hosted Supermemory engine and streams them through gpt-4o-mini; the real retrieval IP lives in Supermemory (a vector-graph memory engine), not in this thin client.
repos.core_innovation: The orchestration treats personalization as a single namespace-scoped memory search whose results are returned at the SMALLEST SUFFICIENT GRANULARITY via a fallback ladder (summary > title > concatenated chunks), rather than always shipping raw chunks. Memory is extracted facts with temporal supersession (isLatest flag) instead of stateless verbatim RAG chunks.
key_techniques: containerTags: per-tenant namespace partitioning of a single shared store (scope = [user.email, 'opensearch']) so one index serves many isolated views without separate files
Summary-first retrieval fallback ladder: return mem.summary ?? mem.title ?? chunks.join('\n') -- pick the most compressed representation that still answers, instead of always returning raw spans
isLatest temporal-supersession flag in the memory graph: contradictions resolved by timestamp/update-pattern so stale facts are deprioritized while history is preserved (not deleted)

Memory-vs-RAG: ingest-time fact extraction into a 'facts-on-facts' vector-graph with ontology-aware edges, vs storing verbatim chunks (note: academic counterpoint says extraction discards the verbatim substrate, capping recall ~20pts below a verbatim ceiling)
Hybrid retrieval: parallel dense-vector + keyword/BM25-style lexical match, merged then context-aware reranked with temporal filtering, all under ~400ms
Two-tier user profile: stable static facts + dynamic episodic context, assembled at query time (~50ms) and injected as a compact system-prompt preamble
Edge-runtime stateless orchestration: no session/state in the app layer because the memory store is the durable state primitive
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add OPTIONAL additive per-chunk summary section (id 0x09+, no field-meaning change so still v1) feeding nest-runtime materialize a compressed representative. nest-runtime: implement summary>canonical>raw fallback ladder in search/materialize; add deterministic version/isLatest u32 in provenance to collapse superseded duplicate chunks at build time before encoding (shrinks tiny/compressed presets); layer a deterministic provenance-timestamp 'temporal rerank' boost ON TOP of the mandatory exact-cosine rerank (cosine stays ground truth). containerTags -> optional per-chunk tag set in provenance for multi-tenant filtering inside one .nest file, exposed as nest-cli search --tag.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. The one transferable compression idea is the summary-first granularity ladder: storing and serving a small synopsis per chunk lets nest return a representative far smaller than the canonical span (good for context packing and citation previews), and build-time supersession/dedup of contradicting facts removes redundant chunks before encoding, directly improving size ratios of the tiny/compressed presets. Everything else (knowledge graph, fact extraction, hosted reranker) is orchestration-layer and orthogonal to nest's byte-level codec goals; nest's exact-cosine-rerank guarantee is actually stronger than supermemory's ANN-proxy scores.
repos.license: MIT (opensearch-ai repo); Supermemory engine is a hosted closed/proprietary API behind the client
repos.perf_notes: Client is Vercel edge-runtime, streaming via Vercel AI SDK; no local compute. Supermemory engine reports profile assembly ~50ms, full hybrid+rerank+temporal-filter retrieval <400ms, with no caller-configured embedding infra. Benchmarks (vendor-reported): 85.4% LongMemEval-S, #1 LoCoMo P@1 59.7%, #1 ConvoMem; an arXiv counterpoint measured ~65.4% citing the verbatim-discard weakness of extraction-first memory. No SIMD/quantization relevance -- all heavy lifting is remote and opaque.

repos.one_liner: A Rust daemon that exposes a remote Supermemory container as a real mountable POSIX directory (FUSE on Linux, a pure-Rust loopback NFSv3 server on macOS) backed by a SQLite write-back cache, a Semaphore(8) bidirectional sync engine, and a transparent grep shim that turns flagless `grep` inside the mount into a hybrid semantic-search call.
repos.core_innovation: "Retrieval-as-a-filesystem": present an opaque memory/vector store as a navigable directory tree so standard Unix tools (ls, cat, tree, grep) become the query interface. The signature trick is that flagless `grep` inside the mount is transparently rerouted to semantic/vector search while any flag (or `grep -F`) falls back to literal substring matching; mount context is detected via a hidden `.smfs` marker file so the shim is a no-op everywhere else. This makes a vector DB consumable by any agent/tool that can read a file, with zero bespoke SDK.
key_techniques: Pure-Rust NFSv3 loopback server bound to 127.0.0.1:<auto>, mounted via /sbin/mount_nfs, no kernel extension (macOS path)
Zero-setup FUSE mount via the `fuser` crate (Linux path)
SQLite as a persistent write-back cache that survives daemon restarts and serves offline reads (replaced an in-memory store)
Bidirectional sync engine: pull on cache-miss/TTL-expiry, push dirty writes with exponential-backoff retry, parallelized by a Semaphore(8) fan-out with independent pull/push sides
Transparent grep interception keyed on a hidden `.smfs` marker: flagless grep => semantic search, any flag / `grep -F` => literal grep
Scoped indexing via path globs (trailing slash = recursive folder, no slash = exact file) decide which writes get embedded vs stored as inert bytes
Virtual synthesized file `profile.md` at mount root: never stored, regenerated on read from all memories via an API endpoint (computed-on-read pseudo-file)
VFS hot-path optimization (v0.0.4) that short-circuits local-only reads/writes to skip sync/IPC overhead
repos.nest_application: Two adaptable patterns that keep nest's offline/single-file/no-socket guarantees. (1) A NEW optional crate nest-fuse, deliberately kept OUT of nest-runtime so the socketless core is untouched: mmap a .nest file and expose chunks_canonical as virtual read-only files (e.g. /chunks/<chunk_id>.txt) plus a synthesized /search/<query>.txt computed-on-read pseudo-file that runs the existing exact-cosine search path and emits ranked `nest://content_hash/chunk_id` citations -- SMFS's profile.md-on-read pattern applied to nest's deterministic search, so any agent can grep/cat a .nest with no SDK. FUSE opens no network socket, preserving 'offline by construction'; the loopback-NFSv3 variant must be REJECTED because it binds a socket. (2) The flagless-vs-flagged grep split maps onto a thin nest-cli addition: `nest grep <pattern>` where a bare pattern => semantic (embed query + mandatory exact-cosine rerank over nest-runtime's search) and `-F`/regex => literal scan of chunks_canonical, giving the same dual-mode UX inside the existing clap surface. The SQLite write-back cache is a REFERENCE only for nest's future real-time-edit roadmap (stage dirty chunk edits in a sidecar, flush via a deterministic rebuild) since the FROZEN additive container forbids in-place mutation.
repos.compression_relevance: n/a -- SMFS discloses no compression, entropy coding, quantization, or on-disk vector format; it is a filesystem/sync facade that delegates all retrieval to a remote hybrid-search API. It offers nothing for the 'compress more than everyone' north star. Its value to nest is purely ergonomic (retrieval-as-filesystem) and architectural (computed-on-read virtual files, dual-mode grep), not byte size.
repos.license: Not confirmed from README; supermemory-ecosystem repos are typically MIT or Apache-2.0 but treat as unverified. Only design patterns (FUSE mount, grep shim, on-read virtual file) would be reimplemented from scratch, not vendored, so license exposure is minimal.
repos.perf_notes: Sync concurrency capped at Semaphore(8); default 30s pull interval; 30s unmount drain-timeout; exponential-backoff push retry. macOS pays NFSv3-over-loopback marshalling cost; Linux FUSE pays a kernel<->userspace context switch per syscall. v0.0.4 added a VFS hot path to skip sync overhead on local-only ops. No SIMD, no vector-scan kernels, no mmap'd embedded index -- all retrieval is remote, so there are no on-device throughput numbers to steal.

repos.one_liner: A Python GraphRAG orchestration library that builds a lexical+entity knowledge graph from text/PDF (chunk -> entity -> relation) via schema-guided LLM extraction, then serves it through vector, hybrid (vector+fulltext), graph-traversal-Cypher, and text2cypher retrievers backed by Neo4j's HNSW vector index and Lucene fulltext index.
repos.core_innovation: The "lexical graph" overlay: every chunk becomes a node wired with typed edges (NEXT_CHUNK for sequential context, FROM_DOCUMENT to source, FROM_CHUNK/PART_OF_CHUNK to extracted entities), so retrieval can expand a vector hit into its neighborhood (prior/next chunks, co-mentioned entities) instead of returning isolated chunks. This is the minimal, deterministic graph layer that turns a flat chunk store into a navigable graph -- exactly what nest needs to add "graph search" without a graph DB.
key_techniques: Lexical graph: Document->Chunk->Entity nodes with typed edges NEXT_CHUNK, FROM_DOCUMENT, FROM_CHUNK, PART_OF_CHUNK (an adjacency overlay over existing chunk_ids)
Hybrid fusion via UNION of vector + fulltext branches with max-score normalization (n.score / index_max_score) then per-node max() aggregation (the default RRF/'naive' ranker)
Linear ranker: final = alpha*norm_vector + (1-alpha)*norm_fulltext, alpha in [0,1] -- one tunable weight instead of RRF
VectorCypherRetriever pattern: run ANN first, then a parameterized graph-traversal query over the (node, score) seeds to pull connected context
Schema-guided LLM entity/relation extraction with allowed node/rel/triplet patterns and structured Pydantic/JSON output for validation
FixedSizeSplitter with chunk_size/chunk_overlap and 'approximate' boundary mode that avoids cutting words mid-token
Entity resolution tiers: exact-property match, RapidFuzz Levenshtein fuzzy match, spaCy-embedding cosine semantic match
effective_search_ratio: over-fetch top_k*ratio ANN candidates then trim to recover recall lost to approximation (mirrors nest's exact-rerank over-fetch)
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals. (1) nest-format: add a RESERVED optional section graph_edges (next free id 0x09) holding a deterministic CSR/adjacency list over chunk_ids -- src=chunk_id u32, dst=chunk_id u32, edge_type u8 (0=NEXT_CHUNK, 1=FROM_DOCUMENT, 2=ENTITY_LINK). All integers LE unsigned, repr(C), built python-side, sorted by (src,edge_type,dst) for byte-identical reproducibility; gets its own per-section SHA-256 and feeds content_hash. Additive-only, stays single-file/offline. (2) nest-runtime: a small graph::Adjacency reader (mmap, no panic, ~150 loc under the 300-line cap) plus a 'search-graph' path that seeds from exact-cosine top-k then does a bounded BFS over NEXT_CHUNK/ENTITY_LINK edges and re-runs exact cosine rerank on the expanded set so returned scores stay real cosine, never an ann proxy. (3) nest-runtime fusion: augment the current bm25/hnsw RRF with max-score-normalization + an optional linear-alpha ranker (one f32 weight) for a deterministic, tunable vector/text blend. nest-cli adds 'search-graph' as a 9th subcommand. Entity extraction stays in nest-python build tooling, out of the frozen rust core.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. The lexical-graph adjacency is a compact integer overlay (CSR of u32 chunk ids + u8 edge type), highly compressible with zstd as a non-embedding section, and it lets nest reconstruct cross-chunk context WITHOUT duplicating overlapping text -- drop chunk_overlap redundancy from chunks_canonical and recover neighbor context via NEXT_CHUNK edges, shrinking the largest text section. The linear/max-norm fusion adds zero storage. Entity dedup (fuzzy/exact) collapses repeated mentions, reducing stored entity strings. Net: unlocks graph-search and removes overlap redundancy while keeping single-file/offline/deterministic guarantees.
repos.license: Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: Fusion is pure arithmetic over already-fetched top_k sets (negligible). Graph expansion is a bounded BFS over a mmap'd CSR adjacency -- O(seeds * fanout * depth), no hot-path allocations if depth/fanout are capped; the cost driver is the exact-cosine rerank over the expanded candidate set, which reuses nest's existing SIMD dot products (AVX2/NEON/scalar). The over-fetch ratio trades a few extra ANN candidates for recall, matching nest's existing exact-rerank-after-ANN design.

repos.one_liner: A Python GraphRAG orchestration SDK that does schema-guided LLM entity/relation extraction into a FalkorDB knowledge graph (a Redis module whose engine stores every relation type as a GraphBLAS sparse adjacency matrix and executes Cypher traversals as sparse linear algebra), then answers via multi-path retrieval (vector + full-text + text-to-Cypher + relationship expansion) merged by ranked fusion and a final local cosine rerank.
repos.core_innovation: Represent the graph as typed sparse adjacency matrices (CSC) and turn graph traversal into sparse matrix multiplication.
key_techniques: Typed sparse adjacency matrices: one CSC (compressed-sparse-column) matrix per relation type + one type-agnostic global adjacency matrix; node labels as diagonal identity matrices
Traversal as semiring matrix multiplication (GraphBLAS): k-hop reachability = matrix power, pattern join = A * B * transpose(A); planner compiles Cypher to a matrix expression
3D sparse tensor (src x dst x edge_id) so a cell holds either a single relationship-id scalar or a vector of edge-ids for parallel multi-edges between the same pair

Copy-on-write versioned/delta matrix: writes accumulate in a delta overlay, flushed/fused into the base matrix in batch; enables MVCC snapshot isolation (concurrent reads on snapshots, writes serialized through a single mpsc channel)
Schema-guided / ontology-constrained extraction: a small ontology (3-7 node types, 5-15 relations) bounds open-world LLM extraction into a closed, queryable schema
Multi-path hybrid retrieval with ranked result merging: vector cosine + DB full-text + text-to-Cypher + relationship expansion, candidates fused then reranked
Local cosine rerank as the final, non-LLM scoring stage so the returned score is true cosine, decoupled from expensive model calls

Incremental graph sync: SHA-256 per-document change detection driving idempotent apply_changes(added/modified/deleted) via graph merge instead of full rebuild, with MENTIONS edges linking entities back to source chunks for provenance
repos.nest_application: See above: section 0x09 graph_adjacency (CSC, per-type matrices) in nest-format; pure-Rust deterministic SpMV/SpGEMM k-hop traversal in nest-runtime reusing the SIMD dispatcher; expose as a search path fused into the existing RRF + mandatory exact-cosine-rerank contract; new nest-cli subcommand (e.g. search-graph) and pyo3 binding. Avoids vendoring GraphBLAS/Redis; preserves offline/single-file/deterministic/additive-format constraints and <300 LOC/file.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct. CSC/CSR sparse-matrix storage IS a compression scheme for graphs: storing only nonzeros as (indptr,indices) is O(edges) not O(nodes^2), and for a sparse relation graph this is dramatically smaller than an edge-list-of-strings. Combined with nest's existing zstd codec on non-embedding sections, the indices arrays (monotone within each column) are highly delta+varint+zstd compressible, letting nest carry a whole relationship graph in kilobytes and advance the 'compress AND serve graphs/databases/repos' mission. The delta-matrix/copy-on-write idea also hints at how nest could later support real-time edit without rewriting the frozen base (overlay deltas), another north-star goal.
repos.perf_notes: SpMV/SpGEMM over CSC is bandwidth-bound and extremely cache-friendly vs pointer-chasing; the same memory-locality argument nest already uses for mmap'd SIMD dot products applies to CSC column dot products, so the existing AVX2/NEON dispatcher can be reused for boolean/weighted SpMV. FalkorDB's full GraphBLAS (SuiteSparse) is a large C dependency and offline-hostile (Redis module); nest should NOT vendor it -- a minimal pure-Rust CSC matvec (tens of lines) covers k-hop traversal without the dependency, threading, or MVCC machinery. MVCC/mpsc write serialization is irrelevant to nest's frozen, read-only, single-process mmap model and should be skipped.
repos.license: GraphRAG-SDK is MIT (FalkorDB org). FalkorDB engine core is dual-licensed Server Side Public License (SSPL) / commercial -- engine NOT vendorable; only the algorithmic ideas (CSC, traversal-as-matmul) are free to reimplement. SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS is Apache-2.0 but a heavy C dep to avoid.

repos.one_liner: Verba ("The Golden RAGtriever") is a modular Python RAG orchestrator over Weaviate, built around swappable Manager stages (Reader/Chunker/Embedder/Retriever/Generator) whose retrieval-path innovations (WindowRetriever neighbor expansion, document-level score grouping, Weaviate semantic answer cache, format-aware chunkers) are orchestration logic layered on a remote vector DB.
repos.core_innovation: WindowRetriever: after a top-k hybrid (vector + BM25) search, every chunk whose score clears a configurable threshold (1-100) is expanded to its N neighboring chunks fetched by contiguous chunk index within the same parent document, then chunks are grouped per document and re-scored at the document level. This decouples embedding/retrieval granularity (small, precise chunks) from generation granularity (wide, coherent context) with zero extra index storage, since neighbors are addressed by deterministic positional id rather than re-searched.
key_techniques: WindowRetriever: positional neighbor-chunk expansion by chunk index within a document, gated by a score threshold and window-size N
document-level score aggregation: group retrieved chunks by parent document and compute a doc score to rank/merge fragmented hits
hybrid search via Weaviate: parallel dense-vector + BM25 sparse search fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
semantic answer cache: embed both query and generated answer, serve cached answers on cosine-similar repeat queries (skip retrieval+generation)
format-aware chunkers: Markdown/HTML/Code/JSON/Recursive/Semantic/Sentence/Token splitters preserving structural boundaries vs blind fixed-size splits
spaCy-driven token and sentence segmentation as chunk-unit primitives
SemanticChunker: group adjacent sentences by embedding similarity into variable-length coherent chunks
Manager/component plug-in registry: each pipeline stage is a swappable interface selected by config
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime search path: add a 'window expansion' post-step in crates/nest-runtime/src/search after the exact-cosine rerank. nest already has zero-cost ingredients: chunk_ids (deterministic, ordered) + chunks_original_spans (byte span per chunk) + provenance (parent-doc grouping). Implement: for each reranked hit above a configurable threshold, materialize chunk_ids[i-w .. i+w] from the same provenance source by id adjacency, dedup, and merge their original_spans into one contiguous citation range so nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations widen to a coherent passage with no re-search. NO format change (additive, reads existing FROZEN sections), determinism preserved (seeded order). Document-level aggregation maps to a new nest-cli flag (search --group-by-doc) over provenance. The format-aware chunkers + SemanticChunker belong in nest-python (builder writing chunks_canonical + chunks_original_spans): boundary-aware markdown/code/json chunking improves recall AND compression. The Weaviate semantic-answer-cache is the one piece nest must NOT steal: it needs online state and a network DB, violating offline/single-file/no-socket constraints.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real, via two levers. (1) Decoupling retrieval granularity from context granularity (WindowRetriever) lets nest embed/store smaller, more uniform chunks that quantize (int8) and dedup/zstd more predictably, shrinking embeddings + chunks_canonical, while window expansion restores context at query time for free from chunk_ids adjacency. (2) Structure-aware chunkers produce boundary-aligned chunks_canonical that zstd-compress better (more repeated structural tokens, fewer mid-token splits) and reduce chunks_original_spans fragmentation. Neither adds a new on-disk section; both reuse existing FROZEN sections, advancing 'compress more than everyone' without format risk.
repos.perf_notes: WindowRetriever expansion is O(hits * window) id lookups plus span merges, no extra vector math, so it adds negligible cost on nest's mmap hot path and stays off the SIMD dot-product loop. nest's known ~300-500ms search-text python boot overhead is unrelated. Verba itself is pure-Python orchestration with no SIMD/quantization of its own; all vector math, RRF fusion, and HNSW live inside Weaviate (Go), so there is no kernel or codec to vendor, only the retrieval-flow algorithm to reimplement in Rust.
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause

repos.one_liner: A collection of ~92% Jupyter notebooks demonstrating Weaviate features and integrations (RAG, agents, hybrid/multi-vector search, multi-tenancy) whose only deeply transferable systems content is the family of vector-quantization codecs the recipes exercise: Product Quantization (PQ), Scalar (SQ), Binary (BQ), and the newest 8-bit Rotational Quantization (RQ), all paired with an exact-vector rescoring step.
repos.core_innovation: Rotational Quantization: a seeded Fast Walsh-Hadamard rotation before 8-bit scalar quantization gaussianizes the vector so a single short quantization interval works for all dimensions, giving ~99% recall at 4x compression where naive int8 loses recall, all deterministically and with a SIMD integer-dot hot path plus exact rescoring.
key_techniques: Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) as O(D log D) pseudo-random orthogonal rotation: 3 rounds of blocked FWHT + random sign flips + element swaps, replacing an O(D^2) random orthogonal matrix
Per-dimension 8-bit scalar quantization into 256 evenly-spaced levels between a stored min/max interval, stored as [u8*dim, f32 lo, f32 hi, f32 squared_norm]
Asymmetric/expanded inner-product estimate: expand q.x into 4 terms where the dominant term is an integer byte-vector dot product done with SIMD (~2.3x faster than f32)
Exact-vector rescoring: ANN returns top-m on quantized distance, then recompute exact distance on uncompressed vectors for those m to erase recall loss

Product Quantization: split D into segments, k-means 256 centroids per segment (8 bits/segment) into a codebook, Asymmetric Distance Computation via precomputed per-segment lookup tables, sparse Fisher-Yates training-set sampling
Binary Quantization: 1 bit per dim (sign only), 32x compression, Hamming-distance prefilter then rescore
Scalar Quantization with data-trained per-dimension buckets rather than a single global scale
repos.nest_application: Adapt RQ to upgrade nest-format's int8 codec (crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs, which today does naive per-vector max-abs scalar quant) into a rotated-int8 codec. Concretely: (1) add a deterministic seeded FWHT rotation in nest-format encoding (new helper, well under the 300-line cap) applied at build time in nest-python/build_fn.rs before quantization; (2) store the rotation seed + per-vector or per-section min/max interval in the int8 payload header (the format is additive: bump INT8_PAYLOAD_VERSION or add a new scale_kind, NO NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump, no new encoding id needed since it stays encoding=3); (3) at query time in nest-runtime, rotate the query with the same seeded FWHT, run the existing SIMD i8 dot kernel over mmap, then let the ALREADY-MANDATORY exact cosine rerank in search.rs (score_subset on ANN/hybrid candidates) recover full recall against unrotated f32 ground truth. This is pure additive change confined to one codec file plus a rotation helper, fully deterministic (seeded), offline, single-file. It directly improves the 'tiny' preset: same int8/4x footprint but recall jumps toward 0.99+ instead of degrading on outlier-heavy embeddings, and could let nest push toward sub-4x (with PQ next) without a server. PQ/BQ are the natural follow-on as new encoding ids (4-255 reserved range) for even smaller files.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. nest's north star is 'compress data more than everyone' while serving from mmap. RQ is a near-drop-in win: it makes the existing int8/4x path nearly lossless (99% recall@10) by adding only a deterministic O(D log D) rotation and a tiny header, and it keeps the SIMD-on-mmap hot path (rotation happens at build time on data, only the query is rotated at search time). PQ (compute lookup tables, store 8-bit codes per segment, ~8-16x) and BQ (1 bit/dim, 32x) chart nest's roadmap to far smaller files; both fit nest's mandatory-exact-rerank model because nest already always reranks ANN/hybrid candidates against true cosine, which is exactly the rescoring step these codecs require for accuracy.
repos.perf_notes: RQ rotation ~7us for 1536-dim (O(D log D) FWHT). Quantized int8 SIMD distance ~2.3x faster than f32; end-to-end 15-50% faster without rescore, 5-42% faster with rescore in high-recall ranges. 1M x 1536 OpenAI embeddings: 1465 MB (RQ) vs 5859 MB (f32) = 4x. BQ ~97% memory reduction (32x), PQ ~85% (split-segment codebook), SQ ~75%. All quantizers store uncompressed vectors alongside for rescoring (a tradeoff nest avoids since it keeps f32/canonical separately and reranks from them).
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause (weaviate/recipes repo); underlying Weaviate engine is BSD-3-Clause. Techniques (FWHT rotation, PQ, BQ, SQ) are public algorithms, not patented by Weaviate; safe to reimplement.

synthesis.summary: Across 18 RAG/agent/memory repos, almost none ship a compression codec or on-disk vector format worth vendoring directly (most delegate storage to Postgres/Qdrant/LanceDB/Weaviate and are pure orchestration Python). The genuinely transferable value clusters in three layers. (1) Embedding-codec frontier (Weaviate recipes, RAGFlow/Infinity, semtools, supermemory): Rotational Quantization (seeded Fast Walsh-Hadamard rotate -> int8) makes a 4x int8 codec near-lossless at ~99% recall; LVQ (mean-center then per-vector residual quant) lets the HNSW graph traverse on compressed codes so the full-f32 RAM snapshot disappears; PQ/BQ chart the path to 8-32x; Matryoshka (MRL) prefix truncation turns embedding dimensionality into a model-backed lossy knob that stacks multiplicatively with quantization and is what the hot SIMD loop actually reads. All four fit nest's existing mandatory exact-cosine rerank, which IS the rescoring step every one of these codecs requires. (2) Structural dedup / versioning data-model (langchain record-manager, langgraph version-keyed blobs, FalkorDB CSC matrices, neo4j lexical graph): content-hash dedup of repeated chunks+embeddings, append-only version maps that reference unchanged content-hashed blobs instead of recopying, and CSR/CSC integer adjacency overlays that add graph search and let you drop chunk-overlap text redundancy. These advance the 'compress whole repos/databases' north star structurally. (3) Zero-byte retrieval-quality wins (llama_index auto-merge hierarchy, langroid rank_to_periphery + RRF generalization, Verba/langroid window expansion, dify/neo4j weighted fusion): coarse context reconstructed from existing spans at ~9 bytes/edge with no parent text stored. nest is already AHEAD of every repo here on storage (it is the only one with f16/int8/zstd/mmap-SIMD and a true content_hash). The single biggest near-term steal is Rotational Quantization, a self-contained additive upgrade to crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs that keeps encoding=3 and needs no format-version bump.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The category's collective state of the art for a sovereign embedded engine is: (a) embeddings stored quantized but always paired with an exact rescoring pass over higher-precision vectors for the final-k candidates -- nest already enforces this as a format invariant (rerank_policy=exact, score_subset), which is stronger than most repos' ANN-proxy scores. (b) The best quantizers gaussianize or decorrelate before scalar quantization: Weaviate's Rotational Quantization (3-round blocked FWHT + sign flips, O(D log D), ~7us at 1536-dim) gives ~99% recall@10 at 4x where naive max-abs int8 (exactly nest's current int8.rs) degrades on outlier-heavy dims; Infinity's LVQ mean-centers then per-vector-scales the residual so NN ordering is preserved on the compressed codes, letting HNSW build/traverse without any full-precision copy. (c) Matryoshka embeddings make dimensionality a graceful lossy axis (3072->256 prefix + L2-renorm), enabling coarse(truncated)-to-fine(full) two-pass search that multiplies with quantization. (d) Structural dedup is treated as a first-class compressor: version-keyed content-addressed blobs (langgraph), content-hash record managers (langchain), and CSC sparse graph matrices (FalkorDB) store edit history and relationships by reference, not by copy. (e) Retrieval granularity is decoupled from storage granularity: only leaf chunks are embedded, coarse context is reconstructed on read from a tiny parent-child edge table or positional neighbor ids (llama_index AutoMerging, Verba/langroid windowing, neo4j NEXT_CHUNK), spending ~9 bytes/edge and zero embedding rows. (f) Offline static embedders (model2vec/POTION: per-token vector table + mean-pool, no matmul/GPU/network, byte-deterministic) make the embedding step itself sovereign and the model a few-MB int8+zstd table instead of multi-GB weights. Fusion has converged on RRF k=60 (which nest already has) with weighted-sum/linear-alpha as deterministic tunable alternatives.
top_innovations: Rotational Quantization (Weaviate): seeded Fast Walsh-Hadamard rotation gaussianizes the vector so one 8-bit interval fits all dims -> ~99% recall@10 at 4x, near-drop-in upgrade to nest's naive max-abs int8 codec, recall recovered by the already-mandatory exact rerank.

LVQ two-stage residual quant (Infinity/RAGFlow): subtract global corpus mean, per-vector scale the residual; HNSW builds and traverses on the int8 codes alone, eliminating nest's wasteful full-f32 `vectors: Vec<f32>` RAM snapshot in ann/mod.rs while preserving NN order.

Matryoshka (MRL) prefix truncation (supermemory): importance-ordered dims mean a 256-d prefix is just the first K contiguous floats already on disk; coarse(prefix)-to-fine(full) two-pass search stacks multiplicatively with int8 (~48x fewer bytes touched in pass 1) and maps exactly onto nest's ANN-then-exact-rerank contract.

Version-keyed content-addressed blob dedup (langgraph): store edit history by referencing unchanged content-hashed chunk/embedding blobs via a small version map instead of recopying -> structural cross-snapshot dedup, the core primitive for real-time edit + whole-repo ingestion without breaking the frozen single-file guarantee.

Content-hash record manager (langchain): per-chunk content_hash + source_id manifest enables skip-if-present dedup and incremental re-embed of only changed chunks; nest already computes content_hash so this is near-zero marginal cost and collapses repeated boilerplate (and its fp32 embeddings) to one physical copy referenced by many spans.

PQ / Binary Quantization (Weaviate recipes, semtools IVF-PQ): 8-16x (PQ, codebook + 1 byte/segment) and 32x (BQ, 1 bit/dim, Hamming MaxSim via popcnt/vcnt already in nest's SIMD dispatcher) compressors as new reserved encoding ids, both ranking-preserving under nest's exact rerank.

CSC/CSR typed sparse adjacency + lexical graph (FalkorDB, neo4j-graphrag): O(edges) integer overlay (src/dst u32 + edge_type u8, sorted, zstd-friendly) adds graph search and lets nest drop chunk-overlap text by reconstructing neighbor context from NEXT_CHUNK edges.

Auto-merge hierarchy (llama_index): parent-child edge table where parent text is reconstructed from children's existing chunks_original_spans -> multi-resolution retrieval at ~9 bytes/edge and zero extra text/embedding bytes.

model2vec/POTION static embedder (semtools): vocab x 256 token-vector table + mean-pool gives a byte-deterministic, GPU-free, network-free embedding backend; the table ships as int8+zstd, making nest's embedding step itself sovereign and reproducible.

rank_to_periphery + window expansion (langroid, Verba): pure-integer deterministic post-rerank reorder (anti lost-in-middle) and positional neighbor-chunk expansion from existing chunk_ids/spans -- zero-storage retrieval-quality wins on the returned chunk list.

nest_recommendations.idea: Upgrade the int8 codec to Rotational Quantization: add a seeded Fast Walsh-Hadamard rotation helper, apply it at build time before quantization, store the rotation seed (and per-section min/max interval) in the int8 payload header via a new scale_kind, rotate the query with the same seed at search time, then let the existing exact rerank recover recall.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs (new scale_kind=1 + rotation seed in the 8-byte prefix; bump INT8_PAYLOAD_VERSION, NOT NEST_FORMAT_VERSION, stays encoding=3); a new ~80-line fwht helper in nest-format/src/encoding/; query-side rotation in crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs validate_query/score paths; rerank already present via score_subset.
nest_recommendations.impact: Pushes the tiny preset's recall from degrading toward ~0.99 at the SAME 4x footprint; makes int8 the safe default and unlocks going below the 0.283 size ratio. Highest value-per-line in the whole category.

nest_recommendations.idea: Make the HNSW graph traverse on int8/LVQ codes and delete the full-f32 vectors snapshot. Store a single global f32 mean[dim] prefix + per-vector scale + i8 residual; build and search the graph using the existing dot_f32_i8 SIMD kernel instead of the f32 copy.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/ann/mod.rs (drop `vectors: Vec<f32>`), ann/build.rs + ann/search.rs (traverse on codes), and nest-runtime/src/materialize.rs (mean-centered decode); pairs with an int8_lvq variant in nest-format/src/encoding/int8.rs.
nest_recommendations.impact: Removes the ~n*dim*4 byte RAM snapshot the runtime currently holds beyond mmap (called out as a cost in ann/mod.rs), shrinking memory for the tiny/hybrid presets while recall stays intact via exact rerank.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an optional chunk_dedup manifest section: a sorted array of {content_hash -> source_id, original_span_ref} so a future `nest update`/`nest merge` re-embeds ONLY chunks whose hash is absent, copies embeddings/spans for unchanged hashes byte-for-byte from the old mmap, and collapses identical chunks across documents to one physical chunk+embedding referenced by many spans.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/ (new RESERVED section id 0x09, additive, own SHA-256 surface, sorted for byte-identical output); builder logic in crates/nest-python/src/build_fn.rs; new nest-cli subcommand.
nest_recommendations.impact: Cross-file content-hash dedup collapses repeated boilerplate AND its fp32 embeddings (the largest section) when packing whole repos/datasets -- the biggest structural compression lever for the north star; also enables incremental edit.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a Matryoshka-aware prefix layout to the embeddings section: record mrl_prefix_dims in the manifest extra map and, because importance-ordered dims are already contiguous on disk, run pass-1 SIMD scoring over the truncated K-dim prefix (L2-renormalized) to gather candidates, then reuse the mandatory exact-cosine rerank over full-dim vectors.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: manifest `extra` field in crates/nest-format/src/manifest/mod.rs (additive, no version bump); two-pass path in crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs alongside score_subset; store a per-prefix L2-renorm scale or renormalize at score time for honest cosine.
nest_recommendations.impact: Cuts hot-loop bytes-touched per candidate ~6-48x (e.g. 256-d int8 prefix vs 3072-d f32) improving BOTH size and throughput, stacking multiplicatively with int8/RQ; requires an MRL-trained model but is pure additive and deterministic.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a graph_edges section: a deterministic CSR/CSC adjacency over chunk_ids (src u32, dst u32, edge_type u8: 0=NEXT_CHUNK,1=FROM_DOCUMENT,2=ENTITY_LINK), sorted by (src,edge_type,dst), plus a bounded-BFS search-graph path that seeds from exact-cosine top-k, expands over edges, and re-runs exact cosine rerank on the expanded set.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/ (RESERVED section id 0x09+, own SHA-256); a ~150-line mmap graph::Adjacency reader + search-graph path in crates/nest-runtime/src/; 9th nest-cli subcommand; entity extraction stays python-side in nest-python.
nest_recommendations.impact: Adds the north-star 'graph search' pillar with an O(edges) integer overlay that is highly zstd-compressible, and lets nest drop chunk_overlap redundancy from chunks_canonical by recovering neighbor context from NEXT_CHUNK edges.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a chunk_hierarchy section (child_chunk_id u32 -> parent_chunk_id u32, level u8 + per-parent child-count) and a post-rerank auto-merge pass: count retrieved leaves per parent and, above a deterministic majority threshold, swap them for the parent before materialize resolves spans. Parent text is NOT stored -- it is reconstructed by concatenating children's chunks_original_spans.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/ (RESERVED 0x09+); auto-merge pass in crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs after rerank, before materialize_hits; hierarchical chunker in crates/nest-python.
nest_recommendations.impact: Multi-resolution retrieval at ~9 bytes/edge and zero extra text/embedding bytes; only leaf chunks get embedding rows so the hot mmap-scored section stays minimal. Pure recall-context-per-byte win.

nest_recommendations.idea: Generalize RRF to a rank-only sum over N>=2 lists with c exposed in search_contract, add a deterministic weighted-sum/linear-alpha fusion mode (final = w_vec*exact_cosine + w_kw*normalized_bm25, min-max normalized), and add a pure-integer rank_to_periphery final reorder (odds + reversed evens) plus positional window expansion from chunk_ids/spans.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/bm25/fusion.rs (generalize rrf_union, add weighted_sum_union); search_contract field in crates/nest-format/src/sections/contract.rs; rank_to_periphery + window expansion in crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs / materialize (reads existing FROZEN sections only).
nest_recommendations.impact: Zero added bytes, all deterministic and panic-free, well under the 300-line cap; improves downstream LLM answer quality and lets a future third (fuzzy/CJK) signal drop into the hybrid path without touching the codec.

nest_recommendations.idea: Vendor a model2vec/POTION-style static embedder as an offline, deterministic, zero-dependency embedding backend in nest-python: a potion token-vector table (vocab x 256, shipped int8+zstd) where embedding = tokenize + gather + mean-pool, and provenance.model_hash becomes the table's SHA-256.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-python (or a tiny nest-runtime helper module under the 300-line cap); table can ship as a separate nest-encoded asset; wires into the existing model_hash/model_fingerprint provenance fields.
nest_recommendations.impact: Makes the embedding step itself sovereign and byte-reproducible (no PyTorch/GPU/network), replacing a multi-GB neural model with a few-MB lookup table -- directly serves the offline/deterministic mission and shrinks the toolchain footprint. Caveat: CJK/Thai tokenization quality depends on the underlying sentencepiece.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a deterministic on-disk embedding cache in the nest-python builder keyed by SHA-256(canonical_chunk_text) prefixed by model_fingerprint namespace, so rebuilds and cross-corpus dedup never re-embed identical text and aggressive re-encoding experiments (int8/RQ/PQ) become cheap to iterate.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-python/src/build_fn.rs (a sidecar cache, NOT in the frozen container); reuses provenance model_hash as the namespace.
nest_recommendations.impact: Build-time/operational only (saves recompute, not bytes), but it is what makes the whole quantization-codec roadmap above cheap to A/B; preserves byte-identical output since cache hits return the same f32 vectors.

nest_recommendations.idea: Roadmap PQ and Binary Quantization as new reserved embedding encoding ids (4-255 range): PQ = split D into segments, 256-centroid seeded k-means codebook per segment, 1 byte/segment with ADC lookup tables (~8-16x); BQ = 1 bit/dim sign, Hamming prefilter via popcnt(x86)/vcnt(NEON) already in the SIMD dispatcher, then exact rerank (~32x).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/encoding/ (new pq.rs / bq.rs, new SECTION_ENCODING_* ids 4 and 5, additive within v1); SIMD Hamming kernel in crates/nest-runtime/src/simd/; both gated behind nest's existing mandatory exact rerank.
nest_recommendations.impact: Charts the path well past the tiny preset's 0.283 ratio toward 8-32x embedding compression while keeping real-cosine ground truth -- the deepest compression lever for 'compress more than everyone'.

compression_wins: Rotational Quantization makes the existing int8/4x path near-lossless (~99% recall@10) by adding only a deterministic O(D log D) FWHT rotation + a few header bytes -- same footprint, far better recall, so int8 becomes the default and the 0.283 tiny ratio can drop further.
LVQ lets the HNSW graph traverse on int8 codes, deleting the runtime's full-f32 `vectors: Vec<f32>` snapshot (n*dim*4 bytes of RAM beyond mmap) at equal recall.

PQ (~8-16x) and BQ (~32x, 1 bit/dim, ranking-preserving via Hamming MaxSim) as new reserved encoding ids push the embeddings section -- nest's largest and the only never-zstd'd section -- far below int8, all safe under the mandatory exact rerank.

Matryoshka prefix truncation (3072->256 ~12x) stacks multiplicatively with int8/RQ (4x) and BQ, and the smaller prefix is what the hot SIMD loop actually reads, improving size AND throughput simultaneously.

Content-hash dedup collapses repeated/boilerplate chunks AND their fp32 embeddings to one physical copy referenced by many spans -- the biggest structural lever when packing whole repos/datasets/databases into one container.

Version-keyed content-addressed blob dedup stores edit/version history by referencing unchanged hashed blobs instead of recopying, so a new corpus version is mostly free; composes with zstd/int8 by deduping before encoding the delta.
CSC/CSR sparse adjacency stores a whole relationship graph in O(edges) (monotone indices arrays, delta+varint+zstd friendly) instead of O(nodes^2) edge-list-of-strings, carrying graphs in kilobytes.

Hierarchy/lexical-graph edge tables (~9 bytes/edge) plus NEXT_CHUNK neighbor reconstruction let nest drop chunk_overlap text from chunks_canonical and rebuild context on read -- multi-resolution retrieval for near-zero extra bytes.
Structure-aware and semantic chunkers (markdown/code/json/AST boundaries) produce more self-similar, boundary-aligned chunks_canonical that zstd compresses better and reduce span fragmentation.

MegaParse-style canonicalize-before-hash (normalize PDF/DOCX/parquet to deterministic markdown before chunking) exposes far more cross-document redundancy for zstd and strengthens the content_hash stability guarantee -- a precondition for compressing heterogeneous formats at all.
watch_outs: REJECT the loopback-NFSv3 path in smfs and Weaviate/Verba's semantic answer cache -- both bind a socket / need online state and would violate nest's offline-by-construction, no-socket guarantee. A read-only FUSE mount in a SEPARATE nest-fuse crate (kept out of nest-runtime) is acceptable since FUSE opens no network socket.

REJECT every network/GPU dependency: MegaParse vision-LLM table reconstruction, Cohere/Jina rerankers, OpenAI/gpt-4o calls, hosted Supermemory, FalkorDB/Redis engine. Only the ALGORITHMS (budget trimming, chunk indexing, fusion math, CSC traversal) are stealable, never the runtimes.

Do NOT vendor SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS (heavy C dep, threading) or FalkorDB engine (SSPL-licensed, not vendorable) -- a minimal pure-Rust CSC matvec (tens of lines) covers k-hop traversal without the dependency. Skip its MVCC/mpsc machinery entirely; nest is frozen read-only single-process mmap.

Adopt langgraph's CWE-502 lesson as a hard rule: nest must NEVER deserialize arbitrary types from a container. Keep fixed section decoders + typed thiserror only; any new section (dedup/graph/hierarchy/tensor) must be a strict repr(C) LE decoder, never a constructor-style deserializer.

All new codecs (RQ rotation, LVQ mean, PQ k-means, BQ) MUST be seeded/deterministic so same input => byte-identical file. PQ/RQ k-means and any sampling must use a seeded RNG like the existing seeded HNSW; otherwise the reproducible-build contract breaks.

Matryoshka requires an MRL-trained model AND per-prefix L2-renormalization of the truncated slice -- skipping the renorm silently corrupts cosine. Bake renorm into the writer or materialize path; do not ship MRL search without it.

Keep additive-only discipline: new sections must use reserved ids 0x09+, new encodings ids 4-255, and must NOT enter content_hash (optional sections are excluded by design so citations stay stable). Only bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION for a true v2 where an existing field changes meaning; codec changes use payload-version bumps like INT8_PAYLOAD_VERSION.

Respect the file-hygiene cap: every new module (fwht, pq, bq, graph adjacency, hierarchy, fusion variants) must stay <=300 lines (333 hard cap), single-responsibility -- split codec/reader/search as the existing ann/ and bm25/ modules do.

model2vec/jieba/tree-sitter tokenizers carry large dictionaries or model files -- pick a small-footprint, offline, deterministic segmenter or the sovereign/reproducible guarantee and the tiny-footprint mission regress. The known CJK/Thai BM25 gap is real but must be fixed without a multi-MB dictionary download.

NEVER general-compress (zstd/lz4) the embeddings section -- it is scored directly from mmap on the hot path; this is the opposite of Jina/DocArray's outer-codec approach and is a core nest invariant. Embedding size reduction must come from quantization/dim-reduction (RQ/PQ/BQ/MRL), never entropy coding of the live dense bytes.

Build-time embedding cache and any incremental-edit staging must live in a sidecar / nest-python, NOT mutate the frozen container in place; flush edits via a deterministic rebuild so byte-identical reproducibility holds.

categories.name: data-pipeline
categories.focus: ML data lakes, dataset tooling, embedding benchmarks

repos.one_liner: Deep Lake is a columnar "tensor storage format" data lake that stores ML data as chunked, natively-compressed arrays and keeps a separate, run-length-encoded triplet of index maps (ChunkIdEncoder, BytePositionsEncoder, ShapeEncoder) mapping each sample index to its chunk, byte range, and shape without loading the bulk payload.
repos.core_innovation: Sidecar index maps are stored as 2D integer arrays of "runs" where each row holds a value plus the CUMULATIVE last-sample-index that run covers; consecutive identical values (same chunk, same shape, same per-sample byte size) collapse into a single row, and lookups are a binary search over the cumulative-index column. This run-length + cumulative-prefix-index hybrid makes per-sample sidecar metadata grow only when a value actually changes (a fixed-shape tensor of 1B samples needs one shape row; ~150MB chunk-id encoder per 1PB), while staying O(log n) random-addressable.
key_techniques: Run-length + cumulative-index encoders: rows = (value, last_index_covered); identical consecutive samples collapse to one row
Binary search over the cumulative last-index column for O(log n) sample->location lookup
Triplet split of sidecar metadata: ChunkIdEncoder (sample->chunk), BytePositionsEncoder (per-sample byte size, offsets derived by prefix sum), ShapeEncoder (sample shape)
Metadata fully separated from bulk data so shape/offset queries never decode payload chunks
Native sample-level compression: store jpeg/png/mp4 bytes verbatim, copy-without-recode when raw codec matches tensor codec
Chunk-size bounds (lower/upper) packing variable-length samples into ~8MB chunks instead of static per-sample chunking
Tiling: samples larger than a chunk split across multiple chunks via a tile encoder
TQL + optimized hnswlib HNSW with exact linear-scan fallback under ~100k rows
repos.nest_application: Adopt the run-length + cumulative-index encoder in nest-format for the chunks_original_spans (0x03) section and optionally chunk_ids (0x01). Today crates/nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs writes the full source_uri string plus two raw u64 (byte_start, byte_end) for EVERY chunk; when 5k chunks come from one document this is ~5k repeated URIs and ~80KB of offsets that are almost always contiguous (end[i]==start[i+1]). Replace with: (a) a deduplicated source_uri dictionary plus a per-chunk uri_id run-length encoded (one run per source document), and (b) delta/cumulative encoding of spans where contiguous chunks store only a run-length plus per-chunk length, reconstructing absolute offsets by prefix sum exactly like BytePositionsEncoder. This is an internal encoding of a non-embedding (cold-path) section, so it is zstd-eligible and never touches the SIMD scoring hot path. It fits the frozen v1 format as a NEW encoding id in the reserved 4-255 range (or a transparent re-encode within the existing section that decodes identically) with no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump. content_hash stays stable because it hashes DECODED canonical sections, and determinism holds via an insertion-stable dictionary. It shrinks provenance/spans metadata that currently scales O(num_chunks) with redundant strings, directly serving the compress-more-than-everyone north star.
repos.compression_relevance: High. nest's metadata sections (spans, chunk_ids, provenance) currently scale O(num_chunks) with verbatim repeated source URIs and raw 8-byte offsets. The run-length + cumulative-index scheme collapses these to O(num_distinct_runs), often near-constant for single-document corpora, removing structural redundancy that zstd alone leaves on the table (entropy coding shrinks bytes but not the inherent redundancy of contiguous 64-bit offsets, which is better eliminated before compression). It targets exactly the non-embedding part of the .nest file, complementing int8/f16 embedding quantization.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (re-implement the idea from the CIDR 2023 paper rather than vendoring code; the encoder concept is freely transferable)
repos.perf_notes: Encoders are tiny: ~150MB ChunkIdEncoder per 1PB tensor; a fixed-shape tensor needs a single ShapeEncoder row. Lookups are O(log n) binary search over the cumulative column using only integer ops, with no payload decompression, so they stay off any SIMD hot path. For nest the span/uri encoder is read once during materialize/cite (not during scoring), so binary-search cost is irrelevant to query latency; the win is on-disk size plus faster section parse (fewer length-prefixed strings). Deep Lake's hnswlib HNSW handles ~35M embeddings in <1s with exact linear scan under ~100k rows, mirroring nest's mandatory-exact-rerank philosophy.

repos.one_liner: A multiprocess/multithreaded downloader that turns billion-scale image-URL lists into sharded WebDataset tar files paired 1:1 with lightweight columnar parquet sidecars and order-aligned embedding .npy arrays, all addressed by a deterministic positional composite key.
repos.core_innovation: The "shadow sidecar" split: heavy opaque payload (jpg bytes in tar) is stored separately from a parallel lightweight columnar metadata file (parquet) that mirrors it 1:1, so all filtering, statistics, and validation happen against the small columnar file without ever touching the heavy payload, while a deterministic positional composite key (SSSSSIIII = 5-digit shard id + 4-digit in-shard index) preserves exact order alignment across every parallel artifact (tar payload, parquet metadata, npy embeddings) and makes builds resumable.
key_techniques: composite positional key SSSSSIIII: zero-padded shard-id prefix + in-shard index, encoding both location and order in a sortable integer string
1:1 ordered alignment invariant: input urls -> tar payload -> parquet metadata -> npy embeddings all in identical sample order, addressable by offset
shadow columnar sidecar (parquet) mirrors heavy tar so stats/filtering run without decoding payloads (41455 tars <-> 41455 parquets, ~1.6MB vs ~270MB)
WebDataset key convention: files sharing a basename before the first dot form one logical sample; extension selects type (.jpg/.txt/.json)
incremental/resumable builds keyed on shard completion (incremental | overwrite | extend), retry up to max_shard_retry
multi-tier hash integrity: optional md5/sha256/sha512 per sample, verify_hash drops mismatches vs externally-supplied checksums
sequential-I/O-first tar packaging: 3-10x over random access, collapses millions of file handles to single digits
post-hoc small-file consolidation: pyspark compacts hundreds of thousands of parquet shards into ~32 large files
repos.nest_application: Three concrete steals. (1) nest-format: formalize the "shadow columnar sidecar" inside the single .nest container. Today provenance + search_contract carry coarse metadata; add an optional additive section (reserved id 0x09+, never bump v1) holding a compact columnar SoA of per-chunk filterable scalars (source_id, lang, byte_len, token_count, dataset tag) so nest-cli stats/filtered-search and nest-runtime can pre-filter candidate chunks WITHOUT decoding chunks_canonical text or touching embeddings on the hot path -- a pure metadata scan, mirroring parquet-without-tar. The scalar columns are tiny, delta/zstd-friendly (zstd already allowed on non-embedding sections), and let search skip-list before SIMD scoring. (2) nest-format hashing/layout: adopt the 1:1 ordered-alignment invariant explicitly as a frozen guarantee -- chunk_ids[i], chunks_canonical[i], chunks_original_spans[i], embeddings[i] and any new scalar column[i] all share index i, so nest://content_hash/chunk_id resolves to one offset across every section; this is the on-disk analog of tar<->parquet<->npy alignment and strengthens the deterministic contract. (3) nest-cli: borrow the composite positional key idea for chunk_ids -- a deterministic sortable key (source-shard prefix + monotone index) makes builds reproducible and enables future incremental/extend rebuilds (append new chunks as a new logical shard range) without rewriting prior sections, aligning with the additive-only rule. The downloader/distributed/fsspec machinery is out of scope (nest is offline-by-construction, never opens a socket); only the on-disk layout discipline transfers.
repos.compression_relevance: Medium-high but indirect. img2dataset is a downloader, not a codec, so it offers no entropy coder or quantization scheme to beat. The transferable compression lever is the shadow-sidecar layout: separating tiny filterable scalar columns from the heavy text/embedding payload lets nest (a) zstd-compress the scalar columns extremely well via columnar SoA + delta coding (homogeneous columns compress far better than row-interleaved metadata), and (b) prune candidates before scoring so less of the file is touched on the hot path. It reinforces nest's existing principle that embeddings stay raw/mmap-scored while everything else is squeezed.
repos.perf_notes: Reference numbers: ~1350 images/s/machine (~116M/24h) via K=10000 shards, N=cpu-count processes, M threads each, one tar per process to avoid disk contention. Parquet sidecar in LAION-400M is ~1.6MB vs ~270MB tar (>150x smaller) -- the quantitative case for metadata-only scans. Sequential tar I/O is cited at 3-10x faster than random access on local drives. None of this involves SIMD or a custom codec; it is process/thread orchestration plus I/O layout. For nest the takeaway is purely architectural: keep the scored array contiguous and order-aligned, keep filterable metadata in a separate tiny columnar block.
repos.license: MIT

repos.one_liner: MTEB is a Python embedding/retrieval evaluation harness that standardizes datasets (corpus/queries/relevant_docs/top_ranked), runs chunked top-k similarity search over multiple metrics, scores with pytrec_eval (nDCG@k, MRR@k, Recall@k, MAP), and persists results as content-addressed per-(model,revision,task) JSON in a tiered remote/disk/in-memory cache.
repos.core_innovation: A standardized, reproducible retrieval-quality measurement protocol: a fixed task schema (corpus, queries, relevant_docs as query_id->corpus_id->relevance, top_ranked candidate lists) feeding a chunked exact top-k search that computes cosine/dot/euclidean and reports the best, scored by an established trec_eval metric set (nDCG@k, MRR@k, Recall@k, capped recall), with results stored under deterministic content-keyed paths so an identical (model, revision, task) never recomputes.
key_techniques: RetrievalEvaluator: chunked exact top-k via corpus_chunk_size, sub-batch similarity matmul, per-query (corpus_id, score) collected then descending sort, avoiding O(N) memory blowup
Multi-metric scoring: compute cosine, dot, and euclidean and report the best; cosine = inner product on L2-normalized vectors
pytrec_eval (trec_eval bindings) for nDCG@k / MRR@k / Recall@k / MAP, plus custom recall_cap (cap by #relevant) and calculate_pmrr (MRR delta under instruction change)
BEIR-derived task schema: dataset[subset][split] = {corpus, queries, relevant_docs: qid->cid->rel, top_ranked: qid->[cid]}
Content-addressed result cache: composite key = hash(benchmark name + language tuple); layout results/{model_path}/{revision}/{task}.json with experiments/{name}/ subtree
TaskResult validation on load: required-split checks (test/train) reject stale cache that no longer matches task requirements
SearchProtocol index()/search() interface accepting encode_kwargs so custom indexes (e.g. PLAID) plug into the same eval loop
Tiered cache: HuggingFace Hub remote -> local filesystem JSON -> in-memory object cache, rooted at MTEB_CACHE / ~/.cache/mteb
repos.nest_application: Three steals. (1) nest-cli benchmark subcommand: adopt MTEB's retrieval-task schema (corpus/queries/relevant_docs/top_ranked) and pytrec_eval-equivalent metrics (nDCG@k, MRR@k, Recall@k) as a deterministic Rust quality harness over a .nest file, turning today's anecdotal 'tiny preset recall@10 0.992' into a reproducible seeded per-preset report; pure compute, no socket, fits offline/deterministic constraints and the <=300-line single-responsibility rule (one metrics module per metric). (2) nest-runtime search path: MTEB's chunked exact top-k (corpus_chunk_size sub-batches, descending sort) mirrors nest's mandatory exact-cosine rerank; formalize a corpus_chunk_size loop in the SIMD dispatcher so the exact rerank streams over mmap'd embedding sub-blocks (bounded working set, cache-friendly) rather than one big pass, hardening the search_contract guarantee. (3) nest-format: an optional additive eval-results section (reserved id 0x09+) recording metric scores lets a .nest container self-certify its recall vs the exact f32 baseline without re-running; nest's existing content_hash already delivers MTEB-style 'same inputs never recompute' for free.
repos.compression_relevance: Low-to-indirect. MTEB has no entropy coder, quantization codec, or on-disk compression to steal; it stores results as plain JSON. Its value to nest's compress-more-than-everyone goal is as a rigorous quality yardstick: it lets nest prove that aggressive compression (int8, f16, hnsw in the tiny preset) preserves retrieval recall (nDCG@k/Recall@k vs the exact f32 baseline), so compression can be pushed harder with measured, non-regressing quality rather than guesswork.
repos.license: Apache-2.0
repos.perf_notes: RetrievalEvaluator's corpus_chunk_size keeps the similarity matmul working set bounded so corpora larger than RAM are scored in sub-batches; cosine is implemented as inner product on L2-normalized vectors (one normalization, then BLAS/SIMD dot), matching nest's mmap SIMD dot kernels (AVX2/NEON/scalar). Scoring throughput is dominated by pytrec_eval (C trec_eval), not Python. MTEB itself ships no SIMD or quantization; it relies on the model and FAISS/numpy for heavy linear algebra.

synthesis.summary: Three reference systems define the state of the art for ML data-lake / dataset tooling, and their transferable value to nest is almost entirely architectural and metadata-layout, not codec: nest already wins on the embedding hot path (mmap SIMD dot, int8/f16 quantization, mandatory exact rerank). Deep Lake (Apache-2.0) is the highest-value steal: its run-length + cumulative-prefix-index encoders (ChunkIdEncoder/BytePositionsEncoder/ShapeEncoder) collapse per-sample sidecar metadata to O(distinct-runs) with O(log n) random access and no payload decode. This maps directly onto nest's cold-path metadata problem: crates/nest-format/src/sections/spans.rs today writes a full source_uri string plus two raw little-endian u64 per chunk for every chunk, so a 5k-chunk single-document corpus stores ~5k repeated URIs and ~80KB of offsets that are almost always contiguous (end[i]==start[i+1]) — structural redundancy zstd only partially removes. img2dataset (MIT) contributes the "shadow columnar sidecar" idea (tiny filterable SoA scalar columns separated from heavy payload, scanned without decoding the bulk) and the explicit 1:1 positional-alignment invariant; both fit nest's single-file model as a new additive section (reserved id 0x09+) plus a hardened frozen guarantee. MTEB (Apache-2.0) contributes a rigorous retrieval-quality protocol (nDCG@k / MRR@k / Recall@k via a trec_eval-equivalent metric set, content-addressed result caching, chunked exact top-k) that turns nest's anecdotal "tiny preset recall@10 0.992" into a reproducible, seeded, per-preset quality report and lets nest push compression harder with measured non-regression. None of the three offers a new entropy coder or quantizer to beat nest's embedding stack; the wins are structural-redundancy elimination in metadata, candidate pre-filtering before SIMD scoring, and a quality yardstick. All three respect nest's offline/deterministic/single-file constraints if the network/distributed machinery is dropped (img2dataset's downloader, MTEB's HF Hub cache tier) and re-implemented in-crate from the published ideas rather than vendored.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The data-pipeline category converges on one dominant pattern: separate heavy opaque payload from tiny structured metadata, and make per-sample metadata grow with information content (distinct runs) rather than with sample count. Deep Lake formalizes this with run-length + cumulative-last-index encoders: each sidecar row is (value, cumulative_last_sample_index_covered); consecutive identical values (same chunk, same shape, same per-sample byte size) collapse to one row, and lookup is a binary search over the cumulative column — so a fixed-shape 1B-sample tensor needs ONE shape row and ~150MB of chunk-id encoder per 1PB, all addressable in O(log n) integer ops with zero payload decompression. It splits sidecar metadata into a triplet (ChunkIdEncoder: sample->chunk, BytePositionsEncoder: per-sample byte size with offsets recovered by prefix sum, ShapeEncoder: sample shape), stores codec bytes verbatim (copy-without-recode when codecs match), packs variable-length samples into ~8MB bounded chunks, tiles oversized samples, and serves vectors with hnswlib HNSW that exact-linear-scans under ~100k rows — the same mandatory-exact philosophy nest enforces. img2dataset operationalizes the split as a "shadow sidecar": a parquet metadata file mirrors the heavy WebDataset tar 1:1 (~1.6MB vs ~270MB tar in LAION-400M, >150x smaller), so all filtering/stats/validation run on the small columnar file without touching payload, while a deterministic positional composite key (SSSSSIIII = shard-id prefix + in-shard index) preserves exact order alignment across tar/parquet/npy and makes builds resumable; multi-tier optional hashing (md5/sha256/sha512) verifies samples. MTEB defines the quality-measurement state of the art: a fixed BEIR-derived task schema (corpus, queries, relevant_docs as qid->cid->rel, top_ranked candidate lists), chunked exact top-k similarity (corpus_chunk_size sub-batches keep the matmul working set bounded so corpora larger than RAM still score), cosine implemented as inner product on L2-normalized vectors, scoring via pytrec_eval (nDCG@k, MRR@k, Recall@k, MAP, capped recall), and content-addressed per-(model,revision,task) JSON results in a tiered HF-Hub/disk/in-memory cache so identical inputs never recompute. The unifying lesson for nest: the scored array stays contiguous, raw, and order-aligned; everything else is small, columnar, structurally de-redundant, and quality-certified.
top_innovations: Deep Lake run-length + cumulative-prefix-index encoder: rows of (value, cumulative_last_index_covered), identical consecutive samples collapse to one row, O(log n) binary-search lookup with zero payload decode — eliminates structural redundancy in per-chunk metadata that zstd alone leaves on the table.

Triplet split of sidecar metadata (chunk-id / byte-positions / shape) with offsets recovered by prefix sum rather than stored verbatim — directly maps to nest spans where contiguous chunks satisfy end[i]==start[i+1] and need only a per-chunk length plus run boundaries.

img2dataset shadow columnar sidecar: tiny filterable SoA scalar columns (source_id, lang, byte_len, token_count, tag) stored apart from heavy payload, scanned to pre-filter candidates WITHOUT decoding text or touching embeddings (>150x size gap demonstrated).

Deduplicated value dictionary + run-length id stream for repeated strings (source_uri) — one run per source document instead of one verbatim string per chunk; insertion-stable dictionary keeps it deterministic.

Explicit 1:1 positional-alignment invariant across all parallel artifacts addressable by index i — nest's on-disk analog hardens the chunk_ids[i]/canonical[i]/spans[i]/embeddings[i] contract that nest://content_hash/chunk_id already relies on.

MTEB reproducible retrieval-quality protocol: nDCG@k / MRR@k / Recall@k via trec_eval-equivalent scoring over a fixed task schema, turning anecdotal recall claims into seeded per-preset reports that justify pushing compression harder.

MTEB chunked exact top-k (corpus_chunk_size sub-batches, descending sort, bounded working set) — formalizes nest's exact rerank as a cache-friendly streaming pass over mmap'd embedding sub-blocks for corpora larger than cache.
Content-addressed 'same inputs never recompute' result caching — nest's content_hash already delivers this for free; can self-certify recall inside the container.
Deep Lake native copy-without-recode (store codec bytes verbatim when codecs match) — principle for future nest payload types (pdf/audio/video) to avoid lossy re-encode round-trips.

img2dataset composite positional key (sortable shard-prefix + monotone index) enabling append-only incremental/extend rebuilds as new logical shard ranges without rewriting prior sections — aligns with nest's additive-only rule.

Add a new section-encoding id (e.g. SECTION_ENCODING_SPANS_RLE = 4, within the reserved 4-255 range) so decode_payload dispatches to the new codec and decodes byte-identically to the current OriginalSpan vec.
