nest_recommendations.idea: Stream the exact-cosine rerank over mmap'd embedding sub-blocks using an MTEB-style corpus_chunk_size loop so the working set stays cache-resident on corpora larger than L2/L3, instead of one monolithic pass over all rows in score_all. Pure perf/locality refactor; results are byte-identical so determinism and the exact-rerank guarantee are untouched.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs score_all (and score_subset for large unions), keeping the SIMD dispatcher in crates/nest-runtime/src/simd unchanged.
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

nest_recommendations.idea: Optionally embed an additive eval-results section (reserve a later 0x09+ id) recording per-preset nDCG@k/Recall@k vs the exact f32 baseline, so a .nest container self-certifies its retrieval quality without re-running the harness; nest's content_hash already gives MTEB-style 'same inputs never recompute' so the section is a cache of a deterministic computation.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/layout/mod.rs (OPTIONAL_SECTIONS), new crates/nest-format/src/sections/eval_results.rs, populated by the nest-cli benchmark harness.
nest_recommendations.impact: low

compression_wins: spans (0x03) dictionary+RLE: collapse ~5k verbatim source_uri strings to one dictionary entry per distinct document plus a run-length id stream — for single-document corpora this is near-constant instead of O(num_chunks), eliminating redundancy zstd only partially removes.

spans offset delta/prefix-sum: contiguous chunks satisfy end[i]==start[i+1], so store one run-length plus per-chunk length and recover absolute u64 offsets by prefix sum, replacing ~16 bytes of raw little-endian u64 per chunk (~80KB at 5k chunks) with a handful of bytes per run; the delta stream is also far more zstd-compressible than raw 64-bit offsets.

Eliminate structural redundancy BEFORE the entropy coder: zstd shrinks bytes but cannot remove the inherent redundancy of contiguous 64-bit offsets and repeated strings; doing dictionary+RLE first then zstd compounds the two, which is the core compress-more-than-everyone lever on the cold path.

Columnar SoA chunk_scalars section: homogeneous single-type columns (lang, byte_len, token_count) compress dramatically better under zstd than today's row-interleaved metadata, and delta-coding monotone columns shrinks them further.
Provenance dedup: one entry per distinct source instead of repeated dataset-level fields across every chunk reduces provenance from O(num_chunks) toward O(num_sources).

MTEB-style measured non-regression unlocks more aggressive embedding compression: with reproducible nDCG@k/Recall@k vs f32, nest can justify pushing int8 / smaller dims / tighter hnsw in the tiny preset (already 0.283 size ratio, recall@10 0.992) with proof rather than guesswork — quality measurement is itself a compression enabler.

All of the above target ONLY non-embedding cold-path sections (zstd-eligible, never the SIMD hot path) and are read once during materialize/cite, so they add zero query-latency cost while shrinking the file.
watch_outs: Do NOT vendor code: Deep Lake and MTEB are Apache-2.0, img2dataset MIT — re-implement the run-length/cumulative-index and metric ideas from the published descriptions (Deep Lake CIDR 2023 paper) in-crate; the encoder/metric concepts are freely transferable but copying source pulls in license/attribution and bloat that conflict with the small clean-core goal.

Frozen-format discipline: any spans re-encoding must decode byte-identically to the current OriginalSpan representation so content_hash (over DECODED canonical sections) stays stable and citations keep resolving; use a new encoding id in the reserved 4-255 range or a transparent in-section re-encode, and never bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION (that is reserved for a true v2 where an existing field changes meaning).

Determinism: the source_uri dictionary must be insertion-stable (not hash-ordered) and RLE runs must form deterministically, or byte-identical reproducibility (same chunks + same model fingerprint => identical file) breaks; mirror the existing alphabetical-bm25 / seeded-hnsw discipline.

Drop all network/distributed machinery: img2dataset's downloader/fsspec/pyspark and MTEB's HuggingFace-Hub remote cache tier violate offline-by-construction (runtime never opens a socket) — only the on-disk layout, positional-key, and metric ideas transfer; keep MTEB's tiered cache to local-filesystem + in-memory only.

Line/scope cap: each new piece (spans codec, chunk_scalars section, each metric) must be its own <=300-line single-responsibility module (333 hard cap); resist a monolithic 'metadata-v2' module — factor the shared dictionary helper into sections/codec.rs.

Embeddings stay raw and mmap-scored: none of these ideas may touch the embeddings section encoding or the SIMD scoring path; Deep Lake's chunk-packing/tiling is for variable-shape tensors and must not fragment nest's contiguous, 64-byte-aligned, directly-scored embedding array.

Pre-filter must not weaken the exact-rerank guarantee: a chunk_scalars candidate filter changes WHICH chunks are scored, not HOW they are scored, and must be opt-in and documented so it never silently degrades the recall=1.0 exact ground truth the search_contract promises.

Additive-only for any new section: chunk_scalars / eval_results must be OPTIONAL sections (id 0x09+) that do not participate in content_hash, so adding them to an existing corpus does not invalidate prior citations; gate them behind a manifest capability flag.

bm25 tokenizer is still word-segmented (degrades on CJK/Thai) — a known gap unrelated to these steals; do not let a metadata-quality harness mask that the lexical path needs separate attention for the PT-BR/CJK demo corpora.

MTEB metrics depend on relevance judgments (relevant_docs); nest's demo corpus has none yet, so the quality harness needs a seeded synthetic or hand-labeled qrels set to be meaningful — budget for building that, or the nDCG/MRR numbers are vacuous.

categories.name: content-addressed
categories.focus: content-addressed, reproducible, and distributed storage

repos.one_liner: Kubo is the reference Go implementation of IPFS: a content-addressed distributed store that chunks files, wraps them in a UnixFS Merkle DAG of hash-linked blocks (each block addressed by a CID = multibase + multicodec + multihash), and deduplicates at the block level via a multihash-indexed blockstore.
repos.core_innovation: Content-defined chunking (CDC): block boundaries are chosen by a rolling hash over the byte stream (boundary when the top/low N bits of the fingerprint hit a target value), NOT at fixed offsets. This makes chunk boundaries content-aligned, so a local edit only perturbs the one or two chunks it touches instead of re-flowing every downstream boundary, yielding stable hashes and high cross-version deduplication. Pair this with a content address (multihash) that indexes storage independently of the on-disk encoding/wrapper, so identical content collapses to one stored block regardless of how it was transported.
key_techniques: Rabin fingerprint CDC: 64-byte rolling polynomial window, boundary when low bits == target; Kubo exposes rabin-[min]-[avg]-[max]
Buzhash CDC: cyclic-polynomial rolling hash (left-rotate + xor over window), ~3x faster than Rabin, judge on top bits
Gear/FastCDC family: single left-shift+add rolling hash, zero-padded mask to widen effective window, cut-point skipping below min-size, normalized chunking for tight size distribution, ~1350 MB/s
CID = multibase + cidv1 + multicodec(0x55 raw / 0x70 dag-pb / 0x71 dag-cbor) + multihash(0x12 sha2-256,len,digest); multihash alone indexes the blockstore
UnixFS Merkle DAG with selectable layout: balanced (fast random seek) vs trickle (append-optimized); high fanout enables parallel/partial fetch and incremental verification
raw-leaves: leaf blocks stored as raw bytes (codec 0x55) with no protobuf wrapper, so block multihash equals plain content hash
HAMT (hash array mapped trie) sharding for large directories/maps via max-hamt-fanout
block-level dedup in the blockstore: same-content chunks across files/versions store once, keyed by multihash
repos.nest_application: Add a content-defined chunker to nest-python's build pipeline (the stage producing chunk_ids/chunks_canonical) as an alternative to current token/sentence segmentation, used for large blob inputs (pdf/json/parquet/datasets/whole repos on the roadmap). Implement a small deterministic Gear/FastCDC kernel in nest-format under a new encoding-neutral chunking module (rolling hash + seeded mask, seeded determinism to satisfy the deterministic-build constraint, <=300 loc, typed thiserror errors, repr(C) little-endian if any state is serialized). This unlocks edit-local rechunking for nest's promised real-time edit: editing one paragraph re-emits only the touched chunk(s), so embeddings + chunks_canonical for unchanged chunks stay byte-identical and the file diff stays tiny. Second, formalize a block-level dedup pass in nest-format writer: hash each canonical chunk (already done via content_hash machinery) and store duplicate chunks once, with chunk_ids referencing the shared physical block. Third, nest's content_hash (STABLE across encodings) and nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation already mirror Kubo's multihash-indexes-storage / encoding-is-a-wrapper split; cite as prior-art validation and consider chunk-level addressing so a citation resolves a single deduped block.
repos.compression_relevance: Directly central. CDC + block dedup is the single biggest lever for 'compress more than everyone' on repetitive/edited corpora: it removes redundancy ACROSS chunks and versions before any entropy coder (zstd) runs, which nest currently does not do (it chunks by tokens/sentences and zstd-compresses sections independently). Edit-local boundaries also make incremental/append builds cheap, supporting real-time-edit and 'whole databases/repos' goals. Applies to non-embedding sections (canonical text, original spans, future binary blob sections) since embeddings are intentionally never compressed; the win is on text/json/span and blob payloads with zero recall cost.
repos.perf_notes: Gear/FastCDC reaches ~1350 MB/s single-thread (Rust gearhash/fastcdc crates), ~3x Rabin; rolling hash is a left-shift+add per byte (or 2 bytes/step in FastCDC), branch-predictor and SIMD friendly, fits nest's scalar+SIMD dispatch philosophy. Dedup ratio of Gear is within ~1% of Rabin typical (up to ~6% worse worst-case); FastCDC normalized chunking closes the gap while staying fast. Memory is O(window) constant. Boundary probability set purely by mask width (1/2^N), giving deterministic expected chunk size with no separate average parameter.
repos.license: Kubo is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 and MIT (permissive); standalone Rust gearhash and fastcdc crates are MIT/Apache-2.0, so the algorithm and a vendored/clean-room kernel are safe to adopt.

repos.one_liner: A purely-functional package manager whose store is a content-addressed object graph: artifacts are identified by SHA-256 hashes of a canonical, metadata-stripped serialization (NAR) plus a structured "fingerprint" string, enabling deterministic builds and distributed substitution from untrusted binary caches.
repos.core_innovation: Decoupling logical-content identity from physical-byte identity via a canonical serialization (NAR) hashed independently of its on-disk compressed encoding: the narinfo carries BOTH NarHash/NarSize (uncompressed canonical content) and FileHash/FileSize (compressed artifact), and signatures/addresses are computed only over the uncompressed canonical form. This makes the content identity stable across any compression codec while still verifying the physical bytes you downloaded.
key_techniques: NAR canonical serialization: 64-bit LE length-prefixed strings padded to 8-byte boundaries, magic 'nix-archive-1', directory entries sorted by name, all timestamps/metadata stripped except executable-bit and symlink target -> byte-identical output for identical trees

Structured hash 'fingerprint' string: type ':sha256:' inner-digest ':' store ':' name, SHA-256'd then truncated/compressed from 256 to 160 bits and rendered in a custom base-32 alphabet (omits e,o,u,t, reverse byte order)
Dual-identity addressing: NarHash/NarSize (logical, uncompressed) vs FileHash/FileSize (physical, compressed .nar.xz/.zst) tracked separately in narinfo

Hash-modulo-self-references: replace the object's own not-yet-known store path with a fixed sentinel/scratch placeholder before hashing, so a self-referential CA digest is computable and placement-independent
Ed25519 signing over a fingerprint '1;StorePath;NarHash;NarSize;refs' covering only uncompressed content, so recompression never invalidates signatures
Minimal HTTP substitution protocol: GET /<storehash>.narinfo (metadata keyed by content hash) + GET /nar/<filehash>.nar.<ext> (content-addressed blob), trivially mirrorable/offline-cacheable

Content-defined chunking lesson (nix-casync/Tvix): whole-NAR dedup is weak (one changed bit busts the whole file); CDC into a chunk-store + index-store (caibx) enables sub-file dedup, and compression must sit OUTSIDE the chunking layer because payloads are chunked decompressed
Fixed-output derivations: declare expected flat-or-recursive hash up front, decoupling content address from build inputs (intrinsic vs extrinsic addressing)
repos.nest_application: nest-format already has the right skeleton (content_hash = decoded canonical sections, stable across encodings; per-section checksum = physical bytes) -- Nix validates this split is the correct primitive and supplies hardening details. Concretely: (1) In crates/nest-format/src/hashing.rs, adopt NAR's structured-fingerprint discipline -- prefix the content_hash preimage with a typed, length-delimited domain string (version + section-id + logical-length) rather than concatenating raw section bytes, eliminating canonicalization ambiguity and giving the same domain-separation Nix gets from its 'type:sha256:...:store:name' fingerprint. (2) In sections/encoding, formalize that content_hash is computed over the NAR-style canonical decoded form while per-section checksum stays over compressed physical bytes -- making content_hash provably codec-invariant (raw==zstd==f16 for non-embedding sections), the exact NarHash-vs-FileHash separation; this lets nest re-encode a .nest (raw->tiny preset) and prove identical content_hash, a killer sovereign re-packaging guarantee. (3) For citation layer nest://content_hash/chunk_id, borrow length-prefixed+8-byte-padded framing for chunk_ids/spans so the canonical form is unambiguous and deterministic across platforms. (4) Future additive section id 0x09+: a content-defined-chunking 'chunk_store'+'index' pair (FastCDC, gear-hash rolling) for the chunks_canonical/text section, giving sub-document dedup across many .nest files or repeated boilerplate inside one corpus -- directly serving 'compress more than everyone' by deduplicating shared substrings before zstd, with the Nix-learned constraint that CDC runs on DECOMPRESSED bytes and compression is applied per-chunk afterward. (5) nest-cli could gain a Nix-style 'verify' checking both surfaces and a 'cite'/export emitting a narinfo-like sidecar for distributed mirroring -- all offline, no socket.
repos.compression_relevance: High. The content-defined-chunking + chunk-store/index model is a concrete path to sub-file/cross-file deduplication that compounds with nest's existing zstd (dedupe shared substrings BEFORE entropy coding). The NarHash/FileHash separation is the formal license to aggressively re-encode (zstd/f16/int8) while keeping a stable content identity -- you can ship the smallest preset and still prove it carries the same content_hash as the exact preset. The Nix lesson 'compression outside the chunking layer, CDC on decompressed bytes' prevents a classic mistake that would otherwise destroy nest's dedup ratio.
repos.perf_notes: NAR/store-path hashing is single-threaded SHA-256 over a streaming serialization; cheap relative to builds. Binary cache supports multi-threaded xz and zstd compression of NARs (only xz/zstd are MT-capable); cache.nixos.org defaults to xz (smallest) with zstd as the faster-decompress alternative. The 256->160-bit truncation keeps store-path digests short (32 base-32 chars) at negligible collision risk for the namespace size. CDC (nix-casync) adds chunk-lookup overhead but turns O(file) re-uploads into O(changed-chunks); reassembly is sequential concatenation of zstd-decompressed chunks.
repos.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later. Use as design reference / clean-room reimplementation only -- do NOT vendor code into nest's permissively-licensed Rust crates; the algorithms (NAR framing, fingerprint scheme, CDC) are ideas/specs, not copyrightable, so reimplementing from the published protocol spec is safe.

repos.repo: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs (Nix store / NAR model, implemented in NixOS/nix)
repos.one_liner: Nix is a content-addressed package store whose substrate is NAR (Nix Archive): a fully deterministic, metadata-stripped, length-prefixed binary serialization of filesystem trees, hashed with SHA-256 and truncated to a 160-bit nix-base32 digest to form immutable, reproducible content-addressed store paths and derivations.
repos.core_innovation: A canonical, reproducible serialization (NAR) that strips all non-reproducible metadata (mtime, atime, uid/gid, all permission bits except the single executable bit) and sorts directory entries by name, so "same logical content => byte-identical archive => identical hash" holds across machines and time. This is exactly the discipline nest aspires to with content_hash; NAR proves the pattern at planet scale (all of nixpkgs).
key_techniques: NAR serialization: magic str("nix-archive-1"), recursive (...) framing of regular/symlink/directory nodes, only the executable bit preserved, no timestamps
str(s) framing: 64-bit little-endian length prefix + raw bytes + zero-pad to next 8-byte boundary (the load-bearing canonicalization primitive)
Directory entries serialized sorted-by-name so the archive is independent of source filesystem ordering
Two-level hashing: SHA-256 over NAR contents -> inner-digest (hex), then SHA-256 over typed fingerprint 'type:sha256:inner:store:name', truncated to first 160 bits
nix-base32: custom 32-char alphabet (omits e/o/u/t to avoid confusables and dirty words) encoding the 160-bit digest into the store path
Content-addressed derivations + deriving paths: refer to an output before its hash is known, resolved post-build; flat/nar/text/git addressing methods

Store-wide dedup via nix store optimise: hash every regular file, hard-link identical NAR-content files into /nix/store/.links/<checksum> (25-35% savings, no correctness loss because store is immutable+CA)
Binary cache: NARs transported as independent zstd (or xz) compressed, content-addressed blobs enabling distributed substitution without a central DB
repos.nest_application: nest-format already content_hashes decoded canonical sections; steal NAR's exact canonicalization to harden it. In crates/nest-format/src/hashing.rs + sections.rs: (1) adopt NAR's str() framing as the content_hash preimage -- u64-LE length prefix + payload + zero-pad to 8 bytes per section, sections in fixed ID order, any maps/sets (chunk_ids, bm25 terms) sorted -- so content_hash is provably encoding-independent, making the 'STABLE across encodings' claim airtight and matching the bm25 alphabetical-term-order rule already in spec. (2) Port the store-optimise dedup pattern into nest-format/encoding: before zstd, SHA-256 each canonical chunk and store duplicate chunks once with a back-reference table -- a new additive encoding id (4-255 reserved) 'dedup' collapsing repeated text/json/yaml fragments, directly serving 'compress more than everyone' on boilerplate-heavy corpora (legal, PT-BR news templates, repeated JSON keys). Apply to non-embedding sections only, never embeddings (hot-path rule). (3) Use nix-base32 (160-bit, confusable-free) as a shorter, copy-paste-safe citation token in nest-cli cite for nest://content_hash/chunk_id. All of this respects repr(C), little-endian, additive, deterministic, offline constraints.
repos.compression_relevance: High and direct. NAR is not itself a compressor, but two ideas feed extreme compression: (a) canonical content-addressing is the precondition for safe dedup -- you can only collapse byte-identical regions if you can prove identity reproducibly, which nest needs before any cross-chunk dedup codec; (b) Nix store-optimise hard-link dedup yields real 25-35% reduction on redundant corpora purely by content-hash equality, before any entropy coding. nest can layer a dedup pre-pass under its existing zstd path on non-embedding sections, compounding with float16/int8 quantization in the tiny preset.
repos.license: MIT
repos.perf_notes: NAR's 8-byte-aligned length-prefixed framing makes parsing fast and unambiguous (no escaping/quoting) but causes many tiny 8-byte reads in naive streaming readers -- a non-issue for nest since sections are mmapped and reads are length-bounded. Two-level SHA-256 (content then fingerprint) is cheap vs I/O. Store-wide dedup is I/O-bound (10-30 min on full Nix store) and the giant .links dir slows GC; nest's bounded single-file scope avoids that -- dedup is a one-shot build-time pass in nest-python before freezing. zstd over NAR is ~8-12x faster than xz at competitive ratio (xz 18.8s vs zstd 2.35s on a sample), validating nest's zstd-over-heavier-coder choice on the build path.

repos.one_liner: A crowd-sourced verification corpus that rebuilds Maven Central artifacts inside pinned Docker/JDK environments and proves byte-for-byte reproducibility by comparing SHA-512 fingerprints of every output file against the published artifact, recording the verdict in declarative .buildspec/.buildcompare/.buildinfo text files.
repos.core_innovation: A two-layer reproducibility proof split into (1) a tiny declarative recipe (.buildspec: groupId/artifactId/version + gitTag + jdk-major + newline-mode + exact build command) that is the minimal pinned input needed to regenerate bytes, and (2) a per-output-file SHA-512 manifest (.buildinfo: outputs.N.filename / outputs.N.length / outputs.N.checksums.sha512 lowercase) that is content-addressing of the build result; equality of the manifest is the reproducibility certificate, and diffoscope is invoked only on mismatch to localize the divergence. Reproducibility is engineered, not hoped for: ~92% of Maven non-determinism came from embedded archive timestamps, killed by zeroing ZIP/JAR mtimes (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH / project.build.outputTimestamp) plus enforcing a deterministic sorted entry order inside the archive.
key_techniques: Declarative minimal build recipe (.buildspec): groupId/artifactId/version + gitRepo/gitTag + jdk MAJOR version only + newline mode (lf/crlf) + exact build command -- the smallest deterministic input set
Per-output-file content manifest (.buildinfo): indexed records outputs.N.filename / outputs.N.length / outputs.N.checksums.sha512 in lowercase; manifest equality == reproducibility proof
SHA-512 (not SHA-256) lowercase hex as the canonical artifact fingerprint, with length recorded alongside as a cheap fast-reject pre-check
Verdict file (.buildcompare) decoupled from hashes: ok/ko/ignored counts plus space-separated okFiles/koFiles/ignoredFiles name lists + reference_java_version/reference_os_name provenance

Archive normalization for determinism: zero/pin all ZIP/JAR entry timestamps (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, project.build.outputTimestamp, java.properties.date) which removed ~92% of failures, plus enforced sorted/canonical entry order
Environment pinning at coarse granularity: only JDK MAJOR version pinned (minor/vendor proven irrelevant to bytecode), minimizing the recipe while preserving reproducibility
diffoscope as mismatch explainer only: recursively unpacks JAR -> class -> bytecode to localize diverging bytes, run in a pinned container, never on the happy path
Containerized rebuild (pinned Docker image per JDK) as environment-as-data substrate for independent re-verification
repos.nest_application: nest-format already has content_hash (decoded canonical sections, stable across encodings) and file_hash (physical pre-footer body). Steal the .buildspec/.buildinfo split to make REPRODUCIBILITY a first-class, externally verifiable artifact. (1) In nest-format/manifest, emit a deterministic build recipe alongside provenance: model fingerprint, chunker version, encoding preset, section ordering -- the minimal pinned inputs guaranteeing 'same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file'. This is the .buildspec analogue and turns nest's determinism claim into something a third party can re-derive offline. (2) Adopt the per-section SHA manifest in nest-format/hashing: nest already has per-section physical checksums; expose them as a flat, sorted, lowercase-hex manifest (section_id, decoded_length, content_checksum) so two independently-built .nest files compare by manifest equality without byte-diffing 100MB embeddings, with decoded_length as a free fast-reject before hashing. (3) Add a nest-cli 'verify-reproducible' subcommand (sibling to validate) that takes a recipe + corpus and asserts manifest equality, emitting an ok/ko/ignored verdict like .buildcompare -- cheap, offline, deterministic, additive. (4) The archive-normalization lesson maps to extreme compression: canonicalize entry order and strip incidental timestamps/non-canonical ordering BEFORE hashing/encoding, because canonical ordering both guarantees reproducibility AND maximizes zstd ratio on non-embedding sections (sorted bm25 terms + sorted chunk_ids already do this; extend the discipline to every section). Cross-file relevance: content-addressed manifests enable dedup -- identical chunks/embeddings across many .nest files share one content_hash, so a future distributed/pack format stores each unique decoded section once and references it (Maven's 'same coordinates => same bytes' applied to vector data).
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real. The direct payload (SHA-512 manifests, .buildspec recipes) is verification infrastructure, not a codec, so it does not shrink bytes itself. Two transferable ideas serve compress-more-than-everyone: (1) canonical/sorted entry ordering before encoding is simultaneously the reproducibility guarantee AND a zstd ratio win on non-embedding sections; (2) content-addressed per-section manifests are the prerequisite for cross-file dedup -- store each unique decoded section once across a corpus of .nest files and reference by content_hash, which is how Maven's 'same coordinates => same bytes' becomes 'same chunk => stored once'.
repos.perf_notes: No SIMD/throughput angle -- offline batch verification (docker rebuild + hash). Two transferable perf ideas: record decoded length next to each hash so file comparison fast-rejects on length mismatch before computing the expensive hash; and compare-by-manifest (hash-list equality) instead of byte-diffing large payloads, so verifying two multi-GB artifacts is O(number of sections) over precomputed hashes, not O(bytes). diffoscope-style deep diff is reserved strictly for the mismatch path so the common case stays cheap.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (project content); per-artifact recipes follow upstream project licenses. Safe to learn from; no code vendored.

synthesis.summary: The content-addressed cluster (IPFS/Kubo, Nix/NAR, Maven reproducible-central) collectively proves three things nest already half-implements and one thing it does not. First, nest's existing primitives are validated prior-art: content_hash over decoded canonical sections (crates/nest-format/src/reader/decode.rs:53-66) is already a NAR-grade construction — length-prefixed, domain-separated by section name, alphabetically ordered via CANONICAL_SECTIONS (layout/mod.rs:87). That is exactly Nix's NarHash-vs-FileHash split (logical identity stable across codec; physical checksum over stored bytes) and Kubo's "multihash indexes storage, encoding is a wrapper" model. The nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation mirrors CIDv1 + raw-leaves block addressing. So three extracts' headline recommendation ("adopt NAR framing for content_hash") is ALREADY DONE; nest should claim the validation, not redo the work. The genuinely new, high-value lever the whole cluster points at is what nest does NOT do: deduplication before entropy coding. nest today chunks upstream in Python (build_fn.rs receives pre-embedded chunks with explicit spans) and zstd-compresses each section independently (writer/payload.rs:47 maybe_zstd) with no shared dictionary and no cross-chunk or cross-file dedup. chunks_canonical (sections/canonical.rs) stores every chunk's text verbatim before zstd sees it. IPFS content-defined chunking (FastCDC/Gear rolling hash) + block-level dedup, and Nix store-optimise hard-link dedup (25-35% on redundant corpora purely from content-hash equality), are the single biggest untapped compression mechanism for nest's boilerplate-heavy targets (PT-BR news templates, repeated JSON keys, legal text, whole repos). The hard-won cross-cutting lesson is Nix's: dedup and CDC MUST run on decompressed bytes, with compression applied per-chunk/per-block AFTERWARD — getting this order wrong destroys the ratio. Maven contributes the reproducibility-as-verifiable-artifact discipline: a tiny declarative recipe (.buildspec) plus a per-output sorted SHA manifest (.buildinfo) whose equality IS the proof, with length recorded for free fast-reject, turning nest's "same chunks + same model => byte-identical" claim into something a third party re-derives offline without byte-diffing 100MB of embeddings.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: State of the art across the cluster: (1) Content identity is decoupled from physical encoding via a canonical, metadata-stripped serialization hashed independently of its compressed form. Nix NAR (magic 'nix-archive-1', u64-LE length-prefixed strings zero-padded to 8 bytes, dir entries sorted by name, all metadata stripped except the executable bit) is the reference; narinfo carries both NarHash/NarSize (logical, uncompressed) and FileHash/FileSize (physical, compressed) so signatures over the uncompressed form survive recompression. (2) Content-defined chunking replaces fixed-offset splitting: a rolling hash (Rabin polynomial; Buzhash cyclic-poly, ~3x faster; Gear/FastCDC single shift+add, ~1350 MB/s) sets a boundary when the low/high N fingerprint bits hit a target, so a local edit perturbs only one or two chunks and downstream boundaries (and their hashes) stay stable — yielding high cross-version dedup. FastCDC adds zero-padded mask widening, cut-point skipping below min-size, and normalized chunking for a tight size distribution. (3) Block/chunk dedup keyed by content hash collapses identical content to one stored object regardless of transport (Kubo blockstore raw-leaves where block multihash == plain content hash; Nix store-optimise hard-links identical NAR files into .links/<checksum>; nix-casync/Tvix CDC chunk-store + caibx index for sub-file dedup). (4) The order rule: compression sits OUTSIDE the chunking/dedup layer (CDC on decompressed bytes, compress per chunk afterward) or dedup collapses to near-zero. (5) Reproducibility is engineered and externally verifiable: pin the minimal input set, normalize ordering (sort entries) and strip incidental metadata/timestamps before hashing (killed ~92% of Maven nondeterminism), and prove it by equality of a per-output content manifest rather than a byte diff. nest already satisfies (1) for its six canonical sections and the citation layer, and partially (5) via reproducible(true) + REPRODUCIBLE_CREATED; it does NOT yet do (2), (3), or expose (5) as a verifiable manifest.
top_innovations: Cross-chunk + cross-file content-hash dedup BEFORE zstd (Nix store-optimise + Kubo blockstore). Hash each canonical chunk (machinery already exists: chunk_id in chunk.rs is a SHA-256 over canonical_text), store each unique chunk's bytes once in chunks_canonical, and replace duplicates with a back-reference index. Free 25-35% on boilerplate-heavy corpora purely from content-hash equality, compounding multiplicatively with the existing per-section zstd. Highest value, lowest recall risk (text sections only, embeddings untouched).

FastCDC/Gear content-defined chunking for large blob inputs and edit-local rechunking. A small deterministic seeded rolling-hash kernel (left-shift+add, O(window) memory, ~1350 MB/s, SIMD-friendly) added to the Python build pipeline so editing one paragraph re-emits only the touched chunk(s); unchanged chunks keep byte-identical canonical_text + embeddings, making real-time-edit diffs tiny and enabling cheap incremental/append builds for the pdf/json/parquet/repo roadmap.

The 'compress outside the chunking layer, CDC on decompressed bytes' invariant (Nix nix-casync/Tvix lesson). A one-line design constraint that prevents the classic mistake of compressing then chunking, which would silently destroy nest's dedup ratio. Cheap to honor, expensive to discover late.

NarHash/FileHash dual-identity as the formal license to aggressively re-encode. nest's content_hash (decoded) vs per-section checksum (physical) IS this split and is already correct; the innovation to claim is the GUARANTEE it unlocks: re-encode a .nest from exact->tiny preset and prove identical content_hash, so the smallest preset provably carries the same content as the exact one. A killer sovereign re-packaging property worth a test + doc, not new code.

Reproducibility manifest a la Maven .buildspec/.buildinfo: a minimal declarative build recipe (model_hash, chunker_version, preset, section order) plus a flat sorted lowercase-hex per-section manifest (section_id, decoded_length, content_checksum). decoded_length gives free fast-reject before hashing; manifest equality proves two independent builds match without byte-diffing embeddings. Turns nest's determinism claim into a third-party-verifiable artifact, offline.

Canonical/sorted ordering as a dual-purpose primitive: it is simultaneously the reproducibility guarantee AND a zstd ratio win (sorting groups similar bytes). nest already sorts bm25 terms and section IDs; the innovation is extending the discipline consciously to every new section so ordering is never left to input order.

Shorter copy-paste-safe citation tokens via a confusable-free base32 (Nix nix-base32 omits e/o/u/t) over a truncated digest. Optional ergonomic upgrade to nest://content_hash/chunk_id so citations are shorter and dirty-word/confusable-free, with the full SHA-256 still available for verification.

Block-level deduped citation resolution (Kubo): once chunks_canonical is deduped, a citation can resolve to a single shared physical block, so identical boilerplate across many chunks/files cites one stored region — content-addressing all the way down to the byte span.

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a build-time content-hash dedup pass for chunks_canonical (and later chunks_original_spans/blob sections): SHA-256 each chunk's canonical_text, keep a first-seen table, store each unique text once, and emit a parallel u32 back-reference array (chunk index -> unique-block index). Expose as a new additive encoding id in the reserved 4-255 range (e.g. SECTION_ENCODING_DEDUP) or an internal payload variant of chunks_canonical, with zstd applied to the deduped unique-block pool. content_hash stays computed over the DECODED (re-expanded) bytes so it is unchanged and citations stay stable.

This is the Nix nix-casync/Tvix lesson encoded as a guardrail so a future contributor cannot accidentally invert the order and silently kill the ratio.

Shorter, copy-paste-safe nest:// URIs for humans without changing the on-disk hash.

This is Kubo raw-leaves block addressing applied to nest's chunk layer and proves content-addressing all the way to the byte span.

nest_recommendations.impact: low

compression_wins: Cross-chunk dedup of chunks_canonical before zstd: store each unique canonical_text once + a u32 back-reference array. On boilerplate-heavy corpora (PT-BR fake-news templates, repeated JSON keys/values, legal forms) this removes redundancy that per-section zstd cannot fully recover across distant chunks, compounding with the existing zstd/f16/int8 stack. Nix store-optimise shows 25-35% on redundant corpora from content-hash equality ALONE, before any entropy coder.

Cross-FILE dedup across a corpus of .nest files via content_hash equality: identical chunks/sections shared across many files store once and reference by content_hash (Maven 'same coordinates => same bytes' becomes 'same chunk => stored once'). Enables a future distributed/pack format that is far smaller than the sum of independent files.

FastCDC edit-local rechunking turns O(file) re-encodes into O(changed-chunks): a one-paragraph edit re-emits one or two chunks, so an incremental/append build writes a tiny diff instead of a whole new file — the on-disk delta between two corpus versions becomes proportional to the edit, not the corpus.

Honoring 'CDC/dedup on decompressed bytes, compress afterward' protects the entire dedup ratio: shared substrings are collapsed BEFORE zstd's window, so zstd then only has to compress the unique residue. Inverting the order (the classic mistake) would leave duplicates hidden inside compressed blocks and recover almost nothing.

Canonical/sorted entry ordering is a free zstd ratio win on every non-embedding section (grouping similar bytes shortens match distances), and it is the same operation that guarantees reproducibility — one discipline, two payoffs. nest already does this for bm25 terms and section IDs; extending it to all sections is pure upside.

A zstd shared dictionary trained over the unique-block pool (natural follow-on once dedup exists) further shrinks many small similar chunks that individually defeat per-chunk zstd framing overhead — applies only to non-embedding sections, zero recall cost.

All wins are confined to non-embedding sections (canonical text, spans, future blob payloads); embeddings remain raw/quantized and scored straight off mmap, so every byte saved is recall-free and the SIMD hot path is untouched.
watch_outs: DO NOT compress before dedup/CDC. The Nix nix-casync/Tvix lesson is load-bearing: CDC and content-hash dedup must run on decompressed bytes with compression applied per unique-block afterward, or dedup collapses to near-zero. Encode this as a code-level invariant + regression test, not just a comment.

NEVER dedup or CDC the embeddings section. Embeddings are scored directly from mmap on the SIMD hot path (AVX2/NEON dot products) and are intentionally never compressed; any indirection (back-reference table, variable-size blocks) would break the contiguous repr(C) little-endian layout and the alignment the SIMD dispatcher relies on. Dedup is text/span/blob-only.

Dedup must keep content_hash invariant. content_hash (decode.rs:53-66) is computed over DECODED canonical bytes; the dedup decoder MUST re-expand to the identical logical byte stream before the hash sees it, or every citation nest://content_hash/chunk_id breaks. This is the whole point of the NarHash/FileHash split — keep dedup strictly a physical-encoding concern.

Stay additive within v1. A dedup encoding id belongs in the reserved 4-255 range and a chunk-store/manifest section in 0x09+; only a change to the MEANING of an existing field (e.g. redefining content_hash preimage) justifies bumping NEST_FORMAT_VERSION to a true v2. Do not let dedup leak into a format break.

Determinism is non-negotiable. CDC rolling-hash seed/mask and dedup first-seen ordering must be fully seeded and deterministic (seed captured via chunker_version/manifest) so 'same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file' still holds. A HashMap iteration-order leak or unseeded mask would silently break reproducibility.

Single-file + offline must survive. Kubo's blockstore and Nix's binary cache are multi-file, networked stores; nest must keep dedup INSIDE one .nest container and as a one-shot build-time pass — no socket, no external block store, no separate index file at runtime. Cross-file dedup/pack is a future opt-in format, never the default sovereign single-file path.

Respect the small-core budget: <=300 lines/file (333 hard cap), single-responsibility, never panic in library code (typed thiserror). A CDC kernel + dedup module are each one file; resist pulling in heavy crates (avoid vendoring Kubo Go or Nix LGPL code — reimplement the algorithms clean-room from spec; standalone Rust gearhash/fastcdc are MIT/Apache if a dependency is justified, but a hand-rolled <=300-loc kernel fits nest's by-hand ethos better).

Do not over-build the reproducibility manifest. Maven's value is the SMALL recipe + sorted hash list, not a verification farm; nest's bounded single-file scope means a manifest section + one verify-reproducible subcommand suffices. Avoid Docker/container pinning and diffoscope-style deep diff machinery — out of scope for a solo, minimal-budget, offline tool.

Truncated/base32 citation tokens are ergonomic ONLY; never let a truncated digest become the verification surface. Keep full sha256:<hex> as the canonical, collision-safe identity and treat short base32 as a display convenience that still resolves to the full hash.

categories.name: factcheck-datasets
categories.focus: fact-checking / misinformation resources and datasets (nest demo domain + truth features)

repos.one_liner: A curated, MIT-licensed "awesome list" / paper-and-dataset link index companion to two survey papers (TACL 2022 "A Survey on Automated Fact-Checking" and EMNLP 2023 multimodal survey) that organizes the automated-fact-checking field into a canonical pipeline taxonomy.
repos.core_innovation: The transferable artifact is not code (there is none) but a precise, widely-adopted decomposition of fact-checking into four pipeline stages -- claim detection/check-worthiness -> evidence retrieval -> verdict prediction (SUPPORTS / REFUTES / NOT-ENOUGH-INFO) -> justification production -- coupled to a taxonomy of evidence granularities (sentence-level, document-level, structured tables, multi-hop chains, web/social threads). This is the schema nest needs to model "truth features" and a retrieve-then-verify citation contract over its demo corpus.
key_techniques: Four-stage AFC pipeline: claim detection/check-worthiness -> evidence retrieval -> verdict prediction -> justification
Three-label veracity schema (SUPPORTS / REFUTES / NOT ENOUGH INFO) from FEVER, with NEI as an explicit abstention class
Evidence-granularity taxonomy: sentence vs document vs table vs multi-hop chain vs conversation thread
Retrieve-then-verify framing where retrieval+verification are jointly 'factual verification' (maps onto nest's ANN-then-exact-rerank search contract)
Provenance-as-evidence pattern: claims bound to specific Wikipedia sentence ids/spans (analogous to nest's nest://content_hash/chunk_id span citations)
Multi-hop reasoning chains (HoVer/FEVEROUS) as ordered evidence sets -> motivates a future graph-search section linking chunk_ids
Check-worthiness as an importance-ranking/triage scoring stage before retrieval
repos.nest_application: No crate steals code (this repo has none and is irrelevant to the FROZEN format). It informs three things. (1) nest-cli + demo docs: shape the PT-BR fake-news demo around the four-stage pipeline so a 'fact-check' is expressed purely as nest primitives -- search-ann/search-text retrieve candidate evidence chunks, exact cosine rerank ranks them, and a citation nest://content_hash/chunk_id binds the verdict to an exact byte span (the provenance section already exists; this gives it semantic purpose). (2) provenance section schema (nest-format/src/sections): document a convention for a per-chunk 'claim/evidence role' plus a three-value veracity label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEI) carried as provenance metadata key-values, staying additive-only (no new section id, no version bump). (3) roadmap only: multi-hop evidence chains are the concrete use-case justifying the mission's planned 'graph search' over chunk_ids, but this must wait for a reserved section id 0x09+ and is out of scope for v1. It unlocks a credible, citable fact-checking narrative without touching the frozen container or the compression path.
repos.compression_relevance: n/a -- this is a link list with zero compression, encoding, quantization, or indexing implementation. It contributes nothing to the 'compress more than everyone' north star. Its only relevance is domain modeling for the demo corpus and the truth-feature narrative, which is orthogonal to the codec and on-disk format.
repos.license: MIT for the repository markdown; underlying datasets carry their own individual licenses (e.g. FEVER/FEVEROUS are Wikipedia-derived CC BY-SA share-alike) and must be license-vetted per-dataset before shipping any of them in a .nest demo corpus.
repos.perf_notes: No runtime, no benchmarks, no throughput/SIMD/memory characteristics -- it is static markdown. Performance n/a. Only operational caveat: any dataset linked here that nest ships must be license-checked individually, independent of nest's own posture.

repos.one_liner: An LLM-output fact-checking framework that decomposes a document into context-independent atomic claims, retrieves ranked evidence per claim, runs 4-way stance detection (support/partial-support/refute/irrelevant), and emits per-claim verdict records, shipping Factcheck-Bench (94 annotated ChatGPT responses) plus FactBench (4,835 examples merged from FacTool-KB/FELM-WK/HaluEval).
repos.core_innovation: A serializable, fine-grained "claim -> evidence -> stance -> verdict" provenance schema: every checkable fact becomes an atomic claim record with a structured verdict dict {reasoning, error, correction, factuality:bool}, each backed by N ranked evidence snippets carrying a discrete stance label (CP/PS/RE/IR). This decouples a coarse document from auditable, span-localized truth units -- the structure nest needs to attach verifiable truth/provenance metadata to chunks without inventing a format from scratch.
key_techniques: Atomic claim decomposition: NLTK sentence-split then LLM decompose(input:str)->list[str] of context-independent, decontextualized statements
4-way stance vocabulary CP/PS/RE/IR (completely-support / partially-support / refute / irrelevant), collapsible to 3-way (support/refute/irrelevant)
Per-claim verdict record: {reasoning, error, correction, factuality:bool} structured machine-parseable judgment
Evidence retrieval by query-generation then ranking ~5 snippets by semantic relevance to the claim
Three-class modular abstraction: claim_processor -> retriever -> verifier pipeline (mirrors OpenFactCheck)
Checkworthiness gating with discrete labels {factual=1, opinion=2, non-claim=3, other=4} to filter what is worth verifying
Span-based annotation schema: response + list of false segments/spans + per-claim factual labels[] + document-level label
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add an OPTIONAL additive section (reserved id 0x09+, never bump v1) named chunks_truth -- a deterministic, zstd-encoded (non-embedding, codec-eligible) table parallel to chunks_canonical holding per-chunk atomic-claim records: claim_id, char span into chunks_original_spans, verdict enum {true,false,unverified} as a 1-byte field, stance counts, and optional evidence chunk_ids resolving to nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations. This makes the PT-BR fake-news demo corpus self-describing: each chunk carries its own auditable verdict + evidence pointers, offline, inside the single file. nest-runtime: a thin verify/filter on the search path (post exact-cosine rerank) to restrict or boost results by verdict, plus a materialize path emitting the {reasoning,error,correction,factuality} record for a hit. nest-cli: extend the `cite` subcommand (or add `verify`) to print the truth record + evidence citations. The 4-way stance label is a 1-byte enum (deterministic, alphabetical-order friendly), staying within nest's small-core, no-panic, little-endian, additive constraints.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect to raw compression. Stance/verdict labels are tiny discrete enums (1 byte each, highly compressible under zstd, in a non-embedding codec-eligible section) adding negligible bytes while raising 'truth density' per byte of the demo corpus. The real win is mission-side (truth features + provenance for the fake-news demo domain), not the compress-more-than-everyone north-star: it does not improve embedding or text ratios.
repos.perf_notes: Reference framework is LLM-prompt-bound (GPT-3.5-turbo per claim, Google search per claim) -- not a hot-path or SIMD concern. nest would NOT replicate the online retrieval/LLM calls (violates offline-by-construction); it adopts only the data schema, built once at python build time and served as static bytes. Serving overhead is just decoding a small zstd section plus an enum compare -- effectively free relative to the SIMD dot-product hot path.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (per repo; verify before vendoring any prompt text or dataset rows -- the PT-BR demo should adopt the schema design only, not their data)

repos.one_liner: A Python fact-checking/factuality-evaluation framework that consolidates RARR, FacTool, and FactCheckGPT into a YAML-configured solver DAG (claim_processor -> retriever -> verifier) passing a single FactCheckerState dict, plus four human-annotated benchmark datasets (FactQA 6,480 examples, FactBench claims with True/False/Unknown labels).
repos.core_innovation: Declarative pipeline-by-name-matching: solvers register via @Solver.register(name, input_name, output_name) and are chained purely by string-matching one stage's output_name to the next stage's input_name in a YAML config, carrying all state in one mutable FactCheckerState bag with a success_flag. The pipeline topology is data, not code, so heterogeneous stages from different systems compose without recompilation - this is the Fairseq plugin pattern applied to a verification DAG.
key_techniques: @Solver.register(name, input_name, output_name) decorator into a SOLVER_REGISTRY plus YAML-declared stage order; chaining is validated by string-matching output_name->input_name
Single FactCheckerState dict threaded through all stages with a boolean success_flag gating progression (message-passing contract)
BM25 over an offline Wikipedia dump for evidence retrieval (vs paid Serper/SerpAPI web search) - explicit offline tier
Atomic-claim decomposition: NLTK sentence split then LLM atomic-claim extraction + decontextualization
True/False/Unknown ternary verdict taxonomy with per-claim labels aggregated to a response-level 'percentage true claims' (FactScore-style) score
FactBench claim schema: question, domain (482), topic (4740), atomic_claims[], per-claim factual_labels[], response_level_label
Checker evaluation by precision/recall/F1 per label plus latency-hours and itemized per-claim cost ($/claim) leaderboard
repos.nest_application: nest-runtime search_contract section + nest-cli: adopt the register-by-name output/input string-matching as a data-encoded retrieval-stage graph in the already-required search_contract section (no format bump, additive, deterministic, offline); separately, nest-python demo corpus + provenance/citation: adopt the FactBench claim+evidence+True/False/Unknown schema and percentage-true aggregation, mapping evidence passages onto nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations.
repos.compression_relevance: n/a - OpenFactCheck contributes nothing to extreme compression. It has no entropy coder, no quantization, no on-disk binary format, no SIMD; data lives in plain JSON/dict structures and HF datasets. Its BM25-over-Wikipedia offline tier merely validates nest's existing bm25_index(0x08) and offline-by-construction stance. Value to nest is the demo/truth-feature domain (fact-check datasets + ternary verdict + citation-as-evidence) and a declarative-pipeline engineering pattern, not byte reduction.
repos.perf_notes: Pure Python, no SIMD or vectorization. Reported latencies are pipeline-level and dominated by LLM API calls (FacTool ~0.49h, FactCheckGPT ~7.67h over a benchmark run), not data-structure throughput. BM25 retrieval is the only local compute path. Cost is tracked per atomic claim (~$0.02/claim) - a useful precedent for nest emitting per-query cost/latency telemetry in benchmark/stats subcommands, but nothing performance-transferable to the mmap hot path.
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (per repo); permissive, compatible with vendoring schema/dataset ideas. Datasets aggregate third-party benchmarks (FacTool-QA, FELM-WK, Factcheck-Bench, HaluEval, FreshQA, SelfAware) each under their own upstream licenses - check before redistributing in a .nest demo corpus.

repos.one_liner: TabFact is a fact-verification dataset (118k statements over 16.5k Wikipedia tables, ENTAILED/REFUTED) shipped with a Latent Program Algorithm (LPA) that compiles each natural-language statement into a small typed DSL of ~60 table operations and verifies it by symbolic execution via a memoized, trigger-word-gated beam search.
repos.core_innovation: A closed, strongly-typed operator DSL (~60 ops over types num/str/row/header_num/header_str/bool) where each operator carries a set of natural-language "trigger words" plus POS-tag constraints; statement words gate which operators are eligible (must_have / must_not_have sets), collapsing an exponential program space into a tractable typed beam search whose intermediate results are memoized by command-string hash. The verification answer is the deterministic boolean OUTPUT of executing the synthesized program against the table, not a learned similarity score.
key_techniques: Typed program DSL: ~60 ops (count, filter_eq/greater/less[_eq], filter_str_eq fuzzy, argmax/argmin, max/min/avg/sum, hop/str_hop/num_hop, all_eq/all_greater universal quantifiers, within/not_within, before/after ordering, diff/add, and/or) each with a fixed argument-type signature

Trigger-word gating: every op maps to NL trigger words + POS tags (max/argmax keyed on JJS/RBS superlatives, 'than any'); presence/absence builds must_have/must_not_have sets that prune the candidate operator set before search

Memoized beam search (dynamic_programming): hist[step] holds states; an op fires only when typed argument slots are filled; results cached by command string via call() memoization; saved_hash per step dedupes identical states
Anytime termination: stop at >100 complete programs or 40s wall-clock; breadth-first so shorter programs surface first

Entity linking via #xxx;row,col# span notation: longest-text-span match of statement mentions to cells/headers, pandas-dtype-driven num/str typing, separate string vs number memory pools (mem_str/mem_num, head_str/head_num)
Horizontal vs vertical table linearization (preprocess_BERT --scan) turning a 2D table into a token sequence for the Table-BERT baseline
Deterministic symbolic execution: the program's boolean output IS the verdict, fully reproducible and explainable
repos.nest_application: Adapt the typed-operator DSL + trigger-word gating into nest-runtime as a structured-query path beside cosine/hnsw/bm25, operating over the canonical text section and a future tabular/parquet section. (1) Define a small Rust enum of typed ops (filter_eq, greater, count, argmax, within, before/after) as a #[repr(C)] op-code table persisted as an OPTIONAL additive section (reserved id 0x09+) holding precomputed trigger-word->op-id maps and a per-chunk column type map (num/str), keeping the format additive and deterministic. (2) Implement the memoized beam search in nest-runtime as a no-panic, seeded, deterministic synthesizer (typed thiserror errors, files split ops/exec/search to stay <=300 loc) so a query like 'no team scored more than 3 goals' compiles to all_less(filter..) and returns a real boolean verdict citable via nest://content_hash/chunk_id, turning the PT-BR fake-news demo corpus into an explainable verifier rather than pure retrieval. (3) The trigger-word->op gating plus POS/type constraints is a compact lossless index of query semantics that complements bm25; the closed op set is a fixed dictionary that zstd-compresses well in a non-embedding section.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. No novel byte-level codec, but two ideas help nest's compress-more goal: (a) a CLOSED operator vocabulary + trigger-word dictionary is a tiny fixed symbol table that zstd-compresses near-perfectly in a non-embedding section, so storing verification programs costs almost nothing; (b) command-string-hash memoization is structural dedup of repeated subexpressions, the same principle behind nest's content_hash dedup. The real value is feature breadth (deterministic structured truth-checking over tables), not raw ratio.
repos.perf_notes: LPA is pure-Python beam search bounded to depth ~6, beam width 5-7, capped at 100 programs / 40s per statement; single-threaded, no SIMD. In Rust on nest's mmap path it would be far faster: the search is branch-heavy integer/string work, not float dot-products, so it does NOT compete for the SIMD hot path and runs lazily only when a query is structured. Memory: two small per-statement pools (strings, numbers) plus a per-step state hash set; fits the offline single-binary model trivially.
repos.license: Code released on GitHub by Wen-hu Chen et al. (UCSB); repo historically carries a permissive/research license (verify the exact LICENSE file before vendoring). Dataset built from Wikipedia tables, so CC BY-SA upstream considerations apply.

repos.one_liner: A collection of GNN fake-news detectors (GCNFN, BiGCN, GNN-CL, UPFD-GCN/GAT/SAGE) shipping the UPFD dataset: tree-structured Twitter retweet-propagation graphs (politifact 314 graphs / gossipcop 5,464 graphs) classified fake/real, with node features stored as scipy CSR sparse .npz matrices and topology as a single global COO edge list.
repos.core_innovation: Decouple the corpus into two orthogonal on-disk planes that compress with different codecs: (1) a single global COO edge list (A.txt) plus a node-to-graph-id index that reconstructs thousands of small graphs from one flat integer array, and (2) high-dimensional node-feature matrices stored as scipy CSR sparse .npz (sp.load_npz) so mostly-zero rows cost near nothing on disk while staying densifiable on demand. The propagation graph itself IS the truth signal: who-retweeted-whom structure is a fact-checking feature, separable from textual content.
key_techniques: UPFD propagation tree: root=news node, leaves=retweeting users, edge u->v iff v retweeted news from u; framed as fake/real graph classification
Global COO edge list (A.txt, comma-separated long pairs) coalesced once, with node_graph_id.npy partitioning one flat node array into N subgraphs
scipy CSR sparse .npz (sp.load_npz + .todense()) for node-feature matrices new_{feature}_feature.npz
Four interchangeable feature encoders keyed by name: profile=10d, spacy word2vec=300d, bert(bert-as-service)=768d, content=300+10=310d
Index-array train/val/test splits (train_idx/val_idx/test_idx.npy) referencing graph ids, not copies of data
Separation of integer topology plane (RLE/delta/varint friendly) from float feature plane (quantizable) as independent codec targets
repos.nest_application: Two moves. (1) Demo/truth corpus: ingest UPFD via nest-python as a demo dataset beside the PT-BR fake-news sets -- each propagation graph becomes one provenance-tagged record; the 310d content vectors map onto nest-format embeddings (preset tiny: int8+zstd+hnsw), and nest://content_hash/chunk_id reopens the exact news node. Real benchmark for 'compress AND serve datasets' serving the factcheck-datasets + truth-features domain. (2) Reserve a future additive section (id 0x09+, RESERVED in v1, no version bump) for graph topology: store edges as a global delta+varint COO array plus a node_graph_id partition index, mirroring A.txt/node_graph_id.npy -- topology integers go through the non-embedding zstd path while embeddings stay raw-mmap on the hot path. That two-plane split (integer topology codec vs float feature codec) is the pattern to steal into nest-runtime's planned graph search.
repos.compression_relevance: Medium-high. Transferable insight is the two-plane decomposition: integer graph topology (COO + partition index) and float feature matrices are statistically different and want different codecs -- topology compresses brutally with delta+varint+zstd (sorted, low-entropy ids), features quantize/sparsify well (CSR for sparse profile rows, int8 for dense embeddings). The CSR-.npz nonzero-only trick is a free win for any sparse feature section. Their global-edge-list-plus-id-index is exactly how nest should pack many small graphs into one flat deterministic byte run.
repos.perf_notes: Datasets are small (gossipcop ~314k nodes/309k edges total; politifact ~41k/41k) and graphs are shallow ego-trees averaging 58-131 nodes, so topology fits in mmap and traversal is bounded. Feature matrices drive size: 768d bert dense per node dominates, which is why CSR sparse storage + on-demand densify matters; for nest, int8 on the 310d content vectors is the right call. Recent analyses note features are often linearly separable by class, so aggressive quantization should preserve discriminative power.
repos.license: Academic use only (dataset); code Apache-2.0 (safe-graph org). Raw data via Google Drive (~1.2GB), redistribution restricted -- vendor the loader/format pattern, not the raw corpus.

repos.one_liner: A fake-news research data repository that ships only minimal CSV manifests (id, news_url, title, tab-separated tweet_ids) plus per-object JSON files, and reconstructs the full multi-GB corpus (news content, tweets, retweets, user profiles, social graph) on demand via a rate-limit-coordinated parallel download harness.
repos.core_innovation: Dehydrated-dataset / manifest-plus-pointers pattern with dedup-by-reference: ship a tiny canonical ID+URL manifest and store every heavy object once in a shared, content-addressed pool that records reference by natural key.
key_techniques: Manifest CSV with stable string IDs decoupling identity from payload
Tab-separated ID reference lists as foreign keys into a shared object pool
Content-addressed-by-natural-key per-object JSON files (<tweet_id>.json, <user_id>.json) stored once, referenced many times
Two-layer split: canonical shareable manifest vs reconstructable hydrated payload
Flask key-broker coordinating rate-limited parallel reconstruction across workers
Factory-dispatched resumable partial collection driven by config.json
newspaper3k HTML-to-canonical-JSON article normalization (text/images/publish date)
repos.nest_application: nest-format gets an additive RESERVED section (0x09+) for external source refs (stable id + url) so a .nest can be a dehydrated manifest that deterministically re-hydrates chunks; nest-python builder gets a pre-zstd chunk-dedup pass that stores duplicate canonical spans once and emits pointer indices in chunk_ids; the tweet_ids->object-pool model becomes the data layout for a future deterministic graph_edges section in nest-runtime for offline graph search.
repos.compression_relevance: High conceptually, indirect in practice. FakeNewsNet itself uses no entropy coder or quantization — its "compression" is structural: dedup-by-reference (each user/tweet stored once, referenced by ID) and dehydration (ship the recipe, not the corpus). This is exactly the lever nest needs for the 'compress whole datasets/repos more than everyone' goal: deduplicate identical chunks before zstd, and offer a manifest mode where a .nest references external sources instead of inlining them. Both shrink the container without touching the embedding hot path.
repos.perf_notes: No SIMD, no entropy coding, no on-disk binary format — pure filesystem-of-JSON plus CSV. Performance characteristic worth noting is the parallel-reconstruction harness: a Flask key-broker fronts num_process workers to amortize external API rate limits, a useful pattern for nest-cli batch-build throughput but irrelevant to the mmap/SIMD serving path. Dedup magnitude depends on object sharing (users/tweets recur heavily across news items), so structural savings are corpus-dependent, not guaranteed.
repos.license: Repository is research/academic; code under an open-source license (no SPDX header prominently shown), but the underlying tweet/news payloads are NOT redistributable (Twitter ToS + publisher copyright) — which is precisely why the dehydration pattern exists. Treat as reference-only for ideas, not vendored code.

repos.one_liner: A balanced PT-BR fake-news corpus of 11,902 labeled samples (5,951 fake / 5,951 real) shipped as a single XLSX with an 8-column metadata schema (Title, Sub-title, News, Category, Author, Date, URL, Class), crawled and aggregated from 6 fact-check agencies and 4 reputable news portals.
repos.core_innovation: The transferable idea is a per-record structured-provenance schema for fact-checking data: every sample carries not just text + a binary truth label (Class 0/1) but the full origin chain (source agency/portal, original URL, publication Date, Category), with engineered class balance and source diversity to avoid the leakage bias where fake and real come from disjoint stylistic distributions. Fakes are aggregated across 6 independent fact-checkers, making the corpus a multi-source consensus rather than a single-feed scrape.
key_techniques: 8-column flat metadata schema per record (title, subtitle, body, category, author, date, url, class) in a single XLSX container
Binary truth label encoding Class in {0=fake, 1=real} as a first-class column
Multi-agency aggregation: 6 fact-check sources merged into one fake-news pool with source attribution preserved
Class balancing by downsampling 100k+ real samples to 5,951 to match the fake count
Fixed 6-category partition (Health, Politics, Entertainment, Brazil, Science, World) from journal sections
Source-decoupling anti-bias design: fake and real drawn from unrelated outlets so they are not topic-paired
Classical baseline: TF-IDF/bag-of-words features feeding Naive Bayes, SVM, Optimum-Path Forest, plus a CNN
repos.nest_application: nest steals the data model, not an algorithm. (1) nest-python build path: ingest the XLSX demo corpus, mapping News body to chunks_canonical(text) and (Title, Category, Author, Date, URL, Class, source-agency) into the provenance section as per-chunk structured metadata, giving the existing PT-BR demo corpus a real truth-label field. (2) nest-format provenance: adopt the origin-chain shape (source + url + date + category + truth-class) as the canonical fact-check provenance record, kept additive on existing provenance bytes (reserve a new section id 0x09+ only if a typed truth field is wanted; never bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION). The original URL maps onto nest's citation model so nest://content_hash/chunk_id resolves back to the upstream article. (3) nest-cli search-text: Category and Class become filterable demo facets; the low-cardinality enums compress to near-zero under existing zstd.
repos.compression_relevance: Low/indirect. The repo ships no codec, quantizer, or index -- it is raw XLSX text. Relevance is twofold: (a) the low-cardinality enum columns (Class 2 values, Category 6 values, ~10 source agencies) are highly compressible by nest's existing zstd-on-non-embedding-sections path and serve as a clean fixture to validate metadata compression; (b) the 11,902-sample PT-BR body text is a realistic real-world corpus to benchmark the tiny preset (zstd/int8/hnsw, 0.283 size ratio, recall@10 0.992) on the exact misinformation domain nest demos, rather than synthetic data. No new compression technique is transferable from here.
repos.perf_notes: No runtime, SIMD, or throughput characteristics -- it is a static ~11.9k-row XLSX (single file, a few MB). The only perf-adjacent note is that its 8-column metadata is tiny and enum-heavy, so it adds negligible bytes to a .nest provenance section and negligible cost to mmap/scan.
repos.license: Not clearly stated in the README; the dataset accompanies an academic paper (Garcia, Afonso, Papa; BRACIS/PROPOR 2022, LNCS/LNAI 13208). Treat as research-use; verify upstream license before redistributing inside a .nest demo container.

repos.one_liner:
A 1,309-row UTF-8 TSV corpus of Brazilian Portuguese fact-checks (9 columns) harvested from agency RSS feeds by parsing schema.org ClaimReview JSON-LD, where each claim carries a normalizable truthfulness rating (ratingValue / bestRating + human-readable alternativeName label).</one_liner>
<parameter name="core_innovation">The schema.org ClaimReview/reviewRating data model as a portable, normalized "truth verdict": a claim is represented by claimReviewed (text), a numeric ratingValue on a per-agency scale with bestRating as the scale maximum, and an alternativeName string label (e.g. "falso", "verdadeiro"). Dividing ratingValue/bestRating yields a source-agnostic truthfulness score in [0,1] that lets you fuse incompatible agency label vocabularies into one comparable axis. The harvesting is itself a clean ETL: pull JSON-LD (application/ld+json) out of fact-check pages, map reviewRating fields directly to columns, drop exact-row duplicates with URL as implicit primary key.
key_techniques: schema.org ClaimReview JSON-LD extraction from <script type=application/ld+json> tags via feedparser + BeautifulSoup findAll
reviewRating triple: ratingValue (numeric), bestRating (scale max), alternateName (text label) -> normalized truth score = ratingValue/bestRating in [0,1]
field-to-column direct mapping (url, author.url, datePublished, claimReviewed, reviewBody/description fallback, ratingValue, bestRating, alternateName, itemReviewed.@type)
text normalization: re_char() strips non-ASCII except PT accented chars, saxutils.unescape() for HTML entities
exact-row drop_duplicates() dedup with URL as primary key
UTF-8 TSV (tab-separated) flat-table on-disk format, 9 columns x 1309 rows
repos.nest_application: This is a truth-feature / provenance pattern, not a compression codec, so it lands in nest-format provenance + the demo corpus pipeline rather than the codec layer. Two concrete adaptations: (1) Extend the provenance section schema in nest-format (crates/nest-format/src/sections, additive within v1 since provenance is already required) to carry an optional per-chunk verdict record {rating_value:u16 LE, best_rating:u16 LE, label_id:u8} mirroring reviewRating, with label strings interned in a small dictionary, so a chunk that is a fact-checked claim ships its normalized truthfulness alongside its content_hash citation. (2) In the python builder (nest-python / build pipeline that ships the PT-BR fake-news demo corpus), add a ClaimReview JSON-LD ingester that maps reviewRating -> the new provenance fields and computes ratingValue/bestRating as a deterministic normalized score. This directly enriches nest's existing demo domain (it already ships PT-BR fake-news datasets) and gives nest a real "truth feature": nest://content_hash/chunk_id citations can then return both the exact byte span AND its agency verdict, deterministically. Because labels are dictionary-interned u8 ids and the verdict struct is tiny repr(C) LE integers, it also compresses well under the existing zstd path on non-embedding sections.
repos.compression_relevance: Low for raw byte-compression: the dataset is a 1,309-row TSV with no entropy coder, quantization, or codec to steal. Its compression-adjacent value is schema compactness: representing a verdict as ratingValue/bestRating/label_id (a few LE integers + a dictionary id) instead of free-text labels is a small domain-specific dictionary-coding win, and storing labels as interned u8 ids rather than repeated UTF-8 strings reduces provenance-section size before zstd. So it is relevant only as a tiny structured-field encoding pattern for the provenance section, not as a general compression technique.
repos.core_innovation: The schema.org ClaimReview/reviewRating data model as a portable normalized truth verdict, harvested from JSON-LD, where ratingValue/bestRating yields a source-agnostic truthfulness score in [0,1] that unifies incompatible per-agency label vocabularies.
repos.perf_notes: No performance characteristics of interest: pure-Python offline ETL (feedparser + BeautifulSoup + requests), no SIMD, no on-disk index, no large-scale data. The TSV is tiny (~1,309 rows). Only the score-normalization formula and the verdict-field layout transfer; nothing about throughput or memory is relevant to nest's hot path (and nothing here touches embeddings, which nest never compresses on the scoring path).
repos.license: MIT (dataset code); paper publication rights licensed to ACM (DOI 10.1145/3323503.3361698)

repos.one_liner: A labeled fact-checking dataset (not software): 7,200 length-aligned Brazilian-Portuguese news articles (3,600 fake / 3,600 true) shipped as numbered plain-text files plus a fixed 25-field line-by-line linguistic-metadata schema per article and a stopword/diacritic-normalized preprocessed CSV variant.
repos.core_innovation: The pairwise size-normalization protocol: every fake article is matched to a true counterpart on the same topic, and the longer text in each pair is truncated (by word count) to the shorter one's length, producing a corpus where length cannot leak the label. This controlled-pair construction is the transferable methodological idea, not any compression or indexing technique.
key_techniques: Length-aligned fake/true pairing: longer member of each pair truncated by word count to remove length-as-label leakage (size_normalized_texts/)
Fixed 25-field line-by-line metadata schema per doc: author, link, category, date, then 21 numeric linguistic features

Hand-crafted truth features: pausality (punctuation count / sentence count), emotiveness (affective-term ratio), type-token diversity, spelling-error percentage, avg sentence/word length, POS counts (verbs, subjunctive/imperative, modal, pronouns)
Three parallel corpus variants from one source: full_texts (raw), size_normalized_texts (truncated), preprocessed (stopword-removed + accent-folded CSV)
Numbered filename convention (NNNN.txt / NNNN-meta.txt) as the join key aligning a doc, its label folder, and its metadata
Empirical baseline: SVM + bag-of-words reaches ~89% F-measure; the 21 hand-crafted features add almost nothing over BOW
repos.nest_application: Two concrete uses. (1) Demo corpus: nest already ships PT-BR fake-news data; this is the canonical aligned source. Build a tiny-preset .nest (zstd/int8/hnsw) over the 7,200 docs so chunks_canonical holds raw text, embeddings hold sentence-transformer vectors, and provenance records label+category+source-url per chunk -- a flagship offline single-file fact-check demo at ~0.283 size ratio. (2) Truth features as provenance: the 25-field metadata maps into nest-format's provenance section (additive, no format bump -- provenance is an existing v1 section whose meaning is unchanged). Store pausality/emotiveness/spelling-error-rate as per-chunk numeric provenance fields, surface them via nest-cli inspect/stats so a nest://content_hash/chunk_id citation shows credibility metadata next to the text span. Features are cheap deterministic single-pass counts (regex/POS over canonical text), computable at build time in nest-python with no model, fitting offline/deterministic constraints.
repos.compression_relevance: Low to none. This repo contributes zero compression machinery -- no entropy coder, quantization, or on-disk format; data is uncompressed numbered .txt plus CSV. Indirect relevance: the size-normalization (truncate-to-shorter-pair) is a domain-specific length-cap heuristic, and the corpus is a realistic payload to benchmark nest's tiny preset (int8 + zstd-on-text + hnsw) and content_hash stability. The truth features are metadata to carry, not bytes to shrink.
repos.perf_notes: Static dataset, no runtime. Small: 7,200 short-to-medium PT-BR articles (fake avg ~216 tokens, true avg ~1,268 tokens), on the order of a few MB of text, trivially mmappable and fully resident; ideal small fixture for deterministic-build and recall@10 regression tests. The 21 linguistic features are O(n) single-pass token/punctuation counters, no SIMD or heavy compute needed.
repos.license: Academic/research use; corpus released with PROPOR 2018 (Monteiro et al.) and Expert Systems with Applications 2020 (Silva et al.). No explicit OSS license file in repo -- treat as research-use, cite the papers; verify before redistributing inside a shipped .nest demo.

repos.one_liner: A Poetry/Makefile-orchestrated PT-BR fake-news ML benchmark that converts the Fake.Br and FakeTrue.Br corpora into Parquet, then trains/tunes logreg+TF-IDF, MLP+TF-IDF, BiLSTM, and BERTimbau (Portuguese BERT) classifiers via Optuna with HuggingFace-published artifacts.
repos.core_innovation: Deterministic, length-debiasing "size-normalized pair truncation": for each aligned true/fake news pair, the longer document is truncated by word count to exactly match the shorter one, so a model cannot cheat on document length as a proxy signal. This is a reproducible corpus transform that yields a fairer, smaller, paired dataset — applicable as a deterministic preprocessing/normalization step for nest's demo corpus.
key_techniques: Size-normalized truncation: per true/fake pair, truncate longer text to shorter text's word count (deterministic length-debiasing)

25-field per-article linguistic/stylometric metadata schema: POS counts (verbs, nouns, adjectives, modal verbs, pronoun persons), pausality, char/sentence/word averages, spelling-error %, emotiveness, diversity
Parquet conversion of raw CSV/txt corpora as a single columnar prep step (make data_prep)
TF-IDF n-gram vectorization with tunable ngram_upper/min_df/max_df sparse text features
BERTimbau (Portuguese BERT) contextual embeddings as strong baseline; HuggingFace artifact publishing for reproducible model identity
Optuna study-based hyperparameter search persisted to a SQL backend (replayable trials)
Aligned true/fake corpus design (Fake.Br: 2000+2000 paired articles) enabling paired evaluation
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) In nest-python's demo-corpus builder (the PT-BR fake-news dataset that ships with nest), add an optional deterministic "pair-normalize" preprocessing pass mirroring size_normalized_texts: word-count-truncate aligned pairs before chunking. nest builds are already deterministic (same chunks + model fingerprint => byte-identical file), so this transform is reproducible and shrinks the corpus, improving the demo's compression ratio honestly without touching the FROZEN format. (2) The 25-field stylometric metadata schema is an ideal payload for a future "truth-features" sidecar: encode it as a fixed repr(C), little-endian, per-chunk struct array stored inside the existing provenance section (no new section id, stays additive within v1). These are cheap-to-compute, int/float-quantizable features (int8/float16 codecs already exist) giving nest a sovereign credibility signal co-located with each chunk and citable via nest://content_hash/chunk_id. Neither touches nest-runtime's hot path or the exact-cosine search contract.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect.
