Size-normalized truncation is a lossy-but-deterministic corpus transform that legitimately reduces demo-corpus bytes (and embedding count), improving nest's headline size ratio on its shipped PT-BR fake-news dataset. The stylometric features are quantization-friendly (int8/float16) but are additive metadata, not a general entropy coder, so they add bytes rather than remove them. No new codec, graph layout, or SIMD kernel here that advances the "compress more than everyone" north star.
repos.perf_notes: Pure Python/sklearn/PyTorch training pipeline; no SIMD, no custom on-disk format, no compression codec. BERTimbau inference is the throughput bottleneck. Parquet (likely Snappy/zstd column compression) is the only storage-efficiency mechanism. Nothing performance-relevant transfers to nest's mmap+SIMD runtime; the value is entirely in the corpus-prep and metadata-schema layer.
repos.license: Repository license not confirmed from README; underlying Fake.Br corpus is research-released and FACTCK.BR is MIT. Treat the classifiers repo license as unknown/unverified before vendoring any code; the size-normalization and metadata schema are method ideas (not copyrightable) safe to reimplement.

repos.one_liner: A curated corpus-of-corpora that scrapes fact-checking sites (Snopes, BuzzFeed, PolitiFact, Emergent) and stores each article as a row carrying the original news text, the checked claim, the source URL, the fact-checker's native veracity rating, and a hand-normalized truth label projected onto a common ordinal scale.
repos.core_innovation: A dual-label veracity normalization schema preserving both original and normalized truth labels per record.
key_techniques: Per-record dual labels: original_label (verbatim fact-checker string) + normalized_label (mapped ordinal), so the projection is lossless w.r.t. provenance
Heterogeneous-scale unification: collapse 2/4/5/6-way fact-checker taxonomies onto one canonical ordinal {false, mostly-false, mixture, mostly-true, true} with optional binary {fake, real} reduction
Provenance triple per row: source fact-checker id + original article URL + checked claim string, enabling reopen/re-verification
Out-of-scale rating handling: non-veracity Snopes ratings (Outdated, Miscaptioned, Satire) routed to explicit side categories rather than forced onto the truth axis
Two-stage curation: automatic scraper crawl then manual annotator alignment verification of claim<->article<->label (Figure Eight crowd platform for larger sets)
CSV-as-interchange: flat columns (claim, text, url, original_label, normalized_label) zipped per collection
repos.nest_application: nest-format: add an OPTIONAL truth/veracity metadata section (reserve a v1-additive section id in the 0x09+ space) that attaches, per chunk_id, a small fixed record {source_id:u16 LE, original_label_idx:u8, normalized_ordinal:u8 (0..=4 false..true), claim_chunk_ref, source_url provenance ref}. All integers little-endian unsigned, repr(C), deterministic. Store the source-label <-> ordinal mapping table once in the provenance/manifest section so normalization is reproducible and byte-stable (same mapping => same bytes). This pairs cleanly with the existing chunks_canonical/chunks_original_spans split: original_label is the "original span," normalized_ordinal is the "canonical" derived value. nest-runtime: expose a label filter/facet on the search path (post-rerank predicate on normalized_ordinal, e.g. return only false<=1 claims) and let cite emit nest://content_hash/chunk_id pointing at the exact checked claim. nest-cli: extend stats to histogram the ordinal distribution. Compression relevance: the ordinal is a u8 (or 3 bits) and source_id is small-cardinality, so the truth column is a textbook target for the int8/zstd path already in nest -- dictionary-encode source labels and bit-pack the 5-level ordinal, turning verbose fact-checker strings ("Pants on Fire!") into ~3 bits while keeping the verbatim string recoverable via the mapping table; this is real per-section compression on the PT-BR fake-news demo corpus nest already ships.
repos.compression_relevance: Direct: veracity labels are low-cardinality categoricals. The dual-label idea lets nest store a verbose source string once in a manifest mapping table, then represent each row's truth value as a 3-bit ordinal + small source_id, bit-packed and zstd'd on the non-embedding path. Verbose label text collapses to a few bits per chunk while staying losslessly recoverable, a clean win for the demo corpus and for the broader "compress datasets" north star.
repos.perf_notes: No runtime/codec engineering here -- this is a data resource, not a system. Volumes are tiny by nest standards (largest published collections ~1.3k-12.8k rows; CSV-zipped). No SIMD, no on-disk binary format, no index. The only perf-relevant fact is that the truth column is extremely low entropy (<=6 distinct values), so it costs near-zero space under nest's existing int8/zstd encodings and adds negligible scoring cost as a post-rerank facet predicate.
repos.license: Not clearly stated in README; datasets aggregate third-party fact-checker content (Snopes/PolitiFact/BuzzFeed/Emergent) under their respective terms plus academic-citation requests (Asr & Taboada 2019, Big Data & Society). Treat as reference/citation-ware, not a vendorable code license -- do not bundle the data, only adopt the schema idea.

repos.one_liner: A pure-Python RSS pipeline that fetches feeds, deduplicates and clusters near-duplicate articles via TF-IDF/cosine + agglomerative clustering, LLM-rewrites each cluster, and scores output with a ~30-metric text-quality evaluation suite (BLEU/ROUGE-L/METEOR/CIDEr/NIST, edit/Levenshtein/Hamming, TF-IDF & BoW & LSA cosine, plus readability indices) merged into a single weighted Ugly Score.
repos.core_innovation: A deterministic, dependency-light recipe for collapsing a corpus of near-duplicate documents into representative clusters: build a sparse vectorizer (tfidf/count/hashing with configurable ngram_range, min_df/max_df), compute a dense cosine-similarity matrix, convert to a precomputed distance matrix (1 - sim, clamped to >=0), then run AgglomerativeClustering(metric=precomputed, linkage=average, distance_threshold=0.66, n_clusters=None). Cluster cohesion is reported as the mean pairwise intra-cluster similarity. This is a pre-storage dedup/segmentation primitive that directly reduces how many documents you must store at all.
key_techniques: TF-IDF/Count/Hashing vectorizer with ngram_range, max_df=0.85, min_df=0.01 to bound vocabulary
Cosine-similarity matrix -> precomputed distance (1-sim clamped >=0) feeding AgglomerativeClustering(linkage=average, distance_threshold, n_clusters=None) for threshold-driven near-duplicate grouping
Alternative clustering backends behind one config key: DBSCAN(metric=precomputed,eps,min_samples) and KMeans
Mean intra-cluster pairwise similarity as a per-group cohesion/confidence score stored with the group
Exact-dedup pre-pass keyed on (content, link) tuple-set before expensive vectorization
Reference-free readability/lexical battery: Gunning-Fog, SMOG, Coleman-Liau, ARI, type-token ratio, lexical density, entropy
Reference-based similarity battery: BLEU-n via Counter n-gram intersection, ROUGE-L/LCS, METEOR, CIDEr, NIST, Jaccard/Dice/Overlap, WER
Normalize-then-weighted-sum aggregation of ~30 heterogeneous metrics into one scalar (per-metric max-value normalization to 0-100, fixed weight vector)
repos.nest_application: Two targeted lifts. (1) A nest-python build-time dedup/cluster pass (Python is the builder, so sklearn-class deps are acceptable): before embedding/encoding, run TF-IDF-or-embedding cosine + agglomerative threshold clustering to detect near-duplicate chunks; keep one canonical chunk per cluster and record collapsed members as additive provenance metadata, so chunks_canonical shrinks at the source. Pure pre-compression leverage (fewer chunks = fewer embeddings, the dominant byte cost) and stays deterministic if you fix linkage=average plus a sorted tie-break, matching nest reproducible-build rule. (2) For nest-runtime bm25 path, this repo confirms the TF-IDF/cosine-over-sparse-vectors recipe and the precomputed-distance trick; nest already does mandatory exact cosine rerank, so the reusable bit is the cluster cohesion score (mean intra-group similarity) as a cheap storable confidence signal for a future graph-search/dedup section (reserved section id 0x09+). The ~30-metric eval suite is reference material for a nest-cli benchmark/quality-report surface and for scoring the shipped PT-BR fake-news demo corpus, not core-format code.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: agglomerative near-duplicate clustering is a dedup primitive that can run at build time in nest-python to drop redundant chunks before embeddings are generated, attacking the single largest byte cost (per-chunk f32/f16/int8 vectors) at its source. It compresses corpus cardinality, orthogonal to and multiplicative with nest per-section codecs (zstd/f16/int8). The metric suite itself compresses nothing.
repos.perf_notes: O(n^2) memory/time: materializes a dense n-by-n cosine-similarity and distance matrix with precomputed-metric agglomerative clustering, so it does not scale past a few thousand docs per batch (fine for RSS, a hard wall for whole databases). KMeans/agglomerative call vectors.toarray(), densifying the sparse TF-IDF matrix. For nest, any borrowed dedup pass must be blocked/batched or swapped to an ANN-neighbor graph (nest already ships HnswIndex) to avoid quadratic blowup. Pure Python/sklearn/nltk/spacy stack, no SIMD, no native kernels worth importing into the Rust core.
repos.license: AGPL-3.0 (copyleft; vendoring source into a permissive core is incompatible, so reimplement the algorithm cleanly rather than copying code).

synthesis.summary: This category contributes zero codec/SIMD/on-disk machinery to nest's "compress more than everyone" north star; every repo is either a dataset or a pure-Python LLM/sklearn framework. Its real value is domain modeling for the demo corpus and a credible "truth feature" narrative, plus three structural-compression levers (dedup-by-reference, near-duplicate clustering, low-cardinality enum dictionary-coding) that attack corpus cardinality before the codec runs. The collective state of the art is a converged "claim -> evidence -> stance/verdict -> justification" pipeline with a normalizable veracity axis (FEVER 3-way SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEI; ClaimReview ratingValue/bestRating in [0,1]; dual original+normalized labels). Critically, nest's provenance section (0x05) is already a schema-free per-build JSON blob (crates/nest-format/src/sections/provenance.rs) threaded straight from Python (build_fn.rs), so nearly all "truth feature" work is additive metadata + a post-rerank facet in search.rs materialize_hits — NO new section id, NO NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump. Most extracts over-reach by proposing reserved sections 0x09+; for v1 that is unnecessary except for true graph topology. The one genuinely structured Rust opportunity is TabFact's typed-operator DSL (deterministic symbolic table verification), but it is a large new subsystem and should stay roadmap-only.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: The field has converged on a four-stage pipeline (claim detection/check-worthiness -> evidence retrieval -> verdict prediction -> justification) over a normalizable veracity axis. Three labeling schemes dominate and interconvert: FEVER 3-way SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NOT-ENOUGH-INFO (NEI = explicit abstention); Factcheck-GPT/OpenFactCheck stance vocabularies (CP/PS/RE/IR collapsible to 3-way, or True/False/Unknown ternary); and schema.org ClaimReview's numeric ratingValue/bestRating giving a source-agnostic [0,1] truth score, with MisInfoText's dual-label idea (keep verbatim original_label AND a normalized ordinal {false..true}) making the projection lossless. Evidence is granularity-typed (sentence/document/table/multi-hop chain/conversation) and bound to spans (Wikipedia sentence ids), directly analogous to nest://content_hash/chunk_id. Two divergent verification paradigms: (a) retrieve-then-verify with neural similarity + LLM stance (FactCheck-GPT, OpenFactCheck — but these are online/LLM-bound, violating nest's offline-by-construction rule), and (b) TabFact's deterministic symbolic execution — compile NL statements into a closed ~60-op typed DSL with trigger-word gating and memoized beam search, where the program's boolean OUTPUT is the verdict (fully reproducible, explainable, no learned score). On the data-engineering side: FakeNewsNet's dehydration (ship manifest + content-addressed object pool, hydrate on demand) and GNN-FakeNews's two-plane split (integer graph topology via COO+partition-index vs float feature matrices, different codecs each) are the transferable storage patterns. PT-BR demo sources (Fake.br, FakeRecogna, FACTCK.BR, FakeTrue.Br) ship aligned/length-debiased corpora with 8-25 field metadata schemas.
top_innovations: ClaimReview ratingValue/bestRating normalized [0,1] verdict (FACTCK.BR)
Dual original+normalized ordinal label, lossless projection (MisInfoText)
Dedup-by-reference + dehydrated manifest mode (FakeNewsNet)
Build-time near-duplicate clustering to cut embedding count (UglyFeed)
Two-plane integer-topology vs float-feature codec split (GNN-FakeNews)
TabFact typed-operator DSL, boolean output IS the verdict (TabFact)
Atomic-claim -> evidence -> stance -> verdict record schema (FactCheck-GPT)
Deterministic size-normalization pair truncation (Fake.br)
Register-by-name pipeline-as-data in search_contract (OpenFactCheck)
Aligned multi-source PT-BR corpora with enum-heavy metadata (FakeRecogna)

nest_recommendations.idea: Define a documented per-chunk truth record carried INSIDE the existing schema-free provenance JSON blob: {chunk_id, verdict_ordinal:u8 (0=false..4=true, with an explicit NEI/unverified sentinel), rating_value:u16, best_rating:u16, source_id:u16, label_dict_id:u8}, plus a once-stored source_label<->ordinal mapping table. No new section id, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump — provenance (0x05) already decodes arbitrary JSON and is threaded from Python untouched.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/sections/provenance.rs (document the convention only; encoder already accepts any serde_json::Value) and crates/nest-python/src/build_fn.rs (provenance dict already passed through, lines 89-96)
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Add an optional post-rerank verdict facet/predicate to the search path: after the mandatory exact cosine rerank, filter or boost hits by verdict_ordinal (e.g. return only verdict<=mostly-false). Must run STRICTLY after rerank so the returned score stays real cosine and the search contract is untouched; verdict comes from the decoded provenance map, an O(1) enum compare per hit.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime/src/search.rs materialize_hits (lines 229-256) — add an optional predicate over a per-index verdict slice loaded at open time; surface as a flag in crates/nest-cli/src/cmd/search.rs and search_ann.rs
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

nest_recommendations.idea: Extend the cite subcommand to print the truth record + normalized verdict + evidence citations alongside the byte span, so nest://content_hash/chunk_id returns BOTH the exact span AND its agency verdict deterministically. Add a parallel `verify` alias if cite's output gets crowded.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-cli/src/cmd/cite.rs (after line 60, decode provenance and print verdict fields; already decodes chunk_ids/canonical/spans)
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

nest_recommendations.idea: Add a pure-Python ingester layer that maps fact-check sources into the truth-record provenance shape: ClaimReview JSON-LD (ratingValue/bestRating -> normalized [0,1]), FakeRecogna XLSX (8-col), Fake.br/FakeTrue.Br (25-field stylometry + length-normalized pairs), FACTCK.BR TSV. Computes verdict_ordinal + normalized score deterministically at build time; no model, no network — fully offline.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: python/ demo-corpus builder (the PT-BR ingestion scripts) feeding the provenance kwarg of nest_python build()
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Build-time near-duplicate dedup pass: before embedding, cluster chunks by cosine + agglomerative threshold (reuse the HnswIndex neighbor graph to avoid UglyFeed's O(n^2) dense-matrix blowup), keep one canonical chunk per cluster, record collapsed members + cohesion score as provenance. Fewer chunks = fewer embeddings = the dominant byte cost removed at source. Deterministic if linkage + sorted tie-break are fixed (matches reproducible-build rule).
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: python/ build pipeline as an optional pre-pass before nest_python build(); cohesion metadata into provenance. Reuses crates/nest-runtime ann::HnswIndex for neighbor candidates instead of a dense matrix
nest_recommendations.impact: high

nest_recommendations.idea: Deterministic size-normalization corpus transform for the demo: for each aligned true/fake pair, word-count-truncate the longer doc to the shorter's length before chunking. Legitimately shrinks demo bytes + embedding count and debiases length-as-label leakage; reproducible because nest builds are byte-deterministic given identical chunks.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: python/ demo-corpus prep (before chunking, feeds build()); document as the canonical PT-BR demo transform
nest_recommendations.impact: low

nest_recommendations.idea: ROADMAP ONLY (reserved section id 0x09+, no v1 bump): two-plane graph topology section for propagation/evidence graphs — integer COO edge list (delta+varint+zstd) + a node->graph partition index, stored separately from float features which stay on the existing embedding path. This is the concrete data layout for the mission's planned graph search and multi-hop evidence chains. Out of scope for v1; only the additive section-id reservation is in play now.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/layout/mod.rs (reserve a SECTION_GRAPH_EDGES = 0x09 constant + OPTIONAL_SECTIONS entry, additive, excluded from content_hash); future crates/nest-runtime graph module
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

nest_recommendations.idea: ROADMAP ONLY: a structured-query / symbolic verification path beside cosine/hnsw/bm25 — a small Rust enum of TabFact-style typed ops (filter_eq, greater, count, argmax, within, before/after) over a future tabular/parquet section, with a trigger-word->op-id dictionary and memoized seeded beam search. The boolean program output is a real, citable verdict, turning retrieval into explainable verification. Split ops/exec/search files to stay <=300 loc, typed thiserror, no panic. Large subsystem — defer past v1 core.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-runtime new structured-query module (ops.rs/exec.rs/search.rs); op-code table + trigger-word map as an additive section 0x0A+ in nest-format
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

nest_recommendations.idea: ROADMAP ONLY: a dehydrated/manifest mode where a .nest stores stable external source refs (id + url) instead of inlining heavy payloads, deterministically re-hydrating chunks on demand. Combined with content_hash dedup-by-reference, this is the lever for 'compress whole datasets/repos more than everyone' without bloating the container or touching the embedding hot path. Needs an additive RESERVED section for source refs.
nest_recommendations.where_in_nest: crates/nest-format/src/layout/mod.rs (reserve a source-refs section id) + python builder hydration logic; sits beside the dedup pass
nest_recommendations.impact: medium

compression_wins: Low-cardinality verdict/category enums are textbook dictionary-coding wins: store the verbose source label string once in a manifest mapping table, then represent each chunk's truth value as a 3-bit/u8 normalized ordinal + small source_id, bit-packed and zstd'd on the existing non-embedding path. 'Pants on Fire!' -> ~3 bits, losslessly recoverable. Class (2 values), Category (6 values), ~10 agencies all collapse to near-zero bytes (MisInfoText, FACTCK.BR, FakeRecogna).

Build-time near-duplicate dedup (agglomerative/ANN-neighbor clustering) attacks corpus CARDINALITY — fewer chunks means fewer per-chunk f32/f16/int8 embedding vectors, which are the single largest byte cost. This is orthogonal to and multiplicative with the per-section codecs (zstd/f16/int8), and is the highest-leverage compression idea in the category (UglyFeed, FakeNewsNet).

Dedup-by-reference: deduplicate identical canonical spans before zstd and emit pointer indices in chunk_ids, storing each duplicate span once — exactly the same principle as nest's content_hash dedup, applied at chunk granularity (FakeNewsNet).

ClaimReview ratingValue/bestRating as two u16 LE + the derived [0,1] score stored implicitly via the mapping table: a compact domain-specific encoding that replaces free-text rating labels (FACTCK.BR).

Two-plane integer-vs-float split for graph topology: COO edge lists are sorted, low-entropy id streams that compress brutally with delta+varint+zstd, kept on the non-embedding path while float features stay raw-mmap on the hot path. Right codec for the right statistics (GNN-FakeNews).

Deterministic size-normalization (truncate longer pair member to shorter's word count) legitimately reduces demo-corpus bytes AND embedding count while debiasing length-as-label, without touching the FROZEN format (Fake.br).

Closed operator vocabulary + trigger-word dictionary (if the symbolic-query path is ever built) is a tiny fixed symbol table that zstd-compresses near-perfectly; command-string-hash memoization is structural subexpression dedup, the same dedup principle as content_hash (TabFact).
watch_outs: Most extracts reflexively propose a NEW section id (0x09+) for truth metadata. This is unnecessary and risks scope creep: provenance (0x05) is already a schema-free per-build JSON blob (provenance.rs only enforces 'parses as JSON') threaded straight from Python (build_fn.rs lines 89-96). Carry verdict records THERE for v1 — no new section, no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump. Reserve 0x09+ only for genuine graph topology / structured-op tables, which are roadmap.

FactCheck-GPT, OpenFactCheck and FactCheck-GPT's retrieval are online/LLM-bound (GPT-3.5 per claim, Google/Serper search per claim). nest is offline-by-construction and NEVER opens a socket — adopt only the static data SCHEMA, computed once at build time; never replicate the live retrieval/LLM calls. The 'BM25-over-offline-Wikipedia' tier merely validates nest's existing bm25_index(0x08).

Per-chunk verdict provenance must NOT live in the canonical six sections that feed content_hash, or every label re-annotation would invalidate all citations. Carry it in the schema-free provenance blob (which IS one of the canonical six but whose meaning is unchanged) being careful that adding fields stays byte-stable and deterministic, OR in a future OPTIONAL section explicitly excluded from content_hash. Confirm whichever path keeps citations stable across re-labeling.

Any verdict facet/filter MUST run strictly AFTER the mandatory exact cosine rerank in materialize_hits — the returned score must remain real cosine, never a verdict-weighted proxy. Do not let a 'boost by verdict' knob leak into the score the search contract guarantees.

UglyFeed's clustering is AGPL-3.0 (copyleft) and materializes a dense O(n^2) cosine/distance matrix that walls at a few thousand docs — reimplement the algorithm cleanly (do not vendor) AND swap the dense matrix for nest's existing HnswIndex neighbor graph to avoid quadratic blowup on whole-database corpora.

Dataset LICENSING is the real ship-blocker: FEVER/FEVEROUS/TabFact are Wikipedia-derived CC BY-SA (share-alike); UPFD (GNN-FakeNews) and FakeNewsNet payloads are academic-only / not redistributable (Twitter ToS); FakeRecogna, Fake.br, MisInfoText have no clear OSS license. Vendor the loader/schema PATTERNS, not the raw corpora, and license-vet every dataset individually before shipping it in a .nest demo container. FACTCK.BR (MIT), Factcheck-GPT/OpenFactCheck (Apache-2.0), Automated-Fact-Checking-Resources (MIT) are the safe schema sources.

The bm25 tokenizer is word-segmented (confirmed in bm25/tokenize.rs: splits on non-alphanumerics) and degrades on CJK/Thai — fine for the PT-BR demo (it handles ã/ç/õ via char iteration) but do not over-invest a multilingual fact-check narrative on top of it without addressing the known tokenizer gap first.

The TabFact symbolic DSL and the graph-topology section are genuinely valuable but are LARGE new subsystems (multiple Rust files, new section ids, beam-search engine). They conflict with the small-core / <=300-loc-per-file / minimal-budget reality of a solo author — keep them firmly roadmap-only and ship the additive provenance truth-feature + dedup wins first.

categories.name: bindings-cli
categories.focus: language bindings, CLI ergonomics, distribution/client surfaces

repos.one_liner: PyO3 is a macro-driven Rust<->CPython FFI binding layer that compiles a single cdylib extension module against Python's stable ABI (abi3 / Py_LIMITED_API) and enforces GIL-correct, refcount-correct interop at compile time via lifetime-tagged smart pointers (Python<'py>, Bound<'py,T>, Py<T>).
repos.core_innovation: The "stable ABI as a build feature, not a source macro" model: opting into abi3-pyXY via a Cargo feature makes the linker emit only Py_LIMITED_API symbols, so ONE compiled .so/.pyd is loadable by every CPython >= XY without recompilation -- decoupling the binary artifact from the interpreter patch version. Paired with this is the zero-copy borrow discipline: Bound<'py,T> is morally (Py<T>, Python<'py>) and the buffer protocol / PyBuffer<T> let Rust read a Python array's backing memory in place rather than marshalling element-by-element.
key_techniques: abi3 / Py_LIMITED_API: compile against the limited C-API subset so symbols resolve on any future CPython >= floor (lowest abi3-pyXY feature wins); single wheel per OS/arch
abi3t (PEP 803): opaque-PyObject stable-ABI variant loadable on BOTH GIL and free-threaded builds, forward-compatible to all future 3.X
Bound<'py,T> smart pointer = Py<T> handle + Python<'py> GIL-proof token; drops the Python refcount immediately on Drop (no GILPool surprise)
Py<T> as a Send+Sync, GIL-independent Arc-like handle for storing Python objects in Rust structs without a lifetime param
buffer protocol via PyBuffer<f32> / rust-numpy PyReadonlyArray1: borrow a contiguous numpy/array backing store as &[f32] with zero copy
macro codegen: #[pymodule]/#[pyclass]/#[pymethods]/#[pyfunction] generate the limited-API wrapper shims, hiding Py_LIMITED_API entirely
FromPyObject / IntoPyObject trait-based bidirectional marshalling at the FFI boundary
Python::detach (formerly allow_threads): release the GIL around a long Rust compute so other threads run; requires unbinding to Py<T>
repos.nest_application: nest-python already does the right baseline (PyO3 0.28, crate-type=cdylib, features=[\"abi3-py312\"], Bound API in nest_file.rs/lib.rs), so the steal is two concrete upgrades, not adoption. (1) ZERO-COPY QUERY INGESTION on the hot path: nest_file.rs:21-24/34-37/47-56 currently do query.extract::<Vec<f32>>(), a full heap copy of every query embedding (which arrives from the model as a numpy float32 array) before the SIMD dot-product runs. Replace with PyBuffer<f32> (pure-pyo3, no numpy dep, abi3 buffer API is available since py3.11 so py312 floor is fine) or an optional rust-numpy PyReadonlyArray1 feature, borrowing the array's backing memory as &[f32] passed straight to nest-runtime's simd dispatcher -- eliminates one alloc+memcpy per search, complementing the already zero-copy mmap read of stored embeddings. (2) DISTRIBUTION: wire maturin + pyproject.toml (PyPI/maturin is a listed known gap) producing ONE cp312-abi3 manylinux/macos/windows wheel that runs on 3.12/3.13/3.14+, and add the abi3t feature path so the single wheel also loads on free-threaded builds -- this is the entire \"portable, single-file, install-anywhere\" leg of the north star for the python-builds half. Both respect hard constraints: no socket, no panic (keep PyValueError mapping of typed thiserror errors), determinism untouched, and nest-format/nest-runtime stay pure Rust with PyO3 confined to nest-python.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. abi3/abi3t and the macro layer do not compress bytes; their relevance is to the \"portable, cheap, light, install-anywhere\" axis of the north star -- one tiny wheel serving every Python on every OS keeps the distribution surface minimal. The directly load-bearing compression-adjacent idea is the zero-copy buffer-protocol borrow: it keeps the search hot path allocation-free end-to-end (mmap'd compressed/quantized embeddings in, borrowed query in), so the int8/f16/zstd compression wins in nest-format are not paid back as marshalling overhead at the python boundary.
repos.perf_notes: Query path today incurs one Vec<f32> alloc + element marshalling copy per search call (nest_file.rs:21-24); PyBuffer/PyReadonlyArray borrow removes it, leaving only the mmap SIMD kernel cost. abi3 has a small, documented runtime cost vs version-specific builds (cannot inline against a known struct layout) -- acceptable for nest since the hot loop is in pure-Rust nest-runtime, not across the FFI boundary. GIL note: nest searches are read-only against an mmap, so wrapping the nest-runtime compute in Python::detach would let concurrent Python threads issue parallel searches against one open NestFile; deterministic because the file is immutable post-build. PyO3 0.28 requires Rust >= 1.83 (nest is edition 2024 so already on a newer toolchain).
repos.license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (dual-licensed; permissive, compatible with vendoring/linking)

repos.one_liner: A Rust CLI argument parser with a dual builder/derive API, a modular feature-gated crate split (clap_builder/clap_derive/clap_lex/clap_complete/clap_mangen), Jaro-distance typo correction, and a runtime "ask the binary" dynamic shell-completion protocol.
repos.core_innovation: The binary, not a static script, is the source of truth for valid inputs at runtime.
key_techniques: strsim::jaro did_you_mean at 0.7 cutoff, candidates sorted ascending by similarity
CompleteEnv env-var re-exec completion protocol (COMPLETE/_CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX/_CLAP_IFS)
CompletionCandidate type decoupling generation from per-shell rendering
feature-gated crate split (clap re-exports clap_builder) for binary-size minimization
clap_lex OsStr-aware lossless arg tokenizer
derive layer compiling to the same Command/Arg builder model
ArgValueCompleter per-arg dynamic candidate closures
repos.nest_application: nest-cli gets Jaro did_you_mean over its 8 subcommand names (clap's `suggestions` feature, deterministic). Extend the same Jaro scorer over real container chunk_ids (mmapped by nest-runtime) so a missed `nest cite` suggests the nearest valid id without altering the frozen format. Adopt CompleteEnv-style re-exec completion that reads the actual .nest file for content_hash/chunk_id/preset completion, staying offline and single-file. Mirror clap's feature-gated crate split to keep hnsw/bm25/pyo3 opt-in for the smallest sovereign binary.
repos.compression_relevance: n/a directly. clap is a CLI ergonomics/distribution-surface project with no entropy coder, quantizer, or on-disk codec to lift; it does not advance the compress-more-than-everyone north star. Its value to nest is purely the client surface (typo correction, dynamic completion, binary-size minimization), which improves the portable/clean/light pillars but not raw compression ratio.
repos.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual-licensed)
repos.perf_notes: Parsing is allocation-light; clap_lex avoids premature UTF-8 decoding (works on OsStr) and the builder model is the runtime data structure with no reflection. Binary size is controlled by opt-in cargo features rather than a monolith. No SIMD or hot-path numerics relevant to nest's scoring kernels; the Jaro suggestion path runs only on the error branch so its cost is irrelevant. CompleteEnv runs before app init to keep completion latency low, but a nest re-exec would still pay the process-start cost (cheap for the Rust binary, but note the known ~300-500ms python boot overhead must NOT be on this path -- completion must stay in the pure-rust nest-cli/nest-runtime layer).

repos.one_liner: The official Python client for Weaviate: a gRPC/protobuf v4 client where vectors are serialized as length-prefixed flat float32 byte blobs, batching is auto-tuned for throughput, and a VectorType enum tags single vs multi-vector layouts inside one wire field.
repos.core_innovation: Tag-then-pack vector serialization: a single bytes field carries an entire vector (or a flattened multi-vector matrix) as a contiguous little-endian float32 blob, prefixed only with the per-row dimension as a uint16, and disambiguated by a tiny VectorType enum (VECTOR_TYPE_SINGLE_FP32 / MULTI_FP32). One field, one struct.pack call, no per-element protobuf framing -- the dtype/layout lives in a side enum, not in the bytes. This is exactly the "type tag + raw contiguous payload, mmap/decode in one shot" discipline nest needs for its embeddings and named-vector sections.
key_techniques: Vector wire encoding: struct.pack("{}f".format(n), *vec) -> one contiguous float32 blob, zero per-element framing
Multi-vector encoding: struct.pack("<H", row_dim) prefix + flattened float32 matrix; row width from the uint16, count from len(bytes)//(dim*4)
VectorType side-enum (SINGLE_FP32 / MULTI_FP32) tags layout/dtype out-of-band so the payload stays a raw blob -- additive room for future int8/fp16 tags
Symmetric _ByteOps decoder: struct.unpack(f"{len//UINT32_LEN}f") infers element count from byte length, no stored count needed
Three explicit batching policies: dynamic (auto-tunes batch size + concurrency for throughput), fixed_size, rate_limit -- a tuning taxonomy, not one magic knob
Context-manager batch lifecycle with auto-flush on __exit__ and early-abort on error threshold (number_errors)
Layered .proto schema (base -> batch/search_get -> weaviate) keeping wire structs additive and codegen-stable across grpcio/protobuf skew
Producer/consumer queue feeding gRPC unary-unary BatchObjects, decoupling Python object-creation rate from server request concurrency
repos.nest_application: nest-python (the pyo3 builder) and nest-format encoding/sections: adopt the same tag-then-pack discipline for any future named/multi-vector embeddings section. Today nest stores a single embeddings matrix; when it adds named vectors (text + image per chunk), copy Weaviate's layout exactly -- a per-section dtype enum (already implied by nest's encoding ids f32/f16/int8) plus a uint16/uint32 little-endian row-dim prefix, then a contiguous blob the rust runtime mmaps straight into the SIMD dot-product kernel with zero per-element decode. nest already mandates repr(C), little-endian unsigned, contiguous-for-mmap; Weaviate validates that the flat-blob-plus-side-tag shape is correct and shows recovering element count from byte length (len//4) instead of storing a redundant count, saving header bytes. Separately, nest-python's bulk-build path should borrow the producer/consumer + auto-flush + error-threshold batch ergonomics so large-corpus builds stream chunks without holding everything in memory. Relevance to extreme compression: the side-enum-tags-dtype pattern is precisely what lets nest swap f32->f16->int8 per named-vector without touching byte layout or bumping NEST_FORMAT_VERSION, keeping the format additive while the codec gets smaller.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect. No entropy coder or quantization codec here -- vectors ship raw fp32, no compression on the embedding payload. The transferable compression-adjacent lesson is the side-enum-tags-dtype pattern: it makes per-vector dtype (fp32/fp16/int8) a 1-byte tag rather than a layout change, so nest can shrink embedding sections by swapping codecs without format churn. The dimension-as-uint16-prefix + count-from-byte-length trick also shaves redundant header bytes. Batching/throughput work is orthogonal to compression.
repos.perf_notes: Single struct.pack per vector emits a contiguous fp32 blob with no per-element protobuf tag overhead -- the documented "key efficiency feature" of the gRPC path vs the old REST/JSON client. Decode side (_ByteOps) is a single struct.unpack over the whole buffer. Dynamic batching co-tunes batch size and concurrent request count to maximize ingest throughput while bounding memory (no unbounded batch growth). gRPC default port 50051, unary-unary RPCs. Note: this is a network client (REST+gRPC over sockets) -- nest is offline-by-construction and must NOT adopt the transport, only the byte-layout and batch-ergonomics ideas.
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause

repos.one_liner: A native Go client for Weaviate that layers a fluent builder-pattern API over dual GraphQL (precise field selection) and gRPC/protobuf transports, with the gRPC path packing dense vectors as raw little-endian float32 byte blobs rather than repeated proto float fields.
repos.core_innovation: On the gRPC wire path, vectors are not sent as `repeated float` (which costs ~5 bytes/element with protobuf varint+tag framing and forces per-element decode); they are packed into a single opaque `bytes` field carrying contiguous little-endian float32 (the `_Packing{bytes_, type_}` wrapper), with an enum tag discriminating 1D vectors, 2D multi-vectors, and quantized forms. This is exactly nest's hot-path principle: a vector section is one contiguous mmap-able byte run scored directly, never a decode-per-element structure.
key_techniques: gRPC vector byte-packing: dense embeddings serialized as one contiguous little-endian float32 `bytes` blob + a type enum (1D / 2D multivector / quantized), instead of `repeated float` proto fields
relativeScoreFusion: per-result-set min-max normalization (max->1, min->0, linear in between) of vector-distance and BM25 scores, then weighted sum -- an alternative to pure reciprocal-rank fusion
BM25 OR/AND operator with `minimumOrTokensMatch` (minimum_should_match): a tunable knob requiring N of the query tokens to be present before a doc is eligible

Builder-pattern argument unification: every search argument (NearVector, NearObject, Hybrid, BM25, filters) is one typed builder with `WithCertainty/WithLimit/WithTargetVectors/...`, replacing v2's stringly-typed GraphQL/filter construction
Named/target vectors: `WithTargetVectors` selects which of multiple per-object vector spaces to score against in a single request
Transport abstraction with graceful fallback: gRPC enabled when `GrpcConfig` present, else REST/HTTP; cloud auto-derives the gRPC endpoint from the REST URL
API-group partitioning of the surface (Batch/Data/GraphQL/Schema/Backup/...) so each subcommand is a small single-responsibility unit
repos.nest_application: Two concrete steals. (1) Codec/format insight, nest-format encoding + nest-runtime/search.rs: weaviate's `bytes`-not-`repeated-float` packing validates nest's mmap-contiguous embedding layout and points at a cheap win -- when nest exposes vectors over any future bridge (nest-python pyo3 or a thin export), hand back the raw contiguous f32/f16/int8 slice + a 1-byte encoding-id discriminator (mirror of weaviate's type enum) so the consumer slices the mmap directly with zero per-element decode, matching nest's existing encoding ids (raw/zstd/float16/int8) without touching the frozen layout (additive: it is a read-side view, no new section). (2) Search semantics, nest-runtime/bm25 + search.rs: adopt `minimum_should_match`/OR-operator as a deterministic BM25 knob (alphabetical term order preserved, fully reproducible) and evaluate relativeScoreFusion (min-max normalized weighted sum) as a typed alternative to nest's current reciprocal-rank fusion in the hybrid preset -- both feed the SAME mandatory exact-cosine rerank, so ground-truth scoring is unchanged. Surface both as flags on nest-cli `search-text`/hybrid, mirroring weaviate's builder ergonomics with clap.
repos.compression_relevance: Indirect but real: the gRPC `bytes`-packing trick is the wire-format twin of nest's core compression decision to keep embeddings as a raw contiguous mmap run scored directly (never zstd, never per-element proto framing). It confirms that for vectors the win is layout + quantization (int8/f16), not entropy coding, and that the read surface should expose the packed bytes + a small encoding tag so downstream tools never re-inflate. No new entropy coder, quantizer, or graph layout is offered here -- this is a bindings/ergonomics repo, so its compression contribution is validation of an existing nest choice plus a clean discriminator-tag pattern.
repos.perf_notes: gRPC path is HTTP/2 + protobuf; the byte-packed vector blob avoids protobuf's per-element varint/tag overhead (~5 bytes/float for repeated) and per-element allocation, giving a measurably smaller, faster-to-decode payload than GraphQL JSON -- the stated motivation for the experimental gRPC Search being a drop-in replacement for GraphQL Get. Java v6 client switched embeddings to `float[]` (vs boxed) for GC-friendliness, a parallel lesson: keep vectors as flat primitive arrays. Go's net/http provides default connection pooling; client connection timeout defaults to 60s.
repos.license: BSD-3-Clause

repos.one_liner: A Helm chart (Go-templated Kubernetes YAML) that deploys the Weaviate vector DB as a StatefulSet, driven by a single layered values.yaml whose uniform per-module schema (enabled/repo/tag/registry/inferenceUrl/envconfig/resources) is compiled into ConfigMaps, Secrets, and an aggregated ENABLE_MODULES env var.
repos.core_innovation: The single-source-of-truth declarative config compiler: one flat values.yaml with a strictly uniform per-feature block schema, where every optional capability is a self-describing record carrying its own enable flag, version pin (tag), and key/value envconfig, and a helper layer (_helpers.tpl) deterministically folds the set of enabled blocks into one aggregated activation list (ENABLE_MODULES) plus generated secrets. The config schema IS the feature manifest; toggling a boolean adds/removes a whole subsystem with zero imperative wiring.
key_techniques: Uniform per-feature config record schema: every optional subsystem (module/backup/offload/auth) shares identical fields {enabled, tag, registry, repo, envconfig, resources}, so the parser/validator is written once and reused for all features
Deterministic aggregation fold: enabled blocks are collected and emitted as one comma-joined activation string (ENABLE_MODULES) in declaration order, a reproducible reduce over the config set
Version pinning by 'tag' on every component with a documented warning that unpinned tags break reproducibility on chart upgrade
Dual-source config: inline 'env'/'envconfig' values vs 'envSecrets' references, with a fixed precedence rule (env overrides static blocks)
inferenceUrl indirection: a capability is satisfied locally (deploy a pod) OR by pointing at an external endpoint, selected by one field without changing the rest of the schema
enabled:false short-circuit: nested settings under a disabled block are ignored entirely, keeping config trees inert until activated
PVC naming as a pure function of {storage.name, replica-index} for stable predictable on-disk identity
Pinned distribution channel: chart published to a static GitHub Pages Helm repo, versioned releases tied to git tags
repos.nest_application: Adapt the uniform-config-record + deterministic-fold pattern to nest-cli and the nest-format manifest. (1) nest-cli: replace ad-hoc preset flags with a single declarative build profile (TOML/YAML) where each section/codec is a uniform record {enabled, encoding, params} mirroring presets exact/compressed/tiny/hybrid; a helper folds enabled records into the section table the writer emits, so adding hnsw_index(0x07)/bm25_index(0x08) is one boolean, never imperative wiring -- an additive-format-friendly config surface nest currently lacks. (2) nest-format manifest: formalize the manifest as the single source of truth (each section a self-describing record carrying its encoding id + per-section checksum) that a deterministic fold turns into physical layout, reinforcing reproducible byte-identical builds. (3) nest-python maturin/PyPI gap: copy version-pinning-by-tag discipline and the static-repo distribution model (GitHub Pages Helm repo == a pinned wheel index) so profiles record exact model fingerprint + codec versions, guaranteeing same-input => same-file. (4) inferenceUrl indirection maps to nest's local-vs-external embedding source: one field selects 'embed locally' vs 'ingest precomputed embeddings' without schema change.
repos.compression_relevance: Essentially none directly. This repo contains zero compression, quantization, entropy-coding, graph-layout, or SIMD content -- it is pure Kubernetes deployment YAML. The only oblique relevance to the compress-more-than-everyone north star is meta: a clean declarative build-profile schema (uniform codec records folded deterministically into the section table) makes it cheaper to add and combine new codecs/presets in nest-cli and keeps reproducible builds honest, indirectly accelerating compression experimentation. It does not move the compression ratio itself.
repos.perf_notes: Not applicable -- no runtime/data-plane code; Helm is build-time template rendering. The only perf-adjacent design choice is StatefulSet podManagementPolicy=Parallel (all pods start simultaneously for Raft bootstrap), which is irrelevant to nest's offline single-file no-socket model.

synthesis.summary: This category is about nest's client/distribution surface (nest-python pyo3 bridge, nest-cli clap surface) and how vector data crosses language boundaries. None of these repos contains an entropy coder, quantizer, or on-disk codec, so their direct compression contribution is zero; their value is to the "portable, cheap, light, install-anywhere, allocation-free-at-the-boundary" pillars of the north star. The collective state of the art has four pillars. (1) PyO3 stable-ABI distribution: one cp312-abi3 wheel per OS/arch loads on every CPython >= 3.12 (and via abi3t/PEP-803 on free-threaded builds too), decoupling the binary from the interpreter patch version; paired with zero-copy buffer-protocol borrows (PyBuffer<f32>/PyReadonlyArray1) so a numpy query array is read in place as &[f32] instead of marshalled element-by-element. (2) Weaviate's tag-then-pack vector wire discipline: a vector is ONE contiguous little-endian float32 bytes blob plus a tiny side-enum (SINGLE/MULTI/quantized) — never `repeated float` proto framing (~5 bytes/elt) — with element count recovered from byte-length (len//4) rather than stored, exactly mirroring nest's mmap-contiguous, scored-directly embeddings layout and confirming the win for vectors is layout+quantization, not entropy coding. (3) clap's "the binary is the source of truth": Jaro did_you_mean typo correction on the error branch, and a re-exec dynamic-completion protocol (CompleteEnv) that can read the actual file for candidate completion, plus feature-gated crate split for minimal binary size. (4) Weaviate's search-semantics knobs (minimum_should_match / OR operator, relativeScoreFusion min-max normalized weighted sum) and Helm's uniform-config-record + deterministic-fold pattern for declarative, reproducible build profiles. Critically, I verified against nest's source: nest_file.rs:22-24/35-37/54-56 do query.extract::<Vec<f32>>() (a full heap alloc+memcpy per search), every nest-runtime search fn (search.rs:124/147/181) already takes &[f32], the search is read-only over an immutable mmap (so Python::detach is sound and deterministic), nest-python is on pyo3 0.28 + abi3-py312 + cdylib (baseline correct), there is NO maturin/pyproject build path (pyproject.toml explicitly disclaims publishing), and nest-cli uses clap v4 with only the `derive` feature (no `suggestions`/`unicode`). So the steals are concrete upgrades, not green-field adoption.
synthesis.state_of_the_art: Four converging pillars. ABI/DISTRIBUTION (PyO3): the stable ABI is a *build feature* not a source macro — opting into abi3-pyXY makes the linker emit only Py_LIMITED_API symbols so one .so loads on every CPython >= floor; PEP-803 abi3t extends this to free-threaded builds with an opaque-PyObject variant forward-compatible to all future 3.X; maturin produces the single cp312-abi3 manylinux/macos/windows wheel. ZERO-COPY FFI (PyO3): Bound<'py,T> = (Py<T> handle, Python<'py> GIL token) drops the refcount on Drop; the buffer protocol via PyBuffer<f32> / rust-numpy PyReadonlyArray1 borrows a contiguous backing store as &[f32] with no copy; Python::detach releases the GIL around a pure-Rust compute so concurrent threads run. VECTOR WIRE LAYOUT (Weaviate py/go clients): tag-then-pack — one struct.pack contiguous little-endian f32 bytes blob + a side VectorType enum carrying dtype/layout out-of-band, count derived from len//4, additive room for int8/fp16 tags without touching the byte run; this is the wire twin of mmap-and-score-directly and explicitly avoids protobuf's ~5 bytes/float repeated-field overhead. CLI ERGONOMICS (clap): the binary is the runtime source of truth for valid inputs — strsim::jaro did_you_mean at 0.7 cutoff on the error path, CompleteEnv re-exec completion that can interrogate real data, CompletionCandidate decoupling generation from per-shell rendering, feature-gated crate split for binary-size minimization. SEARCH SEMANTICS + CONFIG (Weaviate + Helm): minimum_should_match/OR BM25 operator and relativeScoreFusion (per-result-set min-max normalize then weighted sum) as deterministic alternatives/additions to reciprocal-rank fusion, both feeding a single rerank; and the uniform-config-record schema folded deterministically into a feature manifest (Helm's ENABLE_MODULES fold, version-pinning-by-tag for reproducibility, static pinned distribution channel).
top_innovations: PyO3 buffer-protocol zero-copy borrow (PyBuffer<f32>/PyReadonlyArray1): read the numpy query array's backing memory in place as &[f32], eliminating the per-search Vec<f32> alloc+memcpy that nest_file.rs currently pays before the SIMD kernel — highest value, smallest surface, hot path.

abi3 + abi3t single-wheel distribution via maturin: one cp312-abi3 wheel runs on 3.12/3.13/3.14+ and (with abi3t) free-threaded builds, directly closing nest's listed PyPI/maturin gap and delivering the 'install-anywhere' leg of the north star for the python-builds half.

Weaviate tag-then-pack vector layout (contiguous LE-f32 bytes + 1-byte dtype side-enum, count = len//4): validates nest's mmap-contiguous embeddings choice and gives the discriminator-tag pattern that lets nest swap f32->f16->int8 per named-vector with zero per-element decode and no NEST_FORMAT_VERSION bump.

Python::detach (release GIL) around the read-only mmap search: lets concurrent Python threads issue parallel deterministic searches against one open NestFile, since the file is immutable post-build — free throughput with no correctness/determinism cost.

clap Jaro did_you_mean (suggestions feature, deterministic 0.7 cutoff): typo correction over the 8 subcommand names AND extensible over real container chunk_ids so a missed `nest cite` suggests the nearest valid id, on the error branch only (zero hot-path cost).

clap CompleteEnv re-exec dynamic completion that reads the actual .nest file for content_hash/chunk_id/preset completion — offline, single-file, but MUST stay in pure-rust nest-cli/nest-runtime so the ~300-500ms python boot never lands on the completion path.

Weaviate search-semantics knobs: minimum_should_match/OR BM25 operator (alphabetical term order = reproducible) and relativeScoreFusion as a typed alternative to reciprocal-rank fusion, both feeding the SAME mandatory exact-cosine rerank so ground-truth scoring is unchanged.

Helm uniform-config-record + deterministic-fold: a declarative build profile (TOML) where each section/codec is a {enabled, encoding, params} record folded into the writer's section table, making 'add hnsw_index(0x07)/bm25_index(0x08)' one boolean and keeping reproducible builds honest via version-pinning-by-tag (model fingerprint + codec versions).
clap feature-gated crate split: make hnsw/bm25/pyo3 opt-in cargo features so the smallest sovereign binary ships only what a given deployment needs.

Count-from-byte-length trick (len//(dim*elt_size)): derive element/row counts from the section byte length instead of storing a redundant count, shaving header bytes — a micro-win consistent with nest's compress-more discipline.

compression_wins: Count-from-byte-length (Weaviate): derive vector/row counts as len/(dim*elt_size) instead of storing a redundant count field per section — shaves header bytes on every embeddings/named-vector section, consistent with nest's compress-more discipline.

1-byte dtype side-enum tag (Weaviate tag-then-pack): makes per-(named-)vector dtype fp32/fp16/int8 a single discriminator byte rather than a layout change, so nest can shrink an embeddings section by swapping codecs WITHOUT touching the byte run or bumping NEST_FORMAT_VERSION — keeps the format additive while the codec gets smaller (enables future per-vector int8 on the image side while text stays f16, etc.).

Zero-copy buffer-protocol borrow (PyO3): keeps the search hot path allocation-free end-to-end (mmap'd quantized/compressed embeddings in, borrowed query in), so the int8/f16/zstd compression wins in nest-format are NOT given back as alloc+memcpy marshalling overhead at the python boundary — protecting realized compression gains at serve time.

abi3/abi3t single-tiny-wheel distribution (PyO3): not a byte-codec, but the minimal-distribution-surface leg of 'compress more / be lighter than everyone' — one small artifact per OS serving every Python on every machine instead of N interpreter-specific binaries.

Validation that for vectors the win is layout + quantization, NOT entropy coding (Weaviate confirms `bytes`-not-`repeated-float` is the right call): reinforces nest's correct decision to keep embeddings as a raw contiguous mmap run scored directly (never zstd on embeddings) and to invest compression effort in better quantization (int8 today, candidates: per-vector scale int8, product/scalar quantization later) rather than entropy-coding the hot-path floats.
watch_outs: NEVER adopt any transport from the Weaviate clients: both are network clients (REST + gRPC over sockets, default :50051) — nest is offline-by-construction and must NOT open a socket. Steal ONLY the byte-layout (tag-then-pack), the count-from-length trick, the fusion math, and the batch ergonomics; leave gRPC/HTTP entirely.

clap dynamic completion (CompleteEnv) re-execs the binary — the ~300-500ms python boot overhead from search-text MUST never land on the completion path. Keep completion candidate generation in pure-rust nest-cli/nest-runtime (mmap reads only), never invoking python/embed_query.py.

abi3 has a small documented runtime cost vs version-specific builds (cannot inline against a known CPython struct layout). Acceptable for nest because the hot loop is pure-Rust nest-runtime, NOT across the FFI boundary — but do not move numeric/scoring work across the pyo3 boundary to 'use' the binding; PyO3 must stay confined to nest-python, with nest-format/nest-runtime pure Rust.

Keep the typed-thiserror -> PyValueError mapping intact when refactoring the query path: library code must never panic (HARD CONSTRAINT). A PyBuffer borrow that fails (non-contiguous, wrong dtype, wrong shape) must map to a typed PyValueError, not unwrap/expect.

relativeScoreFusion (min-max normalize) and minimum_should_match must remain fully deterministic to respect nest's reproducibility guarantee: preserve alphabetical BM25 term order and seeded behavior; min-max normalization is order-independent but verify tie-breaking is deterministic. Both MUST still feed the mandatory exact-cosine rerank — never return an ANN/BM25 proxy score.

Helm's value is meta only (declarative config + version-pinning), and the extract itself rates it low/none for compression — do not let the build-profile refactor balloon nest-cli or the manifest. Respect the <=300-line-per-file (333 hard cap), single-responsibility, edition-2024 conventions; a config compiler can easily violate the line cap.

The named/multi-vector layout steal is FUTURE work (nest stores a single embeddings matrix today). When added it MUST use a RESERVED section id 0x09+ and the additive-only rule — do NOT bump NEST_FORMAT_VERSION unless an existing field changes meaning. Reuse existing SECTION_ENCODING ids; do not invent a parallel dtype tag scheme that diverges from the encoding ids.

maturin/PyPI introduces a network-fetch install step and an external supply chain — this is for distribution convenience and does NOT compromise runtime sovereignty (the runtime still mmaps a local file, no socket). But pin everything (model fingerprint, codec versions, wheel hashes) so the 'same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical file' guarantee survives the install boundary; an unpinned dependency would silently break reproducibility (Helm's explicit warning).

PyReadonlyArray1 (rust-numpy) would add a numpy build dependency and a heavier dep tree; prefer pure-pyo3 PyBuffer<f32> to keep the small-core/light pillar. Only add the rust-numpy feature path as an OPTIONAL feature if a numpy-native ergonomic API is demanded.

Python::detach requires the borrowed query data to be safely held across the GIL release; ensure the buffer's backing memory cannot be mutated/freed by Python during the detached compute (copy into an owned Vec before detach if the buffer's lifetime cannot be guaranteed) — getting this wrong is a use-after-free, the one place the zero-copy win must be traded for safety.

plans.framing: COMPRESSION-AND-FORMAT-FIRST. The moat is the byte container. nest wins or loses on one number: bytes-on-disk at equal retrieval fidelity. Every subsystem (SIMD, ANN, BM25, bindings) exists to serve that number or to keep the sovereign/offline/single-file/deterministic guarantees while the codec stack drives size down. The container is treated as a layered, self-describing codec engine: content-defined chunking + content-hash dedup -> domain-specific decorrelation (delta/FOR/bitpack for integers, shuffle for numeric planes, rotation+sub-byte quantization for embeddings, tape/columnar for structured docs) -> a trained-dictionary entropy stage -> cost-driven per-section codec selection. Everything else hangs off the .nest file.
plans.thesis: nest's durable advantage is a frozen, additive, self-describing byte container that compresses every data type harder than the field while keeping four properties no competitor combines: sovereign/offline (never opens a socket), single-file (one mmap), deterministic (same chunks + same model fingerprint => byte-identical), and citable (nest://content_hash/chunk_id reopens an exact byte span). The grounded reality of the codebase makes this winnable cheaply: content_hash already hashes DECODED canonical-six bytes with NAR-grade length-prefixed name-domain framing, decode_payload already rejects unknown encodings cleanly, and int8.rs already carries a scale_kind discriminator. So the entire compression roadmap is ADDITIVE within v1 (new encoding ids 4-255, new section ids 0x09+, per-payload version bumps), with exactly ONE place a true v2 is justified. The largest unrealized wins are concentrated and verifiable in-tree: (1) embeddings are the dominant, never-zstd'd bytes and sit at an 8 bpw int8 floor while the field has converged on rotation + sub-byte quantization (RQ at 4x near-lossless, RaBitQ/PQ/binary at 8-32x) guarded by an exact rerank nest ALREADY mandates; (2) the integer/string metadata sections (HNSW neighbor u32, BM25 raw u32 doc/tf, per-chunk u64 spans, 71-byte ascii chunk_ids) are stored with zero structural compression and are textbook delta+bitpack/FST/raw-digest targets; (3) the text sections run level-19 zstd with no trained dictionary across nest's many-short-similar-chunk corpora; (4) there is no cross-chunk/cross-file content-hash dedup before the entropy coder. Two correctness truths gate the aggressive path and must be designed in, not bolted on: score_subset currently reranks against the SAME lossy stored dtype (so 'returned score is real cosine' becomes 'real cosine at stored precision' once you go below int8 - sub-int8 REQUIRES a separate full-precision/f16 rerank-source section), and materialize.rs expands EVERY dtype to an n*dim*4 f32 buffer whenever HNSW is attached (so any embedding shrink is paid back in RAM unless the ANN distance path scores packed blocks directly). Execute the additive codec stack in dependency order behind these two guardrails and nest pushes the tiny preset's 0.283 ratio toward sub-0.1 on embedding-dominated corpora with recall@10 held by the mandatory exact rerank.

pillars.name: Universal layered byte container (the moat)
pillars.what: Make .nest a self-describing, additive codec engine: a section/encoding registry where each codec implements decode(&[u8])->Cow in its own <=300-line file, a skippable-OPTIONAL vs unskippable-REQUIRED flag on section entries so old runtimes serve unknown optional sections and error cleanly on unknown required ones, and cost-driven per-section codec selection (trial-encode each non-embedding section under all candidates, keep smallest measured output, record the chosen id per section). decode_payload already cleanly rejects unknown encodings and content_hash already hashes DECODED canonical-six bytes, so every new codec stays content_hash-stable and citation-safe. This is the scaffolding all other pillars register into.

pillars.name: Embedding compression frontier (the dominant bytes)
pillars.what: Drive the embeddings section - nest's largest and only never-zstd'd section - from the 8 bpw int8 floor down through a deterministic, rotation-first quantization ladder, all scored in-place off mmap and all guarded by the mandatory exact rerank: (a) block-scaled / rotational int8 as scale_kind=1 in the EXISTING int8 codec (near-lossless 4x, no new id, no version bump); (b) int4 block-scaled (~4.25 bpw) and NF4/MXFP4 sub-byte codecs as new encoding ids 4-5; (c) RaBitQ 1-bit (sign codes + ~2 f32 correctors, AND+popcount scoring, ~32x) and PQ4-FastScan (asymmetric LUT) as the frontier. Rotations are seeded from the model fingerprint (store the seed, never a dense matrix; use FHT for O(D log D)). Matryoshka prefix truncation makes dimensionality a deterministic lossy knob that multiplies with every codec. Every quantizer is a pure function of input -> byte-identical builds.

pillars.name: Integer + string metadata compression (the free wins)
pillars.what: Replace the structurally-uncompressed cold sections with the canonical integer/string codecs, all decoding byte-identically so content_hash and citations are unchanged: delta(d1)+per-block-minimal-bitpack (FOR/PForDelta) for HNSW neighbor ids (sort-per-list, ~log2(n) bits vs 32) and BM25 doc-id gaps + tf bitpacking, delta+varint/FOR for per-source monotone span offsets, raw 32-byte SHA-256 digests instead of 71-byte ascii chunk_ids (~2.2x) with an FST or front-coded term/id dictionary that stays binary-searchable off mmap, and a deduped source_uri string pool referenced by index. Index changes bump only HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION / BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION; spans/chunk_ids use a new reserved encoding id. FOR/EF select() keeps O(1) random access so citation reopen never inflates a whole section.

pillars.name: Text / structured-document codec stack (compress-AND-serve everything)
pillars.what: Beat generic zstd on text by ordering the stack correctly: corpus-trained shared zstd dictionary (ZDICT over chunks_canonical/spans/provenance/bm25 terms, fed sorted so it is a pure function) to kill per-section cold-start + cross-chunk redundancy; FSST as a transparent text codec so single chunks decode O(1) off mmap for citation reopen where block-zstd forces a whole-section inflate; byte-level subword tokenization (BPE/Unigram, byte_fallback, U+2581 reversible markup) as a dictionary front-end that ALSO closes the CJK/Thai BM25 gap with the same shipped model; and for the json/yaml/parquet/dataset roadmap a fixed-stride u64 structural tape + separate length-prefixed value blob (simdjson-style) and FlexBuffers/VPack min-width offset tables + key-interning so structured payloads are sub-document-citable AND zstd-friendly. Canonical text stays byte-exact so content_hash is stable.

pillars.name: Corpus-level dedup, versioning + real-time edit
pillars.what: Add the cross-chunk/cross-file dedup layer that attacks redundancy BEFORE the entropy coder (the field's biggest structural lever on whole-repo/dataset/db payloads): content-defined chunking (FastCDC/Gear, seeded, edit-local boundaries) + content-hash dedup so identical/near-identical spans store once with refcounts, run STRICTLY on decompressed bytes with compression applied per unique block afterward. Layer an append-only edit journal (new reserved section, overlaid in memory at open, never mutating frozen bytes) plus a deterministic compact() that re-derives a minimal maximally-compressed container - the moment to re-run the trained dictionary, re-quantize, and drop dead chunks. A reproducibility manifest (sorted per-section content-hash + decoded_length + recipe) makes 'same chunks => byte-identical' third-party-verifiable offline.

pillars.name: Graph search + sovereign serve guarantees
pillars.what: Deliver the north-star graph-search pillar as a cheap additive integer overlay: an optional CSR/CSC adjacency section (chunk-to-chunk semantic/citation/NEXT_CHUNK edges) reusing the integer bitpack codec, traversed off mmap, seeded from exact-cosine top-k and feeding the SAME mandatory exact rerank so graph traversal is a candidate generator that never changes returned scores - and which lets nest DROP chunk-overlap text by reconstructing neighbor context from edges. Keep the runtime sovereign and fast: generalize the SimdBackend OnceLock into a functable so new kernels (f16/F16C, i8-VNNI/dotprod integer-domain dot for true bit-determinism, popcount, nibble-unpack) register one entry each under the 300-line cap, fix the materialize-to-f32 RAM leak by scoring packed blocks in the ANN distance path, and keep the scalar fallback a first-class verified sibling. Bindings ship one cp312-abi3 wheel with zero-copy PyBuffer query borrows so realized compression is never paid back as marshalling overhead.

plans.compression_strategy: A single layered codec stack, applied per data type, with two invariants: embeddings are NEVER entropy-coded/zstd'd (scored in-place off mmap) so they shrink only via fixed-stride quantization read by stride; everything else is decorrelated then entropy-coded, with codec choice cost-driven and recorded per section. The universal pipeline is: content-defined chunk + content-hash dedup (decompressed bytes) -> domain decorrelation -> trained-dictionary entropy stage -> cost-driven pick-smallest. PER TYPE: (1) TEXT/JSON/YAML chunks_canonical: optional byte-level subword tokenization (dense ids before entropy) -> FSST (transparent, O(1) per-chunk random access for citations) OR corpus-trained-ZDICT zstd (whole-section scan) chosen by measured size; structured json/yaml encoded as a fixed-stride u64 tape + length-prefixed value blob with min-width offset tables and per-file key-interning, then zstd on the cold parts. Canonical text stays byte-exact (content_hash stable). (2) EMBEDDINGS (dominant bytes, never zstd): deterministic rotation-first quantization ladder scored in-place - block-scaled/rotational int8 (scale_kind=1, 4x near-lossless, no new id) -> int4 block-64 + NF4/MXFP4 (~4.25 bpw, new ids 4-5) -> RaBitQ 1-bit AND+popcount and PQ4-FastScan (8-32x), with Matryoshka prefix truncation as a multiplicative dim knob and PCA-whitening before quantize as a free quality lift. Sub-int8 codecs MUST ship a separate f16 (or f32) rerank-source section so the exact rerank stays honest. Rotation/codebook/k-means all seeded from the model fingerprint -> byte-identical. (3) PARQUET/COLUMNAR/DATASETS: per-column lightweight codec cascade (RLE/FOR/delta/dictionary/FSST/bitpack) chosen by a deterministic sampling Analyze pass (DuckDB pattern), byte-shuffle/bytedelta in front of zstd on numeric planes, frame-of-reference + delta on monotone id columns, dictionary-encode low-cardinality enums (verdict/category/lang) to a few bits; dedup-by-reference before zstd. (4) PDF: canonicalize to deterministic markdown/text BEFORE chunking (exposes cross-document redundancy and stabilizes content_hash), then treat as text; keep original byte spans for citation. (5) AUDIO/VIDEO: store native/transcoded payload bytes verbatim (copy-without-recode when codecs match, the Deep Lake/ggml lesson) addressed by content_hash with a CDC chunk index, never lossy-re-encoded inside the container; embeddings (CLIP-style, L2-normalized, shared section) ride the same quantization ladder as text. (6) WHOLE-DB/REPO: content-defined chunking + global content-hash dedup is the headline lever (cross-file duplication dominates the codec), zstd level 22 + long-distance-matching for far-apart cross-file matches, and the reproducibility manifest + append-only edit journal so versions store deltas not copies. The integer metadata stack (delta+bitpack/FOR for HNSW adjacency and BM25 postings, delta+varint for spans, raw-32-byte digests + FST dictionary for ids) applies under all types and is pure structural-redundancy removal that stacks under zstd. Net: the headline single move is rotation-first sub-byte embedding quantization (embeddings are most of the bytes); the headline structural move is content-hash dedup before the entropy coder; the headline 'free' move is integer-section delta+bitpack; the headline text move is the trained shared dictionary + FSST.
plans.format_evolution: v1 STAYS FROZEN AND ADDITIVE for the entire compression roadmap. NEST_FORMAT_VERSION is bumped ONLY when an existing field changes meaning. Three additive lanes carry everything: (A) NEW WIRE ENCODINGS in the reserved 4-255 space (raw=0/zstd=1/float16=2/int8=3 occupied): SECTION_ENCODING_INTPACK (delta+bitpack/FOR for integer sections), SECTION_ENCODING_SPANS_DELTA, SECTION_ENCODING_ZSTD_DICT (trained-dictionary zstd), SECTION_ENCODING_SHUF_ZSTD (byte-shuffle pre-codec), SECTION_ENCODING_FSST (transparent text), and embedding codecs SECTION_ENCODING_INT4/NF4/MXFP4/RABITQ/PQ. decode_payload's existing default arm rejects unknown ids with UnsupportedSectionEncoding, so an old runtime fails closed and a new runtime dispatches by id - additive by construction. content_hash hashes DECODED bytes, so any codec that round-trips bit-exactly to the same canonical bytes yields the SAME content_hash (verify with a roundtrip+hash test per codec); only embeddings are precision-dependent, which is already documented and accepted. (B) NEW OPTIONAL SECTIONS at id 0x09+ (0x01-0x08 occupied): SECTION_DICTIONARY (trained zstd dict blob), SECTION_EMBEDDINGS_FP (full-precision/f16 rerank source for sub-int8 presets), SECTION_GRAPH_ADJACENCY (CSR edges), SECTION_CHUNK_SCALARS (columnar pre-filter metadata), SECTION_TOKENIZER_MODEL (frozen vocab/FST), SECTION_EDIT_JOURNAL (append-only deltas), SECTION_MERKLE_INDEX (BLAKE3 chunk-group parent CVs for partial citation verification), SECTION_DEDUP_MAP (content-hash refcount table), SECTION_STRUCTURE_TAPE (json/yaml fixed-stride tape), SECTION_REPRO_MANIFEST (sorted per-section content-hash + decoded_length + recipe), SECTION_EVAL_RESULTS (self-certified per-preset nDCG/recall). Optional sections are EXCLUDED from content_hash by the existing spec, so adding them never invalidates citations. (C) PER-PAYLOAD VERSION BUMPS internal to a section (HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION, BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION, INT8_PAYLOAD_VERSION, new int8 scale_kind=1) for codec changes inside an already-defined section - never NEST_FORMAT_VERSION. HARDENING that stays additive: add a skippable-OPTIONAL vs unskippable-REQUIRED flag on SectionEntry (reserved bits) so old runtimes serve unknown optional sections and error cleanly on unknown required ones; verify (not just declare) the 64-byte embeddings alignment at open for SIMD aligned loads + tail-safe scanning. THE ONE TRUE v2 (NEST_FORMAT_VERSION=2, justified, deferred to its own phase): make content_hash a BLAKE3 Merkle ROOT over per-section/per-chunk content hashes instead of a flat SHA-256 over concatenated canonical-six bytes. This CHANGES the meaning of the existing content_hash field (it is the citation identity anchor and the four-integrity-surface contract), so it cannot be additive - it must be v2, with v1 readers retained. The payoff (O(touched-bytes) partial verification, single-chunk citation proof against the root, corpus-level identical-subtree dedup by hash equality) is large enough to warrant a v2, but ONLY after the additive codec stack has shipped and proven its ratio; until then SHA-256 over decoded canonical-six stays frozen and a NEW additive blake3 algorithm-id can be offered for large-blob addressing without touching the v1 default.

roadmap.phase: Phase 0 - guardrails + scaffolding (unblock everything, zero ratio yet)
roadmap.goal: Make the format a clean additive codec engine and remove the two correctness/RAM blockers that gate aggressive embedding compression, before adding any codec.
workstreams: Codec registry refactor: turn encoding/mod.rs decode_payload into a visitor-style registry where each encoding id is one <=300-line module implementing decode(&[u8])->Cow; reserve the 4-255 ids and 0x09+ section ids as named constants in layout/mod.rs (no behavior change yet).

Cost-driven encoding selection: generalize writer/encoding_choice.rs + payload.rs::maybe_zstd from a binary raw-vs-zstd switch into a deterministic try-all-pick-smallest chooser recording the chosen id per section (raw always a candidate so it never regresses).

Honest-rerank design + RAM-leak fix: add SECTION_EMBEDDINGS_FP (optional f16/f32 rerank source) plumbing and make score_subset rerank against it for quantized presets; teach the ANN distance path (materialize.rs / ann) to score packed blocks (or keep f16, not f32) so block-quant is not expanded to n*dim*4 in RAM.

SIMD functable + alignment verify: generalize the SimdBackend OnceLock into a functable so new kernels register one entry each; verify 64-byte embeddings alignment at reader open and add a NEST_FORCE_SCALAR-style parity test harness (exact-equality where integer-domain).

Reproducibility + per-codec roundtrip gates: add a roundtrip+content_hash-equality test per new codec slot and a SECTION_REPRO_MANIFEST writer (sorted per-section content-hash + decoded_length + recipe) so byte-identical builds become third-party verifiable; wire one cp312-abi3 maturin wheel + zero-copy PyBuffer<f32> query borrow + Python::detach around the read-only mmap search.

roadmap.phase: Phase 1 - the free integer + string wins (ship ratio with near-zero risk)
roadmap.goal: Compress the structurally-uncompressed cold metadata sections that today store raw u32/u64/ascii, all decoding byte-identically so content_hash and citations are unchanged.
workstreams: intpack codec (delta(d1)+zigzag+per-128-block minimal-bitpack, FOR variant with select() for O(1) random access) as SECTION_ENCODING_INTPACK; shared module used by HNSW/BM25/spans.
HNSW neighbor ids: sort-per-list + delta+bitpack in ann/codec.rs (bump HNSW_PAYLOAD_VERSION only); shrinks the tiny-preset index section with zero recall change (identical id set).
BM25 postings: delta-gap doc ids + bitpacked tf + 1-byte log-quantized fieldnorm doc_lengths in bm25/codec.rs (bump BM25_PAYLOAD_VERSION); front-code or FST the alphabetical term dictionary.

chunk_ids + spans: store 32 raw SHA-256 digest bytes instead of 71-byte ascii (~2.2x); delta+varint/FOR per-source monotone span offsets and a deduped source_uri string pool (new reserved encoding id; content_hash stable because decoded OriginalSpan values are identical).
byte-shuffle/bytedelta pre-codec (SECTION_ENCODING_SHUF_ZSTD) on numeric planes (int8 scale array, span offset high bytes) strictly gated off the embeddings body.

roadmap.phase: Phase 2 - text dictionary + the safe embedding step (the headline ratio levers)
roadmap.goal: Beat generic zstd on text and take the first near-lossless embedding compression step that needs no rerank-source.
workstreams: Trained shared zstd dictionary: SECTION_DICTIONARY blob + SECTION_ENCODING_ZSTD_DICT, ZDICT trained build-time over sorted chunks_canonical/spans/provenance/bm25 terms (pure function -> deterministic); compress text sections against it.
FSST transparent text codec (SECTION_ENCODING_FSST) for chunks_canonical so single-chunk citation reopen decodes O(1) without whole-section inflate; chosen vs ZDICT-zstd by the cost-driven selector.

Block-scaled / rotational int8 as int8 scale_kind=1 (seeded FWHT rotation from model fingerprint, one f16 scale per 32-dim block): near-lossless 4x with NO new encoding id and NO version bump; recovers per-vector-outlier loss.
Matryoshka prefix truncation: build-time truncate+L2-renormalize to mrl_dim, two-pass coarse(prefix)->exact(full) search; additive manifest fields, multiplies with int8.
zstd level/LDM knobs (replace hardcoded level-19) for large whole-db/repo payloads; ship a 'micro' preset (ZDICT/FSST text + block-int8 + hnsw) below tiny's 0.283.

roadmap.phase: Phase 3 - sub-byte embeddings + dedup (push toward sub-0.1)
roadmap.goal: Cross the int8 floor with rotation-first sub-byte quantization (guarded by the Phase-0 rerank source) and add the corpus-level dedup that attacks redundancy before the entropy coder.
workstreams: int4 block-64 codec (SECTION_ENCODING_INT4, ~4.25 bpw) + NF4/MXFP4 sub-byte codecs (ids 5-6) with a fused dequant+dot SIMD kernel (SQNBitGemm pattern, never materializing f32 in RAM); PCA-whiten build-time before quantize for free quality.

RaBitQ 1-bit codec (sign codes + ~2 f32 correctors, AND+popcount kernel, ~32x) and PQ4-FastScan (asymmetric LUT) as candidate-generation codecs feeding the mandatory exact rerank against SECTION_EMBEDDINGS_FP; a 'nano' preset.

Content-defined chunking (FastCDC/Gear, seeded) + content-hash dedup (SECTION_DEDUP_MAP, refcounts) on chunks_canonical, run on decompressed bytes BEFORE zstd, with a guardrail test that compress-then-dedup is never done.
Integer-domain int8/int4 dot via VNNI/dotprod (vpdpbusd/vdotq_s32) for ~4x speed AND true cross-CPU bit-determinism on the quantized path; F16C tier for the f16 path.
SECTION_CHUNK_SCALARS columnar pre-filter (lang/byte_len/source_id, low-cardinality enums dictionary-coded) scanned before SIMD scoring, opt-in so it never weakens the exact-rerank ground truth.

roadmap.phase: Phase 4 - structured docs, graph search, edit + the v2 decision
roadmap.goal: Extend compress-AND-serve to json/yaml/parquet and whole-repos, add the graph-search pillar, enable real-time edit, and only now evaluate the one true v2.
workstreams: Structured tape: SECTION_STRUCTURE_TAPE (fixed-stride u64 tape + length-prefixed value blob, simdjson-style) + min-width offset tables + key-interning for json/yaml/parquet, sub-document citable (nest://content_hash/chunk_id#json_pointer); per-column DuckDB-style codec cascade chosen by deterministic Analyze.
